entries.subject: module-map
entries.name: Bilinear map
entries.definition: For $R$-modules $M,N,P$, a map of sets $M\times N\to P$ is bilinear if it is $R$-linear in each variable after the other variable is fixed.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Bimodule with commuting actions
entries.definition: An $(A,B)$-bimodule is an abelian group with an $A$-module structure and a $B$-module structure whose scalar actions commute. Writing the $B$-action on the right gives $(am)b=a(mb)$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Base change of a ring homomorphism
entries.definition: Given $R\to S$ and $R\to R'$, the base change of the first map along the second is $R'\to S\otimes_R R'$, where $r'\mapsto 1\otimes r'$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Base change of a module
entries.definition: For $R\to S$, an $S$-module $M$, and $R\to R'$, the base change is the $S\otimes_R R'$-module $M\otimes_R R'$. The tensor product agrees with $M\otimes_S(S\otimes_R R')$.

entries.subject: ring-subset
entries.name: Vanishing set in a prime spectrum
entries.definition: For a subset $T\subseteq R$, the set $V(T)$ consists of primes of $R$ containing every element of $T$.

entries.subject: algebra-element
entries.name: Standard open in a prime spectrum
entries.definition: For $f\in R$, the set $D(f)$ consists of the primes of $R$ that do not contain $f$. It is the complement of $V(\{f\})$.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Zariski topology on a prime spectrum
entries.definition: The closed sets of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ are the subsets $V(T)$ as $T$ ranges over subsets of $R$. Their complements are unions of standard opens.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Oka family of ideals
entries.definition: A family $\mathcal F$ of ideals in $R$ is Oka when it contains $R$ and when $(I:a)$ and $I+(a)$ belonging to $\mathcal F$ force $I$ to belong to $\mathcal F$, for every ideal $I$ and every $a\in R$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Integral closure of the source in the target
entries.definition: For $R\to S$, the integral closure of $R$ in $S$ is the subring of $S$ consisting of elements satisfying monic polynomials with coefficients in the image of $R$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Integrally closed in a specified overring
entries.definition: The map is an inclusion $R\subseteq S$ and every element of $S$ integral over $R$ belongs to $R$.

entries.subject: algebra-element
entries.name: Almost integral element of a fraction field
entries.definition: For a domain $R$ and $g\in\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, there is a nonzero $r\in R$ with $rg^n\in R$ for every $n\geq 0$.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Completely normal domain
entries.definition: The ring is a domain $R$ and every almost integral element of its fraction field belongs to $R$.

entries.subject: algebra-element
entries.name: Element integral over a chosen ideal
entries.definition: For $R\to S$, $I\subseteq R$, and $g\in S$, there is a monic polynomial $T^d+\sum_{j<d}a_jT^j$ with $a_j\in I^{d-j}$ that vanishes at $g$ after applying $R\to S$ to its coefficients.

entries.subject: module-element
entries.name: Annihilator of a module element
entries.definition: For $m\in M$, its annihilator is the ideal $\{a\in R:am=0\}$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Annihilator of a module
entries.definition: The annihilator of an $R$-module $M$ is the intersection of the annihilators of all its elements, or equivalently the kernel of the scalar action on $M$.

entries.subject: field
entries.name: Perfect closure of a field
entries.definition: For a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, take the subfield of an algebraic closure formed by all elements some $p^n$-th power of which lies in $k$. For a field of characteristic zero take $k$ itself. This is a perfect, purely inseparable extension of $k$.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Value group of a valuation ring
entries.definition: For a valuation ring $A$ with fraction field $K$, use $K^\times/A^\times$ in additive notation. Declare $[u]\geq[v]$ when $u/v$ belongs to $A$. This gives a totally ordered abelian group.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Valuation associated to a valuation ring
entries.definition: For a valuation ring $A$ with fraction field $K$, the valuation on $K^\times$ is the quotient map to $K^\times/A^\times$ with the order defined by $A$. Its restriction to $A\setminus\{0\}$ takes nonnegative values.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Essentially finite type ring map
entries.definition: The target $S$ is isomorphic as an $R$-algebra to a localization of a finite type $R$-algebra.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Essentially finitely presented ring map
entries.definition: The target $S$ is isomorphic as an $R$-algebra to a localization of a finitely presented $R$-algebra.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Homogeneous spectrum of a graded ring
entries.definition: For a nonnegatively graded ring $S$, the space $\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ is the set of homogeneous prime ideals that do not contain the ideal $S_+$ of positive-degree elements. Use the subspace topology from $\operatorname{Spec}(S)$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Numerical polynomial valued in an abelian group
entries.definition: An eventually defined function on the integers with values in an abelian group is a numerical polynomial if it agrees for all sufficiently large $n$ with a finite sum $\sum_i\binom ni a_i$ with coefficients $a_i$ in that group.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Hilbert polynomial of a finite module over a Noetherian local ring
entries.definition: For a finite $R$-module $M$ over a Noetherian local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$, the Hilbert polynomial is the unique rational polynomial agreeing eventually with $n\mapsto \operatorname{length}_R(\mathfrak m^nM/\mathfrak m^{n+1}M)$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Degree of the cumulative Hilbert function
entries.definition: For a finite module $M$ over a Noetherian local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$, put $d(M)=-\infty$ when $M=0$. Otherwise $d(M)$ is the degree of the eventual numerical polynomial of $n\mapsto\operatorname{length}_R(M/\mathfrak m^{n+1}M)$.

entries.subject: ideal
entries.name: Height of a prime ideal
entries.definition: For a prime $\mathfrak p\subseteq R$, its height is the Krull dimension of $R_{\mathfrak p}$, equivalently the supremum of lengths of chains of primes ending at $\mathfrak p$.

entries.subject: ideal
entries.name: Symbolic power of a prime ideal
entries.definition: For a prime $\mathfrak p\subseteq R$ and $n\geq0$, the symbolic power $\mathfrak p^{(n)}$ is the contraction of $\mathfrak p^nR_{\mathfrak p}$ to $R$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Relative assassin of a module
entries.definition: For $R\to S$ and an $S$-module $N$, the relative assassin consists of primes $\mathfrak q\subseteq S$ associated to $N\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ as an $S$-module, where $\mathfrak p$ is the contraction of $\mathfrak q$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Weakly associated primes of a module
entries.definition: A prime belongs to the weak assassin of $M$ when it is minimal among the primes containing the annihilator of some $m\in M$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Embedded associated primes of a module
entries.definition: The embedded associated primes of $M$ are the nonminimal elements of its set $\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)$ ordered by inclusion.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Embedded primes of a ring
entries.definition: These are the embedded associated primes of the module $R$ over itself.

entries.subject: module-sequence
entries.name: Regular sequence on a module
entries.definition: For $M$ and a tuple $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in R$, multiplication by $f_i$ is injective on $M/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})M$ for each $i$, and $M/(f_1,\ldots,f_r)M$ is nonzero.

entries.subject: ring-parameters
entries.name: Regular sequence in a ring
entries.definition: A tuple in $R$ is a regular sequence in $R$ when it is regular on $R$ as a module over itself.

entries.subject: module-ideal-pair
entries.name: Regular sequence on a module in a specified ideal
entries.definition: For an $R$-module $M$ and an ideal $I\subseteq R$, this is an $M$-regular tuple $(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ such that every $f_i$ lies in $I$.

entries.subject: ring-ideal-pair
entries.name: Regular sequence in a specified ideal of a ring
entries.definition: For a ring $R$ and an ideal $I\subseteq R$, this is a regular tuple on the module $R$ with every term in $I$.

entries.subject: module-sequence
entries.name: Quasi-regular sequence on a module
entries.definition: For $J=(f_1,\dots,f_r)$, the natural graded map $(M/JM)[X_1,\dots,X_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}J^nM/J^{n+1}M$ is an isomorphism. It sends the coefficient class of $m$ times a monomial to the associated graded class of $m$ times the corresponding monomial in the $f_i$.

entries.subject: ring-parameters
entries.name: Quasi-regular sequence in a ring
entries.definition: A tuple in $R$ is quasi-regular in $R$ when it is quasi-regular on $R$ as a module over itself.

entries.subject: ring-ideal-pair
entries.name: Rees algebra
entries.definition: For a ring $R$ and ideal $I$, the Rees algebra is $\bigoplus_{n\geq0}I^n$ with $I^n$ in degree $n$ and the multiplication induced by $I^m I^n\subseteq I^{m+n}$.

entries.subject: ring-ideal-pair
entries.name: Affine blowup algebra
entries.definition: For $a\in I$, the affine blowup algebra is the degree-zero subring of the localization of the Rees algebra at $a$ viewed in degree one.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Resolution of a module
entries.definition: A left resolution of $M$ is an augmented complex $\cdots\to F_1\to F_0\to M\to0$ that is exact at all terms.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Resolution by free modules
entries.definition: A left resolution $F_\bullet\to M$ in which every $F_i$ is free.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Resolution by finite free modules
entries.definition: A left resolution $F_\bullet\to M$ in which every $F_i$ is finite free. The index $i$ can be unbounded.

entries.subject: module-pair
entries.name: Ext module
entries.definition: For $R$-modules $M,N$ and $i\geq0$, choose a free resolution $F_\bullet\to M$ and take $H^i(\operatorname{Hom}_R(F_\bullet,N))$. Use zero for $i<0$. At $i=0$ this recovers $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,N)$. The construction is canonical up to the natural identifications induced by comparison of resolutions.

entries.subject: module-map
entries.name: Universally injective module map
entries.definition: For every $R$-module $Q$, the map obtained from $f:M\to N$ by tensoring with $Q$ over $R$ is injective.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map universally injective on underlying modules
entries.definition: For every $R$-module $M$, the map $M\to M\otimes_R S$ induced by the given ring map $R\to S$ is injective. This is also called a pure ring map.

entries.subject: module-exact-sequence
entries.name: Universally exact short exact sequence
entries.definition: The sequence $0\to M_1\to M_2\to M_3\to0$ is exact and its first map is universally injective. Equivalently it remains exact after tensoring with any $R$-module.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Direct-sum dévissage
entries.definition: An increasing ordinal-indexed family $(M_\alpha)$ of submodules begins with $M_0=0$, has union $M$, takes unions at limit ordinals, and splits each inclusion $M_\alpha\subseteq M_{\alpha+1}$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Kaplansky dévissage
entries.definition: A direct-sum dévissage for which each successor quotient $M_{\alpha+1}/M_\alpha$ is countably generated.

entries.subject: module-system
entries.name: Mittag-Leffler inverse system
entries.definition: For every $i$ in the directed indexing set, some $j\geq i$ has the property that the images of all transition maps into the $i$th term from indices $k\geq j$ equal the image from $j$. For modules take images of the underlying maps of sets.

entries.subject: module-system
entries.name: Elements killed in the colimit vanish at a later stage
entries.definition: For each $x\in M_i$ that maps to zero in the colimit, some transition $M_i\to M_j$ with $j\geq i$ sends $x$ to zero.

entries.subject: module-system
entries.name: Componentwise injective morphism of module systems
entries.definition: Every component $M_i\to N_i$ of the specified morphism of systems over the same preorder is injective.

entries.subject: module-system
entries.name: Morphism of module systems inducing an injective colimit map
entries.definition: The morphism of systems induces an injective map $\varinjlim M_i\to\varinjlim N_i$.

entries.subject: ring-parameters
entries.name: Regularity in every ordering
entries.definition: Every permutation of the chosen tuple is a regular sequence in the ring.

entries.subject: module-exact-sequence
entries.name: Split short exact sequence
entries.definition: The quotient map has a linear section, equivalently the inclusion has a linear retraction.

entries.subject: module-exact-sequence
entries.name: Short exact sequence with finitely presented quotient
entries.definition: The rightmost module in the given short exact sequence is finitely presented over the base ring.

entries.subject: module-exact-sequence
entries.name: Short exact sequence with flat quotient
entries.definition: The rightmost module in the given short exact sequence is flat over the base ring.

entries.subject: module-exact-sequence
entries.name: Short exact sequence with flat middle term
entries.definition: The middle module in the given short exact sequence is flat over the base ring.

entries.subject: module-exact-sequence
entries.name: Short exact sequence with flat kernel
entries.definition: The leftmost module in the given short exact sequence is flat over the base ring.

entries.subject: module-system
entries.name: Surjective transitions in a directed inverse system
entries.definition: The inverse system is indexed by a directed set and every transition map is surjective.

entries.subject: module-system
entries.name: Mittag–Leffler inverse system
entries.definition: For a directed inverse system of sets or modules $(A_i,\varphi_{ji})$, each $i$ admits $j\geq i$ such that $\varphi_{ki}(A_k)=\varphi_{ji}(A_j)$ for every $k\geq j$. For modules this is the condition on their underlying sets.

entries.subject: module-system
entries.name: Mittag–Leffler directed system of modules
entries.definition: A directed system $(M_i,f_{ij})$ is Mittag–Leffler in this sense if every $M_i$ is finitely presented over $R$ and, for each $R$-module $N$, the inverse system of modules $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_i,N)$ has eventually stable images at each fixed index.

entries.subject: module-map-pair
entries.name: Domination of module maps
entries.definition: For maps $f:M\to N$ and $g:M\to M'$ with common source, $g$ dominates $f$ when $\ker(f\otimes_R Q)\subseteq\ker(g\otimes_R Q)$ for every $R$-module $Q$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Injective comparison with products under tensor
entries.definition: For every family $(Q_i)_{i\in I}$ of $R$-modules the canonical map $M\otimes_R\prod_i Q_i\to\prod_i(M\otimes_R Q_i)$ is injective.

entries.subject: module-ideal-pair
entries.name: Adically complete module
entries.definition: For an ideal $I\subseteq R$ and an $R$-module $M$, the canonical map $M\to\varprojlim_{n\geq1} M/I^nM$ is an isomorphism.

entries.subject: module-ideal-pair
entries.name: Adically separated module
entries.definition: For an ideal $I\subseteq R$ and an $R$-module $M$, one has $\bigcap_{n\geq1} I^nM=0$. Equivalently the canonical map to the $I$-adic completion is injective.

entries.subject: module-map
entries.name: Exterior rank of a map of finite free modules
entries.definition: For a map $\varphi:R^m\to R^n$ over a nonzero ring, this is the largest $r\geq0$ for which $\bigwedge^r\varphi$ is nonzero.

entries.subject: module-map
entries.name: Determinantal ideal at the exterior rank
entries.definition: For a map $\varphi:R^m\to R^n$ of exterior rank $r$, $I(\varphi)$ is generated by the $r\times r$ minors of a matrix of $\varphi$. Here $r$ is the largest exterior degree with a nonzero map.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Cohen–Macaulay module over a Noetherian ring
entries.definition: The ring $R$ is Noetherian, the $R$-module $M$ is finite, and $M_{\mathfrak p}$ is Cohen–Macaulay over $R_{\mathfrak p}$ for every prime $\mathfrak p$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Module without embedded associated primes
entries.definition: Every prime in $\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)$ is minimal in $\operatorname{Supp}_R(M)$.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Finite global dimension as a number
entries.definition: If $R$ has finite global dimension, its global dimension is the least nonnegative integer $n$ for which every $R$-module has a projective resolution of length at most $n$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Finite projective dimension as a number
entries.definition: For a module $M$ that admits a finite projective resolution, its projective dimension is the least nonnegative length of such a resolution. The projective terms may have arbitrary generating sets.

entries.subject: ring-index
entries.name: Serre condition R at a specified index
entries.definition: Let $R$ be Noetherian and $k\geq0$. The pair $(R,k)$ satisfies $(R_k)$ if $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular for every prime $\mathfrak p$ of height at most $k$.

entries.subject: ring-index
entries.name: Serre condition S for a ring at a specified index
entries.definition: Let $R$ be Noetherian and $k\geq0$. The pair $(R,k)$ satisfies $(S_k)$ if $\operatorname{depth}(R_{\mathfrak p})\geq\min\{k,\dim R_{\mathfrak p}\}$ for every prime $\mathfrak p$.

entries.subject: module-index
entries.name: Serre condition S for a module at a specified index
entries.definition: Let $M$ be a finite module over a Noetherian ring $R$ and $k\geq0$. The pair $(M,k)$ satisfies $(S_k)$ if $\operatorname{depth}(M_{\mathfrak p})\geq\min\{k,\dim(\operatorname{Supp}M_{\mathfrak p})\}$ for every prime $\mathfrak p$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Serre condition S₁ for a module
entries.definition: The module $M$ is finite over a Noetherian ring $R$ and $(M,1)$ satisfies the module Serre condition $(S_1)$.

entries.subject: ring-map-point
entries.name: Local ring of a fibre
entries.definition: For $R\to S$ and $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}(S)$ lying over $\mathfrak p$, it is $S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak q}$. It is canonically the localization of $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ at the corresponding prime.

entries.subject: algebra-element
entries.name: Uniformizer of a discrete valuation ring
entries.definition: For a discrete valuation ring $A$, a uniformizer is a generator of its maximal ideal.

entries.subject: algebra-element-pair
entries.name: Associate elements in a domain
entries.definition: Two elements $x,y$ of a domain $R$ are associates if $x=uy$ for some unit $u\in R^\times$.

entries.subject: algebra-element-pair
entries.name: Elements generating the same principal ideal
entries.definition: For two elements $x,y$ of the same domain $R$, the principal ideals satisfy $xR=yR$.

entries.subject: algebra-element
entries.name: Irreducible element of a domain
entries.definition: An element $x$ of a domain $R$ is irreducible if it is nonzero, is not a unit, and whenever $x=yz$, either $y$ or $z$ is a unit.

entries.subject: algebra-element
entries.name: Element generating a prime ideal
entries.definition: For a domain $R$, the Stacks convention calls $x\in R$ prime when $xR$ is a prime ideal. Under this convention $0$ is prime.

entries.subject: algebra-element
entries.name: Nonzero element of an algebra
entries.definition: The chosen element is different from zero in its ambient algebra.

entries.subject: local-ring
entries.name: Order of vanishing
entries.definition: For a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain $R$ with fraction field $K$, the order of a nonzero fraction $x/y\in K$ is $\ell_R(R/xR)-\ell_R(R/yR)$, where $x,y\in R$ are nonzero.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Lattice over a one-dimensional local domain
entries.definition: For a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain $R$ with fraction field $K$ and a finite-dimensional $K$-vector space $V$, a lattice is a finite $R$-submodule $M\subseteq V$ with $K\otimes_R M=V$ via the canonical map.

entries.subject: lattice-pair
entries.name: Signed distance between lattices
entries.definition: For lattices $M,N$ in the same finite-dimensional vector space over the fraction field of a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain $R$, set $d(M,N)=\ell_R(M/(M\cap N))-\ell_R(N/(M\cap N))$.

entries.subject: algebra-element
entries.name: Strongly transcendental element
entries.definition: For a ring inclusion $R\subseteq S$, an element $x\in S$ is strongly transcendental over $R$ if $u\sum_i a_ix^i=0$ with $u\in S$ and coefficients $a_i\in R$ implies $ua_i=0$ for every $i$.

entries.subject: ring-map-point
entries.name: Relative dimension at a target prime
entries.definition: For a finite type map $R\to S$ and a prime $\mathfrak q$ over $\mathfrak p$, take the dimension at the corresponding point of $\operatorname{Spec}(S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$. The dimension at a point is the infimum of the dimensions of its open neighbourhoods.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Relative dimension of a finite type map
entries.definition: For a finite type map $R\to S$, take the supremum of the relative dimensions $\dim_{\mathfrak q}(S/R)$ over all primes $\mathfrak q$ of $S$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Derivation into a module
entries.definition: For a ring map $R\to S$ and an $S$-module $M$, an $R$-derivation $D:S\to M$ is additive, annihilates the image of $R$, and satisfies $D(ab)=aD(b)+bD(a)$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Kähler differentials and universal derivation
entries.definition: For a ring map $R\to S$, the pair $(\Omega_{S/R},\mathrm d)$ represents $R$-derivations from $S$ into $S$-modules. Thus composition with $\mathrm d$ gives $\operatorname{Hom}_S(\Omega_{S/R},M)\cong\operatorname{Der}_R(S,M)$ naturally in $M$.

entries.subject: module-map
entries.name: Differential operator of bounded order
entries.definition: For $S$-modules $M,N$ over a ring map $R\to S$, an operator of order at most $0$ is $S$-linear. For $k\geq1$, an $R$-linear map $D:M\to N$ has order at most $k$ if $m\mapsto D(gm)-gD(m)$ has order at most $k-1$ for every $g\in S$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Module of principal parts
entries.definition: For an $S$-module $M$, a ring map $R\to S$, and $k\geq0$, $P^k_{S/R}(M)$ represents $R$-linear differential operators of order at most $k$ from $M$ into $S$-modules.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Naive cotangent complex
entries.definition: For the canonical polynomial presentation $P=R[S]\twoheadrightarrow S$ with kernel $I$, the naive cotangent complex is $I/I^2\to\Omega_{P/R}\otimes_P S$ in homological degrees $1,0$. The map comes from the universal derivation of $P$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Degree-one homology of the naive cotangent complex
entries.definition: The degree-one homology is the kernel of $I/I^2\to\Omega_{R[S]/R}\otimes_{R[S]}S$. It is denoted $H_1(L_{S/R})$ in this Stacks definition.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Global complete intersection over a field
entries.definition: A finite type algebra $S$ over a field $k$ admits a presentation $k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ with $\dim S=n-c$. The zero ring is included by convention.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Local complete intersection over a field
entries.definition: A finite type algebra $S$ over a field $k$ has a cover of $\operatorname{Spec}(S)$ by principal opens $D(g_i)$ such that each $S_{g_i}$ is a global complete intersection over $k$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Essentially finite type local complete intersection over a field
entries.definition: A local $k$-algebra $S$ essentially of finite type is a quotient of a regular local $k$-algebra essentially of finite type by a regular sequence in its maximal ideal.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Relative global complete intersection
entries.definition: The map $R\to S$ has a presentation $S=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ such that every nonempty fibre of $\operatorname{Spec}(S)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ has Krull dimension $n-c$.

entries.subject: ring-presentation
entries.name: Standard smooth presentation
entries.definition: For $S=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ with $0\leq c\leq n$, the specific ordered presentation is standard smooth when $\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{1\leq i,j\leq c}$ maps to a unit of $S$. For $c=0$ the determinant is one.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Small extension of local Artinian rings
entries.definition: A surjection $B'\to B$ of local Artinian rings is a small extension if its kernel has length one as a $B'$-module.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Universal first-order thickening
entries.definition: For a formally unramified $R\to S$, the universal thickening is a square-zero surjection $S'\to S$. For each square-zero quotient $A\to A/J$ of $R$-algebras and $R$-map $S\to A/J$, there is a unique $R$-map $S'\to A$ inducing the composite $S'\to S\to A/J$ modulo $J$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Conormal module of a formally unramified map
entries.definition: The kernel of the universal first-order thickening $S'\to S$ of the formally unramified $R$-algebra $S$. Its square is zero, so multiplication by lifts from $S'$ gives it an $S$-module structure.

entries.subject: local-ring
entries.name: Henselization of a local ring
entries.definition: For a local ring $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$, its henselization $R\to R^h$ is the local map constructed from pointed étale neighbourhoods in 04GN. Its target is henselian with maximal ideal $\mathfrak mR^h$ and residue field $\kappa$.

entries.subject: local-ring
entries.name: Strict henselization with a specified separable closure
entries.definition: For a local ring $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ and a chosen separable closure $\kappa^{\mathrm{sep}}$ of $\kappa$, the strict henselization is the local map $R\to R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ constructed in 04GP. Its target is strictly henselian with maximal ideal $\mathfrak mR^{\mathrm{sh}}$ and residue field identified with $\kappa^{\mathrm{sep}}$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Local map that is a strict henselization
entries.definition: A local homomorphism with source R is a strict henselization if it is isomorphic as a map with source R to the strict henselization obtained from some separable algebraic closure of the residue field of R.

entries.subject: ring-inclusion
entries.name: Coefficient ring of a complete local ring
entries.definition: For a complete local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$ with residue field of characteristic $p$, a subring $\Lambda\subseteq R$ is a coefficient ring when it is complete local with maximal ideal $\Lambda\cap\mathfrak m$, its residue field maps isomorphically to $R/\mathfrak m$, and $\Lambda\cap\mathfrak m=p\Lambda$. Here $p=0$ in residue characteristic zero.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Domain satisfying N-1
entries.definition: The ring is a domain and its integral closure in its own fraction field is a finite module over it.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Japanese domain (N-2)
entries.definition: The ring is a domain and, in every finite extension of its fraction field, its integral closure is finite as a module over the ring.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Domain of characteristic zero
entries.definition: The ring is a domain and the unital map from the integers is injective. Its fraction field then has characteristic zero.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Analytically unramified local ring
entries.definition: The ring is Noetherian and local, and its completion at its maximal ideal is reduced.

entries.subject: ideal
entries.name: Analytically unramified prime
entries.definition: For a prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of a Noetherian local ring $R$, the completion of the local ring $R/\mathfrak p$ at its maximal ideal is reduced.

entries.topic: Modules with a sequence of scalars
entries.subject: module-sequence
entries.name: Koszul-regular sequence on a module
entries.definition: For an $R$-module $M$ and finite sequence $\mathbf f$ in $R$, require $H_i(K_\bullet(\mathbf f)\otimes_R M)=0$ for every $i>0$.

entries.topic: Modules with a sequence of scalars
entries.subject: module-sequence
entries.name: H₁-regular sequence on a module
entries.definition: For an $R$-module $M$ and finite sequence $\mathbf f$ in $R$, require $H_1(K_\bullet(\mathbf f)\otimes_R M)=0$.

entries.subject: ring-parameters
entries.name: Koszul-regular sequence in a ring
entries.definition: For a finite sequence $\mathbf f$ in $R$, require $H_i(K_\bullet(\mathbf f))=0$ for every $i>0$.

entries.subject: ring-parameters
entries.name: H₁-regular sequence in a ring
entries.definition: For a finite sequence $\mathbf f$ in $R$, require $H_1(K_\bullet(\mathbf f))=0$.

entries.subject: module-pair
entries.name: Stably isomorphic modules
entries.definition: For two $R$-modules $M,N$, there are nonnegative integers $m,n$ with $M\oplus R^m\cong N\oplus R^n$ as $R$-modules.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Stably free module
entries.definition: An $R$-module $M$ is stably isomorphic to some free $R$-module. Equivalently, $M\oplus R^m$ is free for some finite $m\geq0$. The free module need not have finite rank.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Absolutely integrally closed ring
entries.definition: Every monic polynomial in $R[T]$ splits into linear factors over $R$.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: A root for every positive-degree monic polynomial
entries.definition: For every monic polynomial of positive degree in $R[T]$, at least one root belongs to $R$.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Auto-associated local ring
entries.definition: The ring $R$ is local and its maximal ideal is weakly associated to the $R$-module $R$: it is minimal over the annihilator of some element of $R$.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Nonzero annihilators of proper finite ideals
entries.definition: For each proper finitely generated ideal $J\subset R$, the annihilator $\operatorname{Ann}_R(J)$ contains a nonzero element.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Injections of projective modules universally injective
entries.definition: Every injective homomorphism of projective modules remains injective after tensoring with an arbitrary module over the ring.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Inclusions of finite projectives split
entries.definition: Every injective homomorphism between finite projective modules is split as a map of modules.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Inclusions of arbitrary free modules split
entries.definition: Every injective homomorphism between free modules of arbitrary rank is split as a map of modules.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Rank of a module over a domain
entries.definition: For a domain $R$ with fraction field $K$, the rank of $M$ is the cardinal dimension $\dim_K(M\otimes_R K)$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Reflexive module over a domain
entries.definition: For a domain $R$, the evaluation map $M\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R),R)$ taking $x$ to evaluation at $x$ is an isomorphism.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Reflexive localization at every prime
entries.definition: For a domain $R$, the localization $M_{\mathfrak p}$ is a reflexive $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module for every prime $\mathfrak p$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Reflexive localization at every maximal ideal
entries.definition: For a domain $R$, the localization $M_{\mathfrak m}$ is a reflexive $R_{\mathfrak m}$-module for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Finite free embedding with torsion-free cokernel
entries.definition: For a domain $R$, there exists a short exact sequence $0\to M\to F\to N\to0$ in which $F$ is finite free and $N$ is torsion free.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Reflexive hull
entries.definition: For a finite module $M$ over a Noetherian domain $R$, the reflexive hull is its double dual $M^{**}=\operatorname{Hom}_R(\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R),R)$.

entries.subject: module-element
entries.name: Content ideal of an element
entries.definition: For $x\in M$ with $M$ flat over $A$, the content ideal of $x$, when it exists, is the least ideal $I\subseteq A$ satisfying $x\in IM$.

entries.subject: ring-map-module
entries.name: Strict transform on an affine blowup chart
entries.definition: For an ideal $I\subset R$, an element $a\in I$ and the affine blowup algebra $S=R[I/a]$, the strict transform of an $R$-module $M$ is $(M\otimes_R S)$ modulo its $a$-power torsion submodule.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Koszul complex of a linear map
entries.definition: For an $R$-linear map $\varphi:E\to R$, use the exterior algebra $\bigwedge_R E$ with $E$ in homological degree one. The differential of degree $-1$ is the derivation taking $e\in E$ to $\varphi(e)$.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Koszul complex of a sequence
entries.definition: For $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in R$, take the Koszul complex of $R^r\to R$ sending the $i$th basis element to $f_i$.

entries.subject: topological-ring
entries.name: Topological ring
entries.definition: The topology on $R$ makes addition and multiplication continuous on $R\times R$ with its product topology.

entries.subject: topological-module
entries.name: Topological module
entries.definition: For a topological ring $R$, the topology on $M$ makes addition on $M\times M$ and the scalar action on $R\times M$ continuous.

entries.subject: topological-ring-map
entries.name: Homomorphism of topological rings
entries.definition: The ring homomorphism is continuous for the specified topologies.

entries.subject: topological-module-map
entries.name: Homomorphism of topological modules
entries.definition: The $R$-linear map is continuous for the specified topologies.

entries.subject: topological-ring
entries.name: Linearly topologized ring
entries.definition: In a topological ring $R$, the zero element has a neighbourhood basis consisting of ideals of $R$.

entries.subject: topological-module
entries.name: Linearly topologized module
entries.definition: In a topological module, the zero element has a neighbourhood basis consisting of submodules.

entries.topic: Topological rings with a fixed ideal
entries.subject: topological-ring-ideal-pair
entries.name: Ideal of definition
entries.definition: In a linearly topologized ring $R$, an ideal $I$ is an ideal of definition if it is open and every neighbourhood of zero contains some power $I^n$.

entries.subject: topological-ring
entries.name: Pre-admissible topological ring
entries.definition: The ring is linearly topologized and has an ideal of definition.

entries.subject: topological-ring
entries.name: Admissible topological ring
entries.definition: The ring is pre-admissible and complete, with completeness including separatedness in the source convention.

entries.subject: topological-ring
entries.name: Pre-adic topological ring
entries.definition: The ring is linearly topologized and has an ideal of definition $I$ whose powers form a neighbourhood basis at zero.

entries.subject: topological-ring
entries.name: Adic topological ring
entries.definition: The ring is pre-adic and complete, with completeness including separatedness.

entries.subject: topological-ring
entries.name: Complete separated linearly topologized ring
entries.definition: The ring is linearly topologized and the canonical map $R\to\varprojlim_U R/U$ is an isomorphism, with $U$ running over its open ideals.

entries.subject: topological-ring-map
entries.name: Formally smooth map of topological rings
entries.definition: The source and target are linearly topologized and the map $R\to S$ is continuous. For every discrete $R$-algebra $B$ with continuous structure map, square-zero ideal $J\subset B$ and continuous $R$-map $S\to B/J$, there exists a continuous $R$-map $S\to B$ lifting it.

entries.topic: Ring maps with a fixed ideal
entries.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
entries.name: Formally smooth for the target adic topology
entries.definition: For a ring map $R\to S$ and ideal $\mathfrak n\subseteq S$, give $R$ the discrete topology and $S$ the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology. The map is formally smooth as a map of these topological rings.

entries.subject: field-family
entries.name: p-independent subset
entries.definition: For a characteristic-$p$ field extension $K/k$ and a subset $E\subseteq K$, the monomials in $E$ with finite support and exponents less than $p$ are linearly independent over the compositum $kK^p$.

entries.subject: field-family
entries.name: p-basis of a field extension
entries.definition: For a characteristic-$p$ field extension $K/k$ and a subset $E\subseteq K$, the monomials in $E$ with finite support and exponents less than $p$ form a basis of $K$ as a vector space over $kK^p$.

entries.subject: field-family
entries.name: Linearly independent differentials in characteristic p
entries.definition: For a characteristic-$p$ field extension $K/k$ and a subset $E\subseteq K$, the family $(dx)_{x\in E}$ is $K$-linearly independent in $\Omega_{K/k}$.

entries.subject: field-family
entries.name: Differential basis in characteristic p
entries.definition: For a characteristic-$p$ field extension $K/k$ and a subset $E\subseteq K$, the family $(dx)_{x\in E}$ is a $K$-basis of $\Omega_{K/k}$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Character module functor
entries.definition: The character module of $M$ is $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(M,\mathbf Q/\mathbf Z)$, with scalar action $(r\lambda)(x)=\lambda(rx)$. It is contravariantly functorial in $M$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Free cover on the underlying set of a module
entries.definition: The free cover of $M$ is the surjection $\bigoplus_{m\in M}R[m]\to M$ sending $[m]$ to $m$. The construction is covariantly functorial in $M$.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: K-flat complex
entries.definition: A specified complex $K^\bullet$ is K-flat when $\operatorname{Tot}(E^\bullet\otimes_R K^\bullet)$ is acyclic for every acyclic complex $E^\bullet$ of $R$-modules. This predicate applies to a complex representing a derived object.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Derived tensor product
entries.definition: For $K,L\in D(R)$, replace $L$ by a quasi-isomorphic K-flat complex and take the direct-sum total complex of its tensor product with a representative of $K$. This yields the derived object $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L$.

entries.subject: algebra-pair
entries.name: Tor-independent algebras over the base
entries.definition: The pair of $R$-algebras $(A,B)$ satisfies $\operatorname{Tor}^R_i(A,B)=0$ for all $i>0$.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Finite projective dimension of a derived object
entries.definition: The object of $D(R)$ has a bounded representative consisting of projective $R$-modules.

entries.subject: complex-interval
entries.name: Projective amplitude in a specified interval
entries.definition: Given $a\leq b$, the object of $D(R)$ admits a representative consisting of projective modules and concentrated in cohomological degrees $[a,b]$.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Finite injective dimension of a derived object
entries.definition: The object of $D(R)$ has a bounded representative consisting of injective $R$-modules.

entries.subject: complex-interval
entries.name: Injective amplitude in a specified interval
entries.definition: Given $a\leq b$, the object of $D(R)$ admits a representative consisting of injective modules and concentrated in cohomological degrees $[a,b]$.

entries.subject: module-ideal-pair
entries.name: Module projective relative to an ideal
entries.definition: For a module $M$ and an ideal $I$ over $R$, multiplication by every $a\in I$ on $M$ factors through a projective $R$-module. In the source this condition is called $I$-projectivity.

entries.subject: module-ideal-pair
entries.name: Ideal annihilates first Ext from the module
entries.definition: For every $R$-module $N$ the ideal $I$ annihilates $\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(M,N)$.

entries.subject: ring-map-module
entries.name: Relatively finitely presented module
entries.definition: For a finite type map $R\to A$ and an $A$-module $M$, there exists a surjection $R[X_1,\ldots,X_n]\to A$ making $M$ finitely presented over that polynomial ring.

entries.subject: ring-map-complex
entries.name: Relative m-pseudo-coherence of a complex
entries.definition: For a finite type map $R\to A$, an integer $m$ and a complex of $A$-modules $K$, there is a finite polynomial presentation $R[X_1,\ldots,X_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$ for which $K$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent over the polynomial ring.

entries.subject: ring-map-complex
entries.name: Relative pseudo-coherence of a complex
entries.definition: For a finite type map $R\to A$, the complex of $A$-modules is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $R$ for every integer $m$.

entries.subject: ring-map-module
entries.name: Relative m-pseudo-coherence of a module
entries.definition: For a finite type map $R\to A$ and an integer $m$, the complex $M[0]$ of the $A$-module is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $R$.

entries.subject: ring-map-module
entries.name: Relative pseudo-coherence of a module
entries.definition: For a finite type map $R\to A$, the complex $M[0]$ of the $A$-module is pseudo-coherent relative to $R$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Pseudo-coherent ring map
entries.definition: The map $R\to A$ is of finite type and $A$ as an $A$-module is pseudo-coherent relative to $R$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Perfect ring map
entries.definition: The map $R\to A$ is pseudo-coherent and $A$ as an $R$-module has finite Tor dimension.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Perfect target over a finite polynomial presentation
entries.definition: For the map $R\to A$, some surjection $R[X_1,\ldots,X_n]\to A$ makes $A$ admit a finite resolution by finite projective $R[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$-modules.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Target module of finite Tor dimension
entries.definition: For the map $R\to A$, the target $A$ as an $R$-module has finite Tor dimension.

entries.subject: ring-map-complex
entries.name: Perfect complex relative to a ring
entries.definition: For a flat map of finite presentation $R\to A$ and an object $K\in D(A)$, the object $K$ is pseudo-coherent over $A$ and has finite Tor dimension over $R$.

entries.subject: module-ideal-pair
entries.name: Module with ideal-power torsion
entries.definition: For every $x\in M$ some positive power $I^n$ of the chosen ideal annihilates $x$. The exponent can depend on $x$.

entries.subject: module-scalar-pair
entries.name: Module with scalar-power torsion
entries.definition: For every $x\in M$ some positive power $f^n$ of the chosen scalar annihilates $x$. The exponent can depend on $x$.

entries.subject: complex-ideal-pair
entries.name: Derived-complete complex
entries.definition: For $K\in D(A)$ and an ideal $I\subseteq A$, one has $\operatorname{RHom}_A(A_f,K)=0$ for every $f\in I$.

entries.subject: module-ideal-pair
entries.name: Derived-complete module
entries.definition: The object $M[0]$ is derived complete with respect to the chosen ideal $I\subseteq A$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Weakly étale ring map
entries.definition: Both $A\to B$ and the multiplication map $B\otimes_A B\to B$ are flat.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Flat multiplication map of a tensor square
entries.definition: For the chosen map $A\to B$, the multiplication map $B\otimes_A B\to B$ is flat.

entries.subject: local-ring
entries.name: Number of branches of a local ring
entries.definition: Count the minimal primes of the henselization $A^h$, using $\infty$ for an infinite set.

entries.subject: local-ring
entries.name: Number of geometric branches of a local ring
entries.definition: Count the minimal primes of the strict henselization $A^{sh}$, using $\infty$ for an infinite set.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Formally catenary local ring
entries.definition: The ring $A$ is Noetherian local, and for every minimal prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$ the scheme $\operatorname{Spec}(\widehat A/\mathfrak p\widehat A)$ is equidimensional.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Extension of discrete valuation rings
entries.definition: The rings $A,B$ are discrete valuation rings and $A\to B$ is injective and local.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ramification index of an extension of discrete valuation rings
entries.definition: For an extension $A\to B$ of discrete valuation rings, its ramification index is the integer $e\geq1$ with $\mathfrak m_A B=\mathfrak m_B^e$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Weakly unramified extension of discrete valuation rings
entries.definition: The map is an extension of discrete valuation rings with ramification index $e=1$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Extension of discrete valuation rings with separable residue extension
entries.definition: The map is an extension of discrete valuation rings and $\kappa_B/\kappa_A$ is separable as a field extension, without assuming finite degree.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Extension of discrete valuation rings formally smooth for the target adic topology
entries.definition: The map is an extension of discrete valuation rings and is formally smooth for the $\mathfrak m_B$-adic topology, with the source taken discrete in the equivalent definition.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Residue degree of an extension of valuation rings
entries.definition: For an injective local map of valuation rings $A\to B$ with finite residue field extension, the residue degree is $[\kappa_B:\kappa_A]$. This also applies to extensions of discrete valuation rings.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Extension of valuation rings
entries.definition: The rings $A,B$ are valuation rings and $A\to B$ is injective and local.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Weakly unramified extension of valuation rings
entries.definition: The map is an extension of valuation rings whose induced homomorphism of value groups $\Gamma_A\to\Gamma_B$ is an isomorphism.

entries.subject: valued-field-extension
entries.name: Finite separable extension unramified with respect to a DVR
entries.definition: Let $A$ be a DVR with fraction field $K$, let $L/K$ be finite separable, and let $B$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $L$. Every localization of $B$ at a maximal ideal has ramification index one over $A$ and a separable residue extension.

entries.subject: valued-field-extension
entries.name: Finite separable extension tamely ramified with respect to a DVR
entries.definition: Use the integral closure $B$ of a DVR $A$ in the finite separable extension $L/K$ of its fraction field. Either $\kappa_A$ has characteristic zero, or it has characteristic $p>0$ and all maximal-ideal residue extensions are separable with ramification indices prime to $p$.

entries.subject: valued-field-extension
entries.name: Finite separable extension totally ramified with respect to a DVR
entries.definition: For a DVR $A$ and a finite separable extension $L/K$ of its fraction field, the integral closure of $A$ in $L$ has a unique maximal ideal and its residue field is $\kappa_A$.

entries.topic: Galois extensions with a specified prime
entries.subject: galois-prime
entries.name: Decomposition group at a prime
entries.definition: For a finite Galois extension $L/K$ of the fraction field of a DVR $A$ and a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of its integral closure $B$, take the stabilizer of $\mathfrak m$ in $\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)$.

entries.topic: Galois extensions with a specified prime
entries.subject: galois-prime
entries.name: Inertia group at a prime
entries.definition: Let $A$ be a DVR with fraction field $K$, let $L/K$ be finite Galois and let $\mathfrak m$ be a maximal ideal of the integral closure of $A$ in $L$. The inertia group is the kernel of the action of the decomposition group at $\mathfrak m$ on the residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak m)$.

entries.topic: Galois extensions with a specified prime
entries.subject: galois-prime
entries.name: Wild inertia group
entries.definition: For a maximal ideal in the integral closure of a DVR in a finite Galois extension, take the subgroup of inertia acting trivially on $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$.

entries.topic: Galois extensions with a specified prime
entries.subject: galois-prime
entries.name: Tame inertia group
entries.definition: For a maximal ideal in the integral closure of a DVR in a finite Galois extension, take the quotient of inertia by wild inertia.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic
entries.definition: The ring is a discrete valuation ring whose fraction field has characteristic zero and whose residue field has characteristic $p>0$.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Absolute ramification index
entries.definition: For a mixed-characteristic discrete valuation ring $A$ of residue characteristic $p$, take the ramification index of $\mathbf Z_{(p)}\to A$.

entries.subject: ramification-solution
entries.name: Weak solution to eliminating ramification
entries.definition: Fix an extension $A\subset B$ of DVRs with fraction fields $K\subset L$ and a finite extension $K_1/K$. Let $A_1$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $K_1$, and let $B_1$ be the integral closure of $B$ in $(L\otimes_K K_1)_{\mathrm{red}}$. For each maximal ideal $\mathfrak q$ of $B_1$ lying over a maximal ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $A_1$, the map $(A_1)_{\mathfrak p}\to(B_1)_{\mathfrak q}$ must be weakly unramified.

entries.subject: ramification-solution
entries.name: Solution to eliminating ramification
entries.definition: Fix an extension $A\subset B$ of DVRs with fraction fields $K\subset L$ and a finite extension $K_1/K$. Let $A_1$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $K_1$, and let $B_1$ be the integral closure of $B$ in $(L\otimes_K K_1)_{\mathrm{red}}$. For each maximal ideal $\mathfrak q$ of $B_1$ lying over a maximal ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $A_1$, the map $(A_1)_{\mathfrak p}\to(B_1)_{\mathfrak q}$ must be formally smooth for the adic topology of its target maximal ideal.

entries.subject: ramification-solution
entries.name: Separable solution to eliminating ramification
entries.definition: The finite field extension $K_1/K$ is a solution to eliminating ramification for the specified extension of DVRs, and $K_1/K$ is separable.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Invertible module
entries.definition: Tensoring over $R$ with the module gives an equivalence from the category of $R$-modules to itself.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Trivial invertible module
entries.definition: The module is invertible and is isomorphic to $R$ as an $R$-module.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Module with a tensor inverse
entries.definition: There exists an $R$-module $N$ with $M\otimes_R N\cong R$ as $R$-modules.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Finite locally free module of rank one
entries.definition: The module is finite locally free and each localization at a prime is free of rank one.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Bézout domain
entries.definition: The ring is a domain in which every finitely generated ideal is principal.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Elementary divisor domain
entries.definition: The ring is a domain and every finite rectangular matrix can be brought by invertible row and column operations to diagonal form with consecutive diagonal entries ordered by divisibility.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Maps out of a module inject into maps to a filtered colimit
entries.definition: For every filtered system of $R$-modules $(N_i)$, the comparison $\operatorname{colim}_i\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,N_i)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,\operatorname{colim}_iN_i)$ is injective.

entries.topic: Modules with a fixed integer index
entries.subject: module-index
entries.name: Tensor power of a module
entries.definition: For an $R$-module $M$ and integer $n\geq0$, take the tensor product of $n$ copies of $M$ over $R$. The zeroth tensor power is $R$.

entries.topic: Modules with a fixed integer index
entries.subject: module-index
entries.name: Symmetric power of a module
entries.definition: The degree-$n$ part of the symmetric algebra, which is the tensor algebra modulo the two-sided ideal generated by $x\otimes y-y\otimes x$ for $x,y\in M$.

entries.topic: Modules with a fixed integer index
entries.subject: module-index
entries.name: Exterior power of a module
entries.definition: The degree-$n$ part of the exterior algebra, which is the tensor algebra modulo the two-sided ideal generated by $x\otimes x$ for $x\in M$.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Total ring of fractions
entries.definition: The total ring of fractions $Q(R)$ of a commutative ring $R$ is the localization at all elements whose multiplication endomorphisms of $R$ are injective.

entries.subject: module-pair
entries.name: Tensor product of two modules
entries.definition: For $R$-modules $M,N$, the $R$-module $M\otimes_R N$, together with its canonical bilinear map, represents the functor sending an $R$-module $P$ to the $R$-bilinear maps $M\times N\to P$.

entries.subject: ideal
entries.name: Idempotent ideal
entries.definition: The ideal $I$ satisfies $I^2=I$, where the product ideal is generated by products of pairs of elements of $I$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map with a locally nilpotent kernel
entries.definition: Every element of the kernel is nilpotent. The exponent allowed in this condition may depend on the chosen element.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map inducing a dense spectral image
entries.definition: The image of the continuous map $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ associated to $R\to S$ is dense for the Zariski topology.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map reaching every minimal prime of the base
entries.definition: For every minimal prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, a prime of $S$ contracts to $\mathfrak p$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Determinant of a finite projective module
entries.definition: If $M$ is finite projective over $R$, decompose $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ by the locally constant rank of $M$. On the rank-$n$ component, the determinant is $\bigwedge^n M$. The resulting $R$-module is invertible.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Grothendieck group of finite projective modules
entries.definition: The group $K_0(R)$ has generators $[P]$ for isomorphism classes of finite projective $R$-modules and relations $[P\oplus Q]=[P]+[Q]$. Every short exact sequence of such modules splits, so these relations encode short exact sequence additivity.

entries.subject: module-map
entries.name: Determinant of an endomorphism of a finite length module
entries.definition: For a finite length module over a local ring $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ and an endomorphism $\varphi$, take a finite filtration stable under $\varphi$ whose graded pieces are annihilated by $\mathfrak m$. The product of their determinants over $\kappa$ gives $\det_\kappa(\varphi)$, independent of the filtration by refinement.

entries.subject: module-map
entries.name: Trace of an endomorphism of a finite length module
entries.definition: For a finite length module over $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ with an endomorphism, sum the ordinary $\kappa$-linear traces on the graded pieces of a finite stable filtration annihilated by $\mathfrak m$. The sum is independent of the filtration.

entries.subject: module-map
entries.name: Characteristic polynomial of an endomorphism of a finite length module
entries.definition: For a finite length module over $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ with an endomorphism, multiply the ordinary characteristic polynomials over $\kappa$ of the graded pieces of a finite stable filtration annihilated by $\mathfrak m$. The polynomial is independent of the filtration.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Determinant line of a perfect complex of Tor-amplitude [−1,0]
entries.definition: Choose a representative $L^{-1}\to L^0$ of finite projective modules. Its determinant is $\det(L^0)\otimes_R\det(L^{-1})^\vee$. This descends to a covariant functor on the groupoid of such perfect complexes.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Summand of a direct sum of principal cyclic modules
entries.definition: The $R$-module is isomorphic to a direct summand of a direct sum of modules $R/fR$ for elements $f\in R$, including $f=0$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Lifting against the principal-ideal exactness test
entries.definition: For every short exact sequence $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$ of $R$-modules such that $fA=A\cap fB$ for each $f\in R$, the map $\operatorname{Hom}_R(P,B)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(P,C)$ is surjective.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Nonzero ring with totally ordered divisibility
entries.definition: Require $R\neq0$ and that for all $a,b\in R$, either $a$ divides $b$ or $b$ divides $a$.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Nonzero ring with linearly ordered ideals
entries.definition: Require $R\neq0$ and that any two ideals of $R$ be comparable by inclusion.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Dualizable object of the derived category
entries.definition: An object of $D(R)$ admits a left dual with evaluation and coevaluation satisfying the triangle identities for the symmetric monoidal structure given by $\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}$.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Tensor-invertible object of the derived category
entries.definition: An object $M$ of $D(R)$ is invertible if there is an object $N$ with $M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N\cong R$. Symmetry also gives $N\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M\cong R$.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Derived object locally a shift of the free rank-one module
entries.definition: For every prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$ there are $f\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ and $n\in\mathbf Z$ such that $M_f\cong R_f[-n]$ in $D(R_f)$. The integer may vary across the spectrum.

entries.subject: module-map
entries.name: Artin–Rees index of a finite module map
entries.definition: For a map $f:M\to N$ of finite modules over a Noetherian ring $A$ with ideal $I$, an index $c\geq0$ works if $f(M)\cap I^nN\subseteq f(I^{n-c}M)$ for every $n\geq c$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Pullback of two ring maps
entries.definition: For $B\to A$ and $A'\to A$, the pullback $B\times_A A'$ consists of pairs with equal image in $A$, with componentwise ring operations. The one-sided-surjective case imposes surjectivity on $A'\to A$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Compatible pair of modules over a ring pullback
entries.definition: Let $A'\to A$ be a surjection with kernel $I$, let $B\to A$ be any map, and put $B'=B\times_A A'$. Let $(N,M',\varphi)$ consist of a $B$-module, an $A'$-module and an isomorphism $\varphi:N\otimes_B A\xrightarrow{\sim} M'/IM'$. Put $M=M'/IM'$. A morphism of such data is a compatible pair of module homomorphisms.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Compatible pair of modules over a relative ring square
entries.definition: Let $A'\to A$ be a surjection with kernel $I$, let $B\to A$ be any map, and put $B'=B\times_A A'$. Fix a map $B'\to D'$ and set $D=D'\otimes_{B'} B$, $C'=D'\otimes_{B'} A'$, and $C=D'\otimes_{B'} A$. Let $(N,M',\varphi)$ consist of a $D$-module, a $C'$-module and an identification $\varphi:N\otimes_D C\xrightarrow{\sim}M'/IM'$. Put $M=M'/IM'$. This construction uses the relative square even when $D'\to D\times_C C'$ fails to be an isomorphism.

entries.subject: ring-ideal-pair
entries.name: Henselization of a ring–ideal pair
entries.definition: The henselization $(A^h,I^h)$ of $(A,I)$ is its image under the left adjoint to the inclusion of henselian pairs into ring–ideal pairs. A map $(A,I)\to(B,J)$ means a ring map sending $I$ into $J$. The map to the henselization is initial among maps from $(A,I)$ to henselian pairs.

entries.topic: Modules with a fixed integer index
entries.subject: module-index
entries.name: Finite locally free module of rank exactly r
entries.definition: With a fixed integer $r\geq0$, the module is locally free of constant rank $r$ on a standard open cover of the base spectrum.

entries.topic: Modules with a fixed integer index
entries.subject: module-index
entries.name: Two adjacent Fitting ideals detect rank r
entries.definition: For a finite $R$-module $M$ and fixed $r\geq0$, require $\operatorname{Fit}_{r-1}(M)=0$ and $\operatorname{Fit}_r(M)=R$, with $\operatorname{Fit}_{-1}(M)=0$.

entries.topic: Modules with a fixed integer index
entries.subject: module-index
entries.name: Fitting ideals have the rank-r step pattern
entries.definition: For a finite $R$-module $M$ and fixed $r\geq0$, require $\operatorname{Fit}_k(M)=0$ for $0\leq k<r$ and $\operatorname{Fit}_k(M)=R$ for every $k\geq r$.

entries.subject: module-map
entries.name: Surjective unit for module gluing
entries.definition: Let $A'\to A$ be a surjection with kernel $I$, let $B\to A$ be any map, and put $B'=B\times_A A'$. The unit of a $B'$-module $L'$ into the pullback of its restrictions to $B$ and $A'$ over $A$ is surjective.

entries.subject: module-map
entries.name: Injective unit for module gluing
entries.definition: Let $A'\to A$ be a surjection with kernel $I$, let $B\to A$ be any map, and put $B'=B\times_A A'$. The unit of a $B'$-module $L'$ into the pullback of its restrictions to $B$ and $A'$ over $A$ is injective.

entries.subject: ring-ideal-pair
entries.name: Comaximal factors of the reduction of a chosen monic polynomial
entries.definition: Given a ring–ideal pair $(A,I)$, a monic polynomial $f\in A[T]$ and a chosen factorization $\bar f=\bar g\bar h$ in $(A/I)[T]$, the factors $\bar g,\bar h$ generate the unit ideal.

entries.subject: ring-ideal-pair
entries.name: Chosen factorization admits a lift after étale extension
entries.definition: Given a ring–ideal pair $(A,I)$, a monic polynomial $f\in A[T]$ and a chosen factorization $\bar f=\bar g\bar h$ in $(A/I)[T]$, an étale map $A\to A'$ preserving the quotient modulo $I$ admits a factorization $f=g'h'$ reducing to the two chosen factors.

entries.subject: ring-ideal-pair
entries.name: Coproduct of two henselian pairs
entries.definition: The pair $(A,I)$ is the coproduct of two henselian pairs in the category of ring–ideal pairs. Its ring is the tensor product of their rings over $\mathbf Z$, and its ideal is the sum of the two extended ideals.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map with Noetherian target
entries.definition: The target ring satisfies the ascending chain condition on ideals.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map with reduced source
entries.definition: The source ring has zero nilradical.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map with normal source
entries.definition: Every prime localization of the source ring is an integrally closed domain.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map with normal target
entries.definition: Every prime localization of the target ring is an integrally closed domain.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map with regular source
entries.definition: The source is Noetherian and all its prime localizations are regular local rings.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map with regular target
entries.definition: The target is Noetherian and all its prime localizations are regular local rings.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map with Nagata source
entries.definition: The source $R$ is Noetherian and $R/\mathfrak p$ is Japanese for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map with Nagata target
entries.definition: The target $S$ is Noetherian and $S/\mathfrak q$ is Japanese for every prime ideal $\mathfrak q$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map with reduced fibres
entries.definition: For every $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}(R)$, the ring $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is reduced.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map with normal fibres
entries.definition: For every $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}(R)$, the ring $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is normal.

entries.topic: Modules with a sequence of scalars
entries.subject: module-sequence
entries.name: Injective multiplication at every stage of a sequence
entries.definition: For an $R$-module $M$ and a finite sequence $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ in $R$, multiplication by $f_i$ is injective on $M/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})M$ for each $i$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Purely inseparable extensions at all residue fields
entries.definition: For each prime $\mathfrak q\subset S$, the induced extension $\kappa(\mathfrak q)/\kappa(\mathfrak q\cap R)$ is purely inseparable.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Universal homeomorphism of affine spectra
entries.definition: For every $R$-algebra $A$, the projection $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_RS)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ is a homeomorphism.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Geometrically irreducible field extension
entries.definition: For every field extension $E/k$, the spectrum of $K\otimes_k E$ is nonempty and irreducible.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Base field contains every separably algebraic element
entries.definition: Each element of $K$ separably algebraic over the base field $k$ belongs to $k$.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Every prime is an intersection of maximal ideals
entries.definition: For each prime ideal of the ring, the intersection of all maximal ideals containing that prime is the prime itself.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map with Jacobson source
entries.definition: The source $R$ of the specified map $R\to S$ is a Jacobson ring.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map with Jacobson target
entries.definition: The target $S$ of the specified map $R\to S$ is a Jacobson ring.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Spectral map preserving closed points
entries.definition: For each maximal ideal of $S$, its inverse image under $R\to S$ is a maximal ideal of $R$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map with integral domain as source
entries.definition: The source ring $R$ of $R\to S$ is nonzero and has no nonzero zero divisors.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map with integral domain as target
entries.definition: The target ring $S$ of $R\to S$ is nonzero and has no nonzero zero divisors.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Zero module
entries.definition: Every element of the module is zero.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Module with empty support
entries.definition: For every prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, the localization $M_{\mathfrak p}$ vanishes.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Quasi-compact complement of module support
entries.definition: The subspace $\operatorname{Spec}(R)\setminus\operatorname{Supp}(M)$ is quasi-compact with its induced topology.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Open map of prime spectra
entries.definition: The continuous map $\operatorname{Spec}(S)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ sends each Zariski open to a Zariski open.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Closed map of prime spectra
entries.definition: The continuous map $\operatorname{Spec}(S)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ sends each Zariski closed subset to a Zariski closed subset.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Nonzero module
entries.definition: There exists $x\in M$ distinct from the additive identity.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Generic point in the support over a domain
entries.definition: The coefficient ring $R$ is a domain with fraction field $K$, and $M\otimes_R K\ne0$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Generic point as the unique associated prime
entries.definition: Over a domain $R$, the equality $\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)=\{(0)\}$ holds. In particular, the zero ideal occurs as the annihilator of a nonzero element.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Reflexivity at primes of module depth below two
entries.definition: For a finite module $M$ over a Noetherian domain $R$, the evaluation map of $M_{\mathfrak p}$ to its double dual over $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is an isomorphism at every prime where $\operatorname{depth}M_{\mathfrak p}<2$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Module over a Noetherian domain satisfying Serre S₂
entries.definition: The coefficient ring is a Noetherian domain $R$ satisfying $\operatorname{depth}R_{\mathfrak p}\geq\min(2,\dim R_{\mathfrak p})$ for every prime $\mathfrak p$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Universal flattening ideal over an Artinian ring
entries.definition: For an Artinian ring $R$ and an arbitrary $R$-module $M$, this is the least ideal $I$ such that $M/IM$ is flat over $R/I$.

entries.subject: ring-map-module
entries.name: Relative flatness above a closed subset of the base
entries.definition: For $R\to S$, an $S$-module $M$ and an ideal $I\subseteq R$, require $M_{\mathfrak q}$ to be $R$-flat for every $\mathfrak q\supseteq IS$.

entries.subject: ring-map-module
entries.name: Relative flatness on specified closed subsets of source and base
entries.definition: Fix $R\to S$, an $S$-module $M$ and an ideal $J\subseteq S$. For an $R$-algebra $B$ and an ideal $I\subseteq B$, set $T=S\otimes_R B$ and $N=M\otimes_R B$. Require $N_{\mathfrak q}$ to be flat over $B$ for every $\mathfrak q\supseteq IT+JT$.

entries.subject: ring-map-module
entries.name: Closed subset of the source in a relative flattening problem
entries.definition: The datum consists of a ring map $R\to S$, an $S$-module $M$ and a specified ideal $J\subseteq S$ defining the closed subset $V(J)$.

entries.subject: ring-map-module
entries.name: Flattening ideal along the closed fibre of a complete local base
entries.definition: Let $R$ be complete Noetherian local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, let $R\to S$ have Noetherian target and let $M$ be finite over $S$. This is the least ideal $I\subseteq R$ such that $M/IM$ is flat over $R/I$ at every source prime above $\mathfrak m$. It is contained in $\mathfrak m$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Torsion submodule over a domain
entries.definition: For a domain $R$ with fraction field $K$, the submodule $\ker(M\to M\otimes_R K)$ consists of elements annihilated by some nonzero scalar of $R$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Torsion-free stalks at all maximal ideals
entries.definition: The coefficient ring $R$ is a domain and $M_{\mathfrak m}$ is torsion free over $R_{\mathfrak m}$ for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Embedding in a finite free module
entries.definition: There exist $n\geq0$ and an injective $R$-linear map $M\hookrightarrow R^n$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Module over a Dedekind domain
entries.definition: The coefficient ring is a Noetherian integrally closed domain of dimension at most one.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Module over a principal ideal domain
entries.definition: The coefficient ring is a domain in which every ideal is principal.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Module over a normal domain
entries.definition: The coefficient ring $R$ is a domain integrally closed in $\operatorname{Frac}(R)$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Serre condition S₂ for a finite module
entries.definition: For a finite $R$-module over a Noetherian ring, require $\operatorname{depth}_{R_{\mathfrak p}} M_{\mathfrak p}\geq\min(2,\dim\operatorname{Supp}M_{\mathfrak p})$ at each prime of its support.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Recovery from the height-one localizations
entries.definition: For a torsion-free module $M$ over a domain with fraction field $K$, require $M=\bigcap_{\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)=1} M_{\mathfrak p}$ inside $M\otimes_R K$. An empty intersection is the entire ambient vector space.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Injection into finitely many prime localizations
entries.definition: There exist finitely many primes $\mathfrak p_i$ for which the canonical map $R\to\prod_i R_{\mathfrak p_i}$ is injective.

entries.subject: ring-map-module
entries.name: Finite presentation over a polynomial ambient algebra
entries.definition: For the specified polynomial map $R\to P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, an ambient $P$-module $M$ admits a presentation $P^b\to P^a\to M\to0$ with finite $a,b$. Flatness over $R$ is a separate condition.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Mapping cone of a homological chain map
entries.definition: For $f:A_\bullet\to B_\bullet$, set $C(f)_n=B_n\oplus A_{n-1}$ and $d(b,a)=(d_Bb+f(a),-d_Aa)$.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Extended alternating Čech complex of a tuple
entries.definition: For $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in R$, the degree-$p$ terms are $\bigoplus_{|T|=p}M_{\prod_{i\in T} f_i}$ for $0\leq p\leq r$, with $M$ in degree zero. The differential is the signed sum of restriction maps obtained by adjoining one index to $T$, ordered increasingly. The alternating signs cancel in $d^2$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Fibre at a maximal ideal
entries.definition: For a finitely presented module $M$ and a maximal ideal $x$ of $R$, the finite-dimensional space $M(x)=M/xM$ is over $\kappa(x)=R/x$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Quotient of the fibre detected by linear functionals
entries.definition: For finitely presented $M$ and maximal $x$, let $B(x)$ be the annihilator in $M/xM$ of the image of $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R)\to(M/xM)^\vee$. Put $V(x)=(M/xM)/B(x)$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Noetherian maximal spectrum of the base
entries.definition: The subspace $\operatorname{MaxSpec}(R)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ satisfies the descending chain condition on closed sets.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Finite dimension of the maximal spectrum of the base
entries.definition: The lengths of chains of nonempty irreducible closed subsets of $\operatorname{MaxSpec}(R)$ have a finite upper bound.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Local free summand above the dimension of the maximal spectrum
entries.definition: For every maximal ideal $x$, there is an integer $r>\dim\operatorname{MaxSpec}(R)$ for which $M_x$ admits $R_x^r$ as a direct summand.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Free direct summand of rank one
entries.definition: There are $s\in M$ and $\lambda:M\to R$ with $\lambda(s)=1$. Equivalently $M\cong R\oplus N$ for some $N$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Countably generated module
entries.definition: A finite or countably infinite set of elements generates $M$ over $R$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Infinite-dimensional fibre at every maximal ideal
entries.definition: For every maximal ideal $x$, the vector space $M/xM$ has infinite dimension over $R/x$. For projective $M$, this dimension is the rank of the free module $M_x$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Noetherian quotient of the base by its Jacobson radical
entries.definition: The ring $R/\operatorname{Jac}(R)$ is Noetherian.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Free after adding a free module of unrestricted rank
entries.definition: There exists a free $R$-module $F$ of arbitrary rank such that $M\oplus F$ is free. The rank of $F$ is permitted to be infinite.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Every element lies in a finite stably free direct summand
entries.definition: Every $s\in M$ lies in a direct summand $K\subseteq M$ with $K\oplus R^a\cong R^b$ for some nonnegative finite $a,b$.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Cyclotomic deformation of the Artin–Schreier polynomial
entries.definition: For prime $p$ put $w=1-\zeta_p$. Expand $P(z)=((1+wz)^p-1)/w^p$ in $\mathbf Z[\zeta_p][z]$ and then specialize along a ring map from $\mathbf Z[\zeta_p]$. This gives a polynomial even if $w$ becomes a zero divisor.

entries.subject: valued-field-extension
entries.name: Degree-p extension of finite level
entries.definition: Let $A$ be a mixed-characteristic $(0,p)$ DVR with fraction field $K$ containing $\zeta_p\in A$. Fix $w=1-\zeta_p$ and the polynomial $P(z)=((1+wz)^p-1)/w^p$. A degree-$p$ field extension is of finite level if it is generated by some $z$ with $P(z)=\xi\in K$ and $w^p\xi\in\mathfrak m_A$.

entries.subject: valued-field-extension
entries.name: Level of a degree-p extension of finite level
entries.definition: In the preceding mixed-characteristic setting write $v_A$ for the normalized valuation and $e_1=v_A(1-\zeta_p)$. Minimize $\max(0,-v_A(P(z)))/e_1$ over generators $z$ with $P(z)\in K$, taking the numerator to be zero if $P(z)=0$. The minimum lies in $[0,p)$.

entries.subject: valued-field-extension
entries.name: Embeddable into an unramified extension after taking a uniformizer root
entries.definition: For a finite separable extension $L/K$ at a DVR $A$ with fraction field $K$, there exist a uniformizer $\pi$, $e\ge1$ invertible in $\kappa_A$, and an embedding of $L$ over $K$ into a finite extension of $K(\pi^{1/e})$ unramified at $A[\pi^{1/e}]$.

entries.topic: Galois extensions with a specified prime
entries.subject: galois-prime
entries.name: Nontrivial wild inertia group
entries.definition: For a finite Galois extension at a specified maximal ideal of the normalization of a DVR, $P\ne1$.

entries.topic: Galois extensions with a specified prime
entries.subject: galois-prime
entries.name: Wild inertia acts trivially on the second infinitesimal neighbourhood
entries.definition: Every element of the wild inertia group at $\mathfrak m$ acts as the identity on $B/\mathfrak m^2$, where $B$ is the normalization of the base DVR in the given finite Galois extension. In general the action on the graded piece $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ alone imposes a weaker condition.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Invariant subring of a finite group action
entries.definition: For a finite group $G$ acting on a ring $R$, the subring $R^G$ consists of the elements fixed by every $\sigma\in G$.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Unique minimal prime in the henselization
entries.definition: The ring $A$ is local and its henselization $A^h$ has exactly one minimal prime.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Unique minimal prime in the strict henselization
entries.definition: The ring $A$ is local and its strict henselization at a separable closure of the residue field has exactly one minimal prime.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Largest weakly étale subalgebra over a field
entries.definition: For a $K$-algebra $A$, with $K$ a field, $B_{\max}(A)$ is the union of its weakly étale $K$-subalgebras. These form a directed family because the subalgebra generated by two is the image of their tensor product.

entries.topic: Rings with a fixed integer index
entries.subject: ring-index
entries.name: Weak dimension bounded by a specified integer
entries.definition: For a fixed $d\ge0$, every $A$-module has flat dimension at most $d$. Equivalently $\operatorname{Tor}_{d+1}^A(M,N)=0$ for every pair of modules, by dimension shifting.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: All ideals are flat
entries.definition: Each ideal is flat as a module over the ring.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: All finitely generated ideals are flat
entries.definition: Every ideal generated by a finite family is flat as a module over the ring.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Submodules of flat modules are flat
entries.definition: Every submodule of every flat module is flat.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Weak dimension zero bound
entries.definition: Every module has flat dimension at most zero.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Direct product of fields
