entries.definition: The ring is isomorphic to $\prod_{i\in I}K_i$ for a set-indexed family of fields, with coordinatewise operations.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Absolutely flat source ring
entries.definition: Every module over the source ring is flat.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Absolutely flat target ring
entries.definition: Every module over the target ring is flat.

entries.subject: module-system
entries.name: Derived inverse limit of a tower of modules
entries.definition: For a tower $M_1\leftarrow M_2\leftarrow\cdots$ of $R$-modules, $\mathbf R\lim M_n$ is represented by the fibre of $1-\mathrm{shift}$ on $\prod_n M_n$ in $D(R)$. In cohomological degrees zero and one this computes the limit and its first derived functor.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Product total complex of a right half-plane bicomplex
entries.definition: Given columns $A^{p,\bullet}$ for $p\ge0$ forming a complex of complexes, put $\operatorname{Tot}_{\Pi}^n(A)=\prod_{p\ge0}A^{p,n-p}$ with the total differential formed from the horizontal and signed vertical differentials.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Directed colimit of finite free modules
entries.definition: The module is isomorphic to the colimit of a directed system of finite free modules over its base ring.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Tensor comparison for products is surjective
entries.definition: For each set-indexed family $(Q_i)$ the canonical map $M\otimes_R\prod_i Q_i\to\prod_i(M\otimes_RQ_i)$ is surjective.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Tensor comparison for products is bijective
entries.definition: For each set-indexed family $(Q_i)$ the canonical map $M\otimes_R\prod_i Q_i\to\prod_i(M\otimes_RQ_i)$ is an isomorphism.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: All products of flat modules are flat
entries.definition: For every set-indexed family of flat $R$-modules, their product over $R$ is flat.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: All powers of the free module of rank one are flat
entries.definition: For every set $I$, the product $R^I$ is flat as an $R$-module.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Length of a module
entries.definition: The length $\ell_R(M)$ is the supremum of the lengths $n$ of strictly increasing chains of submodules $0=M_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq M_n=M$. It is a nonnegative integer or infinity.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Module of length one
entries.definition: The invariant $\ell_R(M)$ equals $1$.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Chain of prime ideals
entries.definition: A finite list of prime ideals $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_n$ with all successive inclusions strict.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Length of a specified prime chain
entries.definition: The length of $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_n$ is $n$, the number of strict inclusions.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Krull dimension of a ring
entries.definition: The supremum of lengths of finite chains of prime ideals, equivalently the Krull dimension of the prime spectrum. The bound “dimension at most zero” allows an empty spectrum.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Grothendieck group of finite modules
entries.definition: The abelian group $K'_0(R)$ is generated by isomorphism classes of finite $R$-modules, modulo $[M]=[L]+[N]$ for every short exact sequence $0\to L\to M\to N\to0$ of finite modules.

entries.subject: local-ring
entries.name: Formal fibre of a local ring at a prime
entries.definition: For a Noetherian local ring $R$ and a prime $\mathfrak p$, take the fibre $\widehat R\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ of its maximal-ideal-adic completion map.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Formal fibres with a specified property P
entries.definition: Fix a property $P$ of algebras $k\to T$ with $k$ a field and $T$ Noetherian. A Noetherian ring $R$ is a $P$-ring when, for every prime $\mathfrak p$, all formal fibres of $R_{\mathfrak p}$ have $P$ over their respective residue fields.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings
entries.definition: The source and target are Noetherian local rings and the inverse image of the target maximal ideal is the source maximal ideal.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Formal smoothness of a local map in the target maximal-ideal-adic topology
entries.definition: For a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings, equip the source with the discrete topology and the target with its maximal-ideal-adic topology. Require the infinitesimal lifting property for continuous maps to discrete square-zero extensions.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Geometrically regular closed fibre
entries.definition: For a local homomorphism $(A,\mathfrak m,k)\to B$, the fibre algebra $B\otimes_A k$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $k$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Regularity of the source completion map
entries.definition: The source is Noetherian local and the homomorphism from it to its maximal-ideal-adic completion is regular.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Cohen–Macaulay source ring
entries.definition: The source is Noetherian and all its local rings are Cohen–Macaulay.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Cohen–Macaulay target ring
entries.definition: The target is Noetherian and all its local rings are Cohen–Macaulay.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Separable residue field extension of a local homomorphism
entries.definition: For a local ring homomorphism, the induced extension of residue fields is separable, allowing transcendence.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Geometrically reduced formal fibres of a Noetherian local ring
entries.definition: For every prime of the Noetherian local ring, the fibre of its maximal-ideal-adic completion map is geometrically reduced over the corresponding residue field.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Divisibility as an abelian group
entries.definition: For a module over $\mathbf Z$, multiplication by each positive integer is surjective.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Module over the integers
entries.definition: The coefficient ring of the module is $\mathbf Z$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Ext¹ into the module vanishes on every module
entries.definition: For every $R$-module $N$, $\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(N,M)=0$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Ext¹ into the module vanishes on cyclic quotients
entries.definition: For every ideal $I$ of $R$, $\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(R/I,M)=0$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Extension of maps from ideals
entries.definition: For every ideal $I\subseteq R$ every $R$-linear map $I\to M$ extends to an $R$-linear map $R\to M$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Character module
entries.definition: The character module is $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(M,\mathbf Q/\mathbf Z)$ with action $(r\varphi)(x)=\varphi(rx)$.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: K-injective complex
entries.definition: A complex $I$ of $R$-modules is K-injective when every chain map from an acyclic complex to $I$ is null homotopic.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Bounded-above complex of flat modules
entries.definition: The specified cochain representative has flat terms and zero terms in all sufficiently high degrees.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Flat model in a specified finite interval
entries.definition: For the same specified integers $a\leq b$ as in the Tor-amplitude test, the object is represented by a complex of flat modules supported in $[a,b]$.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Bounded-above representative by injectives
entries.definition: There is a cochain representative by injective modules vanishing in all sufficiently high degrees. No lower bound on its terms is imposed.

entries.subject: module-map
entries.name: Map factoring through a projective module
entries.definition: There exist a projective $P$ and a factorization $M\to P\to N$ of the specified map.

entries.subject: module-map
entries.name: Map factoring through a free module
entries.definition: The specified $M\to N$ is a composite through some free module of arbitrary rank.

entries.subject: module-ideal-pair
entries.name: Module annihilated by the specified ideal
entries.definition: The chosen ideal $I$ satisfies $IM=0$.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Internal Hom complex of modules
entries.definition: For cochain complexes $K,L$, the term in degree $n$ is $\prod_p\operatorname{Hom}_R(K^p,L^{p+n})$. Its differential sends a homogeneous $f$ to $d_L f-(-1)^n f d_K$.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Derived internal Hom of modules
entries.definition: For $K,L\in D(R)$ the object $\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,L)$ represents the right adjoint to derived tensoring with $K$. Its $i$th cohomology is $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(K,L)$.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Compact object of the derived category of modules
entries.definition: For every set-indexed family $(X_i)$, the canonical map $\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(K,X_i)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(K,\bigoplus_i X_i)$ is bijective.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Ghost morphism in the derived category
entries.definition: A morphism in $D(R)$ induces zero in every cohomological degree.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: The unit strongly generates the perfect derived category
entries.definition: There exists one $n\ge1$ such that every perfect complex belongs to $\langle R\rangle_n$, obtained from shifts of $R$ using finite sums, summands, and at most $n-1$ successive extensions.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Existence of a strong generator for perfect complexes
entries.definition: For some perfect object $G$ and one $n\ge1$, every perfect complex belongs to $\langle G\rangle_n$.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Cohomology supported in degrees −1 and 0
entries.definition: For $K\in D(R)$ one has $H^i(K)=0$ outside $\{-1,0\}$.

entries.subject: complex-ideal-pair
entries.name: Ideal annihilating first Ext with every module
entries.definition: For the chosen ideal $I$, require $I\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(K,N)=0$ for every module $N$ in degree zero.

entries.subject: module-system
entries.name: Pro-zero tower
entries.definition: For each index $n$, some transition from a later index to $n$ is the zero map.

entries.subject: module-system
entries.name: Inverse tower indexed by the positive integers
entries.definition: The system is specified by one module $M_n$ for each positive integer and adjacent transition maps $M_{n+1}\to M_n$.

entries.subject: module-system
entries.name: Tower acyclic for inverse limit
entries.definition: All positive right derived inverse limits of this countable tower vanish. Equivalently its first derived limit vanishes.

entries.subject: module-system
entries.name: Countable direct sum of copies is limit-acyclic
entries.definition: For an integer-indexed inverse tower, the termwise direct sum of countably many copies of the tower has vanishing first derived inverse limit.

entries.topic: Ring maps with a fixed ideal
entries.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
entries.name: Module gluing data on a formal neighbourhood and its complement
entries.definition: Given $R\to S$ and $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_t)$, specify an $S$-module $M'$, $R_{f_i}$-modules $M_i$, isomorphisms $M'_{f_i}\simeq M_i\otimes_R S$, and overlap identifications $(M_i)_{f_j}\simeq(M_j)_{f_i}$ agreeing after extension to $S$ and satisfying the triple cocycle condition. Morphisms commute with all identifications.

entries.topic: Ring maps with a fixed ideal
entries.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
entries.name: Compatible sections of module gluing data
entries.definition: For gluing data $M',M_i$, take $H^0$ to be the $R$-module of tuples of sections in $M'\times\prod_i M_i$ with equal images under all indicated identifications.

entries.topic: Ring maps with a fixed ideal
entries.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
entries.name: Beauville–Laszlo gluing pair
entries.definition: For a specified $R\to S$ and scalar $f$, all $R/f^n\to S/f^nS$ for $n>0$ must be isomorphisms and $0\to R\to S\oplus R_f\to S_f\to0$ exact with difference as final map.

entries.subject: ring-map-module
entries.name: Gluable module for a specified principal gluing diagram
entries.definition: For fixed $R\to S$ and $f\in R$, tensor $0\to R\to S\oplus R_f\to S_f\to0$ over $R$ with the module. Gluability means the resulting sequence beginning at zero is exact.

entries.topic: Ring maps with a fixed ideal
entries.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
entries.name: Principal completion diagram
entries.definition: The chosen map over the specified principal ideal is the canonical $R\to\lim_n R/f^nR$.

entries.subject: ring-map-module
entries.name: Finitely presented source module in a gluing diagram
entries.definition: The given $R$-module in a principal gluing diagram has a finite presentation over $R$.

entries.subject: module-ideal-pair
entries.name: Finitely generated ideal of a module–ideal pair
entries.definition: The specified ideal $I$ has a finite generating set.

entries.subject: ring-ideal-pair
entries.name: Ring derived complete for the specified ideal
entries.definition: The module $A[0]$ is derived complete for $I$, equivalently $\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_A(A_f,A)=0$ for all $f\in I$.

entries.subject: complex-ideal-pair
entries.name: Derived completion functor
entries.definition: For finitely generated $I$, $\Lambda_I$ is the left adjoint to the inclusion of derived $I$-complete objects into $D(A)$. Its unit is $K\to\Lambda_I K$.
refs: B. Bhatt, Prismatic cohomology, Lecture III, §2, property (1) (left adjoint for a finitely generated ideal)

entries.subject: complex-ideal-pair
entries.name: Koszul tower for powers of chosen generators
entries.definition: For $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ place $K_n=K(f_1^n,\ldots,f_r^n)$ in cochain degrees $-r,\ldots,0$. The transitions multiply each degree-minus-one generator by its corresponding $f_i$ and extend by exterior powers, so on $H^0$ they are the quotient maps.

entries.subject: ring-ideal-pair
entries.name: Bounded torsion for a specified principal ideal
entries.definition: For the specified generator $f$, there is one integer $c\ge1$ with $A[f^\infty]=A[f^c]$.

entries.subject: module-scalar-pair
entries.name: Tate module of a scalar acting on a module
entries.definition: Take $T_f(M)=\lim_n M[f^n]$ with transition multiplication by $f$.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Derived Berthelot–Ogus décalage
entries.definition: For a nonzerodivisor $f$ and an $f$-torsion-free cochain model $M$, take $(\eta_f M)^i=\{x\in f^i M^i:dx\in f^{i+1}M^{i+1}\}$ inside $M[1/f]$ with the induced differential. This computes the additive functor $L\eta_f$.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Determinantal ideal for a term of décalage
entries.definition: For a bounded complex $M$ of finite free modules write $r_i=\operatorname{rank}M^i$. The ideal $I_i(M,f)$ consists of the maximal $r_i$-row minors of $(f,d^i):M^i\to M^i\oplus M^{i+1}$ and contains $f^{r_i}$.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Universal splitting ideal of the reduced décalage graph
entries.definition: When all $I_i(M,f)$ are principal, reduce the split injection $(1,d^i)$ on $(\eta_fM)^i$ modulo $f$. The ideal $J_i(M,f)$ in $A/f$ cuts out the universal locus of scalar extensions on which its image splits into a sum of submodules of its two target summands.

entries.subject: module-system
entries.name: Sequences of finite reductions with morphisms up to bounded ideal torsion
entries.definition: For Noetherian $A$ use sequences of finite $A/I^n$-modules $E_n$, with no transition maps needed. A morphism is represented by $I^cE_n\to F_n/F_n[I^c]$ for $n\ge c$, identified under increasing $c$ by restriction of the source and further quotient of the target. Representatives compose after adding their bounds.

entries.subject: ring-subset
entries.name: Localization at the specified multiplicative subset
entries.definition: For a ring $R$ and multiplicative subset $U$, the ring $U^{-1}R$ consists of classes of fractions $a/u$. Equality $a/u=b/v$ means $w(va-ub)=0$ for some $w\in U$.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Unique closed point of the prime spectrum
entries.definition: The prime spectrum has exactly one closed point.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Units outside a specified maximal ideal
entries.definition: There exists a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ such that every element outside $\mathfrak m$ is a unit.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Complementary unit condition
entries.definition: For every $x\in R$, at least one of $x$ and $1-x$ is invertible.

entries.subject: module-element
entries.name: Vanishing of a module element
entries.definition: The specified element $x$ of the $R$-module $M$ is zero.

entries.subject: module-element
entries.name: Vanishing of a module element at all prime ideals
entries.definition: For every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, $x/1=0$ in $M_{\mathfrak p}$.

entries.subject: module-element
entries.name: Vanishing of a module element at all maximal ideals
entries.definition: For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, $x/1=0$ in $M_{\mathfrak p}$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Vanishing of a module at all prime ideals
entries.definition: For every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, $M_{\mathfrak p}=0$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Vanishing of a module at all maximal ideals
entries.definition: For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, $M_{\mathfrak p}=0$.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Exactness at the specified middle term
entries.definition: The specified three-term complex $L\to M\to N$ is exact at $M$.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Exactness at the specified middle term at all prime ideals
entries.definition: For every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, the localized complex is exact at $M_{\mathfrak p}$.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Exactness at the specified middle term at all maximal ideals
entries.definition: For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, the localized complex is exact at $M_{\mathfrak p}$.

entries.subject: module-map
entries.name: Injective module map
entries.definition: The given module map is injective.

entries.subject: module-map
entries.name: Injective module map at all prime ideals
entries.definition: For every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, the map $f_{\mathfrak p}$ is injective.

entries.subject: module-map
entries.name: Injective module map at all maximal ideals
entries.definition: For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, the map $f_{\mathfrak p}$ is injective.

entries.subject: module-map
entries.name: Surjective module map
entries.definition: The given module map is surjective.

entries.subject: module-map
entries.name: Surjective module map at all prime ideals
entries.definition: For every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, the map $f_{\mathfrak p}$ is surjective.

entries.subject: module-map
entries.name: Surjective module map at all maximal ideals
entries.definition: For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, the map $f_{\mathfrak p}$ is surjective.

entries.subject: module-map
entries.name: Bijective module map
entries.definition: The given module map is bijective.

entries.subject: module-map
entries.name: Bijective module map at all prime ideals
entries.definition: For every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, the map $f_{\mathfrak p}$ is bijective.

entries.subject: module-map
entries.name: Bijective module map at all maximal ideals
entries.definition: For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, the map $f_{\mathfrak p}$ is bijective.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Profinite prime spectrum
entries.definition: The underlying Zariski space is profinite.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Hausdorff prime spectrum
entries.definition: Distinct prime ideals have disjoint Zariski neighbourhoods.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Totally disconnected prime spectrum
entries.definition: Every connected component of the Zariski space is a singleton.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Quasi-compact opens of the spectrum are closed
entries.definition: Every quasi-compact Zariski open is closed.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: All primes maximal
entries.definition: Every prime ideal is maximal.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: All primes minimal
entries.definition: Every prime ideal is minimal.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Principal opens are closed
entries.definition: For every $f\in R$, the principal open $D(f)$ is closed.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Contraction of radicals of extended ideals
entries.definition: For every ideal $I$ of $R$, the inverse image of $\sqrt{IS}$ is $\sqrt I$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Extension and contraction on radical ideals
entries.definition: For every radical ideal $I$ of $R$, the inverse image of $IS$ is $I$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Extension and contraction on prime ideals
entries.definition: For every prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, the inverse image of $\mathfrak p S$ is $\mathfrak p$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Countably generated module
entries.definition: The module admits a countable generating family, allowing finite and empty families.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Ascending chain condition on principal ideals
entries.definition: Every increasing sequence of principal ideals is eventually constant.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Atomic domain
entries.definition: The ring is a domain and each nonzero nonunit is a finite product of irreducible elements.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Domain in which every irreducible element is prime
entries.definition: Every irreducible element of the domain generates a prime ideal.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Closed subsets stable under generalizations are open
entries.definition: Every Zariski closed subset of $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ containing all generalizations of its points is open.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Every finite flat module is finite locally free
entries.definition: For every finite flat $R$-module $M$ and every prime $\mathfrak p$, there is a principal neighbourhood where $M$ is finite free.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Local ring with residue field of finite projective dimension
entries.definition: The ring is local and the projective dimension of its residue field as a module over the ring is finite.

entries.subject: ring-map-point
entries.name: Field as the base ring of a marked point
entries.definition: The source ring of the specified homomorphism is a field.

entries.subject: ring-map-point
entries.name: Characteristic zero at the base ring
entries.definition: The source ring has characteristic zero.

entries.subject: ring-map-point
entries.name: Regular local ring at the target prime
entries.definition: For the target prime $\mathfrak q\subset S$, the ring $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular local.

entries.subject: ring-map-point
entries.name: Finite free localized differentials
entries.definition: At the specified prime $\mathfrak q$ of $S$, the $S_{\mathfrak q}$-module $(\Omega_{S/R})_{\mathfrak q}$ is finite free.

entries.subject: ring-map-point
entries.name: Vanishing cotangent H₁ at a target prime
entries.definition: The localization of $H_1(L_{S/R})$ at the chosen prime of $S$ is zero.

entries.subject: ring-map-point
entries.name: Separable residue extension at a target prime
entries.definition: The field extension $\kappa(\mathfrak q)/\kappa(\mathfrak q\cap R)$ is separable in the general sense, allowing transcendence.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Projective module of relative differentials
entries.definition: The $S$-module $\Omega_{S/R}$ is projective, without a finite-generation assumption.

entries.subject: ring-map-point
entries.name: Isolated point of the scheme-theoretic fibre
entries.definition: For $R\to S$ and $\mathfrak q$ over $\mathfrak p$, the corresponding singleton is open in $\operatorname{Spec}(S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$.

entries.subject: ring-map-point
entries.name: Finite-dimensional local ring of the fibre
entries.definition: For the chosen point $\mathfrak q$ over $\mathfrak p$, the local ring $S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak q}$ has finite dimension as a vector space over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Conductor of a finite polynomial-algebra map
entries.definition: For a finite $R[X]\to S$, its conductor in $S$ is the largest ideal of $S$ contained in the image of $R[X]$. It consists of elements $s$ with $sS$ contained in that image.

entries.subject: ring-map-module
entries.name: Relative flat locus of a module
entries.definition: For $R\to S$ and an $S$-module $M$, this is the set of $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}S$ where $M_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $R$.

entries.subject: ring-map-point
entries.name: Cohen–Macaulay local fibre ring
entries.definition: For a finite type $R\to S$ at $\mathfrak q$ over $\mathfrak p$, the local fibre ring $S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak q}$ is Cohen–Macaulay.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Local dimension formula
entries.definition: For a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings $R\to S$, the equality $\dim S=\dim R+\dim(S/\mathfrak m_RS)$ holds.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Simple roots lift for arbitrary polynomials
entries.definition: The ring is local with residue field $k$. Every simple root in $k$ of the reduction of any $f\in R[T]$ lifts to a root in $R$.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Coprime factorization lifts for monic polynomials
entries.definition: The ring is local with residue field $k$. For each monic $f\in R[T]$ and coprime factorization $\bar f=g_0h_0$, a factorization $f=gh$ lifts both factors.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Coprime factorization lifts for monic polynomials with prescribed first degree
entries.definition: The ring is local with residue field $k$. For each monic $f\in R[T]$ and coprime factorization $\bar f=g_0h_0$, a factorization $f=gh$ lifts both factors with $\deg g=\deg g_0$.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Coprime factorization lifts for arbitrary polynomials
entries.definition: The ring is local with residue field $k$. For each arbitrary $f\in R[T]$ and coprime factorization $\bar f=g_0h_0$, a factorization $f=gh$ lifts both factors.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Coprime factorization lifts for arbitrary polynomials with prescribed first degree
entries.definition: The ring is local with residue field $k$. For each arbitrary $f\in R[T]$ and coprime factorization $\bar f=g_0h_0$, a factorization $f=gh$ lifts both factors with $\deg g=\deg g_0$.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Retraction of étale neighbourhoods with equal residue field
entries.definition: The ring is local with residue field $k$. Each étale $R$-algebra equipped with a prime over $\mathfrak m$ of residue field $k$ admits an $R$-algebra retraction to $R$.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Unique pointed retraction of rational étale neighbourhoods
entries.definition: The ring is local with residue field $k$. For each such étale neighbourhood $(S,\mathfrak q)$ with residue field $k$, exactly one $R$-retraction $S\to R$ contracts $\mathfrak m$ to $\mathfrak q$.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Local product decomposition of finite algebras
entries.definition: The ring is local with residue field $k$. Every finite $R$-algebra is a product of local rings. Such a product necessarily has finitely many nonzero factors. The zero algebra is the empty product.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Finite factor containing all quasi-finite closed-fibre points
entries.definition: The ring is local with residue field $k$. Every finite-type algebra is $A\times B$ with $A$ finite and no point of the closed fibre of $B$ quasi-finite over $R$.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Finite factor with positive-dimensional complementary components
entries.definition: The ring is local with residue field $k$. Every finite-type algebra is $A\times B$ with $A$ finite and each irreducible component of the closed fibre of $B$ of dimension at least one.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Closed-fibre splitting of quasi-finite algebras
entries.definition: The ring is local with residue field $k$. Every quasi-finite algebra is $A\times B$ with $A$ finite over $R$ and $B/\mathfrak m B=0$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ind-étale ring map
entries.definition: As an algebra over the source, the target is a filtered colimit of étale algebras.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Formally unramified field extension
entries.definition: Regard the specified field inclusion $k\subset K$ as a ring homomorphism. The ring homomorphism is formally unramified.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Unramified field extension
entries.definition: Regard the specified field inclusion $k\subset K$ as a ring homomorphism. The ring homomorphism is unramified.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Formally étale field extension
entries.definition: Regard the specified field inclusion $k\subset K$ as a ring homomorphism. The ring homomorphism is formally étale.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Étale field extension
entries.definition: Regard the specified field inclusion $k\subset K$ as a ring homomorphism. The ring homomorphism is étale.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Injectivity on absolute differentials after scalar extension
entries.definition: The map $K\otimes_k\Omega_{k/\mathbf Z}\to\Omega_{K/\mathbf Z}$ is injective. In characteristic $p$ one may take $\mathbf F_p$ as the base for both modules.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Vanishing first cotangent homology for a field extension
entries.definition: For the cotangent complex of $K/k$ one has $H_1(L_{K/k})=0$.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Reduced after adjoining all pth roots to the base
entries.definition: The base has characteristic $p>0$ and $K\otimes_k k^{1/p}$ is reduced, with the roots taken inside an algebraic closure.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Field obtained by localizing a smooth algebra
entries.definition: There exist a smooth $k$-algebra $A$ and a multiplicative set $U$ with $K\cong U^{-1}A$ over $k$.

entries.subject: ring-inclusion
entries.name: Complete local subring with contracted maximal ideal
entries.definition: For the given inclusion $\Lambda\subseteq(R,\mathfrak m)$, the subring is complete local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\cap\Lambda$.

entries.subject: ring-inclusion
entries.name: Isomorphism on residues of a subring
entries.definition: The map $\Lambda/(\Lambda\cap\mathfrak m)\to R/\mathfrak m$ is an isomorphism.

entries.subject: ring-inclusion
entries.name: Contracted maximal ideal generated by the residue characteristic
entries.definition: For $p=\operatorname{char}(R/\mathfrak m)$, one has $\mathfrak m\cap\Lambda=p\Lambda$. This includes $p=0$.

entries.subject: ring-inclusion
entries.name: Complete local ambient ring of a subring
entries.definition: The given ambient ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$ is local and its map to $\lim_nR/\mathfrak m^n$ is an isomorphism.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Finite normalization in every finite separable fraction-field extension
entries.definition: The ring is a domain $R$, and for each finite separable $L/\operatorname{Frac}R$ its integral closure in $L$ is finite over $R$.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Open normal locus
entries.definition: The set of primes $\mathfrak p$ with $R_{\mathfrak p}$ normal is open in $\operatorname{Spec}R$.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Nonempty normal principal open of a domain
entries.definition: The ring is a domain with $R_f$ normal for some nonzero $f\in R$.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: N-1 for all finite-type domain algebras
entries.definition: For each finite-type $R$-algebra $S$ which is a domain, the integral closure of $S$ in its own fraction field is finite over $S$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Universally catenary source
entries.definition: The source ring of the specified map is universally catenary.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Universally catenary target
entries.definition: The target ring of the specified map is universally catenary.

entries.subject: field
entries.name: The field of p elements
entries.definition: For a prime $p$, the field $\mathbf F_p=\mathbf Z/(p)$ is the residue field at the maximal ideal $(p)$ of $\mathbf Z$. Its $p$ residue classes form its underlying set.

entries.subject: field-tower
entries.name: Tower from an ordered generating family
entries.definition: For a finite extension $K/F$ with specified generators $a_1,\ldots,a_n$, set $K_0=F$ and $K_i=K_{i-1}(a_i)$. The data include the minimal polynomial $P_i$ of $a_i$ over $K_{i-1}$ and a chosen algebraic closure of $F$.

entries.subject: field-extension-pair
entries.name: Square of field embeddings into a common overfield
entries.definition: Given field embeddings $k\to K$, $k\to L$, $K\to\Omega$ and $L\to\Omega$, require that the composites from $k$ to $\Omega$ agree. The specified embeddings determine the subfields used in constructing the compositum.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Relative singular ideal
entries.definition: For $R\to A$, the radical ideal $H_{A/R}\subseteq A$ cuts out the complement of the locus where the homomorphism is smooth at a target prime. Smoothness at a point is defined on a principal neighbourhood.

entries.subject: algebra-element
entries.name: Elementary standard element
entries.definition: For a finitely presented algebra $A$ over $R$ and $a\in A$, choose a polynomial presentation $A=P/I$ with $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ in $n$ variables and an integer $0\le c\le\min(m,n)$. Require $a[f_j]\in\langle[f_1],\ldots,[f_c]\rangle$ in $I/I^2$ for every $j>c$. The element is elementary standard if such data exist with $a$ a multiple of one $c$-rowed Jacobian minor of the first $c$ equations, for some $c$ columns after relabeling variables. The empty minor is one.

entries.subject: algebra-element
entries.name: Strictly standard element
entries.definition: For a finitely presented algebra $A$ over $R$ and $a\in A$, choose a polynomial presentation $A=P/I$ with $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ in $n$ variables and an integer $0\le c\le\min(m,n)$. Require $a[f_j]\in\langle[f_1],\ldots,[f_c]\rangle$ in $I/I^2$ for every $j>c$. The element is strictly standard if such data exist with $a$ in the ideal generated by all $c$-rowed Jacobian minors of the first $c$ equations, allowing all choices of $c$ variable columns.

entries.subject: algebra-element
entries.name: Smooth algebra on a specified principal open
entries.definition: For $a$ in the specified finitely presented $R$-algebra $A$, the homomorphism $R\to A_a$ is smooth.

entries.subject: algebra-element
entries.name: Standard smooth algebra on a specified principal open
entries.definition: For $a$ in the specified finitely presented $R$-algebra $A$, the algebra $A_a$ has a standard smooth presentation over $R$.

entries.subject: algebra-element
entries.name: Free differential module on a specified principal open
entries.definition: For $a$ in the specified finitely presented $R$-algebra $A$, the differential module $\Omega_{A_a/R}$ is free over $A_a$.

entries.subject: algebra-element
entries.name: Stably free differential module on a specified principal open
entries.definition: For $a$ in the specified finitely presented $R$-algebra $A$, the module $\Omega_{A_a/R}$ becomes finite free after direct sum with a finite free $A_a$-module.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Quasi-compact smooth locus of a ring map
entries.definition: The subspace of $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ where $R\to A$ is smooth is quasi-compact.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Filtered colimit of standard smooth algebras
entries.definition: The target is isomorphic over the specified source ring to a filtered colimit of standard smooth algebras over that ring.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Affine Néron blowup along the valuation centre
entries.definition: Let $R\subseteq V$ be DVRs of ramification index one with common uniformizer $\pi$. Factor $R\to A\to V$ with $A$ flat of finite type. Write $\mathfrak q=\ker(A\to V)$ and $\mathfrak p$ for the preimage of the maximal ideal of $V$. Let $A'=A[\mathfrak p/\pi]$ with the induced primes $\mathfrak q',\mathfrak p'$. The construction is the subalgebra $A[\mathfrak p/\pi]\subseteq A[1/\pi]$ with the map to $V$ obtained by dividing images of elements of $\mathfrak p$ by $\pi$.

entries.subject: ring-map-point
entries.name: Resolution of a specified desingularization problem
entries.definition: Let $R$ be Noetherian, $A$ finitely presented over $R$, and $A\to L$ an $R$-algebra map with a specified prime $\mathfrak q$ of $L$. For every such algebra $B$ over $R$ mapping to $L$, put $h_B=\sqrt{H_{B/R}L}$. A resolution at $\mathfrak q$ is a factorization through finitely presented $B$ with $h_A\subseteq h_B$ and $h_B\not\subseteq\mathfrak q$. The data consist of the algebra $B$ and the two maps over $R$ whose composite is the specified map to $L$.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Approximation of formal polynomial solutions
entries.definition: For a Noetherian local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$ every tuple solving a finite system of polynomial equations over $R$ inside $\widehat R$ admits, for every $N\ge1$, an exact solution in $R$ with the same residues modulo $\mathfrak m^N\widehat R$.

entries.subject: local-ring
entries.name: Residue field of a local ring
entries.definition: For a local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$ the residue field is the quotient $R/\mathfrak m$. The quotient map is defined using the unique maximal ideal.
refs: Stacks 07BI · residue field of a local ring

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Local homomorphism of local rings
entries.definition: A unital map $R\to S$ of local rings is local if it sends the maximal ideal of $R$ into the maximal ideal of $S$. Equivalently the preimage of the maximal ideal of $S$ is the maximal ideal of $R$.
refs: Stacks 07BI · local homomorphism of local rings

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Regular ring map
entries.definition: A map $R\to A$ is regular if it is flat and each fibre $A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, for every $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}(R)$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Map between Noetherian rings
entries.definition: Both the source ring and the target ring are Noetherian.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Filtered colimit of smooth algebras
entries.definition: For a map $R\to A$, the $R$-algebra $A$ is isomorphic to a filtered colimit of smooth $R$-algebras.
refs: Stacks 07EP · regularity of smooth colimits with Noetherian fibres

theorems.proof: Étale morphisms are smooth. Conversely, around each target point a smooth family has a section after an étale neighbourhood, so the two families generate the same covering sieves.

theorems.subject: classical-cover
theorems.proof: Every fppf family is fpqc. For the converse in this finite-type category over a Noetherian base, every source is locally of finite type over the base, hence locally of finite type over its target. The target is locally Noetherian, so the morphism is locally of finite presentation. An fpqc covering family is flat and jointly surjective, hence fppf here.
refs: Stacks 01T8 · local finite type over the target
Stacks 01T6 · local Noetherianity of schemes locally of finite type over the base
Stacks 01TX · local finite presentation over a locally Noetherian target

theorems.subject: classical-cover
theorems.proof: Every representable restricts from a representable fpqc sheaf on the big site. The indicated full category is closed under fibre products over its objects, so the sheaf condition applies to its fpqc covering families and their overlaps. The canonical topology contains every such covering sieve.
theorems.ambient: Separated schemes of finite type over a separated Noetherian base S; see individual edge scope.
theorems.name: Fpqc topology is coarser than Canonical topology

theorems.subject: classical-cover
theorems.proof: Étale-local finite locally free refinements of fppf coverings show that each covering sieve already covers for the join of étale and finite. Restrict to the finite-type site.

theorems.subject: qcqs-cover
theorems.proof: After base change to $\operatorname{Spec}V$, a faithfully flat cover lifts the specialization from the generic point to the closed point. A valuation-ring extension dominating that lifted specialization gives the required square. For general families use an affine-local standard fpqc refinement.
refs: Stacks 0ETA · valuation lifting and comparison with fpqc and ph
theorems.ambient: The common qcqs ambient category specified in the valuative diagram.
theorems.name: Fpqc topology is coarser than Valuative (v) topology

theorems.subject: qcqs-cover
theorems.proof: Given a proper surjection, choose a point over the generic point after base change to $\operatorname{Spec}V$. Extend the valuation to the residue field of the chosen point and use the valuative criterion of properness. Zariski covers already satisfy the valuation test.
refs: Stacks 0ETA · valuation lifting and comparison with fpqc and ph
theorems.ambient: The common qcqs ambient category specified in the valuative diagram.
theorems.name: Ph topology is coarser than Valuative (v) topology

theorems.subject: qcqs-cover
theorems.proof: The valuation test can be expressed as lifting the specialization from the generic point to the closed point after base change to a valuation spectrum. Over a rank-one valuation ring, lifting that pair of points yields an extension of rank one. Thus an arbitrary-rank cover satisfies the rank-at-most-one test. See Proposition 2.1 and Corollary 2.5 of Bhatt–Mathew.
refs: Rydh, Submersions and effective descent of étale morphisms
theorems.ambient: The common qcqs ambient category specified in the valuative diagram.
theorems.name: Valuative (v) topology is coarser than Arc topology

refs: Stacks 0AG0 · regular local rings are UFDs
theorems.name: Regular local ring ⇒ Unique factorization domain

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Regularity implies Serre (R₁), and the Cohen–Macaulay local rings imply (S₂). Apply the normality criterion.
theorems.name: Regular ring ⇒ Normal ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: In the Noetherian setting finite global dimension is equivalent to finite-dimensional regularity.
refs: Stacks 00OE · finite global dimension and finite dimensional regularity
theorems.name: Regular ring ∧ Finite Krull dimension ⇔ Noetherian ring ∧ Finite global dimension

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Each prime localization is regular local and its self-module in degree zero is a dualizing complex.
theorems.name: Regular ring ⇒ Gorenstein ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The completion is regular local and is its own quotient by the empty regular sequence.
theorems.name: Regular local ring ⇒ Complete intersection local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Every prime localization is regular local, so each is a complete intersection.
theorems.name: Regular ring ⇒ Local complete intersection ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Apply the definition at the maximal ideal. Conversely the complete-intersection property localizes to every prime.
refs: Stacks 09Q3 · local and global complete intersection conditions
theorems.name: Local ring ∧ Local complete intersection ring ⇔ Complete intersection local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: A regular local ring is Gorenstein. A quotient by a regular sequence remains Gorenstein. Apply flat local descent along the completion map.
refs: Stacks 0AWX · regular local rings are Gorenstein
theorems.name: Complete intersection local ring ⇒ Gorenstein local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Each prime localization is complete intersection and hence Gorenstein, by ascent along a regular-sequence quotient and descent from completion.
theorems.name: Local complete intersection ring ⇒ Gorenstein ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: A Noetherian ring is Gorenstein of finite dimension exactly when it has finite injective dimension over itself.
refs: Stacks 0HB2 · finite injective dimension and Gorenstein rings
theorems.name: Gorenstein ring ∧ Finite Krull dimension ⇔ Noetherian ring ∧ Finite injective dimension over itself

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The local direction uses the unique maximal prime. The converse follows by localization of a dualizing complex.
refs: Stacks 0DW7 · global and local Gorenstein definitions
theorems.name: Local ring ∧ Gorenstein ring ⇔ Gorenstein local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The dualizing complex of a Gorenstein local ring is concentrated in one degree, yielding the Cohen–Macaulay property.
theorems.name: Gorenstein ring ⇒ Cohen–Macaulay ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Localize a Cohen–Macaulay local ring at each prime for the global condition. The other direction uses the maximal ideal.
theorems.name: Local ring ∧ Cohen–Macaulay ring ⇔ Cohen–Macaulay local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Polynomial algebras over the ring are Cohen–Macaulay and hence catenary. Catenarity descends to their quotients.
refs: Stacks 00NM · Cohen–Macaulay rings are universally catenary
theorems.name: Cohen–Macaulay ring ⇒ Universally catenary ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Hensel lifting converges in the maximal ideal adic topology.
refs: Stacks 04GM · complete local rings are henselian
theorems.name: Complete local ring ⇒ Henselian local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The maximal ideal is finitely generated if the ring is Noetherian. Conversely apply the Noetherianity criterion for complete local rings.
refs: Stacks 032B · finite maximal ideal in a complete local ring
theorems.name: Complete local ring ∧ Local ring with finitely generated maximal ideal ⇔ Complete local ring ∧ Noetherian ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The predicate specifies a unique maximal ideal.
refs: Stacks 032B · finite maximal ideal in a complete local ring
theorems.name: Local ring with finitely generated maximal ideal ⇒ Local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The definition requires a complete DVR with the stated uniformizer.
theorems.name: Cohen ring ⇒ Complete local ring ∧ Discrete valuation ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The henselian condition is imposed on a local ring.
refs: Stacks 04GF · henselian and strictly henselian local rings
theorems.name: Henselian local ring ⇒ Local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Finite algebras over the ring have only finitely many primes, all maximal. Their local-product decomposition is the finite-algebra criterion for henselianity.
refs: Stacks 06RS · dimension-zero local rings are henselian
theorems.name: Local ring ∧ Krull dimension at most zero ⇒ Henselian local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The maximal ideal is the Jacobson radical, which is nilpotent in an Artinian ring. The system of quotients by its powers is eventually constant.
theorems.name: Local ring ∧ Artinian ring ⇒ Complete local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: This is the definition of strictly henselian.
refs: Stacks 04GF · henselian and strictly henselian local rings
theorems.name: Henselian local ring ∧ Separably closed residue field ⇔ Strictly henselian local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The residue-field predicate is specified for the unique maximal ideal of a local ring.
theorems.name: Separably closed residue field ⇒ Local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: A normal local ring is a normal domain. Its normalization is itself, and its residue field extension is the identity.
theorems.name: Local ring ∧ Normal ring ⇒ Geometrically unibranch local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Geometric unibranchness adds a purely inseparable residue-field condition to unibranchness.
refs: Stacks 0BPZ · unibranch and geometrically unibranch local rings
theorems.name: Geometrically unibranch local ring ⇒ Unibranch local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Locality and a domain reduction are two of the defining conditions.
theorems.name: Unibranch local ring ⇒ Local ring ∧ Reduction is a domain

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The height-zero primes are included among primes of height at most one.
refs: Stacks 031P · Serre conditions for rings and modules
theorems.name: Serre condition (R₁) ⇒ Serre condition (R₀)

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The minimum of two and the local dimension is at least the minimum of one and that dimension.
refs: Stacks 031P · Serre conditions for rings and modules
theorems.name: Serre condition (S₂) ⇒ Serre condition (S₁)

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The stated Serre predicate includes the Noetherian hypothesis.
refs: Stacks 031P · Serre conditions for rings and modules
theorems.name: Serre condition (R₀) ⇒ Noetherian ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The stated Serre predicate includes the Noetherian hypothesis.
refs: Stacks 031P · Serre conditions for rings and modules
theorems.name: Serre condition (S₁) ⇒ Noetherian ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The regular ring condition covers every prime, including all primes of height at most one.
refs: Stacks 031P · Serre conditions for rings and modules
theorems.name: Regular ring ⇒ Serre condition (R₁)

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Depth equal to dimension satisfies every finite Serre depth bound.
refs: Stacks 031P · Serre conditions for rings and modules
theorems.name: Cohen–Macaulay ring ⇒ Serre condition (S₂)

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Use the associated-prime criterion for Serre (S₁) over a Noetherian ring.
theorems.name: Serre condition (S₁) ⇔ No embedded associated primes

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The two Serre conditions and the reducedness criterion are stated for Noetherian rings. The Noetherian premise appears explicitly on the reduced side.
theorems.name: Serre condition (R₀) ∧ Serre condition (S₁) ⇔ Noetherian ring ∧ Reduced ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Serre’s normality criterion applies to a Noetherian ring. The Noetherian premise appears explicitly on the normal side.
theorems.name: Serre condition (R₁) ∧ Serre condition (S₂) ⇔ Noetherian ring ∧ Normal ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: In dimension at most one the (R₁) condition covers every prime. For the converse, a regular ring is Noetherian and normal.
theorems.name: Noetherian ring ∧ Normal ring ∧ Krull dimension at most one ⇔ Regular ring ∧ Krull dimension at most one

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The ring is a finite type algebra over itself.
theorems.name: Condition J-2 ⇒ Condition J-1

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The predicate is defined for Noetherian rings and its regular locus contains a prime.
theorems.name: Condition J-0 ⇒ Noetherian ring ∧ Nonzero ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The regular-locus predicate here uses the Noetherian setting.
theorems.name: Condition J-1 ⇒ Noetherian ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The definition of a G-ring includes the Noetherian hypothesis.
theorems.name: G-ring ⇒ Noetherian ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The entire prime spectrum is the regular locus.
theorems.name: Regular ring ⇒ Condition J-1

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The entire spectrum is regular and is nonempty for a nonzero ring.
theorems.name: Regular ring ∧ Nonzero ring ⇒ Condition J-0

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The three hypotheses are the defining conditions of quasi-excellence.
theorems.name: Noetherian ring ∧ G-ring ∧ Condition J-2 ⇔ Quasi-excellent ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The two hypotheses are the defining conditions of excellence.
theorems.name: Quasi-excellent ring ∧ Universally catenary ring ⇔ Excellent ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Apply the finiteness theorem for normalization over quasi-excellent rings.
theorems.name: Quasi-excellent ring ⇒ Nagata ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: A Noetherian universally Japanese ring is Nagata by the definitions, and the converse is the Nagata theorem.
refs: Stacks 0334 · Nagata rings are universally Japanese
theorems.name: Noetherian ring ∧ Universally Japanese ring ⇔ Nagata ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The theorem on complete local Noetherian rings gives the requisite finiteness for every prime quotient and finite field extension.
refs: Stacks 032W · complete local Noetherian rings are Nagata
theorems.name: Noetherian ring ∧ Complete local ring ⇒ Nagata ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Complete local Noetherian rings are among the standard classes of excellent rings.
theorems.name: Noetherian ring ∧ Complete local ring ⇒ Excellent ring

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The presentation includes a surjection from a finite free module.
refs: J. S. Milne, A Primer of Commutative Algebra, v4.03, Definition 12.2 (the finite set of module generators in a presentation)
theorems.name: Finitely presented module ⇒ Finite module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Finite generators and relations are exactly the condition that the represented Hom functor preserve filtered colimits.
theorems.name: Finitely presented module ⇔ Maps from the module commute with filtered colimits

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A lift against a surjective map can be chosen on each basis vector.
refs: J. S. Milne, A Primer of Commutative Algebra, v4.03, §12, following Definition 12.1 (arbitrary direct sums of copies of the ring)
theorems.name: Free module ⇒ Projective module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Tensoring with a free module gives a direct sum of copies of the input. Direct sums preserve exact sequences.
refs: J. S. Milne, A Primer of Commutative Algebra, v4.03, Example 11.3 (arbitrary free modules)
theorems.name: Free module ⇒ Flat module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: If the base ring is nonzero, an infinite free basis cannot be generated by finitely many vectors with finite support. Over the zero ring the module is zero and admits the empty basis.
theorems.name: Finite module ∧ Free module ⇔ Finite free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A surjection from a free module onto a projective module splits, and a summand of a projective module is projective.
refs: J. S. Milne, A Primer of Commutative Algebra, v4.03, §12, following Definition 12.1 (free summands of arbitrary rank characterize projectives)
theorems.name: Projective module ⇔ Direct summand of a free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The first Ext group vanishes for projective modules, and its vanishing against every module splits any short exact sequence ending in the module.
theorems.name: Projective module ⇔ Module with vanishing first Ext out of it

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Projectivity implies flatness by the characterization. Equivalently, a direct summand of a flat module is flat.
refs: J. S. Milne, A Primer of Commutative Algebra, v4.03, Theorem 12.6, proof of (a) ⇒ (d), using Example 11.3 for arbitrary direct summands
theorems.name: Projective module ⇒ Flat module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: This is the finite-generation and projectivity condition together.
theorems.name: Finite module ∧ Projective module ⇔ Finite projective module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The finite-projective-module theorem identifies these two conditions.
refs: J. S. Milne, A Primer of Commutative Algebra, v4.03, Theorem 12.6(a),(d) (finite projectivity and flat finite presentation)
theorems.name: Finitely presented module ∧ Flat module ⇔ Finite projective module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Projectivity splits a finite free surjection, and a summand of a finite free module is finite projective.
refs: J. S. Milne, A Primer of Commutative Algebra, v4.03, §12, immediately before Theorem 12.6 (summands of finite free modules)
theorems.name: Finite projective module ⇔ Direct summand of a finite free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A finite projective module is finite locally free. Conversely, finite local freeness gives finite presentation and flatness.
refs: J. S. Milne, A Primer of Commutative Algebra, v4.03, Theorem 12.6(a),(c) (finite free trivializations on a principal open cover)
theorems.name: Finite projective module ⇔ Finite locally free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Use the same principal open covering and forget the fixed value of the rank.
theorems.name: Finite locally free module of a prescribed rank ⇒ Finite locally free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Use the same principal open covering and forget the finiteness of the rank.
theorems.name: Finite locally free module ⇒ Locally free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Each localization at a maximal ideal is free, hence flat.
theorems.name: Locally free module ⇒ Flat module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Lift a basis of the residue fibre. Nakayama gives a surjection, and flatness makes the lifted family a basis.
theorems.name: Module over a local ring ∧ Finite module ∧ Flat module ⇒ Finite free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Kaplansky’s theorem applies without finite-generation assumptions.
theorems.name: Module over a local ring ∧ Projective module ⇒ Free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The kernel of a finite free presentation is a submodule of a finite module over a Noetherian ring, hence finite.
theorems.name: Module over a Noetherian ring ∧ Finite module ⇒ Finitely presented module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Every submodule is finite. This is equivalent to the ascending chain condition.
theorems.name: Module over a Noetherian ring ∧ Finite module ⇒ Noetherian module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A module with the ascending chain condition has a maximal finitely generated submodule, which must be the whole module.
theorems.name: Noetherian module ⇒ Finite module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The module is a finite submodule of itself.
theorems.name: Coherent module ⇒ Finitely presented module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Every finite submodule is finitely presented over a Noetherian base.
theorems.name: Module over a Noetherian ring ∧ Finite module ⇒ Coherent module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The finite-ideal criterion for flatness is valid over any ring.
theorems.name: Flat module ⇔ Tensor injectivity for finite ideals

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The ideal criterion for flatness is valid over any ring.
theorems.name: Flat module ⇔ Tensor injectivity for all ideals

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Flatness gives vanishing of the derived functors of tensor. Conversely, the Tor exact sequence gives the injectivity of tensoring any inclusion.
theorems.name: Flat module ⇔ Module with vanishing first Tor against every module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Tensor kernels are detected after localizing at maximal ideals.
refs: J. S. Milne, A Primer of Commutative Algebra, v4.03, Corollary 11.16 (testing at every maximal ideal)
theorems.name: Flat module ⇔ Flatness at every maximal ideal

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The fibre criterion for a flat module detects faithful flatness.
theorems.name: Flat module ∧ Nonzero fibres at all maximal ideals ⇔ Faithfully flat module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The support of a finite module is the vanishing set of its annihilator.
theorems.name: Finite module ⇒ Module with closed support

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Use a prime filtration and the inclusion of the associated primes of an extension in the union of those of its terms.
theorems.name: Module over a Noetherian ring ∧ Finite module ⇒ Module with finitely many associated primes

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A simple module has the composition series consisting of a single factor.
theorems.name: Simple module ⇒ Module of finite length

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Lift finitely many generators of the quotient at each stage of the composition series.
theorems.name: Module of finite length ⇒ Finite module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Strict inclusions increase length, which is bounded by the length of the module.
theorems.name: Module of finite length ⇒ Noetherian module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Tensor multiplication by a nonzero scalar on the domain with the flat module.
theorems.name: Module over a domain ∧ Flat module ⇒ Torsion-free module over a domain

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Being a domain is part of the convention for valuation rings.
theorems.name: Module over a valuation ring ⇒ Module over a domain

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Over a valuation ring, the finite-ideal criterion reduces to injectivity of multiplication by nonzero scalars.
theorems.name: Module over a valuation ring ∧ Torsion-free module over a domain ⇒ Flat module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The characterization of projectivity yields both conditions.
theorems.name: Projective module ⇒ Mittag-Leffler module ∧ Sum of countably generated modules

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: All three conditions are hypotheses of the projectivity characterization.
theorems.name: Flat module ∧ Mittag-Leffler module ∧ Sum of countably generated modules ⇒ Projective module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A finite projective resolution is a finite projective-dimension witness. Its first two terms are finitely presented, so their cokernel is finitely presented.
theorems.name: Perfect module ⇒ Finitely presented module ∧ Module of finite projective dimension

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A finite projective resolution computes derived tensor and is bounded.
theorems.name: Module of finite projective dimension ⇒ Module of finite Tor dimension

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The specified interval is one of the bounded intervals permitted in the definition.
theorems.name: Module of Tor dimension at most d ⇒ Module of finite Tor dimension

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Apply the perfect complex criterion to the module placed in degree zero.
theorems.name: Pseudo-coherent module ∧ Module of finite Tor dimension ⇔ Perfect module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A finite projective module is its own resolution in degree zero.
theorems.name: Finite projective module ⇒ Perfect module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A bounded complex of finite projective modules is pseudo-coherent. Apply this to a finite projective resolution.
theorems.name: Perfect module ⇒ Pseudo-coherent module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A pseudo-coherent module has a resolution by finite free modules. The first two terms give a finite presentation.
theorems.name: Pseudo-coherent module ⇒ Finitely presented module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Successive syzygies over a Noetherian ring are finitely generated.
theorems.name: Module over a Noetherian ring ∧ Finite module ⇒ Pseudo-coherent module

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: A generator is a finite generating family.
theorems.name: Principal ideal ⇒ Finitely generated ideal

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: The quotient by a maximal ideal is a field, hence a domain.
theorems.name: Maximal ideal ⇒ Prime ideal

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: A domain has no nonzero nilpotent elements.
theorems.name: Prime ideal ⇒ Radical ideal

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: A single exponent killing the ideal also kills every element.
theorems.name: Nilpotent ideal ⇒ Locally nilpotent ideal

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: If generators $x_i$ satisfy $x_i^{n_i}=0$, every monomial of total degree greater than the sum of the $n_i-1$ contains one of those powers.
theorems.name: Locally nilpotent ideal ∧ Finitely generated ideal ⇒ Nilpotent ideal

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: Every ideal in a Noetherian ring is finitely generated.
theorems.name: Ideal in a Noetherian ring ⇒ Finitely generated ideal

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: The quotient flatness criterion identifies these conditions.
theorems.name: Pure ideal ⇔ Ideal satisfying the intersection-product test

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: The quotient flatness criterion also gives the condition on individual elements.
theorems.name: Pure ideal ⇔ Ideal with local unit for each element

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: The condition can also be imposed simultaneously on each finite family.
theorems.name: Pure ideal ⇔ Ideal with a common unit for each finite subset

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: Apply the common-unit condition to a generating family. The chosen element is idempotent and generates the ideal.
theorems.name: Pure ideal ∧ Finitely generated ideal ⇔ Ideal generated by an idempotent

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: An idempotent splits the quotient map. Conversely, any section of the quotient splits the ambient module into ideals generated by complementary idempotents.
theorems.name: Ideal generated by an idempotent ⇔ Ideal with projective quotient

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: On every neighbourhood where regular generators exist, the Koszul complex is a resolution.
theorems.name: Regular ideal ⇒ Koszul-regular ideal

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: The same generators satisfy the required vanishing in degree one on each neighbourhood.
theorems.name: Koszul-regular ideal ⇒ H₁-regular ideal

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: The sequence implication from first Koszul homology to quasi-regularity applies on the same neighbourhoods.
theorems.name: H₁-regular ideal ⇒ Quasi-regular ideal

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: Quasi-regular generators locally on the vanishing set, together with the unit generator on its complement, yield finite generation.
theorems.name: Quasi-regular ideal ⇒ Finitely generated ideal

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: The degree-one graded piece is free on each principal neighbourhood from the definition. The conormal module is finite locally free over the quotient.
theorems.name: Quasi-regular ideal ⇒ Ideal with finite projective conormal module

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A finite presentation supplies a finite generating family of the algebra.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite presentation ⇒ Ring map of finite type

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A finite set of module generators also generates the target as an algebra.
theorems.name: Finite ring map ⇒ Ring map of finite type

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A finite module presentation gives finite generation and a finite algebra presentation. Conversely, for a finite and finitely presented ring map apply the module restriction theorem to its target, a free module of rank one over itself.
theorems.name: Ring map with finitely presented target module ⇔ Finite ring map ∧ Ring map of finite presentation

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A finite free module has a finite presentation and its tensor functor is exact.
theorems.name: Ring map with finite free target module ⇒ Ring map with finitely presented target module ∧ Flat ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The determinant trick yields a monic equation for each element of the target.
theorems.name: Finite ring map ⇒ Integral ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Reduce powers of each finite algebra generator using its monic equation. Products of bounded powers then generate the target as a module.
theorems.name: Integral ring map ∧ Ring map of finite type ⇔ Finite ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Apply lying over to the inclusion of the source as a subring of the target.
theorems.name: Integral ring map ∧ Injective ring map ⇒ Ring map surjective on spectra

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Quotient by the chosen prime over the smaller prime and apply lying over.
theorems.name: Integral ring map ⇒ Going up for prime ideals

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The fibre is integral over a field. Every prime in such an algebra is maximal.
theorems.name: Integral ring map ⇒ Incomparability of distinct primes in each fibre

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A polynomial ring in finitely many variables over a Noetherian ring is Noetherian, so the kernel of its map onto the target is finitely generated.
theorems.name: Ring map with Noetherian source ∧ Ring map of finite type ⇒ Ring map of finite presentation

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Apply the finite-presentation theorem for flat algebras of finite type over a valuation ring.
theorems.name: Ring map with valuation-ring source ∧ Flat ring map ∧ Ring map of finite type ⇒ Ring map of finite presentation

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Being a field is part of the definition.
theorems.name: Algebra over a perfect field ⇒ Algebra over a field

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The geometric reducedness theorem over a perfect field supplies the assertion for all field extensions.
theorems.name: Algebra over a perfect field ∧ Ring map with reduced target ⇒ Geometrically reduced algebra over a field

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Use the trivial field extension to test the target.
theorems.name: Geometrically reduced algebra over a field ⇒ Algebra over a field ∧ Ring map with reduced target

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Over each extension the ring is a domain exactly when it is reduced with a nonempty irreducible spectrum.
theorems.name: Geometrically reduced algebra over a field ∧ Geometrically irreducible algebra over a field ⇔ Geometrically integral algebra over a field

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A nonempty irreducible space is connected. Apply this after every field extension.
theorems.name: Geometrically irreducible algebra over a field ⇒ Geometrically connected algebra over a field

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Normality of a ring implies reducedness. Apply this after every field extension.
theorems.name: Geometrically normal algebra over a field ⇒ Geometrically reduced algebra over a field

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Regular rings are normal. Test geometric normality after finitely generated field extensions by the equivalent criterion.
theorems.name: Geometrically regular Noetherian algebra over a field ⇒ Geometrically normal algebra over a field

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: For a flat map, surjectivity on spectra is equivalent to faithful flatness.
refs: J. S. Milne, A Primer of Commutative Algebra, v4.03, Propositions 11.18–11.19 (surjectivity on spectra for a flat map)
theorems.name: Flat ring map ∧ Ring map surjective on spectra ⇔ Faithfully flat ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The spectrum-surjectivity criterion is preserved by every base change.
theorems.name: Ring map surjective on spectra ⇔ Ring map universally surjective on spectra

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A faithfully flat map is universally injective as a module map. In particular, tensoring with the base ring shows ordinary injectivity.
refs: J. S. Milne, A Primer of Commutative Algebra, v4.03, Corollary 11.12 (injectivity and the equalizer for a faithfully flat map)
theorems.name: Faithfully flat ring map ⇒ Injective ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Localize at the given target prime. The induced flat local map is faithfully flat, hence has a surjective map on spectra.
refs: J. S. Milne, A Primer of Commutative Algebra, v4.03, Proposition 11.20 (lifting a specialization downwards along a flat homomorphism)
theorems.name: Flat ring map ⇒ Going down for prime ideals

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The faithfully flat equalizer criterion shows such an epimorphism is an isomorphism.
theorems.name: Faithfully flat ring map ∧ Epimorphism of rings ⇔ Ring isomorphism

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A finite epimorphism is surjective, and a quotient ring is generated by the image of the unit as a module.
theorems.name: Finite ring map ∧ Epimorphism of rings ⇔ Surjective ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The pushout of the two copies of the map is the tensor product of the target algebra with itself.
theorems.name: Epimorphism of rings ⇔ Tensor multiplication is an isomorphism

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A ring epimorphism has at most one prime over each source prime.
theorems.name: Epimorphism of rings ⇒ Ring map injective on spectra

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A quotient ring is of finite type and has zero relative differentials.
theorems.name: Surjective ring map ⇒ Unramified ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Finitely many generators of the kernel give a finite presentation, and relative differentials of a quotient vanish. Conversely a G-unramified map is finitely presented. For a surjection, the polynomial presentation in zero variables then has finitely generated kernel.
theorems.name: Surjective ring map with finitely generated kernel ⇔ Surjective ring map ∧ G-unramified ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Localization is an exact tensor functor.
refs: J. S. Milne, A Primer of Commutative Algebra, v4.03, Proposition 11.14 (flatness at an arbitrary multiplicative subset)
theorems.name: Localization map ⇒ Flat ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: An element invertible modulo a nilpotent ideal already is invertible, and the universal property of localization gives the unique lift.
theorems.name: Localization map ⇒ Formally étale ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A map from a localization is uniquely determined by its restriction to the original ring.
theorems.name: Localization map ⇒ Epimorphism of rings

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A principal localization has a finite presentation and is étale by the stated permanence result.
theorems.name: Principal localization map ⇒ Localization map ∧ Étale ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A finitely presented flat quotient has an idempotent-generated kernel. Conversely a localization at an idempotent is a quotient with a single relation and is flat.
theorems.name: Surjective ring map ∧ Flat ring map ∧ Ring map of finite presentation ⇔ Localization at an idempotent

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: An idempotent is one element, so its localization is principal.
theorems.name: Localization at an idempotent ⇒ Principal localization map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Finite generators and relations detect factorization and equality at a finite stage of a directed system.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite presentation ⇔ Maps from the algebra commute with directed colimits

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Tensor a finite generating family with the residue field.
theorems.name: Finite ring map ⇒ Ring map with finite-dimensional fibre algebras

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The finite-dimensional fibre criterion for a finite type map.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite type ∧ Ring map with finite-dimensional fibre algebras ⇔ Quasi-finite ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The unramified-at-a-prime criterion yields quasi-finiteness at every target prime.
theorems.name: Unramified ring map ⇒ Quasi-finite ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The invertible Jacobian minor gives the splitting of the presentation defining the naive cotangent complex.
theorems.name: Standard smooth ring map ⇒ Smooth ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Use the invertibility of the derivative and the Jacobian criterion for the localized one-variable presentation.
theorems.name: Standard étale ring map ⇒ Étale ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The naive cotangent complex is concentrated in degrees zero and one. The two homology conditions are the smoothness criterion.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite presentation ∧ Ring map with vanishing first naive cotangent homology ∧ Ring map with finite projective differentials ⇔ Smooth ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The standard smooth presentation locally on the target is syntomic.
theorems.name: Smooth ring map ⇒ Syntomic ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A Koszul-regular ideal is quasi-regular, hence finitely generated. Thus a finite polynomial presentation of a local complete intersection map is finitely presented.
theorems.name: Local complete intersection ring map ⇒ Ring map of finite presentation

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The flat local-complete-intersection criterion is equivalent to the fibre definition.
theorems.name: Flat ring map ∧ Local complete intersection ring map ⇔ Syntomic ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Finite presentation occurs in the definition of a syntomic map.
theorems.name: Syntomic ring map ⇒ Ring map of finite presentation

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The naive cotangent complex is quasi-isomorphic to zero precisely when both its homology modules vanish.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite presentation ∧ Ring map with vanishing first naive cotangent homology ∧ Ring map with vanishing differentials ⇔ Étale ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The zero module is finite projective. An étale map meets the smoothness criterion with zero differentials.
theorems.name: Étale ring map ⇒ Smooth ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The criterion requires both flatness and G-unramifiedness, hence finite presentation.
theorems.name: Flat ring map ∧ G-unramified ring map ⇔ Étale ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Étale maps are quasi-finite.
theorems.name: Étale ring map ⇒ Quasi-finite ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The condition is the conjunction of finiteness and étaleness.
theorems.name: Finite ring map ∧ Étale ring map ⇔ Finite étale ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: These are the two conditions defining unramifiedness.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite type ∧ Ring map with vanishing differentials ⇔ Unramified ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: G-unramifiedness uses finite presentation together with vanishing relative differentials.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite presentation ∧ Ring map with vanishing differentials ⇔ G-unramified ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: For a square-zero extension, the difference of two lifts is a derivation and conversely one may add any derivation to a lift.
theorems.name: Ring map with vanishing differentials ⇔ Formally unramified ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The finite presentation hypothesis is part of the equivalence between smoothness and formal smoothness.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite presentation ∧ Formally smooth ring map ⇔ Smooth ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Existence and uniqueness of square-zero lifts are exactly the two lifting conditions together.
theorems.name: Formally smooth ring map ∧ Formally unramified ring map ⇔ Formally étale ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The formal lifting criterion for étaleness requires finite presentation.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite presentation ∧ Formally étale ring map ⇔ Étale ring map
