theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(R)$ and let $P,P'$ be finite projective $R$-modules.
theorems.statement: Every homomorphism $P\to P'$ inducing an isomorphism modulo $I$ is an isomorphism. In particular an isomorphism $P/IP\cong P'/IP'$ lifts to an isomorphism $P\cong P'$.
theorems.proof: Every homomorphism $P\to P'$ inducing an isomorphism modulo $I$ is an isomorphism. In particular an isomorphism $P/IP\cong P'/IP'$ lifts to an isomorphism $P\cong P'$.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: A Zariski pair detects equality of idempotents
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I)$ be a Zariski pair.
theorems.statement: Reduction from idempotents of $A$ to idempotents of $A/I$ is injective.
theorems.proof: Reduction from idempotents of $A$ to idempotents of $A/I$ is injective.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: A Zariski pair detects certain algebra isomorphisms
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I)$ be a Zariski pair and $A\to B$ a flat integral map of finite presentation. Assume that $A/I\to B/IB$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.statement: The map $A\to B$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: The map $A\to B$ is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: A monic annihilator of a lifted idempotent
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I)$ be a Zariski pair and $B$ a finite $A$-algebra. Suppose $B/IB=B_1\times B_2$, $A/I\to B_1$ is surjective and $b\in B$ maps to $(1,0)$.
theorems.statement: There is a monic $F(T)\in A[T]$ with $F(b)=0$ and $F(T)\equiv (T-1)T^d$ modulo $I$ for some $d\geq1$.
theorems.proof: There is a monic $F(T)\in A[T]$ with $F(b)=0$ and $F(T)\equiv (T-1)T^d$ modulo $I$ for some $d\geq1$.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Jacobson localization away from a Zariski pair
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I)$ be a Zariski pair, assume $A$ is Noetherian and take $f\in I$.
theorems.statement: The localization $A_f$ is a Jacobson ring.
theorems.proof: The localization $A_f$ is a Jacobson ring.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Absolute integral closedness passes to quotients and localizations
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be an absolutely integrally closed ring.
theorems.statement: For every ideal $I$ and every multiplicative subset $S$, the rings $A/I$ and $S^{-1}A$ are absolutely integrally closed.
theorems.proof: For every ideal $I$ and every multiplicative subset $S$, the rings $A/I$ and $S^{-1}A$ are absolutely integrally closed.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Descent of absolute integral closedness from a localization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ consist of nonzerodivisors of $A$. Suppose $A$ is integrally closed in $S^{-1}A$ and $S^{-1}A$ is absolutely integrally closed.
theorems.statement: The ring $A$ is absolutely integrally closed.
theorems.proof: The ring $A$ is absolutely integrally closed.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Fraction field criterion for a normal domain
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a normal domain with fraction field $K$.
theorems.statement: The ring $A$ is absolutely integrally closed if and only if $K$ is algebraically closed.
theorems.proof: The ring $A$ is absolutely integrally closed if and only if $K$ is algebraically closed.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Embedding in an absolutely integrally closed algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be any commutative ring.
theorems.statement: There exists an embedding $A\hookrightarrow B$ into an absolutely integrally closed ring such that $B$ is free over $A$ and is a filtered colimit of finite free $A$-algebras.
theorems.proof: There exists an embedding $A\hookrightarrow B$ into an absolutely integrally closed ring such that $B$ is free over $A$ and is a filtered colimit of finite free $A$-algebras.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Localizations of absolutely integrally closed rings are strictly henselian
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be absolutely integrally closed and let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ be prime.
theorems.statement: The local ring $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is strictly henselian.
theorems.proof: The local ring $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is strictly henselian.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Henselianity in an absolutely integrally closed ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be an ideal of an absolutely integrally closed ring $A$.
theorems.statement: The pair $(A,I)$ is henselian exactly when $I\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(A)$ and reduction from idempotents of $A$ to idempotents of $A/I$ is bijective.
theorems.proof: The pair $(A,I)$ is henselian exactly when $I\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(A)$ and reduction from idempotents of $A$ to idempotents of $A/I$ is bijective.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Testing universal injectivity of a projective-module map
theorems.hypotheses: Assume every proper finitely generated ideal of $R$ has a nonzero annihilator. Let $u:N\to M$ be a homomorphism of projective $R$-modules.
theorems.statement: The map $u$ is universally injective if and only if it is injective.
theorems.proof: The map $u$ is universally injective if and only if it is injective.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Rank is invariant under a map with torsion kernel and cokernel
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a domain and let $u:M\to N$ be an $R$-linear map with torsion kernel and cokernel.
theorems.statement: Tensoring with the fraction field makes $u$ an isomorphism, so $\operatorname{rank}_R(M)=\operatorname{rank}_R(N)$.
theorems.proof: Tensoring with the fraction field makes $u$ an isomorphism, so $\operatorname{rank}_R(M)=\operatorname{rank}_R(N)$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Rank is additive in a short exact sequence
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a domain and let $0\to M_1\to M_2\to M_3\to0$ be short exact.
theorems.statement: One has $\operatorname{rank}(M_2)=\operatorname{rank}(M_1)+\operatorname{rank}(M_3)$, with cardinal addition when necessary.
theorems.proof: One has $\operatorname{rank}(M_2)=\operatorname{rank}(M_1)+\operatorname{rank}(M_3)$, with cardinal addition when necessary.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Ranks of tensor products and Hom modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M,N$ be modules over a domain $R$. For the Hom formula assume additionally that $M$ is finitely presented.
theorems.statement: The tensor rank is the cardinal product $\operatorname{rank}(M)\operatorname{rank}(N)$. For Hom the rank is the dimension of $\operatorname{Hom}_K(M\otimes_RK,N\otimes_RK)$ over the fraction field $K$, equal to $\operatorname{rank}(M)\operatorname{rank}(N)$ because $M$ has finite rank.
theorems.proof: The tensor rank is the cardinal product $\operatorname{rank}(M)\operatorname{rank}(N)$. For Hom the rank is the dimension of $\operatorname{Hom}_K(M\otimes_RK,N\otimes_RK)$ over the fraction field $K$, equal to $\operatorname{rank}(M)\operatorname{rank}(N)$ because $M$ has finite rank.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Rank under an injective extension of domains
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\hookrightarrow R'$ be an injective homomorphism of domains and $M$ an $R$-module.
theorems.statement: The rank of $M\otimes_R R'$ over $R'$ is the rank of $M$ over $R$.
theorems.proof: The rank of $M\otimes_R R'$ over $R'$ is the rank of $M$ over $R$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: A finite module is free on a nonempty principal open
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be a finite module of rank $r$ over a domain $R$.
theorems.statement: There is a map $M\to R^r$ with torsion kernel and cokernel. There is a nonzero $f\in R$ with $M_f\cong R_f^r$, and an injection $R^r\to M$ with torsion cokernel.
theorems.proof: There is a map $M\to R^r$ with torsion kernel and cokernel. There is a nonzero $f\in R$ with $M_f\cong R_f^r$, and an injection $R^r\to M$ with torsion cokernel.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Hom into a finite reflexive module is reflexive
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a Noetherian domain and let $M,N$ be finite $R$-modules with $N$ reflexive.
theorems.statement: The module $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,N)$ is reflexive.
theorems.proof: The module $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,N)$ is reflexive.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Codimension-one formula for the reflexive hull
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a Noetherian normal domain with fraction field $K$, and $M$ a finite $R$-module. Write $M_{\mathrm{tors}}$ for its torsion submodule.
theorems.statement: Inside $M\otimes_RK$, the reflexive hull is $\bigcap_{\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p=1}(M/M_{\mathrm{tors}})_{\mathfrak p}$. The intersection over an empty family is the ambient vector space.
theorems.proof: Inside $M\otimes_RK$, the reflexive hull is $\bigcap_{\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p=1}(M/M_{\mathrm{tors}})_{\mathfrak p}$. The intersection over an empty family is the ambient vector space.

theorems.subject: module-element
theorems.name: An existing content ideal is finitely generated
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be flat over $A$, let $x\in M$ and assume its content ideal $I$ exists.
theorems.statement: The ideal $I$ is finitely generated: a finite expression for $x$ in $IM$ already uses a finitely generated subideal of $I$.
theorems.proof: The ideal $I$ is finitely generated: a finite expression for $x$ in $IM$ already uses a finitely generated subideal of $I$.

theorems.subject: module-element
theorems.name: Preservation of content under an injective map on closed fibres
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be local. Let $u:M\to N$ be a homomorphism of flat modules inducing an injection $M/\mathfrak m M\to N/\mathfrak m N$, and let $x\in M$ have content $I$.
theorems.statement: The element $u(x)$ has content $I$.
theorems.proof: The element $u(x)$ has content $I$.

theorems.subject: module-element
theorems.name: Content exists in a flat Mittag–Leffler module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be a flat Mittag–Leffler module over $A$.
theorems.statement: Each $x\in M$ has a content ideal.
theorems.proof: Each $x\in M$ has a content ideal.

theorems.subject: topological-ring-map
theorems.name: Continuity test for adic ring maps
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a ring map with $R$ given the $I$-adic topology and $S$ given the $J$-adic topology.
theorems.statement: The map $\varphi$ is continuous if and only if $\varphi(I^n)\subseteq J$ for some $n\geq1$.
theorems.proof: The map $\varphi$ is continuous if and only if $\varphi(I^n)\subseteq J$ for some $n\geq1$.

theorems.subject: topological-ring-map
theorems.name: The adic formal smoothness test can take the source discrete
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be continuous for the $I$-adic topology on $R$ and the $J$-adic topology on $S$.
theorems.statement: Formal smoothness for these topologies is equivalent to formal smoothness with the discrete topology on $R$ and the $J$-adic topology on $S$.
theorems.proof: Formal smoothness for these topologies is equivalent to formal smoothness with the discrete topology on $R$ and the $J$-adic topology on $S$.

theorems.subject: topological-ring-map
theorems.name: Adic formal smoothness and completion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be continuous for the $I$-adic and $J$-adic topologies, with $I,J$ finitely generated.
theorems.statement: Formal smoothness of $R\to S$, $R\to\widehat S$, and $\widehat R\to\widehat S$ for their adic topologies are equivalent.
theorems.proof: Formal smoothness of $R\to S$, $R\to\widehat S$, and $\widehat R\to\widehat S$ for their adic topologies are equivalent.

theorems.subject: field-family
theorems.name: Extending a p-independent subset to a p-basis
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K/k$ be a field extension of characteristic $p>0$, and let $E\subseteq K$ be $p$-independent over $k$.
theorems.statement: The set $E$ is contained in a $p$-basis of $K/k$. Applying this to the empty set proves existence of a $p$-basis.
theorems.proof: The set $E$ is contained in a $p$-basis of $K/k$. Applying this to the empty set proves existence of a $p$-basis.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Tensoring with a K-flat complex preserves quasi-isomorphisms
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F^\bullet$ be K-flat over $R$ and let $u$ be a quasi-isomorphism of complexes over $R$.
theorems.statement: Tensoring $u$ with $F^\bullet$ and taking the direct-sum total complex yields a quasi-isomorphism.
theorems.proof: Tensoring $u$ with $F^\bullet$ and taking the direct-sum total complex yields a quasi-isomorphism.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: K-flatness is preserved by scalar extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be any ring homomorphism and let $F^\bullet$ be K-flat over $R$.
theorems.statement: The complex $F^\bullet\otimes_R S$ is K-flat over $S$.
theorems.proof: The complex $F^\bullet\otimes_R S$ is K-flat over $S$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: The total tensor of K-flat complexes is K-flat
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F^\bullet,G^\bullet$ be K-flat complexes over $R$.
theorems.statement: The direct-sum total complex of $F^\bullet\otimes_R G^\bullet$ is K-flat.
theorems.proof: The direct-sum total complex of $F^\bullet\otimes_R G^\bullet$ is K-flat.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: K-flatness satisfies two-out-of-three in a distinguished triangle
theorems.hypotheses: Consider a distinguished triangle of complexes in the homotopy category $K(R)$.
theorems.statement: If two of its vertices are K-flat, so is the third.
theorems.proof: If two of its vertices are K-flat, so is the third.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: K-flatness in a short exact sequence with termwise flat quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Let a short exact sequence of complexes have a quotient complex whose terms are flat modules.
theorems.statement: If two of the complexes are K-flat, so is the third.
theorems.proof: If two of the complexes are K-flat, so is the third.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Filtered colimits of K-flat complexes are K-flat
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(F_i^\bullet)$ be a filtered diagram of K-flat complexes over $R$.
theorems.statement: Its termwise colimit is K-flat.
theorems.proof: Its termwise colimit is K-flat.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: A test for K-flatness using finitely presented modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F^\bullet$ be a complex of $R$-modules. Assume that $F^\bullet\otimes_R M$ is acyclic for every finitely presented $R$-module $M$.
theorems.statement: The complex $F^\bullet$ is K-flat.
theorems.proof: The complex $F^\bullet$ is K-flat.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Termwise flat K-flat resolution
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K^\bullet$ be any complex of $R$-modules.
theorems.statement: There is a termwise surjective quasi-isomorphism $F^\bullet\to K^\bullet$ with $F^\bullet$ K-flat and each term $F^n$ flat over $R$.
theorems.proof: There is a termwise surjective quasi-isomorphism $F^\bullet\to K^\bullet$ with $F^\bullet$ K-flat and each term $F^n$ flat over $R$.

theorems.subject: algebra-pair
theorems.name: Tor independence survives flat base change
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A,B$ be Tor-independent $R$-algebras and $R\to R'$ a flat ring map.
theorems.statement: The $R'$-algebras $A\otimes_RR'$ and $B\otimes_RR'$ are Tor-independent.
theorems.proof: The $R'$-algebras $A\otimes_RR'$ and $B\otimes_RR'$ are Tor-independent.

theorems.subject: complex-interval
theorems.name: Ext criterion for bounded projective amplitude
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K\in D(R)$ and $a\leq b$.
theorems.statement: Projective amplitude in $[a,b]$ is equivalent to $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(K,N)=0$ for every module $N$ and all $i\notin[-b,-a]$. An equivalent test is that $H^n(K)=0$ for $n>b$ and $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(K,N)=0$ for all $N$ and $i>-a$. Another equivalent test is that $H^n(K)=0$ for $n\notin[a-1,b]$ and $\operatorname{Ext}^{1-a}_R(K,N)=0$ for all $N$.
theorems.proof: Projective amplitude in $[a,b]$ is equivalent to $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(K,N)=0$ for every module $N$ and all $i\notin[-b,-a]$. An equivalent test is that $H^n(K)=0$ for $n>b$ and $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(K,N)=0$ for all $N$ and $i>-a$. Another equivalent test is that $H^n(K)=0$ for $n\notin[a-1,b]$ and $\operatorname{Ext}^{1-a}_R(K,N)=0$ for all $N$.

theorems.subject: complex-interval
theorems.name: Ext criterion for bounded injective amplitude
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K\in D(R)$ and $a\leq b$.
theorems.statement: Injective amplitude in $[a,b]$ is equivalent to $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(N,K)=0$ for every module $N$ and all $i\notin[a,b]$. It suffices to test modules $N=R/J$ for all ideals $J\subset R$.
theorems.proof: Injective amplitude in $[a,b]$ is equivalent to $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(N,K)=0$ for every module $N$ and all $i\notin[a,b]$. It suffices to test modules $N=R/J$ for all ideals $J\subset R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Relative finite presentation is independent of polynomial presentation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be of finite type and let $M$ be an $A$-module.
theorems.statement: Finite presentation of $M$ over one finite polynomial algebra mapping onto $A$ is equivalent to finite presentation over each such algebra and over every finitely presented $R$-algebra mapping onto $A$. In this case $M$ is finitely presented over $A$.
theorems.proof: Finite presentation of $M$ over one finite polynomial algebra mapping onto $A$ is equivalent to finite presentation over each such algebra and over every finitely presented $R$-algebra mapping onto $A$. In this case $M$ is finitely presented over $A$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Relative pseudo-coherence is independent of polynomial presentation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be of finite type and let $K$ be a complex of $A$-modules. Fix an integer $m$.
theorems.statement: Being $m$-pseudo-coherent over one finite polynomial algebra mapping onto $A$ is equivalent to being $m$-pseudo-coherent over every such algebra. The corresponding equivalence holds for pseudo-coherence.
theorems.proof: Being $m$-pseudo-coherent over one finite polynomial algebra mapping onto $A$ is equivalent to being $m$-pseudo-coherent over every such algebra. The corresponding equivalence holds for pseudo-coherence.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite type maps from regular rings of finite dimension are perfect
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a regular ring of finite Krull dimension and $R\to A$ be of finite type.
theorems.statement: The map $R\to A$ is perfect.
theorems.proof: The map $R\to A$ is perfect.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Absolute and relative pseudo-coherence for a pseudo-coherent map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be pseudo-coherent and let $K\in D(A)$.
theorems.statement: For each $m$, being $m$-pseudo-coherent over $A$ is equivalent to being $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $R$. The corresponding equivalence holds for pseudo-coherence.
theorems.proof: For each $m$, being $m$-pseudo-coherent over $A$ is equivalent to being $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $R$. The corresponding equivalence holds for pseudo-coherence.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Flatness over a flat diagonal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a ring map whose multiplication map $B\otimes_A B\to B$ is flat and let $N$ be a $B$-module flat over $A$.
theorems.statement: The module $N$ is flat over $B$.
theorems.proof: The module $N$ is flat over $B$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Maps between weakly étale algebras are weakly étale
theorems.hypotheses: Let $B,C$ be weakly étale $A$-algebras and let $B\to C$ be an $A$-algebra map.
theorems.statement: The map $B\to C$ is weakly étale.
theorems.proof: The map $B\to C$ is weakly étale.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Weakly étale algebras over a field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field and let $A$ be a $k$-algebra.
theorems.statement: A flat multiplication map $A\otimes_k A\to A$, weak étaleness over $k$, and expression as a filtered colimit of étale $k$-algebras are equivalent. In this case all finite type $k$-subalgebras of $A$ are étale over $k$.
theorems.proof: A flat multiplication map $A\otimes_k A\to A$, weak étaleness over $k$, and expression as a filtered colimit of étale $k$-algebras are equivalent. In this case all finite type $k$-subalgebras of $A$ are étale over $k$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Integral closedness under weakly étale extension of a normal domain
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a normal domain with fraction field $K$ and $A\to B$ weakly étale.
theorems.statement: The ring $B$ is integrally closed in $B\otimes_AK$.
theorems.proof: The ring $B$ is integrally closed in $B\otimes_AK$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Integral domain extensions of henselian local rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be henselian local and let $A\to B$ be an integral ring map with $B$ a domain.
theorems.statement: The ring $B$ is local henselian. If $A$ is strictly henselian, then $B$ is strictly henselian and the residue field extension is purely inseparable.
theorems.proof: The ring $B$ is local henselian. If $A$ is strictly henselian, then $B$ is strictly henselian and the residue field extension is purely inseparable.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Local weakly étale maps out of a strictly henselian ring are isomorphisms
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a weakly étale local homomorphism of local rings and assume $A$ is strictly henselian.
theorems.statement: The map $A\to B$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: The map $A\to B$ is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Computing the numbers of branches
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a local ring with residue field $\kappa$.
theorems.statement: Having one branch is equivalent to being unibranch, and having one geometric branch is equivalent to being geometrically unibranch. If $A$ has infinitely many minimal primes, both counts are infinite. Otherwise use the normalization $B$ of $A_{\mathrm{red}}$: the ordinary count is the number of maximal ideals $\mathfrak m$ of $B$, and the geometric count is the sum of $[\kappa(\mathfrak m):\kappa]_{\mathrm{sep}}$ over those ideals, using $\infty$ for an infinite count.
theorems.proof: Having one branch is equivalent to being unibranch, and having one geometric branch is equivalent to being geometrically unibranch. If $A$ has infinitely many minimal primes, both counts are infinite. Otherwise use the normalization $B$ of $A_{\mathrm{red}}$: the ordinary count is the number of maximal ideals $\mathfrak m$ of $B$, and the geometric count is the sum of $[\kappa(\mathfrak m):\kappa]_{\mathrm{sep}}$ over those ideals, using $\infty$ for an infinite count.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Branch counts under a localized smooth map
theorems.hypotheses: Let a local homomorphism of local rings be a localization of a smooth ring map.
theorems.statement: The geometric branch counts agree. The ordinary branch counts agree if the extension of residue fields is purely inseparable.
theorems.proof: The geometric branch counts agree. The ordinary branch counts agree if the extension of residue fields is purely inseparable.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Fundamental inequality for extensions of DVRs
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\subset B$ be an extension of DVRs with fraction fields $K\subset L$ and $[L:K]<\infty$.
theorems.statement: The residue degree $f=[\kappa_B:\kappa_A]$ is finite and $ef\leq[L:K]$.
theorems.proof: The residue degree $f=[\kappa_B:\kappa_A]$ is finite and $ef\leq[L:K]$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Ramification indices in a tower of DVR extensions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\subset B\subset C$ be a tower of extensions of discrete valuation rings.
theorems.statement: The ramification index is multiplicative: $e(C/A)=e(C/B)e(B/A)$. The residue degrees satisfy the analogous formula when finite.
theorems.proof: The ramification index is multiplicative: $e(C/A)=e(C/B)e(B/A)$. The residue degrees satisfy the analogous formula when finite.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Ramification in a purely inseparable field extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\subset B$ be an extension of DVRs whose fraction fields form a purely inseparable extension in characteristic $p>0$.
theorems.statement: Its ramification index is a power of $p$.
theorems.proof: Its ramification index is a power of $p$.

theorems.subject: valued-field-extension
theorems.name: Unramified subextensions and common extensions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a DVR with fraction field $K$. Consider finite separable extensions of $K$.
theorems.statement: Every intermediate extension of an extension unramified with respect to $A$ is unramified with respect to $A$. Each unramified extension embeds in a finite Galois extension unramified with respect to $A$. Any two unramified extensions in a common algebraic closure of $K$ are contained in a common finite separable unramified extension.
theorems.proof: Every intermediate extension of an extension unramified with respect to $A$ is unramified with respect to $A$. Each unramified extension embeds in a finite Galois extension unramified with respect to $A$. Any two unramified extensions in a common algebraic closure of $K$ are contained in a common finite separable unramified extension.

theorems.subject: valued-field-extension
theorems.name: Unramified extensions compose in a tower
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a DVR with fraction field $K$, and let $M/L/K$ be a tower of finite separable extensions. Let $B$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $L$. Suppose $L/K$ is unramified with respect to $A$, and $M/L$ is unramified with respect to $B_{\mathfrak m}$ for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $B$.
theorems.statement: The extension $M/K$ is unramified with respect to $A$.
theorems.proof: The extension $M/K$ is unramified with respect to $A$.

theorems.subject: galois-prime
theorems.name: Canonical exact sequence of the inertia group
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a DVR with fraction field $K$. Let $L/K$ be finite Galois, $B$ the integral closure of $A$ in $L$, and $\mathfrak m$ a maximal ideal of $B$ with ramification index $e$ over $A$. Write $D,I$ for the decomposition and inertia groups and $p=\operatorname{char}\kappa_A$.
theorems.statement: There is a canonical exact sequence $1\to P\to I\to I_t\to1$. The subgroup $P$ is normal in $D$ and equals the subgroup of $I$ acting trivially on $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$, equivalently the subgroup of $D$ acting trivially on the whole associated graded ring. If $p>0$, $P$ is a $p$-group and $I_t$ is cyclic of order the prime-to-$p$ part of $e$. If $p=0$, $P$ is trivial and $I_t$ has order $e$. Canonically $I_t\cong\mu_e(\kappa(\mathfrak m))$. When the residue extension is separable, $P$ is also the subgroup of $D$ acting trivially on $B/\mathfrak m^2$.
theorems.proof: There is a canonical exact sequence $1\to P\to I\to I_t\to1$. The subgroup $P$ is normal in $D$ and equals the subgroup of $I$ acting trivially on $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$, equivalently the subgroup of $D$ acting trivially on the whole associated graded ring. If $p>0$, $P$ is a $p$-group and $I_t$ is cyclic of order the prime-to-$p$ part of $e$. If $p=0$, $P$ is trivial and $I_t$ has order $e$. Canonically $I_t\cong\mu_e(\kappa(\mathfrak m))$. When the residue extension is separable, $P$ is also the subgroup of $D$ acting trivially on $B/\mathfrak m^2$.

theorems.subject: ramification-solution
theorems.name: Existence of a weak solution to elimination of ramification
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\subset B$ be an extension of DVRs with fraction fields $K\subset L$. When $\operatorname{char}(\kappa_A)=p>0$, assume every element of $\bigcap_{n\geq1}\kappa_B^{p^n}$ is separable algebraic over $\kappa_A$.
theorems.statement: There is a finite extension $K_1/K$ that is a weak solution for $A\subset B$.
theorems.proof: There is a finite extension $K_1/K$ that is a weak solution for $A\subset B$.

theorems.subject: ramification-solution
theorems.name: A DVR extension requiring inseparability in every weak solution
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be perfect of characteristic $p>0$. Set $A=k[[x]]$, $K=k((x))$, and $B=A[x^{1/p}]$.
theorems.statement: Every weak solution $K_1/K$ for $A\subset B$ is inseparable, and every finite inseparable extension of $K$ is a solution.
theorems.proof: Every weak solution $K_1/K$ for $A\subset B$ is inseparable, and every finite inseparable extension of $K$ is a solution.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: The tensor inverse of an invertible module is its dual
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be an invertible $R$-module.
theorems.statement: Evaluation induces an isomorphism $M\otimes_R\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R)\cong R$.
theorems.proof: Evaluation induces an isomorphism $M\otimes_R\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R)\cong R$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Invertible modules over a UFD are trivial
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a unique factorization domain.
theorems.statement: Every invertible $R$-module is isomorphic to $R$, so $\operatorname{Pic}(R)=0$.
theorems.proof: Every invertible $R$-module is isomorphic to $R$, so $\operatorname{Pic}(R)=0$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Fundamental inequality for valuation extensions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\subset B$ be an extension of valuation rings with fraction fields $K\subset L$ and $[L:K]<\infty$.
theorems.statement: Both indices in $[\Gamma_B:\Gamma_A]\,[\kappa_B:\kappa_A]$ are finite and their product is at most $[L:K]$.
theorems.proof: Both indices in $[\Gamma_B:\Gamma_A]\,[\kappa_B:\kappa_A]$ are finite and their product is at most $[L:K]$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Localized étale algebras over valuation rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a valuation ring, $B$ an étale $A$-algebra and $\mathfrak q$ a prime of $B$ over the maximal ideal of $A$.
theorems.statement: The map $A\to B_{\mathfrak q}$ is a weakly unramified extension of valuation rings.
theorems.proof: The map $A\to B_{\mathfrak q}$ is a weakly unramified extension of valuation rings.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Henselization and strict henselization of a valuation ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a valuation ring and choose a compatible strict henselization.
theorems.statement: The maps $A\to A^h$ and $A^h\to A^{sh}$ are weakly unramified extensions of valuation rings.
theorems.proof: The maps $A\to A^h$ and $A^h\to A^{sh}$ are weakly unramified extensions of valuation rings.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Localizations of a Bézout domain
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a Bézout domain and let $S$ be a multiplicative subset of $R$ excluding zero.
theorems.statement: The localization $S^{-1}R$ is Bézout. In particular $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a valuation ring at each prime $\mathfrak p$.
theorems.proof: The localization $S^{-1}R$ is Bézout. In particular $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a valuation ring at each prime $\mathfrak p$.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: The snake lemma and the connecting map
theorems.hypotheses: Take a commutative diagram of abelian groups with exact rows $X\to Y\to Z\to0$ and $0\to U\to V\to W$ and vertical maps $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ in order.
theorems.statement: There is a canonical exact sequence $\ker\alpha\to\ker\beta\to\ker\gamma\to\operatorname{coker}\alpha\to\operatorname{coker}\beta\to\operatorname{coker}\gamma$. Its first map is injective if $X\to Y$ is injective, and its last map is surjective if $V\to W$ is surjective. The connecting map lifts into $Y$, applies $\beta$, and uses exactness at $V$ to obtain a class in $\operatorname{coker}\alpha$.
theorems.proof: There is a canonical exact sequence $\ker\alpha\to\ker\beta\to\ker\gamma\to\operatorname{coker}\alpha\to\operatorname{coker}\beta\to\operatorname{coker}\gamma$. Its first map is injective if $X\to Y$ is injective, and its last map is surjective if $V\to W$ is surjective. The connecting map lifts into $Y$, applies $\beta$, and uses exactness at $V$ to obtain a class in $\operatorname{coker}\alpha$.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Lifting a map from a finite free module through a prescribed image
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\alpha:R^n\to M$ and $\beta:N\to M$ be linear with $\alpha(R^n)\subseteq\beta(N)$.
theorems.statement: There is a linear map $\gamma:R^n\to N$ with $\beta\gamma=\alpha$. Choose a preimage under $\beta$ of the image of each basis vector.
theorems.proof: There is a linear map $\gamma:R^n\to N$ with $\beta\gamma=\alpha$. Choose a preimage under $\beta$ of the image of each basis vector.

theorems.subject: module-exact-sequence
theorems.name: Finiteness and finite presentation in a short exact sequence
theorems.hypotheses: Let $0\to L\to M\to N\to0$ be an exact sequence of $R$-modules.
theorems.statement: Finiteness of $L,N$ implies finiteness of $M$. Finite presentation of $L,N$ implies finite presentation of $M$. Finiteness of $M$ implies finiteness of $N$. Finite presentation of $M$ and finiteness of $L$ imply finite presentation of $N$. Finite presentation of $N$ and finiteness of $M$ imply finiteness of $L$.
theorems.proof: Finiteness of $L,N$ implies finiteness of $M$. Finite presentation of $L,N$ implies finite presentation of $M$. Finiteness of $M$ implies finiteness of $N$. Finite presentation of $M$ and finiteness of $L$ imply finite presentation of $N$. Finite presentation of $N$ and finiteness of $M$ imply finiteness of $L$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: A finite module has a filtration with cyclic quotients
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be a finite module over $R$.
theorems.statement: There is a finite increasing filtration $0=M_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq M_n=M$ by finitely generated submodules in which every factor $M_i/M_{i-1}$ is isomorphic to $R/I_i$ for an ideal $I_i$. Use spans of successive prefixes of a finite list of generators.
theorems.proof: There is a finite increasing filtration $0=M_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq M_n=M$ by finitely generated submodules in which every factor $M_i/M_{i-1}$ is isomorphic to $R/I_i$ for an ideal $I_i$. Use spans of successive prefixes of a finite list of generators.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Finiteness passes to an enlarged scalar ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be any ring map and $M$ an $S$-module finite over $R$.
theorems.statement: The same generators generate $M$ over $S$, so $M$ is finite over $S$.
theorems.proof: The same generators generate $M$ over $S$, so $M$ is finite over $S$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Composition and change of base ring for finiteness of algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Consider composable maps $R\to S'\to S$ of commutative rings.
theorems.statement: Finite type maps and finitely presented maps are each closed under composition. If $R\to S$ is of finite type, then $S'\to S$ is of finite type. If $R\to S$ is finitely presented and $R\to S'$ is of finite type, then $S'\to S$ is finitely presented.
theorems.proof: Finite type maps and finitely presented maps are each closed under composition. If $R\to S$ is of finite type, then $S'\to S$ is of finite type. If $R\to S$ is finitely presented and $R\to S'$ is of finite type, then $S'\to S$ is finitely presented.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Finite presentation over a finite type scalar extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ have finite type and let $M$ be an $S$-module finitely presented over $R$.
theorems.statement: Then $M$ is finitely presented over $S$. Add to an $R$-module presentation the finitely many relations describing the action of the chosen algebra generators on the chosen module generators.
theorems.proof: Then $M$ is finitely presented over $S$. Add to an $R$-module presentation the finitely many relations describing the action of the chosen algebra generators on the chosen module generators.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Restriction of scalars along finite maps preserves finiteness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be finite and let $M$ be an $S$-module.
theorems.statement: The module $M$ is finite over $R$ exactly when it is finite over $S$. Products of $R$-module generators of $S$ and $S$-module generators of $M$ generate $M$ over $R$.
theorems.proof: The module $M$ is finite over $R$ exactly when it is finite over $S$. Products of $R$-module generators of $S$ and $S$-module generators of $M$ generate $M$ over $R$.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Two Hom criteria for exactness
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $R$-linear maps $M_1\to M_2\to M_3$.
theorems.statement: The sequence $M_1\to M_2\to M_3\to0$ is exact if and only if $0\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_3,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_2,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_1,N)$ is exact for every $N$. The sequence $0\to M_1\to M_2\to M_3$ is exact if and only if $0\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(N,M_1)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(N,M_2)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(N,M_3)$ is exact for every $N$. These follow from the universal properties of cokernels and kernels.
theorems.proof: The sequence $M_1\to M_2\to M_3\to0$ is exact if and only if $0\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_3,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_2,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_1,N)$ is exact for every $N$. The sequence $0\to M_1\to M_2\to M_3$ is exact if and only if $0\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(N,M_1)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(N,M_2)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(N,M_3)$ is exact for every $N$. These follow from the universal properties of cokernels and kernels.

theorems.subject: module-pair
theorems.name: Localization of Hom with finitely presented source
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be finitely presented over $R$, let $N$ be an $R$-module, and let $S\subseteq R$ be multiplicative.
theorems.statement: There are natural isomorphisms $S^{-1}\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,N)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{S^{-1}R}(S^{-1}M,S^{-1}N)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_R(S^{-1}M,S^{-1}N)$. Apply exact localization to the kernel computed by a finite presentation of $M$.
theorems.proof: There are natural isomorphisms $S^{-1}\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,N)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{S^{-1}R}(S^{-1}M,S^{-1}N)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_R(S^{-1}M,S^{-1}N)$. Apply exact localization to the kernel computed by a finite presentation of $M$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Every module is a directed colimit of finitely presented modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be an arbitrary $R$-module.
theorems.statement: There is a directed system of finitely presented modules with colimit $M$. Start with a free presentation and use finite subsets of the generators and finitely many relations supported on those subsets.
theorems.proof: There is a directed system of finitely presented modules with colimit $M$. Start with a free presentation and use finite subsets of the generators and finitely many relations supported on those subsets.

theorems.subject: module-pair
theorems.name: Existence and uniqueness of the tensor product
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M,N$ be modules over a commutative ring $R$.
theorems.statement: There is an $R$-module $T$ with a bilinear map $g:M\times N\to T$ such that every bilinear $M\times N\to P$ factors uniquely through a linear map $T\to P$. Construct $T$ from the free module on the set $M\times N$ by imposing additivity and scalar linearity in both variables. The universal property gives a unique isomorphism respecting the universal maps between any two such pairs.
theorems.proof: There is an $R$-module $T$ with a bilinear map $g:M\times N\to T$ such that every bilinear $M\times N\to P$ factors uniquely through a linear map $T\to P$. Construct $T$ from the free module on the set $M\times N$ by imposing additivity and scalar linearity in both variables. The universal property gives a unique isomorphism respecting the universal maps between any two such pairs.

theorems.subject: module-pair
theorems.name: Symmetry, binary sums and the unit of the tensor product
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M,N,P$ be $R$-modules.
theorems.statement: The evident bilinear maps give natural isomorphisms $M\otimes_R N\simeq N\otimes_R M$, $(M\oplus N)\otimes_R P\simeq(M\otimes_R P)\oplus(N\otimes_R P)$, and $R\otimes_R M\simeq M$. For the last isomorphism the inverse is $m\mapsto 1\otimes m$.
theorems.proof: The evident bilinear maps give natural isomorphisms $M\otimes_R N\simeq N\otimes_R M$, $(M\oplus N)\otimes_R P\simeq(M\otimes_R P)\oplus(N\otimes_R P)$, and $R\otimes_R M\simeq M$. For the last isomorphism the inverse is $m\mapsto 1\otimes m$.

theorems.subject: module-index
theorems.name: A finite tensor product represents multilinear maps
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M_1,\ldots,M_r$ be $R$-modules.
theorems.statement: There is a unique representing module up to unique isomorphism: each multilinear map into a module $P$ factors uniquely through an $R$-linear map from $M_1\otimes_R\cdots\otimes_R M_r$ to $P$. The universal map sends a tuple to its pure tensor.
theorems.proof: There is a unique representing module up to unique isomorphism: each multilinear map into a module $P$ factors uniquely through an $R$-linear map from $M_1\otimes_R\cdots\otimes_R M_r$ to $P$. The universal map sends a tuple to its pure tensor.

theorems.subject: module-pair
theorems.name: Associativity of the tensor product
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M,N,P$ be $R$-modules.
theorems.statement: The canonical maps $(M\otimes_R N)\otimes_R P\to M\otimes_R N\otimes_R P\to M\otimes_R(N\otimes_R P)$ preserve pure tensors and are isomorphisms. All three parenthesizations represent the same trilinear maps.
theorems.proof: The canonical maps $(M\otimes_R N)\otimes_R P\to M\otimes_R N\otimes_R P\to M\otimes_R(N\otimes_R P)$ preserve pure tensors and are isomorphisms. All three parenthesizations represent the same trilinear maps.

theorems.subject: module-pair
theorems.name: Associativity across an intermediate bimodule
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be an $A$-module, $P$ a $B$-module and $N$ an $(A,B)$-bimodule, with $A,B$ commutative.
theorems.statement: Both $(M\otimes_A N)\otimes_B P$ and $M\otimes_A(N\otimes_B P)$ inherit the commuting scalar actions and are canonically isomorphic as bimodules. Both tensor quotients impose the same $A$-balancing and $B$-balancing relations on triples.
theorems.proof: Both $(M\otimes_A N)\otimes_B P$ and $M\otimes_A(N\otimes_B P)$ inherit the commuting scalar actions and are canonically isomorphic as bimodules. Both tensor quotients impose the same $A$-balancing and $B$-balancing relations on triples.

theorems.subject: module-pair
theorems.name: Tensor–Hom adjunction
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M,N,P$ be $R$-modules.
theorems.statement: There is a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M\otimes_R N,P)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,\operatorname{Hom}_R(N,P))$. Both Hom modules are naturally the space of bilinear maps from $M\times N$ to $P$.
theorems.proof: There is a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M\otimes_R N,P)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,\operatorname{Hom}_R(N,P))$. Both Hom modules are naturally the space of bilinear maps from $M\times N$ to $P$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Tensoring commutes with colimits of module systems
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(M_i)$ be a system indexed by a preordered set and let $N$ be an $R$-module.
theorems.statement: The canonical map $\operatorname{colim}_i(M_i\otimes_R N)\to(\operatorname{colim}_i M_i)\otimes_R N$ is an isomorphism. Tensoring is a left adjoint, so no directedness of the index preorder is required.
theorems.proof: The canonical map $\operatorname{colim}_i(M_i\otimes_R N)\to(\operatorname{colim}_i M_i)\otimes_R N$ is an isomorphism. Tensoring is a left adjoint, so no directedness of the index preorder is required.

theorems.subject: module-exact-sequence
theorems.name: Tensor product preserves right exact sequences
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M_1\to M_2\to M_3\to0$ be exact over $R$ and take any module $N$.
theorems.statement: The sequence $M_1\otimes_R N\to M_2\otimes_R N\to M_3\otimes_R N\to0$ is exact. The cokernel is a colimit, and tensoring with $N$ preserves colimits.
theorems.proof: The sequence $M_1\otimes_R N\to M_2\otimes_R N\to M_3\otimes_R N\to0$ is exact. The cokernel is a colimit, and tensoring with $N$ preserves colimits.

theorems.subject: module-pair
theorems.name: Finite generation and presentation of tensor products
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M,N$ be $R$-modules.
theorems.statement: If both modules are finite, their tensor product is finite. If both are finitely presented, the tensor product is finitely presented. Take pairwise tensors of generators and impose relations from the chosen presentations in either factor.
theorems.proof: If both modules are finite, their tensor product is finite. If both are finitely presented, the tensor product is finitely presented. Take pairwise tensors of generators and impose relations from the chosen presentations in either factor.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: The tensor model of localization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S\subseteq R$ be multiplicative and let $M$ be an $R$-module.
theorems.statement: The map $S^{-1}R\otimes_R M\to S^{-1}M$ given by $(a/s)\otimes m\mapsto am/s$ is an isomorphism of $S^{-1}R$-modules, with inverse $m/s\mapsto (1/s)\otimes m$.
theorems.proof: The map $S^{-1}R\otimes_R M\to S^{-1}M$ given by $(a/s)\otimes m\mapsto am/s$ is an isomorphism of $S^{-1}R$-modules, with inverse $m/s\mapsto (1/s)\otimes m$.

theorems.subject: module-pair
theorems.name: Localization commutes with a two-factor tensor product
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S\subseteq R$ be multiplicative and let $M,N$ be $R$-modules.
theorems.statement: There is a canonical $S^{-1}R$-linear isomorphism $S^{-1}M\otimes_{S^{-1}R}S^{-1}N\simeq S^{-1}(M\otimes_R N)$ sending $(m/s)\otimes(n/t)$ to $(m\otimes n)/(st)$.
theorems.proof: There is a canonical $S^{-1}R$-linear isomorphism $S^{-1}M\otimes_{S^{-1}R}S^{-1}N\simeq S^{-1}(M\otimes_R N)$ sending $(m/s)\otimes(n/t)$ to $(m\otimes n)/(st)$.

theorems.subject: module-index
theorems.name: Symmetric and exterior powers of a free module are free
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be free over $R$ with a chosen ordered basis, and take $n\geq0$.
theorems.statement: The symmetric power has a basis of weakly increasing words of length $n$ in the basis. The exterior power has a basis of strictly increasing words of that length. For degree zero the empty word gives the basis of $R$.
theorems.proof: The symmetric power has a basis of weakly increasing words of length $n$ in the basis. The exterior power has a basis of strictly increasing words of that length. For degree zero the empty word gives the basis of $R$.

theorems.subject: module-index
theorems.name: Presenting powers of a quotient module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M_2\to M_1\to M\to0$ be exact and let $n\geq1$.
theorems.statement: For $P=\operatorname{Sym}$ or $P=\bigwedge$, multiplication gives the left map in the exact sequence $M_2\otimes_R P^{n-1}(M_1)\to P^n(M_1)\to P^n(M)\to0$. The kernel is the degree-$n$ part of the homogeneous ideal generated by the image of $M_2$ in degree one.
theorems.proof: For $P=\operatorname{Sym}$ or $P=\bigwedge$, multiplication gives the left map in the exact sequence $M_2\otimes_R P^{n-1}(M_1)\to P^n(M_1)\to P^n(M)\to0$. The kernel is the degree-$n$ part of the homogeneous ideal generated by the image of $M_2$ in degree one.

theorems.subject: module-index
theorems.name: Presenting symmetric and exterior powers by slot relations
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(x_i)_{i\in I}$ generate $M$ and take $n\geq2$.
theorems.statement: The kernel of the tensor-to-symmetric power map is generated by differences obtained by swapping two specified slots containing generators. For the exterior power use sums of such transposed tensors and tensors with the same generator in two slots. In both statements the other slots are arbitrary module elements.
theorems.proof: The kernel of the tensor-to-symmetric power map is generated by differences obtained by swapping two specified slots containing generators. For the exterior power use sums of such transposed tensors and tensors with the same generator in two slots. In both statements the other slots are arbitrary module elements.

theorems.subject: module-index
theorems.name: Relations for exterior powers over a larger base ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a ring map, $M$ a $B$-module and $n>1$.
theorems.statement: The kernel of $M^{\otimes_A n}\to\bigwedge_B^n M$ is generated over $A$ by pure tensors with equal entries in two slots, and by differences of tensors obtained by moving a scalar $b\in B$ from one slot to another. The scalar relations impose $B$-balancing and the repeated-entry relations impose alternation.
theorems.proof: The kernel of $M^{\otimes_A n}\to\bigwedge_B^n M$ is generated over $A$ by pure tensors with equal entries in two slots, and by differences of tensors obtained by moving a scalar $b\in B$ from one slot to another. The scalar relations impose $B$-balancing and the repeated-entry relations impose alternation.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Tensor, symmetric and exterior algebras commute with directed colimits
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(M_i)$ be a directed system of $R$-modules.
theorems.statement: For the tensor, symmetric or exterior algebra functor $P$, the natural map $\operatorname{colim}_iP(M_i)\to P(\operatorname{colim}_i M_i)$ is an isomorphism. In each degree the elements and relations in a representative use finitely many stages.
theorems.proof: For the tensor, symmetric or exterior algebra functor $P$, the natural map $\operatorname{colim}_iP(M_i)\to P(\operatorname{colim}_i M_i)$ is an isomorphism. In each degree the elements and relations in a representative use finitely many stages.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Localization commutes with tensor, symmetric and exterior algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be an $R$-module and $S\subseteq R$ a multiplicative subset.
theorems.statement: For the tensor, symmetric and exterior algebras $P$, one has $S^{-1}P_R(M)\simeq P_{S^{-1}R}(S^{-1}M)$ as graded $S^{-1}R$-algebras. Localization commutes with tensor powers and the homogeneous quotients by the defining relations.
theorems.proof: For the tensor, symmetric and exterior algebras $P$, one has $S^{-1}P_R(M)\simeq P_{S^{-1}R}(S^{-1}M)$ as graded $S^{-1}R$-algebras. Localization commutes with tensor powers and the homogeneous quotients by the defining relations.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Base change preserves finiteness and finite presentation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ and $R\to R'$ be maps, let $M$ be an $S$-module and set $S'=S\otimes_R R'$ and $M'=M\otimes_R R'$.
theorems.statement: Finite generation and finite presentation of $M$ over $S$ give the respective properties of $M'$ over $S'$. Finite type and finite presentation of $R\to S$ give the respective properties of $R'\to S'$. Base-change the relevant presentation.
theorems.proof: Finite generation and finite presentation of $M$ over $S$ give the respective properties of $M'$ over $S'$. Finite type and finite presentation of $R\to S$ give the respective properties of $R'\to S'$. Base-change the relevant presentation.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Extension of scalars is left adjoint to restriction
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a ring map, $M$ an $R$-module and $N$ an $S$-module.
theorems.statement: There is a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,N_R)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_S(M\otimes_R S,N)$. An $R$-linear map extends uniquely to an $S$-linear map by $m\otimes s\mapsto sf(m)$.
theorems.proof: There is a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,N_R)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_S(M\otimes_R S,N)$. An $R$-linear map extends uniquely to an $S$-linear map by $m\otimes s\mapsto sf(m)$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Restriction of scalars is left adjoint to coextension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a ring map, $M$ an $R$-module and $N$ an $S$-module. Give $\operatorname{Hom}_R(S,M)$ its $S$-action by precomposition with multiplication on $S$.
theorems.statement: There is a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_R(N_R,M)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_S(N,\operatorname{Hom}_R(S,M))$. Send $f$ to the map $n\mapsto(s\mapsto f(sn))$. The inverse evaluates at $1$.
theorems.proof: There is a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_R(N_R,M)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_S(N,\operatorname{Hom}_R(S,M))$. Send $f$ to the map $n\mapsto(s\mapsto f(sn))$. The inverse evaluates at $1$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Tensor–Hom adjunction with two scalar rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a ring map, $M,N$ be $S$-modules and $P$ an $R$-module. Give $\operatorname{Hom}_R(N,P)$ its $S$-action by precomposition with multiplication on $N$.
theorems.statement: Currying the $S$-balanced representative gives a natural isomorphism $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M\otimes_S N,P)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_S(M,\operatorname{Hom}_R(N,P))$.
theorems.proof: Currying the $S$-balanced representative gives a natural isomorphism $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M\otimes_S N,P)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_S(M,\operatorname{Hom}_R(N,P))$.

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.name: A prime ideal containing a product contains a factor
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I,J\subseteq R$ be ideals and $\mathfrak p$ a prime with $IJ\subseteq\mathfrak p$.
theorems.statement: Either $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$ or $J\subseteq\mathfrak p$. If $a\in I\setminus\mathfrak p$, then $ab\in\mathfrak p$ for every $b\in J$, so primality forces all such $b$ into $\mathfrak p$.
theorems.proof: Either $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$ or $J\subseteq\mathfrak p$. If $a\in I\setminus\mathfrak p$, then $ab\in\mathfrak p$ for every $b\in J$, so primality forces all such $b$ into $\mathfrak p$.

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.name: Finite prime avoidance with at most two nonprime ideals
theorems.hypotheses: Let $J,I_1,\ldots,I_r$ be ideals such that $J\nsubseteq I_i$ for all $i$ and at most two $I_i$ are nonprime.
theorems.statement: There is $x\in J$ outside every $I_i$. Applied to the ideal defining the complement of an open subset, this produces a single standard open containing any given finite set of points in that open subset.
theorems.proof: There is $x\in J$ outside every $I_i$. Applied to the ideal defining the complement of an open subset, this produces a single standard open containing any given finite set of points in that open subset.

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.name: Prime avoidance for one ideal coset
theorems.hypotheses: Let $x\in R$, let $I\subseteq R$ be an ideal and let $\mathfrak p_1,\ldots,\mathfrak p_r$ be primes, none containing the entire coset $x+I$.
theorems.statement: Some $y\in I$ has $x+y\notin\mathfrak p_i$ for every $i$. The assertion concerns finitely many primes and one common representative of the coset.
theorems.proof: Some $y\in I$ has $x+y\notin\mathfrak p_i$ for every $i$. The assertion concerns finitely many primes and one common representative of the coset.

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.name: Chinese remainder theorem for pairwise comaximal ideals
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I_1,\ldots,I_r\subseteq R$ be ideals with $I_a+I_b=R$ whenever $a\ne b$. Distinct maximal ideals satisfy this condition.
theorems.statement: The intersection $I_1\cap\cdots\cap I_r$ equals their product. Reduction gives an isomorphism $R/(I_1\cdots I_r)\simeq\prod_iR/I_i$, whose kernel before quotienting is the intersection.
theorems.proof: The intersection $I_1\cap\cdots\cap I_r$ equals their product. Reduction gives an isomorphism $R/(I_1\cdots I_r)\simeq\prod_iR/I_i$, whose kernel before quotienting is the intersection.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Left inverse up to scalar and maximal minors
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be an $n\times m$ matrix with $n\geq m$ and let $J$ be its ideal of $m\times m$ minors.
theorems.statement: For $f\in J$ there exists an $m\times n$ matrix $B$ with $BA=fI_m$. Apply the adjugate identity to each maximal square submatrix and form the corresponding linear combination. Conversely $BA=fI_m$ implies $f^m\in J$ by the Cauchy–Binet formula.
theorems.proof: For $f\in J$ there exists an $m\times n$ matrix $B$ with $BA=fI_m$. Apply the adjugate identity to each maximal square submatrix and form the corresponding linear combination. Conversely $BA=fI_m$ implies $f^m\in J$ by the Cauchy–Binet formula.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Multiplication by a square-block adjugate tracks maximal minors
theorems.hypotheses: Write an $n\times m$ matrix $A$ as the vertical concatenation of a square $m\times m$ matrix $A_1$ and the remaining block $A_2$, with $n\geq m$. Put $B=\operatorname{adj}(A_1)$ and $f=\det A_1$.
theorems.statement: The top block of $AB$ is $fI_m$. Its remaining entry in row $i$, column $j$ is the determinant of the matrix obtained from $A_1$ by replacing row $j$ with row $i$ of $A$, by expansion of that determinant along the replaced row.
theorems.proof: The top block of $AB$ is $fI_m$. Its remaining entry in row $i$, column $j$ is the determinant of the matrix obtained from $A_1$ by replacing row $j$ with row $i$ of $A$, by expansion of that determinant along the replaced row.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Too few generators obstruct an injection of a finite free module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\ne0$, $n\geq1$, and let $M$ be generated by fewer than $n$ elements.
theorems.statement: Every linear map $R^n\to M$ has a nonzero kernel. Such a map lifts through a surjection $R^m\to M$ with $m<n$. The determinantal argument for the resulting $m\times n$ matrix produces a nonzero vector in its kernel by choosing a maximal nonzero minor, adjoining an extra column, and using the signed minors of that submatrix.
theorems.proof: Every linear map $R^n\to M$ has a nonzero kernel. Such a map lifts through a surjection $R^m\to M$ with $m<n$. The determinantal argument for the resulting $m\times n$ matrix produces a nonzero vector in its kernel by choosing a maximal nonzero minor, adjoining an extra column, and using the signed minors of that submatrix.

theorems.subject: module-index
theorems.name: The rank of a finite free module is unique over a nonzero ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\ne0$ and suppose that $R^n\simeq R^m$ as $R$-modules for nonnegative integers $n,m$.
theorems.statement: Then $n=m$. After tensoring with the residue field at a maximal ideal, the two vector spaces have dimensions $n$ and $m$.
theorems.proof: Then $n=m$. After tensoring with the residue field at a maximal ideal, the two vector spaces have dimensions $n$ and $m$.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Cayley–Hamilton for matrices over a commutative ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\in\operatorname{Mat}_n(R)$ and set $P(T)=\det(TI_n-A)\in R[T]$.
theorems.statement: Then $P(A)=0$. Use the adjugate identity for $TI_n-A$ and compare matrix coefficients.
theorems.proof: Then $P(A)=0$. Use the adjugate identity for $TI_n-A$ and compare matrix coefficients.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Every endomorphism of a finite module satisfies a monic polynomial
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be finite over $R$ and let $\varphi:M\to M$ be $R$-linear.
theorems.statement: There is a monic $P(T)\in R[T]$ with $P(\varphi)=0$. Lift the endomorphism to a matrix on a finite free module surjecting onto $M$ and apply Cayley–Hamilton.
theorems.proof: There is a monic $P(T)\in R[T]$ with $P(\varphi)=0$. Lift the endomorphism to a matrix on a finite free module surjecting onto $M$ and apply Cayley–Hamilton.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Determinant trick with coefficients in successive ideal powers
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\subseteq R$ and $M$ be a finite $R$-module. Assume $\varphi(M)\subseteq IM$ for an endomorphism $\varphi$ of $M$.
theorems.statement: A monic polynomial $T^n+a_1T^{n-1}+\cdots+a_n$ annihilates $\varphi$ with $a_j\in I^j$. A lift of $\varphi$ to a finite free module has matrix entries in $I$, so the characteristic coefficient of degree $n-j$ lies in $I^j$.
theorems.proof: A monic polynomial $T^n+a_1T^{n-1}+\cdots+a_n$ annihilates $\varphi$ with $a_j\in I^j$. A lift of $\varphi$ to a finite free module has matrix entries in $I$, so the characteristic coefficient of degree $n-j$ lies in $I^j$.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: A surjective endomorphism of a finite module is an isomorphism
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be finite over $R$ and let $\varphi:M\to M$ be surjective.
theorems.statement: Regard $M$ as a finite $R[T]$-module where $T$ acts by $\varphi$. Since $TM=M$, the determinantal trick gives $g(T)\in (T)$ acting as the identity. Thus multiplication by $T$ has inverse multiplication by $g(T)/T$.
theorems.proof: Regard $M$ as a finite $R[T]$-module where $T$ acts by $\varphi$. Since $TM=M$, the determinantal trick gives $g(T)\in (T)$ acting as the identity. Thus multiplication by $T$ has inverse multiplication by $g(T)/T$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Local maps between local rings reflect units
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of local rings.
theorems.statement: Locality is equivalent to $\varphi(\mathfrak m_R)\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$, to $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak m_S)=\mathfrak m_R$, and to reflection of invertibility. The nonunits in either ring form its maximal ideal, and homomorphisms preserve units.
theorems.proof: Locality is equivalent to $\varphi(\mathfrak m_R)\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$, to $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak m_S)=\mathfrak m_R$, and to reflection of invertibility. The nonunits in either ring form its maximal ideal, and homomorphisms preserve units.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Fibre and contraction tests for a point in the spectral image
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a ring map and let $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R$. Write $S_{\mathfrak p}=(R\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}S$.
theorems.statement: The point $\mathfrak p$ lies in the image if and only if $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is nonzero. Equivalent conditions are $S_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak p}\ne0$, $(S/\mathfrak pS)_{\mathfrak p}\ne0$, and $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak p S)=\mathfrak p$.
theorems.proof: The point $\mathfrak p$ lies in the image if and only if $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is nonzero. Equivalent conditions are $S_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak p}\ne0$, $(S/\mathfrak pS)_{\mathfrak p}\ne0$, and $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak p S)=\mathfrak p$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: An idempotent and its complement give a clopen partition
theorems.hypotheses: Let $e\in R$ satisfy $e^2=e$.
theorems.statement: There is a partition $\operatorname{Spec}R=D(e)\amalg D(1-e)$. Every prime contains precisely one of $e,1-e$ since their product is zero and their sum is one.
theorems.proof: There is a partition $\operatorname{Spec}R=D(e)\amalg D(1-e)$. Every prime contains precisely one of $e,1-e$ since their product is zero and their sum is one.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: The spectrum of a finite product of two rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R=R_1\times R_2$.
theorems.statement: The two projections induce a homeomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}R_1\amalg\operatorname{Spec}R_2\simeq\operatorname{Spec}R$. The two summands are cut out by the complementary idempotents $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$.
theorems.proof: The two projections induce a homeomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}R_1\amalg\operatorname{Spec}R_2\simeq\operatorname{Spec}R$. The two summands are cut out by the complementary idempotents $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$.

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.name: Finitely generated idempotent ideals cut out clopen subsets
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be finitely generated and satisfy $I^2=I$.
theorems.statement: For an idempotent $e$ generating $I$, the quotient $R/I$ is canonically $R_{1-e}$, and $V(I)=D(1-e)$ is both open and closed.
theorems.proof: For an idempotent $e$ generating $I$, the quotient $R/I$ is canonically $R_{1-e}$, and $V(I)=D(1-e)$ is both open and closed.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Closed unions of components of a ring spectrum
theorems.hypotheses: Let $T$ be a subset of $\operatorname{Spec}R$.
theorems.statement: The following are equivalent. The set $T$ is closed and a union of connected components, or $T$ is an intersection of clopen subsets, or $T=V(I)$ for an ideal $I$ generated by idempotents. Such $I$ is unique. Each connected component of a ring spectrum is an intersection of clopen neighbourhoods of a point.
theorems.proof: The following are equivalent. The set $T$ is closed and a union of connected components, or $T$ is an intersection of clopen subsets, or $T=V(I)$ for an ideal $I$ generated by idempotents. Such $I$ is unique. Each connected component of a ring spectrum is an intersection of clopen neighbourhoods of a point.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: The quotient attached to a connected component
theorems.hypotheses: Let $C$ be a connected component of $\operatorname{Spec}R$.
theorems.statement: There is an ideal $I$ generated by idempotents with $C=V(I)$ such that every idempotent of $R$ has image $0$ or $1$ in $R/I$. An idempotent cuts the full spectrum into two clopen subsets, and $C$ lies entirely in one side.
theorems.proof: There is an ideal $I$ generated by idempotents with $C=V(I)$ such that every idempotent of $R$ has image $0$ or $1$ in $R/I$. An idempotent cuts the full spectrum into two clopen subsets, and $C$ lies entirely in one side.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Local tests on a finite standard open cover of the base
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(f_1,\ldots,f_n)=R$, let $M,N,M',M''$ be $R$-modules, and let $S$ be an $R$-algebra.
theorems.statement: If the condition holds after localizing at every $f_i$, it holds globally for each of the following: vanishing of $M$, finiteness or finite presentation of $M$, isomorphism of a specified map $M\to N$, exactness of a specified short complex $0\to M''\to M\to M'\to0$, Noetherianity of $R$, and finite type or finite presentation of $S$ over $R$.
theorems.proof: If the condition holds after localizing at every $f_i$, it holds globally for each of the following: vanishing of $M$, finiteness or finite presentation of $M$, isomorphism of a specified map $M\to N$, exactness of a specified short complex $0\to M''\to M\to M'\to0$, Noetherianity of $R$, and finite type or finite presentation of $S$ over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite type and finite presentation are checked on a finite source cover
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a ring map and let $(g_1,\ldots,g_n)=S$.
theorems.statement: If all $S_{g_i}$ are finite type $R$-algebras, then $S$ is of finite type over $R$. If all are finitely presented $R$-algebras, then $S$ is finitely presented over $R$. The local algebras here come from localizing the target ring of the given map.
theorems.proof: If all $S_{g_i}$ are finite type $R$-algebras, then $S$ is of finite type over $R$. If all are finitely presented $R$-algebras, then $S$ is finitely presented over $R$. The local algebras here come from localizing the target ring of the given map.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Equalizer of localized sections on a finite standard cover
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(f_1,\ldots,f_n)=R$ and let $M$ be an $R$-module.
theorems.statement: The sequence $0\to M\to\bigoplus_iM_{f_i}\to\bigoplus_{i,j}M_{f_if_j}$ is exact. The first map localizes into each component. The second map takes the difference of restrictions on each intersection.
theorems.proof: The sequence $0\to M\to\bigoplus_iM_{f_i}\to\bigoplus_{i,j}M_{f_if_j}$ is exact. The first map localizes into each component. The second map takes the difference of restrictions on each intersection.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Equalizer of functions on a finite standard cover
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(f_1,\ldots,f_n)=R$.
theorems.statement: The ring $R$ is the equalizer of the two restriction maps $\prod_i R_{f_i}\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}R_{f_if_j}$. As a sequence of $R$-modules, the diagonal followed by the difference is exact at $R$ and the first product.
theorems.proof: The ring $R$ is the equalizer of the two restriction maps $\prod_i R_{f_i}\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}R_{f_if_j}$. As a sequence of $R$-modules, the diagonal followed by the difference is exact at $R$ and the first product.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Disjoint open decomposition gives a product of rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\operatorname{Spec}R=U\amalg V$ with $U,V$ open.
theorems.statement: There are complementary idempotents $e,1-e$ with $U=D(e)$ and $V=D(1-e)$. The natural map $R\to R_e\times R_{1-e}$ is an isomorphism. Both factors are also quotients of $R$.
theorems.proof: There are complementary idempotents $e,1-e$ with $U=D(e)$ and $V=D(1-e)$. The natural map $R\to R_e\times R_{1-e}$ is an isomorphism. Both factors are also quotients of $R$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Detecting injectivity of simultaneous localization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be an $R$-module and let $f_1,\ldots,f_n\in R$ be any finite list.
theorems.statement: The localization map $M\to\bigoplus_iM_{f_i}$ is injective exactly when the common annihilator of $f_1,\ldots,f_n$ in $M$ is zero. If a nonzero element $m$ is killed by some power of every $f_i$, take the smallest $d\geq1$ such that $(f_1,\ldots,f_n)^dm=0$. A nonzero element of $(f_1,\ldots,f_n)^{d-1}m$ lies in the common annihilator.
theorems.proof: The localization map $M\to\bigoplus_iM_{f_i}$ is injective exactly when the common annihilator of $f_1,\ldots,f_n$ in $M$ is zero. If a nonzero element $m$ is killed by some power of every $f_i$, take the smallest $d\geq1$ such that $(f_1,\ldots,f_n)^dm=0$. A nonzero element of $(f_1,\ldots,f_n)^{d-1}m$ lies in the common annihilator.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Gluing module data from finitely many standard opens
theorems.hypotheses: Take $f_1,\ldots,f_n\in R$, modules $M_i$ over $R_{f_i}$, and isomorphisms $\psi_{ij}:(M_i)_{f_j}\simeq(M_j)_{f_i}$ with $\psi_{jk}\psi_{ij}=\psi_{ik}$ on every triple overlap.
theorems.statement: Let $M$ be the submodule of $\prod_iM_i$ of tuples compatible under the $\psi_{ij}$. Each projection induces an isomorphism $M_{f_i}\simeq M_i$, and the induced transition maps agree with the original isomorphisms. This construction works for an arbitrary finite list of $f_i$.
theorems.proof: Let $M$ be the submodule of $\prod_iM_i$ of tuples compatible under the $\psi_{ij}$. Each projection induces an isomorphism $M_{f_i}\simeq M_i$, and the induced transition maps agree with the original isomorphisms. This construction works for an arbitrary finite list of $f_i$.

theorems.subject: ring-subset
theorems.name: Total fractions are invariant under inverting nonzerodivisors
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S\subseteq R$ be a multiplicative subset of nonzerodivisors.
theorems.statement: The induced map $Q(R)\to Q(S^{-1}R)$ is an isomorphism. The element $a/s$ is a nonzerodivisor in the localization exactly when $a$ is one in $R$, since every denominator acts injectively. Inverting all nonzerodivisors gives $Q(Q(R))\simeq Q(R)$.
theorems.proof: The induced map $Q(R)\to Q(S^{-1}R)$ is an isomorphism. The element $a/s$ is a nonzerodivisor in the localization exactly when $a$ is one in $R$, since every denominator acts injectively. Inverting all nonzerodivisors gives $Q(Q(R))\simeq Q(R)$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Product formula for total fractions at finitely many minimal primes
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $R$ has finitely many minimal primes $\mathfrak q_1,\ldots,\mathfrak q_t$ and its zero divisors are precisely $\bigcup_i\mathfrak q_i$.
theorems.statement: Then $Q(R)\simeq\prod_{i=1}^tR_{\mathfrak q_i}$. The primes of $Q(R)$ correspond to primes contained in the union of the minimal primes. Finite prime avoidance makes each equal to one of the minimal primes, so $Q(R)$ has finitely many primes, all maximal. Its clopen decomposition into singleton spectra yields the product formula.
theorems.proof: Then $Q(R)\simeq\prod_{i=1}^tR_{\mathfrak q_i}$. The primes of $Q(R)$ correspond to primes contained in the union of the minimal primes. Finite prime avoidance makes each equal to one of the minimal primes, so $Q(R)$ has finitely many primes, all maximal. Its clopen decomposition into singleton spectra yields the product formula.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Prime ideals identify irreducible closed subsets and components
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a ring with its Zariski prime spectrum.
theorems.statement: The closure of $\{\mathfrak p\}$ is $V(\mathfrak p)$ for every prime $\mathfrak p$. Each irreducible closed subset is of this form, and inclusion is the reverse of inclusion of prime ideals. The irreducible components are the $V(\mathfrak p)$ indexed by minimal primes.
theorems.proof: The closure of $\{\mathfrak p\}$ is $V(\mathfrak p)$ for every prime $\mathfrak p$. Each irreducible closed subset is of this form, and inclusion is the reverse of inclusion of prime ideals. The irreducible components are the $V(\mathfrak p)$ indexed by minimal primes.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: The Zariski spectrum of every commutative ring is spectral
theorems.hypotheses: Give $\operatorname{Spec}R$ its Zariski topology.
theorems.statement: The space is quasi-compact and sober. Its principal opens are quasi-compact, form a basis, and satisfy $D(f)\cap D(g)=D(fg)$. These properties give spectrality, including for the zero ring.
theorems.proof: The space is quasi-compact and sober. Its principal opens are quasi-compact, form a basis, and satisfy $D(f)\cap D(g)=D(fg)$. These properties give spectrality, including for the zero ring.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Irreducible closed subsets through a point of a ring spectrum
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R$.
theorems.statement: Irreducible closed subsets containing $\mathfrak p$ correspond to prime ideals of $R_{\mathfrak p}$. Irreducible components through $\mathfrak p$ correspond to its minimal primes. Both correspondences send a localized prime to the vanishing set of its contraction to $R$.
theorems.proof: Irreducible closed subsets containing $\mathfrak p$ correspond to prime ideals of $R_{\mathfrak p}$. Irreducible components through $\mathfrak p$ correspond to its minimal primes. Both correspondences send a localized prime to the vanishing set of its contraction to $R$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Separate a minimal prime from a quasi-compact open
theorems.hypotheses: Let $W\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R$ be quasi-compact open and let $\mathfrak p$ be a minimal prime outside $W$.
theorems.statement: Some $f\notin\mathfrak p$ satisfies $D(f)\cap W=\varnothing$. Express $W$ as finitely many $D(g_j)$ with $g_j\in\mathfrak p$. Each $g_j$ becomes nilpotent in $R_{\mathfrak p}$, so a product of the finitely many denominators killing the relevant powers provides $f$.
theorems.proof: Some $f\notin\mathfrak p$ satisfies $D(f)\cap W=\varnothing$. Express $W$ as finitely many $D(g_j)$ with $g_j\in\mathfrak p$. Each $g_j$ becomes nilpotent in $R_{\mathfrak p}$, so a product of the finitely many denominators killing the relevant powers provides $f$.

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.name: Recover an ideal inside a principal ideal from its colon
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\subseteq J$ be ideals in $R$ with $J=(a)$ principal. Write $(I:J)=\{r\in R:rJ\subseteq I\}$.
theorems.statement: Then $I=J(I:J)$. Every element of $I$ can be written $ra$ since it lies in $J$, and $ra\in I$ implies $r\in(I:J)$.
theorems.proof: Then $I=J(I:J)$. Every element of $I$ can be written $ra$ since it lies in $J$, and $ra\in I$ implies $r\in(I:J)$.

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.name: A maximal ideal outside an Oka family is prime
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal F$ be an Oka family of ideals of $R$ and let $I$ be maximal by inclusion among the ideals outside $\mathcal F$.
theorems.statement: Then $I$ is prime. If $a,b\notin I$ and $ab\in I$, then $I+(a)$ and $(I:a)$ strictly contain $I$. Maximality puts both in $\mathcal F$, so the Oka condition puts $I$ there, a contradiction. Also $I$ is proper since $R\in\mathcal F$.
theorems.proof: Then $I$ is prime. If $a,b\notin I$ and $ab\in I$, then $I+(a)$ and $(I:a)$ strictly contain $I$. Maximality puts both in $\mathcal F$, so the Oka condition puts $I$ there, a contradiction. Also $I$ is proper since $R\in\mathcal F$.

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.name: Maximal ideals avoiding a multiplicative subset are prime
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S\subseteq R$ be multiplicative, and let $I$ be maximal among ideals disjoint from $S$.
theorems.statement: Then $I$ is prime. If $a,b\notin I$ and $ab\in I$, maximality produces $s\in (I+(a))\cap S$ and $t\in(I+(b))\cap S$. Expanding the product gives $st\in I\cap S$, which is impossible.
theorems.proof: Then $I$ is prime. If $a,b\notin I$ and $ab\in I$, maximality produces $s\in (I+(a))\cap S$ and $t\in(I+(b))\cap S$. Expanding the product gives $st\in I\cap S$, which is impossible.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Cohen’s criterion for Noetherianity from prime ideals
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a commutative ring.
theorems.statement: Every ideal maximal among the ideals that are not finitely generated is prime. Consequently if each prime ideal is finitely generated, $R$ is Noetherian. Apply the prime ideal principle for the Oka family of finitely generated ideals. The union of a chain of ideals outside the family stays outside it, because finitely many generators of a union would occur together in one member.
theorems.proof: Every ideal maximal among the ideals that are not finitely generated is prime. Consequently if each prime ideal is finitely generated, $R$ is Noetherian. Apply the prime ideal principle for the Oka family of finitely generated ideals. The union of a chain of ideals outside the family stays outside it, because finitely many generators of a union would occur together in one member.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: A domain criterion using nonzerodivisors in nonzero primes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a ring.
theorems.statement: An ideal maximal among ideals without a nonzerodivisor is prime, by applying multiplicative avoidance to the set of nonzerodivisors. If $R\ne0$ and every nonzero prime contains a nonzerodivisor, every ideal disjoint from that set lies in the zero prime. In particular a principal ideal generated by a zero divisor lies in the zero ideal, so all nonzero elements are nonzerodivisors.
theorems.proof: An ideal maximal among ideals without a nonzerodivisor is prime, by applying multiplicative avoidance to the set of nonzerodivisors. If $R\ne0$ and every nonzero prime contains a nonzerodivisor, every ideal disjoint from that set lies in the zero prime. In particular a principal ideal generated by a zero divisor lies in the zero ideal, so all nonzero elements are nonzerodivisors.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Quasi-compact opens in an affine spectrum
theorems.hypotheses: Let $U$ be open in $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$. An open is retrocompact when its intersection with each quasi-compact open of $X$ is quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: The following conditions are equivalent. The open $U$ is retrocompact, $U$ is quasi-compact, $U$ is a finite union of principal opens, or $U=X\setminus V(I)$ for a finitely generated ideal $I$. Retrocompactness gives quasi-compactness by testing on $X$. The converse follows from the principal-open basis closed under finite intersection.
theorems.proof: The following conditions are equivalent. The open $U$ is retrocompact, $U$ is quasi-compact, $U$ is a finite union of principal opens, or $U=X\setminus V(I)$ for a finitely generated ideal $I$. Retrocompactness gives quasi-compactness by testing on $X$. The converse follows from the principal-open basis closed under finite intersection.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Affine spectral maps are quasi-compact and pull back constructible sets
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be induced by any ring homomorphism $\varphi:R\to S$.
