theorems.proof: The map factors through a finite projective module. Indeed a map from $M$ into a free module factors through a finite free direct summand.

theorems.subject: module-exact-sequence
theorems.name: Syzygies preserve projectivity relative to an ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $0\to N\to P\to M\to0$ be exact, $P$ projective and $M$ projective relative to an ideal $I$.
theorems.statement: Then $N$ is $I$-projective. Dimension shifting transports annihilation by $I$ of the relevant Ext groups.
theorems.proof: Then $N$ is $I$-projective. Dimension shifting transports annihilation by $I$ of the relevant Ext groups.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Dual of a finite module projective relative to an ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be finite and $I$-projective over $R$.
theorems.statement: The dual $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R)$ is $I$-projective. For $a\in I$, factor multiplication on $M$ through a finite projective and dualize the factorization.
theorems.proof: The dual $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R)$ is $I$-projective. For $a\in I$, factor multiplication on $M$ through a finite projective and dualize the factorization.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Tensor–Hom adjunction as an isomorphism of complexes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K,L,M$ be cochain complexes over $R$. Write $[X,Y]$ for the internal Hom complex and $X\otimes Y$ for the direct-sum total tensor complex over $R$.
theorems.statement: $[K,[L,M]]\cong[K\otimes L,M]$, naturally in all three complexes.
theorems.proof: $[K,[L,M]]\cong[K\otimes L,M]$, naturally in all three complexes.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Tensor–Hom adjunction on cochain maps
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K,L,M$ be cochain complexes over $R$. Write $[X,Y]$ for the internal Hom complex and $X\otimes Y$ for the direct-sum total tensor complex over $R$.
theorems.statement: Taking degree-zero cycles yields $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ch}}(K,[L,M])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ch}}(K\otimes L,M)$.
theorems.proof: Taking degree-zero cycles yields $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ch}}(K,[L,M])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ch}}(K\otimes L,M)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Composition in the internal Hom complex
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K,L,M$ be cochain complexes over $R$. Write $[X,Y]$ for the internal Hom complex and $X\otimes Y$ for the direct-sum total tensor complex over $R$.
theorems.statement: Composition gives a natural cochain map $[L,M]\otimes[K,L]\to[K,M]$.
theorems.proof: Composition gives a natural cochain map $[L,M]\otimes[K,L]\to[K,M]$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: A tensor factor acts on internal Hom
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K,L,M$ be cochain complexes over $R$. Write $[X,Y]$ for the internal Hom complex and $X\otimes Y$ for the direct-sum total tensor complex over $R$.
theorems.statement: There is a natural map $K\otimes[M,L]\to[M,K\otimes L]$.
theorems.proof: There is a natural map $K\otimes[M,L]\to[M,K\otimes L]$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: The tensor–Hom unit for complexes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K,L,M$ be cochain complexes over $R$. Write $[X,Y]$ for the internal Hom complex and $X\otimes Y$ for the direct-sum total tensor complex over $R$.
theorems.statement: The identity of $K\otimes L$ gives a natural map $K\to[L,K\otimes L]$.
theorems.proof: The identity of $K\otimes L$ gives a natural map $K\to[L,K\otimes L]$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Evaluation against a variable map of complexes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K,L,M$ be cochain complexes over $R$. Write $[X,Y]$ for the internal Hom complex and $X\otimes Y$ for the direct-sum total tensor complex over $R$.
theorems.statement: There is a natural cochain map $[L,M]\otimes K\to[[K,L],M]$, obtained by composition and evaluation with the Koszul symmetry.
theorems.proof: There is a natural cochain map $[L,M]\otimes K\to[[K,L],M]$, obtained by composition and evaluation with the Koszul symmetry.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: The symmetry sign in evaluation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K,L,M$ be cochain complexes over $R$. Write $[X,Y]$ for the internal Hom complex and $X\otimes Y$ for the direct-sum total tensor complex over $R$.
theorems.statement: On homogeneous inputs $k\in K^r$ and $u:K^r\to L^q$ the interchange sign is $(-1)^{r(q-r)}=(-1)^{r+qr}$. Evaluating $u(k)$ and then the map from $L$ to $M$ requires no further interchange.
theorems.proof: On homogeneous inputs $k\in K^r$ and $u:K^r\to L^q$ the interchange sign is $(-1)^{r(q-r)}=(-1)^{r+qr}$. Evaluating $u(k)$ and then the map from $L$ to $M$ requires no further interchange.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Derived tensor–Hom adjunction
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K,L,M\in D(R)$. Write $[X,Y]=\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_R(X,Y)$ and $X\otimes Y=X\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Y$.
theorems.statement: The natural equivalence $[K,[L,M]]\simeq[K\otimes L,M]$ induces the tensor–Hom adjunction on degree-zero cohomology.
theorems.proof: The natural equivalence $[K,[L,M]]\simeq[K\otimes L,M]$ induces the tensor–Hom adjunction on degree-zero cohomology.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Composition of derived internal Homs
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K,L,M\in D(R)$. Write $[X,Y]=\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_R(X,Y)$ and $X\otimes Y=X\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Y$.
theorems.statement: There is a natural composition $[L,M]\otimes[K,L]\to[K,M]$.
theorems.proof: There is a natural composition $[L,M]\otimes[K,L]\to[K,M]$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Derived evaluation in two variables
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K,L,M\in D(R)$. Write $[X,Y]=\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_R(X,Y)$ and $X\otimes Y=X\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Y$.
theorems.statement: There is a natural map $[L,M]\otimes K\to[[K,L],M]$.
theorems.proof: There is a natural map $[L,M]\otimes K\to[[K,L],M]$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Tensoring inside a derived Hom
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K,L,M\in D(R)$. Write $[X,Y]=\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_R(X,Y)$ and $X\otimes Y=X\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Y$.
theorems.statement: The natural morphism $K\otimes[M,L]\to[M,K\otimes L]$ is defined without a perfection hypothesis.
theorems.proof: The natural morphism $K\otimes[M,L]\to[M,K\otimes L]$ is defined without a perfection hypothesis.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Unit of derived tensor and internal Hom
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K,L,M\in D(R)$. Write $[X,Y]=\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_R(X,Y)$ and $X\otimes Y=X\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Y$.
theorems.statement: There is a natural morphism $K\to[L,K\otimes L]$.
theorems.proof: There is a natural morphism $K\to[L,K\otimes L]$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Computing derived Hom from a bounded-above projective complex
theorems.hypotheses: Let $P$ be a bounded-above cochain complex of projectives, and $L$ any complex.
theorems.statement: The ordinary internal Hom complex $[P,L]$ represents $\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_R(P,L)$.
theorems.proof: The ordinary internal Hom complex $[P,L]$ represents $\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_R(P,L)$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: A dual in the module category is the finite projective dual
theorems.hypotheses: Let $N$ be a left dual of $M$ in $R$-modules, with coevaluation $\eta$ and evaluation $\epsilon$.
theorems.statement: Both modules are finite projective. Contraction of $\eta(1)$ with a functional gives an isomorphism $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R)\to N$, under which $\epsilon$ is ordinary evaluation.
theorems.proof: Both modules are finite projective. Contraction of $\eta(1)$ with a functional gives an isomorphism $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R)\to N$, under which $\epsilon$ is ordinary evaluation.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Duals in the category of cochain complexes
theorems.hypotheses: Use the ordinary monoidal category of cochain complexes over $R$ with total tensor product.
theorems.statement: A complex has a left dual precisely when it is bounded with finite projective terms. The dual in degree $i$ is $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M^{-i},R)$ with differential $-(-1)^i(d_M^{-i-1})^\vee$. The degreewise evaluation and finite sum of the coevaluations give the duality maps.
theorems.proof: A complex has a left dual precisely when it is bounded with finite projective terms. The dual in degree $i$ is $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M^{-i},R)$ with differential $-(-1)^i(d_M^{-i-1})^\vee$. The degreewise evaluation and finite sum of the coevaluations give the duality maps.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Representing a perfect complex within its exact Tor-amplitude
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K\in D(R)$.
theorems.statement: Perfection is equivalent to pseudo-coherence and finite Tor dimension. For a perfect $K$ of Tor-amplitude in $[a,b]$ there is a representative by finite projectives concentrated in that same interval.
theorems.proof: Perfection is equivalent to pseudo-coherence and finite Tor dimension. For a perfect $K$ of Tor-amplitude in $[a,b]$ there is a representative by finite projectives concentrated in that same interval.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Two-out-of-three for perfection
theorems.hypotheses: Take a distinguished triangle in $D(R)$ with two perfect vertices.
theorems.statement: The remaining vertex is perfect.
theorems.proof: The remaining vertex is perfect.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Perfect direct summands
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $K\oplus L$ is perfect in $D(R)$.
theorems.statement: Both summands are perfect.
theorems.proof: Both summands are perfect.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Bounded complexes of perfect modules
theorems.hypotheses: Every term of a bounded complex is a perfect module.
theorems.statement: The associated derived object is perfect.
theorems.proof: The associated derived object is perfect.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Bounded perfect cohomology implies perfection
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K\in D^b(R)$ and assume all $H^i(K)$ are perfect modules.
theorems.statement: The finite truncation filtration makes the complex perfect.
theorems.proof: The finite truncation filtration makes the complex perfect.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Restriction of scalars preserves perfection along a perfect module algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $A\to B$ makes $B$ perfect as an $A$-module, and $K$ is perfect over $B$.
theorems.statement: After restriction, $K$ is perfect over $A$.
theorems.proof: After restriction, $K$ is perfect over $A$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Arbitrary derived pullback of a perfect complex
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K$ be perfect over $A$ and take any ring map $A\to B$.
theorems.statement: Then $K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B$ is perfect over $B$.
theorems.proof: Then $K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B$ is perfect over $B$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Flat pullback of a perfect module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be flat and $M$ perfect as an $A$-module.
theorems.statement: The ordinary tensor $M\otimes_A B$ is a perfect module over $B$.
theorems.proof: The ordinary tensor $M\otimes_A B$ is a perfect module over $B$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Derived tensor product preserves perfection
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K,L$ be perfect over $R$.
theorems.statement: The object $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L$ is perfect.
theorems.proof: The object $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L$ is perfect.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Perfection on a finite principal open cover
theorems.hypotheses: Elements $f_i$ generate the unit ideal and $K_{f_i}$ is perfect for every member of this finite cover.
theorems.statement: Then $K$ is perfect over $R$.
theorems.proof: Then $K$ is perfect over $R$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Faithfully flat descent of perfection
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to R'$ be faithfully flat and $K\otimes_R R'$ perfect.
theorems.statement: Then $K$ is perfect over $R$.
theorems.proof: Then $K$ is perfect over $R$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Perfect modules and complexes over a regular ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a regular ring in the Noetherian convention.
theorems.statement: An $R$-module is perfect exactly when it is finite. A complex is perfect exactly when it has bounded cohomology consisting of finite modules.
theorems.proof: An $R$-module is perfect exactly when it is finite. A complex is perfect exactly when it has bounded cohomology consisting of finite modules.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Tensor by the perfect dual computes derived Hom
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K$ be perfect in $D(A)$ and put $K^\vee=\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,A)$.
theorems.statement: The dual is perfect, the biduality map is an isomorphism, and $L\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}K^\vee\simeq\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,L)$ naturally for all $L$. In degree zero this gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(K,L)$.
theorems.proof: The dual is perfect, the biduality map is an isomorphism, and $L\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}K^\vee\simeq\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,L)$ naturally for all $L$. In degree zero this gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(K,L)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Tor-amplitude of the dual
theorems.hypotheses: A perfect complex has Tor-amplitude in $[a,b]$.
theorems.statement: Its derived dual has Tor-amplitude in $[-b,-a]$.
theorems.proof: Its derived dual has Tor-amplitude in $[-b,-a]$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Dualizing a sequential homotopy colimit of perfect complexes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K=\operatorname{hocolim}_n K_n$ for a sequence of perfect objects in $D(A)$.
theorems.statement: For any $E$, $\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,E)\simeq\mathbf R\lim_n(E\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}K_n^\vee)$.
theorems.proof: For any $E$, $\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,E)\simeq\mathbf R\lim_n(E\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}K_n^\vee)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Descent of perfect complexes and their maps to a finite stage
theorems.hypotheses: Write $R=\operatorname{colim} R_i$ as a filtered colimit.
theorems.statement: Every perfect complex over $R$ descends to a perfect complex at one stage. For $K_0,L_0$ at one stage with $K_0$ perfect, the morphisms between their derived extensions to $R$ are the filtered colimit of the corresponding morphism groups over later stages.
theorems.proof: Every perfect complex over $R$ descends to a perfect complex at one stage. For $K_0,L_0$ at one stage with $K_0$ perfect, the morphisms between their derived extensions to $R$ are the filtered colimit of the corresponding morphism groups over later stages.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Lifting an acyclic complex of reductions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal P$ consist of projective $R$-modules. Require $Q\in\mathcal P$ when $P,P\oplus Q\in\mathcal P$, and require that a map of members surjective modulo $I$ be surjective over $R$. Let $E$ be acyclic and bounded above with each term isomorphic to $P/IP$ for a member $P$.
theorems.statement: There is an acyclic bounded-above complex of members of $\mathcal P$ reducing termwise and differentially to $E$.
theorems.proof: There is an acyclic bounded-above complex of members of $\mathcal P$ reducing termwise and differentially to $E$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Lifting a chosen projective representative
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $I\subset R$, an object $K\in D(R)$ and a bounded-above complex $E$ representing $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R/I$. Let $\mathcal P$ consist of projective $R$-modules. Require $Q\in\mathcal P$ when $P,P\oplus Q\in\mathcal P$, and require that a map of members surjective modulo $I$ be surjective over $R$. Assume also closure under binary direct sums, that each $E^i$ lifts to a member, and that $K$ already has some bounded-above representative in $\mathcal P$.
theorems.statement: There is such a representative reducing to a complex isomorphic to the prescribed $E$.
theorems.proof: There is such a representative reducing to a complex isomorphic to the prescribed $E$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Lifting projective representatives through nilpotent ideals
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $I\subset R$, an object $K\in D(R)$ and a bounded-above complex $E$ representing $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R/I$. Suppose $I$ nilpotent and $E$ termwise projective over $R/I$.
theorems.statement: A bounded-above complex of projectives over $R$ represents $K$ and reduces to $E$ up to isomorphism of complexes.
theorems.proof: A bounded-above complex of projectives over $R$ represents $K$ and reduces to $E$ up to isomorphism of complexes.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Detecting pseudo-coherence after a nilpotent quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R'\to R$ be surjective with nilpotent kernel, $K'\in D(R')$ and $K=K'\otimes_{R'}^{\mathbf L}R$.
theorems.statement: Pseudo-coherence of $K$ over $R$ is equivalent to pseudo-coherence of $K'$ over $R'$.
theorems.proof: Pseudo-coherence of $K$ over $R$ is equivalent to pseudo-coherence of $K'$ over $R'$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Lifting finite stably free representatives
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $I\subset R$, an object $K\in D(R)$ and a bounded-above complex $E$ representing $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R/I$. Assume $K$ pseudo-coherent, $I\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(R)$, and $E$ termwise finite stably free.
theorems.statement: One may represent $K$ by a bounded-above complex of finite stably free modules whose reduction is isomorphic to $E$. The lifted term can be free in every degree where $E^i$ is free.
theorems.proof: One may represent $K$ by a bounded-above complex of finite stably free modules whose reduction is isomorphic to $E$. The lifted term can be free in every degree where $E^i$ is free.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Minimal free representative over a local ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K$ be pseudo-coherent over $R$ and fix a prime $\mathfrak p$. Write $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $d_j=\dim_k H^j(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}k)$. Suppose $R$ local and $\mathfrak p$ its maximal ideal.
theorems.statement: Each $d_i$ is finite and vanishes for $i\gg0$. A bounded-above complex with term $R^{d_i}$ in degree $i$ represents $K$ and is unique up to isomorphism of complexes.
theorems.proof: Each $d_i$ is finite and vanishes for $i\gg0$. A bounded-above complex with term $R^{d_i}$ in degree $i$ represents $K$ and is unique up to isomorphism of complexes.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Local finite free representative with fibre ranks
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K$ be pseudo-coherent over $R$ and fix a prime $\mathfrak p$. Write $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $d_j=\dim_k H^j(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}k)$. Assume $K$ perfect.
theorems.statement: Only finitely many $d_j$ are nonzero. Over some principal neighbourhood of $\mathfrak p$, $K$ is represented by a complex of free modules of ranks $d_j$.
theorems.proof: Only finitely many $d_j$ are nonzero. Over some principal neighbourhood of $\mathfrak p$, $K$ is represented by a complex of free modules of ranks $d_j$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Comparing perfect representatives after adding trivial complexes
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime of $R$ and two bounded finite projective complexes representing the same derived object.
theorems.statement: Over a principal neighbourhood they become isomorphic as complexes after adding, on either side, a finite direct sum of shifts of the two-term identity complex $R_f\to R_f$.
theorems.proof: Over a principal neighbourhood they become isomorphic as complexes after adding, on either side, a finite direct sum of shifts of the two-term identity complex $R_f\to R_f$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Lifting finite projective representatives along henselian pairs
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $I\subset R$, an object $K\in D(R)$ and a bounded-above complex $E$ representing $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R/I$. Assume $(R,I)$ is henselian, $K$ is pseudo-coherent and every term of $E$ is finite projective.
theorems.statement: One may lift $E$ to a bounded-above finite projective representative of $K$ with isomorphic reduction and free terms in the degrees in which $E$ is free.
theorems.proof: One may lift $E$ to a bounded-above finite projective representative of $K$ with isomorphic reduction and free terms in the degrees in which $E$ is free.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Splitting a triangle below a projective-amplitude interval
theorems.hypotheses: Let $L$ have projective amplitude in $[a,b]$.
theorems.statement: For $K$ vanishing in cohomological degrees $\ge a$, $\operatorname{Hom}(L,K)=0$. A triangle $K\to M\to L\to K[1]$ splits compatibly if $K$ vanishes in degrees $\ge a+1$, and the compatible splitting is unique under the stronger bound $\ge a$.
theorems.proof: For $K$ vanishing in cohomological degrees $\ge a$, $\operatorname{Hom}(L,K)=0$. A triangle $K\to M\to L\to K[1]$ splits compatibly if $K$ vanishes in degrees $\ge a+1$, and the compatible splitting is unique under the stronger bound $\ge a$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Splitting at a surjective cohomology base-change map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K$ be pseudo-coherent over $R$ and fix a prime $\mathfrak p$. Write $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $d_j=\dim_k H^j(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}k)$. Write $u_j$ for the natural map $H^j(K)\otimes_R k\to H^j(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}k)$. Suppose $u_i$ is onto.
theorems.statement: After passing to a principal neighbourhood, $K$ canonically splits as $\tau_{\le i}K\oplus\tau_{\ge i+1}K$ there. The upper truncation is perfect with Tor-amplitude bounded below by $i+1$.
theorems.proof: After passing to a principal neighbourhood, $K$ canonically splits as $\tau_{\le i}K\oplus\tau_{\ge i+1}K$ there. The upper truncation is perfect with Tor-amplitude bounded below by $i+1$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Splitting a single cohomology module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K$ be pseudo-coherent over $R$ and fix a prime $\mathfrak p$. Write $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $d_j=\dim_k H^j(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}k)$. Write $u_j$ for the natural map $H^j(K)\otimes_R k\to H^j(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}k)$. Suppose $u_i$ and $u_{i-1}$ are onto.
theorems.statement: On some principal neighbourhood $H^i(K)$ is finite free and $K$ splits canonically into its truncations below $i$ and above $i$ together with $H^i(K)[-i]$. The upper truncation is perfect with Tor-amplitude bounded below by $i+1$.
theorems.proof: On some principal neighbourhood $H^i(K)$ is finite free and $K$ splits canonically into its truncations below $i$ and above $i$ together with $H^i(K)[-i]$. The upper truncation is perfect with Tor-amplitude bounded below by $i+1$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Splitting across a vanishing fibre group
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K$ be pseudo-coherent over $R$ and fix a prime $\mathfrak p$. Write $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $d_j=\dim_k H^j(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}k)$. Suppose $d_i=0$.
theorems.statement: On a principal neighbourhood $K$ splits canonically as $\tau_{\le i-1}K\oplus\tau_{\ge i+1}K$. The upper truncation is perfect with Tor-amplitude bounded below by $i+1$.
theorems.proof: On a principal neighbourhood $K$ splits canonically as $\tau_{\le i-1}K\oplus\tau_{\ge i+1}K$. The upper truncation is perfect with Tor-amplitude bounded below by $i+1$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Truncation splitting from an Ext injection test
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K\in D^-(R)$, $a\in\mathbf Z$, and suppose each monomorphism of modules induces an injection under $\operatorname{Ext}^{-a}_R(K,-)$.
theorems.statement: There is a unique compatible splitting $K\simeq\tau_{\le a}K\oplus\tau_{\ge a+1}K$ and the upper part has projective amplitude in $[a+1,b]$ for some $b$.
theorems.proof: There is a unique compatible splitting $K\simeq\tau_{\le a}K\oplus\tau_{\ge a+1}K$ and the upper part has projective amplitude in $[a+1,b]$ for some $b$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Truncation splitting from Ext vanishing
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K\in D^-(R)$ and assume $\operatorname{Ext}^{-a}_R(K,N)=0$ for all $R$-modules $N$.
theorems.statement: There is a unique compatible splitting $K\simeq\tau_{\le a-1}K\oplus\tau_{\ge a+1}K$ and the upper part has projective amplitude in some $[a+1,b]$.
theorems.proof: There is a unique compatible splitting $K\simeq\tau_{\le a-1}K\oplus\tau_{\ge a+1}K$ and the upper part has projective amplitude in some $[a+1,b]$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Local perfection from boundedness and a bounded derived fibre
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K$ be pseudo-coherent over $R$ and fix a prime $\mathfrak p$. Write $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $d_j=\dim_k H^j(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}k)$. Assume $K$ bounded below and $d_i=0$ for all $i<a$.
theorems.statement: Near $\mathfrak p$ on a principal open, $K$ has a bounded finite free representative with ranks $d_i$ in degree $i$, hence is perfect there.
theorems.proof: Near $\mathfrak p$ on a principal open, $K$ has a bounded finite free representative with ranks $d_i$ in degree $i$, hence is perfect there.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Uniform residue-field criterion for Tor-amplitude
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K$ be pseudo-coherent over $R$ and fix $a\le b$.
theorems.statement: Perfection with Tor-amplitude in $[a,b]$ is equivalent to the derived fibres having cohomology only in $[a,b]$ at every prime. Checking all maximal ideals suffices.
theorems.proof: Perfection with Tor-amplitude in $[a,b]$ is equivalent to the derived fibres having cohomology only in $[a,b]$ at every prime. Checking all maximal ideals suffices.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Pointwise perfection without a uniform amplitude bound
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $K$ pseudo-coherent over $R$.
theorems.statement: Perfection of all prime localizations, perfection of all maximal localizations, and bounded-below cohomology of all individual derived fibres at primes (or only maximals) are equivalent. Global perfection implies these conditions and follows from them if $K$ is bounded below.
theorems.proof: Perfection of all prime localizations, perfection of all maximal localizations, and bounded-below cohomology of all individual derived fibres at primes (or only maximals) are equivalent. Global perfection implies these conditions and follows from them if $K$ is bounded below.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Finite-presentation Ext tests for projective amplitude
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $K$ pseudo-coherent and fix $a\le b$. In the Ext tests let $N$ range over finitely presented modules.
theorems.statement: Projective amplitude in $[a,b]$ is equivalent to perfection with this Tor-amplitude, and to $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(K,N)=0$ outside $[-b,-a]$. Equivalently require $H^{>b}(K)=0$ and Ext vanishing for $i>-a$. Another equivalent test requires $H^n(K)=0$ outside $[a-1,b]$ and $\operatorname{Ext}^{1-a}_R(K,N)=0$.
theorems.proof: Projective amplitude in $[a,b]$ is equivalent to perfection with this Tor-amplitude, and to $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(K,N)=0$ outside $[-b,-a]$. Equivalently require $H^{>b}(K)=0$ and Ext vanishing for $i>-a$. Another equivalent test requires $H^n(K)=0$ outside $[a-1,b]$ and $\operatorname{Ext}^{1-a}_R(K,N)=0$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: A fibre global-dimension bound controls absolute amplitude
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be flat with every fibre of global dimension at most $d$. Let $K$ be pseudo-coherent over $B$ and of Tor-amplitude in $[a,b]$ over $A$.
theorems.statement: The complex is perfect over $B$ with Tor-amplitude in $[a-d,b]$.
theorems.proof: The complex is perfect over $B$ with Tor-amplitude in $[a-d,b]$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Amplitude over a flat local map with regular closed fibre
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)\to B$ be flat local with regular closed fibre of dimension $d$. Suppose $K$ pseudo-coherent over $B$ and $K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}\kappa(\mathfrak m)$ has cohomology in $[a,b]$.
theorems.statement: Then $K$ is perfect over $B$ with Tor-amplitude in $[a-d,b]$.
theorems.proof: Then $K$ is perfect over $B$ with Tor-amplitude in $[a-d,b]$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Perfects are the thick subcategory generated by the unit
theorems.hypotheses: Over an arbitrary commutative ring with identity.
theorems.statement: The smallest strictly full triangulated subcategory of $D(R)$ containing $R[0]$ and closed under direct summands is precisely the perfect objects.
theorems.proof: The smallest strictly full triangulated subcategory of $D(R)$ containing $R[0]$ and closed under direct summands is precisely the perfect objects.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Commuting with countable sums implies sequential colimit continuity
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(K,-)$ commute with countable direct sums. Take a sequence of cochain complexes $L_n$ and its termwise colimit $L$.
theorems.statement: Then $\operatorname{colim}_n\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(K,L_n)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(K,L)$ is bijective.
theorems.proof: Then $\operatorname{colim}_n\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(K,L_n)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(K,L)$ is bijective.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Perfection detected modulo a nilpotent ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be nilpotent and $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R/I$ perfect over $R/I$.
theorems.statement: Then $K$ is perfect over $R$.
theorems.proof: Then $K$ is perfect over $R$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Perfection modulo a product of ideals
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K\in D(R)$ be perfect after derived restriction to each of $R/I$ and $R/J$.
theorems.statement: Its derived restriction to $R/IJ$ is perfect over $R/IJ$.
theorems.proof: Its derived restriction to $R/IJ$ is perfect over $R/IJ$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Ghost lemma
theorems.hypotheses: Let $n\ge1$, $K\in\langle R\rangle_n$, and take $n$ composable morphisms starting at $K$ which all induce zero on cohomology.
theorems.statement: Their composite vanishes in the derived category.
theorems.proof: Their composite vanishes in the derived category.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Hom vanishing over regular rings in a dimension-dependent gap
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be regular Noetherian of finite dimension $d$. Let $K,L\in D^-(R)$ with $H^i(K)=0$ for $i\le k$ and $H^i(L)=0$ for $i\ge k-d+1$.
theorems.statement: Then $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(K,L)=0$.
theorems.proof: Then $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(K,L)=0$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Truncation gap splitting over a regular ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be regular Noetherian of finite dimension $d\ge1$, $K$ perfect, and $H^i(K)=0$ for $k-d+2\le i\le k$.
theorems.statement: Then $K\simeq\tau_{\le k-d+1}K\oplus\tau_{\ge k+1}K$. When $d=1$ the gap hypothesis is empty.
theorems.proof: Then $K\simeq\tau_{\le k-d+1}K\oplus\tau_{\ge k+1}K$. When $d=1$ the gap hypothesis is empty.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Relative finite presentation across a finite extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be finite between finite type $R$-algebras, with $M$ a $B$-module.
theorems.statement: Finite presentation relative to $R$ as a $B$-module is equivalent to the same property after restriction to $A$.
theorems.proof: Finite presentation relative to $R$ as a $B$-module is equivalent to the same property after restriction to $A$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Relative finite presentation after localization
theorems.hypotheses: Over $R_f$ let $A$ be finite type, $g\in A$, and $M$ finitely presented relative to $R_f$.
theorems.statement: Then $M_g$ over $A_g$ is finitely presented relative to $R$.
theorems.proof: Then $M_g$ over $A_g$ is finitely presented relative to $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Arbitrary base change for relatively finitely presented modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be of finite type. Suppose $M$ finitely presented relative to $R$ and fix any $R\to R'$.
theorems.statement: Then $M\otimes_R R'$ over $A\otimes_R R'$ is finitely presented relative to $R'$.
theorems.proof: Then $M\otimes_R R'$ over $A\otimes_R R'$ is finitely presented relative to $R'$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Relative finite presentation under finitely presented pullback
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be of finite type. Suppose $M$ finitely presented relative to $R$ and $A\to B$ finitely presented.
theorems.statement: Then $M\otimes_A B$ over $B$ is finitely presented relative to $R$.
theorems.proof: Then $M\otimes_A B$ over $B$ is finitely presented relative to $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Composition for relative finite presentation
theorems.hypotheses: Take finite type $R\to A\to B$ with $A$ finitely presented over $R$. Let a $B$-module $M$ be finitely presented relative to $A$.
theorems.statement: Then $M$ is finitely presented relative to $R$.
theorems.proof: Then $M$ is finitely presented relative to $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Principal local criterion for relative finite presentation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be of finite type. Choose a finite principal cover of $\operatorname{Spec}A$.
theorems.statement: An $A$-module is finitely presented relative to $R$ exactly when all restrictions to those opens are finitely presented relative to $R$.
theorems.proof: An $A$-module is finitely presented relative to $R$ exactly when all restrictions to those opens are finitely presented relative to $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Relative presentation in an exact sequence
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be of finite type. Take a short exact sequence $0\to L\to M\to N\to0$ of $A$-modules.
theorems.statement: Relative finite presentation of $L,N$ gives it for $M$. Relative finite presentation of $M$ and finite generation of $L$ over $A$ give relative finite presentation of $N$.
theorems.proof: Relative finite presentation of $L,N$ gives it for $M$. Relative finite presentation of $M$ and finite generation of $L$ over $A$ give relative finite presentation of $N$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Relative finite presentation passes to summands
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be of finite type. Suppose $M\oplus N$ is finitely presented relative to $R$.
theorems.statement: Both $M$ and $N$ are finitely presented relative to $R$.
theorems.proof: Both $M$ and $N$ are finitely presented relative to $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Derived self-intersection of the zero section
theorems.hypotheses: Regard $K\in D(R)$ as an $R[x]$-complex via $x\mapsto0$.
theorems.statement: Then $K\otimes_{R[x]}^{\mathbf L}R\simeq K\oplus K[1]$, by the two-term resolution for $x$.
theorems.proof: Then $K\otimes_{R[x]}^{\mathbf L}R\simeq K\oplus K[1]$, by the two-term resolution for $x$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Pseudo-coherence after adjoining a variable acting by zero
theorems.hypotheses: Regard an $R$-complex as an $R[x]$-complex by $x\mapsto0$ and fix $m$.
theorems.statement: It is $m$-pseudo-coherent over $R$ exactly when it is $m$-pseudo-coherent over $R[x]$.
theorems.proof: It is $m$-pseudo-coherent over $R$ exactly when it is $m$-pseudo-coherent over $R[x]$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Relative pseudo-coherence across finite extensions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be finite between finite type $R$-algebras and $K\in D(B)$. Use either $m$-pseudo-coherence at a fixed integer $m$ or pseudo-coherence in every degree.
theorems.statement: Either condition relative to $R$ is invariant under restriction from $B$ to $A$.
theorems.proof: Either condition relative to $R$ is invariant under restriction from $B$ to $A$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Relative pseudo-coherence in distinguished triangles
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be of finite type. Take a triangle $K\to L\to M\to K[1]$ in $D(A)$. All bounds are relative to $R$.
theorems.statement: Writing $X_j$ for $j$-pseudo-coherence of $X$, one has $K_{m+1}\land L_m\Rightarrow M_m$, $K_m\land M_m\Rightarrow L_m$ and $L_{m+1}\land M_m\Rightarrow K_{m+1}$. In all degrees this gives two-out-of-three.
theorems.proof: Writing $X_j$ for $j$-pseudo-coherence of $X$, one has $K_{m+1}\land L_m\Rightarrow M_m$, $K_m\land M_m\Rightarrow L_m$ and $L_{m+1}\land M_m\Rightarrow K_{m+1}$. In all degrees this gives two-out-of-three.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Relative finite-type and finite-presentation thresholds
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be of finite type. Fix an $A$-module $M$ and any finite polynomial algebra $P$ over $R$ surjecting onto $A$.
theorems.statement: The relative bounds $0,-1$ mean respectively finite generation over $A$ and finite presentation relative to $R$. Bound $-d$ for $d\ge0$ means a finite free $P$-resolution through term $d$, with no injectivity at its left endpoint. Relative pseudo-coherence means an entire resolution by finite free $P$-modules. These criteria work for every such $P$.
theorems.proof: The relative bounds $0,-1$ mean respectively finite generation over $A$ and finite presentation relative to $R$. Bound $-d$ for $d\ge0$ means a finite free $P$-resolution through term $d$, with no injectivity at its left endpoint. Relative pseudo-coherence means an entire resolution by finite free $P$-modules. These criteria work for every such $P$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Relative pseudo-coherence passes to direct summands
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be of finite type. Use either $m$-pseudo-coherence at a fixed integer $m$ or pseudo-coherence in every degree. Suppose $K\oplus L$ has the chosen condition relative to $R$.
theorems.statement: Each summand has that same relative condition.
theorems.proof: Each summand has that same relative condition.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Termwise relative pseudo-coherence for a bounded-above complex
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be of finite type. Let $K$ be a bounded-above complex, with term $K^i$ relatively $(m-i)$-pseudo-coherent for each $i$.
theorems.statement: Then $K$ is relatively $m$-pseudo-coherent. If all terms are relatively pseudo-coherent then so is the complex.
theorems.proof: Then $K$ is relatively $m$-pseudo-coherent. If all terms are relatively pseudo-coherent then so is the complex.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Relative pseudo-coherence from the cohomology modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be of finite type. Let $K\in D^-(A)$ with $H^i(K)$ relatively $(m-i)$-pseudo-coherent for every $i$.
theorems.statement: Then $K$ is relatively $m$-pseudo-coherent. Relative pseudo-coherence of all the cohomology modules gives relative pseudo-coherence of $K$.
theorems.proof: Then $K$ is relatively $m$-pseudo-coherent. Relative pseudo-coherence of all the cohomology modules gives relative pseudo-coherence of $K$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Localizing relative pseudo-coherence
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R_f\to A$ be finite type and $g\in A$. Use either $m$-pseudo-coherence at a fixed integer $m$ or pseudo-coherence in every degree. Let $K$ have the chosen property relative to $R_f$.
theorems.statement: Then $K_g$ has the same property over $A_g$ relative to $R$.
theorems.proof: Then $K_g$ has the same property over $A_g$ relative to $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Tor-independent base change for relative pseudo-coherence
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be of finite type. Suppose $A$ and $R'$ are Tor-independent over $R$ and $A'=A\otimes_R R'$. Use either $m$-pseudo-coherence at a fixed integer $m$ or pseudo-coherence in every degree.
theorems.statement: If $K$ has the relative property over $R$, $K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'$ has it over $R'$.
theorems.proof: If $K$ has the relative property over $R$, $K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'$ has it over $R'$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Derived pullback through a pseudo-coherent algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A\to B$ be finite type and $B$ pseudo-coherent relative to $A$. Use either $m$-pseudo-coherence at a fixed integer $m$ or pseudo-coherence in every degree.
theorems.statement: If $K\in D(A)$ has the chosen property relative to $R$, its derived pullback to $B$ retains it relative to $R$.
theorems.proof: If $K\in D(A)$ has the chosen property relative to $R$, its derived pullback to $B$ retains it relative to $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Flat pullback of relatively pseudo-coherent modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A\to B$ be finite type, $B$ flat over $A$ and pseudo-coherent relative to $A$. Use either $m$-pseudo-coherence at a fixed integer $m$ or pseudo-coherence in every degree.
theorems.statement: For an $A$-module $M$ with the relative condition over $R$, $M\otimes_A B$ has that condition relative to $R$.
theorems.proof: For an $A$-module $M$ with the relative condition over $R$, $M\otimes_A B$ has that condition relative to $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Changing the relative base through a pseudo-coherent algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Take $A\to B$ between finite type $R$-algebras with $A$ pseudo-coherent relative to $R$. Use either $m$-pseudo-coherence at a fixed integer $m$ or pseudo-coherence in every degree.
theorems.statement: For $K\in D(B)$ the chosen property relative to $A$ is equivalent to the property relative to $R$.
theorems.proof: For $K\in D(B)$ the chosen property relative to $A$ is equivalent to the property relative to $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Principal cover test for relative pseudo-coherence
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be of finite type. Fix a finite principal cover of $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Use either $m$-pseudo-coherence at a fixed integer $m$ or pseudo-coherence in every degree.
theorems.statement: An $A$-complex has the chosen condition relative to $R$ precisely when it has it on every member of the cover.
theorems.proof: An $A$-complex has the chosen condition relative to $R$ precisely when it has it on every member of the cover.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Relative pseudo-coherence over a Noetherian base
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be of finite type. Assume $R$ Noetherian.
theorems.statement: Relative $m$-pseudo-coherence means $K\in D^-(A)$ with finite $H^i(K)$ for $i\ge m$. Relative pseudo-coherence means bounded above with all cohomologies finite. For modules in degree zero the latter means finite generation over $A$.
theorems.proof: Relative $m$-pseudo-coherence means $K\in D^-(A)$ with finite $H^i(K)$ for $i\ge m$. Relative pseudo-coherence means bounded above with all cohomologies finite. For modules in degree zero the latter means finite generation over $A$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Pseudo-coherence across flat presentations and a quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Take $R\to B\to A$ with $B\to A$ surjective and both $A,B$ flat and finitely presented over $R$. Use either $m$-pseudo-coherence at a fixed integer $m$ or pseudo-coherence in every degree.
theorems.statement: For $K\in D(A)$, the absolute property over $A$, the properties relative to $R$ and $A$, the absolute property of its restriction over $B$, and the property of that restriction relative to $R$ are equivalent.
theorems.proof: For $K\in D(A)$, the absolute property over $A$, the properties relative to $R$ and $A$, the absolute property of its restriction over $B$, and the property of that restriction relative to $R$ are equivalent.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Relative perfect complexes form a thick subcategory
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be flat of finite presentation.
theorems.statement: In $D(A)$ the $R$-perfect objects form a strictly full triangulated subcategory closed under summands.
theorems.proof: In $D(A)$ the $R$-perfect objects form a strictly full triangulated subcategory closed under summands.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Absolute perfect complexes act on relatively perfect ones
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be flat of finite presentation.
theorems.statement: Every perfect $A$-complex is $R$-perfect. Tensoring an $R$-perfect object over $A$ with a perfect $A$-complex preserves $R$-perfection.
theorems.proof: Every perfect $A$-complex is $R$-perfect. Tensoring an $R$-perfect object over $A$ with a perfect $A$-complex preserves $R$-perfection.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Bounded flat representatives for relative perfection
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be flat of finite presentation.
theorems.statement: An object of $D(A)$ is $R$-perfect exactly when represented by a bounded complex of finitely presented $A$-modules flat over $R$.
theorems.proof: An object of $D(A)$ is $R$-perfect exactly when represented by a bounded complex of finitely presented $A$-modules flat over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Arbitrary base change for relative perfection
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be flat of finite presentation. Let $K$ be $R$-perfect and $A'=A\otimes_R R'$ for any $R$-algebra $R'$.
theorems.statement: Then $K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'$ is $R'$-perfect.
theorems.proof: Then $K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'$ is $R'$-perfect.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: A flat model for derived Hom and arbitrary base change
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be flat over $R$, $K\in D(A)$ pseudo-coherent and $L$ of finite Tor dimension over $R$.
theorems.statement: Choose a bounded-above finite free $A$-model $P$ for $K$ and a bounded $R$-flat $A$-model $F$ for $L$. Their Hom complex is bounded below, $R$-flat termwise, and computes derived Hom. Its ordinary tensor with any $R'$ computes derived Hom over $A\otimes_R R'$ between the derived pullbacks. When $A/R$ is finitely presented and $L$ relatively perfect, $F$ and the Hom complex can have finitely presented $A$-terms.
theorems.proof: Choose a bounded-above finite free $A$-model $P$ for $K$ and a bounded $R$-flat $A$-model $F$ for $L$. Their Hom complex is bounded below, $R$-flat termwise, and computes derived Hom. Its ordinary tensor with any $R'$ computes derived Hom over $A\otimes_R R'$ between the derived pullbacks. When $A/R$ is finitely presented and $L$ relatively perfect, $F$ and the Hom complex can have finitely presented $A$-terms.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Descent of relatively perfect complexes along filtered colimits
theorems.hypotheses: Base change a flat finitely presented $R_0$-algebra $A_0$ to a filtered system of rings $R_i$ and its colimit $R$.
theorems.statement: Every relatively perfect object at the limit descends to one stage. For $K_0$ pseudo-coherent and $L_0$ of finite Tor dimension over $R_0$, morphisms between their derived pullbacks to the limit are the filtered colimit of morphisms between their pullbacks to the stages. Thus the relatively perfect categories have this colimit description.
theorems.proof: Every relatively perfect object at the limit descends to one stage. For $K_0$ pseudo-coherent and $L_0$ of finite Tor dimension over $R_0$, morphisms between their derived pullbacks to the limit are the filtered colimit of morphisms between their pullbacks to the stages. Thus the relatively perfect categories have this colimit description.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Lifting relative perfection across a nilpotent thickening
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R'\to A'$ be flat finitely presented and $R'\to R$ surjective with nilpotent kernel. Let $A=A'\otimes_{R'}R$.
theorems.statement: If the derived pullback of $K'\in D(A')$ to $A$ is $R$-perfect, $K'$ is $R'$-perfect.
theorems.proof: If the derived pullback of $K'\in D(A')$ to $A$ is $R$-perfect, $K'$ is $R'$-perfect.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: A local fibre bound and the number of algebra generators
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be flat of finite presentation. Write $A=R[x_1,\ldots,x_d]/I$. Fix $\mathfrak q$ over $\mathfrak p$. Suppose $K\in D(A)$ pseudo-coherent and $K_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}^{\mathbf L}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ has cohomology in $[a,b]$.
theorems.statement: The Tor-amplitude of $K_{\mathfrak q}$ over $R$ is contained in $[a-d,b]$.
theorems.proof: The Tor-amplitude of $K_{\mathfrak q}$ over $R$ is contained in $[a-d,b]$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Fibrewise boundedness criterion for relative perfection
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be flat of finite presentation. Let $K\in D(A)$ be pseudo-coherent.
theorems.statement: It is $R$-perfect precisely when $K$ is bounded below and each $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is bounded below, for every prime of $R$.
theorems.proof: It is $R$-perfect precisely when $K$ is bounded below and each $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is bounded below, for every prime of $R$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: First Ext detects a projective concentrated in degree zero
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K$ have cohomology only in degrees $-1,0$.
theorems.statement: Vanishing of $\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(K,N)$ for every module $N$ is equivalent to $H^{-1}(K)=0$ and $H^0(K)$ projective. For Noetherian $R$ with finite cohomology one may test finite $N$.
theorems.proof: Vanishing of $\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(K,N)$ for every module $N$ is equivalent to $H^{-1}(K)=0$ and $H^0(K)$ projective. For Noetherian $R$ with finite cohomology one may test finite $N$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Two-term representative with free degree-zero module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K$ have cohomology only in degrees $-1,0$.
theorems.statement: There is a representative $K^{-1}\to K^0$ with $K^0$ free. For Noetherian $R$ with finite cohomology one may choose $K^0$ finite free and $K^{-1}$ finite.
theorems.proof: There is a representative $K^{-1}\to K^0$ with $K^0$ free. For Noetherian $R$ with finite cohomology one may choose $K^0$ finite free and $K^{-1}$ finite.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Explicit representatives and homotopies for maps from a nonpositive complex
theorems.hypotheses: Take a complex $M$ in nonpositive degrees with $M^0$ projective.
theorems.statement: When $K^{<-1}=0$, maps $M\to K$ in the derived category are homotopy classes of chain maps. If $K$ is two-term in $[-1,0]$ with $K^0$ projective, a chain map $a$ kills all induced first Ext maps precisely when $a^{-1}=-h^0d_M^{-1}$ for some $h^0:M^0\to K^{-1}$. If $K^{<-2}=0$, a derived map whose component to $K^{-2}[2]$ is represented by $u:M^{-2}\to K^{-2}$ killing $d_M^{-3}$ has a chain representative with $a^{-2}=u$. Two such representatives of the same map differ by a homotopy in degrees $0,-1$ satisfying $h^{-1}d_M^{-2}=0$.
theorems.proof: When $K^{<-1}=0$, maps $M\to K$ in the derived category are homotopy classes of chain maps. If $K$ is two-term in $[-1,0]$ with $K^0$ projective, a chain map $a$ kills all induced first Ext maps precisely when $a^{-1}=-h^0d_M^{-1}$ for some $h^0:M^0\to K^{-1}$. If $K^{<-2}=0$, a derived map whose component to $K^{-2}[2]$ is represented by $u:M^{-2}\to K^{-2}$ killing $d_M^{-3}$ has a chain representative with $a^{-2}=u$. Two such representatives of the same map differ by a homotopy in degrees $0,-1$ satisfying $h^{-1}d_M^{-2}=0$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: A factorization test for annihilation of first Ext
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K$ have cohomology only in degrees $-1,0$. Fix an ideal $I$.
theorems.statement: The condition $I\operatorname{Ext}^1(K,N)=0$ for every module $N$ means that in some representative $E^{-1}\to E^0$ with $E^0$ free, multiplication by every $a\in I$ on $E^{-1}$ factors through the differential. Equivalently this holds in every such representative with $E^0$ projective. Over a Noetherian ring with finite cohomology, finite test modules suffice, and a representative with $E^{-1}$ finite and $E^0$ finite free works.
theorems.proof: The condition $I\operatorname{Ext}^1(K,N)=0$ for every module $N$ means that in some representative $E^{-1}\to E^0$ with $E^0$ free, multiplication by every $a\in I$ on $E^{-1}$ factors through the differential. Equivalently this holds in every such representative with $E^0$ projective. Over a Noetherian ring with finite cohomology, finite test modules suffice, and a representative with $E^{-1}$ finite and $E^0$ finite free works.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Two-term flat-top model after derived base change
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K$ be given by $E^{-1}\to E^0$ with $E^0$ flat, and take any $R\to S$.
theorems.statement: The termwise tensor of this model with $S$ represents $\tau_{\ge-1}(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S)$.
theorems.proof: The termwise tensor of this model with $S$ represents $\tau_{\ge-1}(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Truncated base change preserves ideal annihilation of first Ext
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K$ have cohomology only in degrees $-1,0$. Suppose $I\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(K,N)=0$ for all $N$.
theorems.statement: For any $R\to S$, the object $\tau_{\ge-1}(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S)$ has first Ext annihilated by $IS$ against every $S$-module.
theorems.proof: For any $R\to S$, the object $\tau_{\ge-1}(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S)$ has first Ext annihilated by $IS$ against every $S$-module.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Descent of a scalar null action to a two-term quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Take $K\to K'$ between objects supported in degrees $-1,0$, inducing an isomorphism on $H^0$ and surjection on $H^{-1}$.
theorems.statement: If multiplication by $f\in R$ vanishes on $K$ as a derived morphism, it vanishes on $K'$ as a derived morphism.
theorems.proof: If multiplication by $f\in R$ vanishes on $K$ as a derived morphism, it vanishes on $K'$ as a derived morphism.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Descent of first Ext annihilation to a two-term quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Take $K\to K'$ between objects supported in degrees $-1,0$, inducing an isomorphism on $H^0$ and surjection on $H^{-1}$.
theorems.statement: If $I$ kills $\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(K,N)$ for every $N$, then it kills $\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(K',N)$ for every $N$.
theorems.proof: If $I$ kills $\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(K,N)$ for every $N$, then it kills $\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(K',N)$ for every $N$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Power annihilation of first Ext and projectivity off a closed set
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K$ have cohomology only in degrees $-1,0$. Fix an ideal $I\subset R$.
theorems.statement: Some power of $I$ kills all $\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(K,N)$ precisely when some power $I^c$ kills $H^{-1}(K)$ and $H^0(K)$ is $I^c$-projective. Exponents may change between these conditions. Under Noetherianity and finite cohomology it suffices to test finite $N$. Equivalently $H^{-1}(K)$ is $I$-power torsion and $H^0(K)$ is projective after localization at each member of a finite generating family up to radical for $I$. One can use any such family, or a finite principal cover of $D(I)$ by opens on which those localizations are projective, allowing their union to contain $D(I)$.
theorems.proof: Some power of $I$ kills all $\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(K,N)$ precisely when some power $I^c$ kills $H^{-1}(K)$ and $H^0(K)$ is $I^c$-projective. Exponents may change between these conditions. Under Noetherianity and finite cohomology it suffices to test finite $N$. Equivalently $H^{-1}(K)$ is $I$-power torsion and $H^0(K)$ is projective after localization at each member of a finite generating family up to radical for $I$. One can use any such family, or a finite principal cover of $D(I)$ by opens on which those localizations are projective, allowing their union to contain $D(I)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Vanishing of a two-term composite
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K_1\xrightarrow{f}K_2\xrightarrow{g}K_3$ have cohomology only in degrees $-1,0$. Assume $H^0(f)=0$ and $H^{-1}(g)=0$.
theorems.statement: The composable product $g\circ f$ is zero in $D(R)$.
theorems.proof: The composable product $g\circ f$ is zero in $D(R)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: The determinant kills a square two-term complex
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K$ be $R^n\xrightarrow{A}R^n$ in degrees $-1,0$.
theorems.statement: Multiplication by $\det A$ is null-homotopic using the adjugate matrix.
theorems.proof: Multiplication by $\det A$ is null-homotopic using the adjugate matrix.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Formal smoothness and smoothness via first Ext of the naive cotangent complex
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a ring map $A\to B$.
theorems.statement: Formal smoothness is equivalent to $\operatorname{Ext}^1_B(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A},N)=0$ for every $B$-module $N$. Smoothness is equivalent to that vanishing plus finite presentation.
theorems.proof: Formal smoothness is equivalent to $\operatorname{Ext}^1_B(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A},N)=0$ for every $B$-module $N$. Smoothness is equivalent to that vanishing plus finite presentation.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Truncated derived tensor of the naive cotangent complex
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S\to S'$ be ring maps.
theorems.statement: The ordinary base change of the standard naive cotangent complex over $S$ represents its derived base change truncated in degrees $\ge-1$. The same statement holds for the model attached to any polynomial presentation.
theorems.proof: The ordinary base change of the standard naive cotangent complex over $S$ represents its derived base change truncated in degrees $\ge-1$. The same statement holds for the model attached to any polynomial presentation.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Naive cotangent base change in degrees zero and minus one
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S'=S\otimes_R R'$ and base change a polynomial presentation of $S/R$.
theorems.statement: The natural map $\mathrm{NL}_{S/R}\otimes_S S'\to\mathrm{NL}_{S'/R'}$ is an isomorphism on $H^0$ and a surjection on $H^{-1}$. The corresponding statement holds for the presentation models.
theorems.proof: The natural map $\mathrm{NL}_{S/R}\otimes_S S'\to\mathrm{NL}_{S'/R'}$ is an isomorphism on $H^0$ and a surjection on $H^{-1}$. The corresponding statement holds for the presentation models.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Flat source algebra and naive cotangent base change
theorems.hypotheses: Let $B$ be flat over $A$ and put $B'=B\otimes_A A'$.
theorems.statement: The ordinary base-change map $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_B B'\to\mathrm{NL}_{B'/A'}$ is a quasi-isomorphism. This also holds with derived tensor when $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}$ has Tor-amplitude in $[-1,0]$.
theorems.proof: The ordinary base-change map $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_B B'\to\mathrm{NL}_{B'/A'}$ is a quasi-isomorphism. This also holds with derived tensor when $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}$ has Tor-amplitude in $[-1,0]$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: The naive cotangent complex of an lci map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a local complete intersection ring map.
theorems.statement: Its naive cotangent complex is perfect over $B$ of Tor-amplitude in $[-1,0]$.
theorems.proof: Its naive cotangent complex is perfect over $B$ of Tor-amplitude in $[-1,0]$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Excess conormal kernel in an lci base change
theorems.hypotheses: Let $B'=B\otimes_A A'$ with both $A\to B$ and $A'\to B'$ local complete intersections.
theorems.statement: The kernel of $H^{-1}(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_B B')\to H^{-1}(\mathrm{NL}_{B'/A'})$ is finite projective over $B'$.
theorems.proof: The kernel of $H^{-1}(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_B B')\to H^{-1}(\mathrm{NL}_{B'/A'})$ is finite projective over $B'$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Derived inverse limit of an abelian tower
theorems.hypotheses: Take a countable inverse tower of abelian groups.
theorems.statement: The derived limit is the two-term difference map $1-\mathrm{shift}$ on the product, in degrees $0,1$, giving zero in higher degrees. A Mittag–Leffler tower has vanishing first derived limit. Every complex of towers admits a termwise limit-acyclic replacement, and on such a replacement taking the ordinary limit in each degree computes the derived limit.
theorems.proof: The derived limit is the two-term difference map $1-\mathrm{shift}$ on the product, in degrees $0,1$, giving zero in higher degrees. A Mittag–Leffler tower has vanishing first derived limit. Every complex of towers admits a termwise limit-acyclic replacement, and on such a replacement taking the ordinary limit in each degree computes the derived limit.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Derived inverse limit over a tower of rings
theorems.hypotheses: Take a tower of rings $(A_n)$ and its limit $A$. A tower of modules has $M_n$ over $A_n$ with transitions linear over $A_{n+1}$ by restriction.
theorems.statement: The derived limit is the two-term difference map $1-\mathrm{shift}$ on the product, in degrees $0,1$, giving zero in higher degrees. A Mittag–Leffler tower has vanishing first derived limit. Every complex of towers admits a termwise limit-acyclic replacement, and on such a replacement taking the ordinary limit in each degree computes the derived limit.
theorems.proof: The derived limit is the two-term difference map $1-\mathrm{shift}$ on the product, in degrees $0,1$, giving zero in higher degrees. A Mittag–Leffler tower has vanishing first derived limit. Every complex of towers admits a termwise limit-acyclic replacement, and on such a replacement taking the ordinary limit in each degree computes the derived limit.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Six-term limit sequence
theorems.hypotheses: Let $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$ be a short exact sequence of abelian towers.
theorems.statement: There is an exact sequence $0\to\lim A\to\lim B\to\lim C\to R^1\lim A\to R^1\lim B\to R^1\lim C\to0$.
theorems.proof: There is an exact sequence $0\to\lim A\to\lim B\to\lim C\to R^1\lim A\to R^1\lim B\to R^1\lim C\to0$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Commuting degree-zero cohomology with inverse limit
theorems.hypotheses: Take a tower of complexes of abelian groups from degrees $-2$ through $1$. Assume $R^1\lim$ vanishes on the term towers in degrees $-2,-1$ and on the tower of $H^{-1}$.
theorems.statement: The degree-zero cohomology of the ordinary termwise limit is the limit of the degree-zero cohomologies.
theorems.proof: The degree-zero cohomology of the ordinary termwise limit is the limit of the degree-zero cohomologies.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Invariance of limit and first derived limit under pro-isomorphism
theorems.hypotheses: Take a countable inverse tower of abelian groups.
theorems.statement: A pro-morphism induces maps on $\lim$ and $R^1\lim$, which are isomorphisms for a pro-isomorphism.
theorems.proof: A pro-morphism induces maps on $\lim$ and $R^1\lim$, which are isomorphisms for a pro-isomorphism.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Maps into a triangulated derived limit
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $K$ is a derived limit of a sequence $K_n$ in a triangulated category, and fix an object $L$.
theorems.statement: There is a natural short exact sequence from $R^1\lim\operatorname{Hom}(L,K_n[-1])$ into $\operatorname{Hom}(L,K)$ onto $\lim\operatorname{Hom}(L,K_n)$.
theorems.proof: There is a natural short exact sequence from $R^1\lim\operatorname{Hom}(L,K_n[-1])$ into $\operatorname{Hom}(L,K)$ onto $\lim\operatorname{Hom}(L,K_n)$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Pro-isomorphic towers in a triangulated category
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose two towers in a triangulated category are pro-isomorphic and both have derived limits.
theorems.statement: The chosen derived limits are isomorphic. The resulting identification can depend on choices.
theorems.proof: The chosen derived limits are isomorphic. The resulting identification can depend on choices.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Maps from a sequential homotopy colimit
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K$ be a derived colimit of $K_n$ in a triangulated category and fix $L$.
theorems.statement: There is a short exact sequence from $R^1\lim\operatorname{Hom}(K_n,L[-1])$ into $\operatorname{Hom}(K,L)$ onto $\lim\operatorname{Hom}(K_n,L)$.
theorems.proof: There is a short exact sequence from $R^1\lim\operatorname{Hom}(K_n,L[-1])$ into $\operatorname{Hom}(K,L)$ onto $\lim\operatorname{Hom}(K_n,L)$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Tower cohomology as sheaf cohomology
theorems.hypotheses: Give the poset $\mathbf N$ the topology in which only maximal sieves cover. A presheaf of abelian groups is then an abelian tower and a sheaf.
theorems.statement: Global sections are the limit and $H^p(\mathbf N,\mathcal F)=R^p\lim\mathcal F_n$.
theorems.proof: Global sections are the limit and $H^p(\mathbf N,\mathcal F)=R^p\lim\mathcal F_n$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Derived global sections over a ringed tower
theorems.hypotheses: Take a tower of rings $(A_n)$ and its limit $A$. A tower of modules has $M_n$ over $A_n$ with transitions linear over $A_{n+1}$ by restriction.
theorems.statement: On the poset site with only maximal covering sieves, $(A_n)$ is a structure sheaf. Sheaves of modules are compatible towers of $A_n$-modules. The derived limit is the derived global sections functor with values in $D(A)$.
theorems.proof: On the poset site with only maximal covering sieves, $(A_n)$ is a structure sheaf. Sheaves of modules are compatible towers of $A_n$-modules. The derived limit is the derived global sections functor with values in $D(A)$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Canonical difference triangle for abelian towers
theorems.hypotheses: Take an object of the derived category of towers of abelian groups.
theorems.statement: There is a canonical triangle $\mathbf R\lim K_n\to\prod K_n\xrightarrow{1-\mathrm{shift}}\prod K_n\to(\mathbf R\lim K_n)[1]$.
theorems.proof: There is a canonical triangle $\mathbf R\lim K_n\to\prod K_n\xrightarrow{1-\mathrm{shift}}\prod K_n\to(\mathbf R\lim K_n)[1]$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Canonical difference triangle for module towers
theorems.hypotheses: Take a tower of rings $(A_n)$ and its limit $A$. A tower of modules has $M_n$ over $A_n$ with transitions linear over $A_{n+1}$ by restriction. Take an object of the derived category of compatible module towers.
theorems.statement: There is a canonical triangle $\mathbf R\lim K_n\to\prod K_n\xrightarrow{1-\mathrm{shift}}\prod K_n\to(\mathbf R\lim K_n)[1]$.
theorems.proof: There is a canonical triangle $\mathbf R\lim K_n\to\prod K_n\xrightarrow{1-\mathrm{shift}}\prod K_n\to(\mathbf R\lim K_n)[1]$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Milnor exact sequence for abelian towers
theorems.hypotheses: Take an object of the derived category of towers of abelian groups.
theorems.statement: In each degree $p$ there is a natural exact sequence $0\to R^1\lim H^{p-1}(K_n)\to H^p(\mathbf R\lim K_n)\to\lim H^p(K_n)\to0$.
theorems.proof: In each degree $p$ there is a natural exact sequence $0\to R^1\lim H^{p-1}(K_n)\to H^p(\mathbf R\lim K_n)\to\lim H^p(K_n)\to0$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Milnor exact sequence for module towers
theorems.hypotheses: Take a tower of rings $(A_n)$ and its limit $A$. A tower of modules has $M_n$ over $A_n$ with transitions linear over $A_{n+1}$ by restriction. Take an object of the derived category of compatible module towers.
theorems.statement: In each degree $p$ there is a natural exact sequence $0\to R^1\lim H^{p-1}(K_n)\to H^p(\mathbf R\lim K_n)\to\lim H^p(K_n)\to0$.
theorems.proof: In each degree $p$ there is a natural exact sequence $0\to R^1\lim H^{p-1}(K_n)\to H^p(\mathbf R\lim K_n)\to\lim H^p(K_n)\to0$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Lifting a tower in the derived category of abelian groups
theorems.hypotheses: Consider a tower in $D(\mathrm{Ab})$.
theorems.statement: It can be represented by a complex of towers with compatible degreewise-derived identifications at every index.
theorems.proof: It can be represented by a complex of towers with compatible degreewise-derived identifications at every index.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Lifting derived systems over a sequence of rings
theorems.hypotheses: Take a tower of rings $(A_n)$ and its limit $A$. A tower of modules has $M_n$ over $A_n$ with transitions linear over $A_{n+1}$ by restriction. Give $K_n\in D(A_n)$ and maps $K_{n+1}\to K_n$ in $D(A_{n+1})$.
theorems.statement: One can represent the entire tower by a complex of compatible module systems with levelwise isomorphisms commuting with the given arrows in the respective derived categories.
theorems.proof: One can represent the entire tower by a complex of compatible module systems with levelwise isomorphisms commuting with the given arrows in the respective derived categories.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Independence of an abelian tower lift
theorems.hypotheses: A tower in $D(\mathrm{Ab})$ is represented by a lifted complex of towers.
theorems.statement: The isomorphism class of its derived inverse limit is independent of the lift, since each lift realizes the product-difference triangle. In each degree $p$ there is a natural exact sequence $0\to R^1\lim H^{p-1}(K_n)\to H^p(\mathbf R\lim K_n)\to\lim H^p(K_n)\to0$.
theorems.proof: The isomorphism class of its derived inverse limit is independent of the lift, since each lift realizes the product-difference triangle. In each degree $p$ there is a natural exact sequence $0\to R^1\lim H^{p-1}(K_n)\to H^p(\mathbf R\lim K_n)\to\lim H^p(K_n)\to0$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Independence of a module tower lift
theorems.hypotheses: Take a tower of rings $(A_n)$ and its limit $A$. A tower of modules has $M_n$ over $A_n$ with transitions linear over $A_{n+1}$ by restriction. Take an object of the derived category of compatible module towers.
theorems.statement: For any lift of a fixed tower of derived objects the resulting derived limit in $D(A)$ has the same isomorphism class. In each degree $p$ there is a natural exact sequence $0\to R^1\lim H^{p-1}(K_n)\to H^p(\mathbf R\lim K_n)\to\lim H^p(K_n)\to0$.
theorems.proof: For any lift of a fixed tower of derived objects the resulting derived limit in $D(A)$ has the same isomorphism class. In each degree $p$ there is a natural exact sequence $0\to R^1\lim H^{p-1}(K_n)\to H^p(\mathbf R\lim K_n)\to\lim H^p(K_n)\to0$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Derived inverse limit of a pro-isomorphic morphism
theorems.hypotheses: A morphism in the derived category of abelian towers induces a pro-isomorphism between the levelwise derived objects.
theorems.statement: Its induced map on derived inverse limits is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: Its induced map on derived inverse limits is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Extensions of Mittag–Leffler towers
theorems.hypotheses: In a short exact sequence of abelian towers suppose the outer terms are Mittag–Leffler.
theorems.statement: The middle tower is Mittag–Leffler.
theorems.proof: The middle tower is Mittag–Leffler.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Zero pro-objects via repeated sums
theorems.hypotheses: Take a countable inverse tower of abelian groups.
theorems.statement: The tower is pro-zero precisely when its limit and first derived limit both vanish and both also vanish for the termwise countable direct sum of copies of the tower.
theorems.proof: The tower is pro-zero precisely when its limit and first derived limit both vanish and both also vanish for the termwise countable direct sum of copies of the tower.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Degreewise surjective representatives of derived towers
theorems.hypotheses: Take a tower of rings $(A_n)$ and its limit $A$. A tower of modules has $M_n$ over $A_n$ with transitions linear over $A_{n+1}$ by restriction. Take an object of the derived category of compatible module towers.
theorems.statement: There exists a representative by complexes with surjective transition maps in each degree.
theorems.proof: There exists a representative by complexes with surjective transition maps in each degree.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Levelwise K-flat representatives of derived towers
theorems.hypotheses: Take a tower of rings $(A_n)$ and its limit $A$. A tower of modules has $M_n$ over $A_n$ with transitions linear over $A_{n+1}$ by restriction. Take an object of the derived category of compatible module towers.
theorems.statement: There exists a representative by a tower whose complex at every level is K-flat.
theorems.proof: There exists a representative by a tower whose complex at every level is K-flat.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Derived tensor products for module towers
theorems.hypotheses: Take a tower of rings $(A_n)$ and its limit $A$. A tower of modules has $M_n$ over $A_n$ with transitions linear over $A_{n+1}$ by restriction. Take an object of the derived category of compatible module towers.
theorems.statement: There is a canonical symmetric derived tensor on the derived category of towers, exact in each argument and computed at each level by the corresponding derived tensor.
theorems.proof: There is a canonical symmetric derived tensor on the derived category of towers, exact in each argument and computed at each level by the corresponding derived tensor.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Functorial tensor followed by derived inverse limit
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a tower $E_n$ in $D(A)$ and choose a lift to the derived category of towers.
theorems.statement: The construction $K\mapsto\mathbf R\lim(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}E_n)$ is exact and functorial in $K$ for this chosen lift, using the constant tower of $K$.
theorems.proof: The construction $K\mapsto\mathbf R\lim(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}E_n)$ is exact and functorial in $K$ for this chosen lift, using the constant tower of $K$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Tensor-limit functors preserve tower triangles
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $K\in D(A)$ and a triangle of complexes of towers over $A$.
theorems.statement: Levelwise derived tensor with the constant tower of the fixed object, followed by derived inverse limit, yields a distinguished triangle.
theorems.proof: Levelwise derived tensor with the constant tower of the fixed object, followed by derived inverse limit, yields a distinguished triangle.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Tensor-limit comparison for pro-isomorphic towers
theorems.hypotheses: A morphism in $D(\mathbf N,A)$ gives a pro-isomorphism on levelwise derived objects. Fix any $K\in D(A)$.
theorems.statement: After tensoring levelwise with the fixed object and taking derived inverse limits, the induced morphism is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: After tensoring levelwise with the fixed object and taking derived inverse limits, the induced morphism is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Cyclic quotient resolution of an ideal-power-torsion module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\subset R$ be any ideal and $M$ an $I$-power-torsion module.
theorems.statement: It has a resolution by direct sums of modules $R/I^n$, with exponents allowed to vary across summands.
theorems.proof: It has a resolution by direct sums of modules $R/I^n$, with exponents allowed to vary across summands.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Vanishing of ideal torsion by a localization test
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_t)$ and $M$ is any module.
theorems.statement: The annihilator $M[I]$ vanishes exactly when every $M[I^n]$ vanishes for $n>0$, equivalently when $M\to\bigoplus_j M_{f_j}$ is injective.
theorems.proof: The annihilator $M[I]$ vanishes exactly when every $M[I^n]$ vanishes for $n>0$, equivalently when $M\to\bigoplus_j M_{f_j}$ is injective.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Removing ideal-power torsion and closure under extensions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be finitely generated.
theorems.statement: The quotient $M/M[I^\infty]$ has no nonzero elements killed by $I$. Extensions of two $I$-power-torsion modules are $I$-power torsion.
theorems.proof: The quotient $M/M[I^\infty]$ has no nonzero elements killed by $I$. Extensions of two $I$-power-torsion modules are $I$-power torsion.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Power-torsion modules form a Serre subcategory
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be a finitely generated ideal.
theorems.statement: The $I$-power-torsion modules are closed under subobjects, quotients and extensions in all $R$-modules.
theorems.proof: The $I$-power-torsion modules are closed under subobjects, quotients and extensions in all $R$-modules.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Support criterion for ideal-power torsion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be finitely generated and $M$ any module.
theorems.statement: The module is $I$-power torsion exactly when $\operatorname{Supp}(M)\subset V(I)$. Thus this subcategory depends only on the closed subset.
theorems.proof: The module is $I$-power torsion exactly when $\operatorname{Supp}(M)\subset V(I)$. Thus this subcategory depends only on the closed subset.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Tensor nonpositivity on torsion modules and complexes
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R/I$ has no positive cohomology for an arbitrary ideal $I$.
theorems.statement: The same holds with $R/I^n$ for $n\ge1$, every $I$-power-torsion module, and every bounded nonpositive-cohomology complex whose cohomologies are $I$-power torsion.
theorems.proof: The same holds with $R/I^n$ for $n\ge1$, every $I$-power-torsion module, and every bounded nonpositive-cohomology complex whose cohomologies are $I$-power torsion.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Vanishing on torsion complexes tested by the quotient ring
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R/I=0$.
theorems.statement: The derived tensor with $K$ vanishes on all $R/I^n$, $n\ge1$, on all $I$-power-torsion modules, and on bounded complexes with $I$-power-torsion cohomology.
theorems.proof: The derived tensor with $K$ vanishes on all $R/I^n$, $n\ge1$, on all $I$-power-torsion modules, and on bounded complexes with $I$-power-torsion cohomology.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Scalar extension on power torsion under adic congruences
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to R'$ induce isomorphisms $R/I^n\cong R'/I^nR'$ for all $n>0$.
theorems.statement: For every $I$-power-torsion $M$, the map $M\to M\otimes_R R'$ is an isomorphism. Adic completion supplies an example for finitely generated $I$.
theorems.proof: For every $I$-power-torsion $M$, the map $M\to M\otimes_R R'$ is an isomorphism. Adic completion supplies an example for finitely generated $I$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Faithfulness over a closed fibre
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be flat and $I\subset R$ an ideal.
theorems.statement: Faithful flatness of $R/I\to S/IS$, surjectivity of its spectrum map, faithfulness of scalar extension on modules killed by $I$, and faithfulness on all $I$-power-torsion modules are equivalent.
theorems.proof: Faithful flatness of $R/I\to S/IS$, surjectivity of its spectrum map, faithfulness of scalar extension on modules killed by $I$, and faithfulness on all $I$-power-torsion modules are equivalent.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Closed fibre isomorphism tested on ideal-power torsion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be flat and $R/I\to S/IS$ faithfully flat.
theorems.statement: This quotient map is an isomorphism precisely when $M\to M\otimes_R S$ is an isomorphism for every $I$-power-torsion module.
