theorems.statement: There exists a finite graded $A$-module $N$ and compatible graded identifications $N/I^nN\simeq N_n$.
theorems.proof: There exists a finite graded $A$-module $N$ and compatible graded identifications $N/I^nN\simeq N_n$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Recovering each degree from a completed comparison
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be graded, $I\subseteq A_+$ homogeneous, $\widehat A=\lim A/I^n$ and $I^nG_n=0$ for a graded inverse system. Suppose compatible graded maps from $M$ induce $M\otimes_A\widehat A\simeq\lim G_n$.
theorems.statement: For each integer $d$, the map $M_d\to\lim_n(G_n)_d$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: For each integer $d$, the map $M_d\to\lim_n(G_n)_d$ is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Fibrewise injectivity into a flat module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)\to S$ be a local map of local rings with $S$ Noetherian. Let $u:N\to M$ be $R$-linear with $N$ finite over $S$ and $M$ flat over $R$.
theorems.statement: Injectivity modulo $\mathfrak m$ implies injectivity of $u$ and flatness of its cokernel over $R$.
theorems.proof: Injectivity modulo $\mathfrak m$ implies injectivity of $u$ and flatness of its cokernel over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Lifting a fibre nonzerodivisor
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)\to S$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Assume the map is flat and the class of $f\in S$ acts injectively on $S/\mathfrak mS$.
theorems.statement: Then $f$ acts injectively on $S$ and $S/fS$ is $R$-flat.
theorems.proof: Then $f$ acts injectively on $S$ and $S/fS$ is $R$-flat.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Lifting a fibre regular sequence
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)\to S$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Assume flatness and let $f_1,\ldots,f_c$ have regular images in $S/\mathfrak mS$.
theorems.statement: The sequence is regular in $S$ and the quotient by each initial segment is flat over $R$.
theorems.proof: The sequence is regular in $S$ and the quotient by each initial segment is flat over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Free closed fibre of a relatively flat module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)\to S$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Take a nonzero finite $S$-module $M$ flat over $R$ and free after reduction modulo $\mathfrak m$ over the fibre ring.
theorems.statement: Then $M$ is $S$-free and $S$ is flat over $R$.
theorems.proof: Then $M$ is $S$-free and $S$ is flat over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Fibrewise exactness for finite complexes of relatively flat modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)\to S$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Let $0\to F_e\to\cdots\to F_0$ be a complex of finite $S$-modules flat over $R$, exact in positive degrees after reduction modulo $\mathfrak m$.
theorems.statement: The complex is exact in positive degrees and its degree-zero cokernel is flat over $R$.
theorems.proof: The complex is exact in positive degrees and its degree-zero cokernel is flat over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Finite length tests from vanishing Tor on a residue field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,k)$ be local and suppose $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(k,M)=0$.
theorems.statement: Then $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(N,M)=0$ for every finite length module $N$, by induction on length.
theorems.proof: Then $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(N,M)=0$ for every finite length module $N$, by induction on length.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Local flatness criterion with the residue field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)\to S$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Let $M$ be finite over $S$.
theorems.statement: Vanishing of $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(R/\mathfrak m,M)$ implies flatness of $M$ over $R$.
theorems.proof: Vanishing of $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(R/\mathfrak m,M)$ implies flatness of $M$ over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Flatness modulo every power of an ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $M/IM$ is flat over $R/I$ and $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(R/I,M)=0$.
theorems.statement: Every $M/I^nM$ is flat over $R/I^n$ for $n\ge1$. The first Tor with $M$ vanishes for any module killed by a power of $I$. For nilpotent $I$ this gives flatness of $M$.
theorems.proof: Every $M/I^nM$ is flat over $R/I^n$ for $n\ge1$. The first Tor with $M$ vanishes for any module killed by a power of $I$. For nilpotent $I$ this gives flatness of $M$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Flatness of finite thickenings by graded multiplication tests
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $M/IM$ is flat over $R/I$ and $M\otimes_R(I^n/I^{n+1})\to I^nM/I^{n+1}M$ is injective for $1\le n\le k$.
theorems.statement: Then $M/I^{k+1}M$ is flat over $R/I^{k+1}$. The first-order thickening is the case $k=1$.
theorems.proof: Then $M/I^{k+1}M$ is flat over $R/I^{k+1}$. The first-order thickening is the case $k=1$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Local flatness criterion for a proper ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)\to S$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Take a proper ideal $I\subset R$ and finite $S$-module $M$.
theorems.statement: If $M/IM$ is flat over $R/I$ and $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,R/I)=0$, then $M$ is flat over $R$.
theorems.proof: If $M/IM$ is flat over $R/I$ and $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,R/I)=0$, then $M$ is flat over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Flatness near the closed locus from flatness of all thickenings
theorems.hypotheses: For a homomorphism of Noetherian rings $R\to S$ take a finite $S$-module $M$ and $I\subset R$. Suppose every $M/I^nM$ is flat over $R/I^n$ for $n\ge1$.
theorems.statement: Each $M_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $R$ for $\mathfrak q\supseteq IS$. In particular $M$ is flat over $R$ when $S$ is local and $IS$ is proper.
theorems.proof: Each $M_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $R$ for $\mathfrak q\supseteq IS$. In particular $M$ is flat over $R$ when $S$ is local and $IS$ is proper.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Surjectivity of the change-of-base map on first Tor
theorems.hypotheses: Take $R\to A\to B$ with $M\otimes_R A$ flat over $A$.
theorems.statement: Then $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,A)\otimes_A B\to\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,B)$ is surjective.
theorems.proof: Then $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,A)\otimes_A B\to\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,B)$ is surjective.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: First Tor after quotient and change of ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$, $I\subset R$, $J=IA$ and $M'=M\otimes_R A$.
theorems.statement: The natural map $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(A/J,M)\to\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(A/J,M')$ is surjective.
theorems.proof: The natural map $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(A/J,M)\to\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(A/J,M')$ is surjective.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: A zero first-Tor map in a localized base-change square
theorems.hypotheses: In a commutative square $R\to S$, $R'\to S'$ of Noetherian local rings with all maps local, assume $S'$ is a localization of $S\otimes_RR'$. Let $M$ be finite over $S$, $I\subset R$ proper, $I'=IR'$, $M'=M\otimes_SS'$.
theorems.statement: If $M/IM$ is flat over $R/I$ and the natural map $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,R/I)\to\operatorname{Tor}_1^{R'}(M',R'/I')$ is zero, then $M'$ is flat over $R'$.
theorems.proof: If $M/IM$ is flat over $R/I$ and the natural map $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,R/I)\to\operatorname{Tor}_1^{R'}(M',R'/I')$ is zero, then $M'$ is flat over $R'$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Fibrewise flatness in a local tower
theorems.hypotheses: Take local homomorphisms $(R,\mathfrak m)\to S\to T$ of Noetherian local rings. Let $M$ be a nonzero finite $T$-module flat over $R$ and $M/\mathfrak mM$ flat over $S/\mathfrak m S$.
theorems.statement: Then $S$ is flat over $R$ and $M$ is flat over $S$.
theorems.proof: Then $S$ is flat over $R$ and $M$ is flat over $S$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Principal closed locus and its complement
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f$ act injectively on both $A$ and its module $M$. Suppose $M_f$ is flat over $A_f$ and $M/fM$ flat over $A/fA$.
theorems.statement: Then $M$ is flat over $A$. If both given flatness conditions are faithful, $M$ is faithfully flat.
theorems.proof: Then $M$ is flat over $A$. If both given flatness conditions are faithful, $M$ is faithfully flat.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Finitely generated closed locus and a bounded Tor test
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ with $r\ge1$. Assume $M_{f_i}$ flat over $A_{f_i}$ for all $i$, $M/IM$ flat over $A/I$, and $\operatorname{Tor}_i^A(M,A/I)=0$ for $1\le i\le r+1$.
theorems.statement: Then $M$ is flat over $A$, and faithfully flat when the specified local and quotient flatness assumptions are faithful.
theorems.proof: Then $M$ is flat over $A$, and faithfully flat when the specified local and quotient flatness assumptions are faithful.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Localized base change for relative flatness
theorems.hypotheses: In a local commutative square $R\to S$, $R'\to S'$ of local rings, assume $S'$ is a localization of $S\otimes_RR'$. Set $M'=M\otimes_SS'$.
theorems.statement: If $M$ is $R$-flat then $M'$ is $R'$-flat. The converse holds when $R\to R'$ is flat. Taking $M=S$ gives the corresponding assertions about the ring maps.
theorems.proof: If $M$ is $R$-flat then $M'$ is $R'$-flat. The converse holds when $R\to R'$ is flat. Taking $M=S$ gives the corresponding assertions about the ring maps.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Flat horizontal arrows with unchanged closed maximal ideal
theorems.hypotheses: In a square of local homomorphisms $R\to S$, $R'\to S'$, assume $R\to R'$, $S\to S'$ flat, $\mathfrak m_RR'=\mathfrak m_{R'}$, and $R',S'$ Noetherian. Let $M$ be finite over $S$ and flat over $R$.
theorems.statement: Then $M\otimes_SS'$ is flat over $R'$.
theorems.proof: Then $M\otimes_SS'$ is flat over $R'$.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Lifting an arbitrary basis over a nilpotent maximal ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be local with $\mathfrak m$ nilpotent, $M$ flat, and $(x_i)$ any indexed family in $M$.
theorems.statement: The family is an $R$-basis precisely when its residues form a basis of $M/\mathfrak mM$. No finiteness assumption on the family is needed.
theorems.proof: The family is an $R$-basis precisely when its residues form a basis of $M/\mathfrak mM$. No finiteness assumption on the family is needed.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Flat, projective and free over a local ring with nilpotent maximal ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Assume the maximal ideal of the local ring $R$ is nilpotent.
theorems.statement: For any $R$-module, flatness, projectivity and freeness are equivalent. Lift a basis over the residue field.
theorems.proof: For any $R$-module, flatness, projectivity and freeness are equivalent. Lift a basis over the residue field.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Lifting a basis modulo a nilpotent ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $I$ nilpotent, the images of a family $(x_i)$ are a basis of $M/IM$ over $R/I$, and $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(R/I,M)=0$.
theorems.statement: Then the family $(x_i)$ is a basis of $M$ over $R$.
theorems.proof: Then the family $(x_i)$ is a basis of $M$ over $R$.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Improving flatness over a contracted ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Given $f:R\to S$, let $M/IM$ be flat over $R/I$ and $S\otimes_RM$ flat over $S$. Define $J=f^{-1}(I^2 S)$.
theorems.statement: Then $M/JM$ is flat over $R/J$.
theorems.proof: Then $M/JM$ is flat over $R/J$.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Lifting flatness through an injective comparison and a nilpotent ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $R\to S$ injective, $I\subset R$ nilpotent, $M/IM$ flat over $R/I$, and $S\otimes_R M$ flat over $S$.
theorems.statement: Then $M$ is flat over $R$.
theorems.proof: Then $M$ is flat over $R$.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Local Artinian Tor criterion for flatness
theorems.hypotheses: Take a proper ideal $I$ of a local Artinian ring $R$.
theorems.statement: An arbitrary $M$ is flat over $R$ exactly when $M/IM$ is flat over $R/I$ and $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(R/I,M)=0$.
theorems.proof: An arbitrary $M$ is flat over $R$ exactly when $M/IM$ is flat over $R/I$ and $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(R/I,M)=0$.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Descent of flatness for injections from an Artinian ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Artinian and $R\to S$ injective. Suppose $M\otimes_R S$ is flat over $S$.
theorems.statement: Then $M$ is flat over $R$.
theorems.proof: Then $M$ is flat over $R$.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Fibre flatness with nilpotent base ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Take $R\to S\to S'$ and a nilpotent ideal $I\subset R$. Suppose the $S'$-module $M$ is flat over $R$ and its reduction modulo $I$ is flat over $S/IS$.
theorems.statement: Then $M$ is flat over $S$ and $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $R$ at each $\mathfrak q$ where $M\otimes_S\kappa(\mathfrak q)\ne0$.
theorems.proof: Then $M$ is flat over $S$ and $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $R$ at each $\mathfrak q$ where $M\otimes_S\kappa(\mathfrak q)\ne0$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Cancelling an invertible entry in a free complex
theorems.hypotheses: Let a differential of a complex of finite free modules have a unit as a matrix coefficient.
theorems.statement: A change of bases splits off the two-term identity complex $R\to R$ in the corresponding degrees, decreasing their two ranks by one.
theorems.proof: A change of bases splits off the two-term identity complex $R\to R$ in the corresponding degrees, decreasing their two ranks by one.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Split free complexes over a depth-zero local ring
theorems.hypotheses: Consider a finite free complex $0\to F_e\to\cdots\to F_0$ with differentials $d_i$ and $n_i=\operatorname{rank}(F_i)$. Assume $R$ is Noetherian local of depth zero and the complex is exact in all positive degrees.
theorems.statement: It splits as a direct sum of two-term identity complexes and copies of $R$ in degree zero. A nonzero socle element forces a unit pivot at the leftmost nonzero differential.
theorems.proof: It splits as a direct sum of two-term identity complexes and copies of $R$ in degree zero. A nonzero socle element forces a unit pivot at the leftmost nonzero differential.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Split free complexes over an Artinian local ring
theorems.hypotheses: Consider a finite free complex $0\to F_e\to\cdots\to F_0$ with differentials $d_i$ and $n_i=\operatorname{rank}(F_i)$. Assume $R$ Artinian local and exactness in positive degrees.
theorems.statement: The complex is a sum of two-term identity complexes and free summands in degree zero, since this ring has depth zero.
theorems.proof: The complex is a sum of two-term identity complexes and free summands in degree zero, since this ring has depth zero.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Ranks and unit minors of a split free complex
theorems.hypotheses: Consider a finite free complex $0\to F_e\to\cdots\to F_0$ with differentials $d_i$ and $n_i=\operatorname{rank}(F_i)$. Assume it is a direct sum of adjacent-degree identity complexes and free summands in degree zero.
theorems.statement: For $i\ge1$ the differential has rank $r_i=\sum_{j=i}^e(-1)^{j-i}n_j$ and its $r_i$-minors generate $R$. At an interior degree, $r_i+r_{i+1}=n_i$.
theorems.proof: For $i\ge1$ the differential has rank $r_i=\sum_{j=i}^e(-1)^{j-i}n_j$ and its $r_i$-minors generate $R$. At an interior degree, $r_i+r_{i+1}=n_i$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Exactness after quotient by a nonzerodivisor
theorems.hypotheses: Consider a finite free complex $0\to F_e\to\cdots\to F_0$ with differentials $d_i$ and $n_i=\operatorname{rank}(F_i)$. Assume $R$ local, the complex exact in positive degrees, and $x$ a nonzerodivisor in the maximal ideal.
theorems.statement: Reduction modulo $x$ preserves exactness in degrees $i\ge2$. Degree one may have homology from the degree-zero cokernel.
theorems.proof: Reduction modulo $x$ preserves exactness in degrees $i\ge2$. Degree one may have homology from the degree-zero cokernel.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Depth of the highest nonzero positive homology
theorems.hypotheses: Let $0\to M_e\to\cdots\to M_0$ be a complex of finite modules over a Noetherian local ring with $\operatorname{depth}(M_i)\ge i$.
theorems.statement: If the largest index with nonvanishing homology is $i>0$, the module $H_i$ has depth at least one.
theorems.proof: If the largest index with nonvanishing homology is $i>0$, the module $H_i$ has depth at least one.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Buchsbaum–Eisenbud exactness criterion
theorems.hypotheses: Consider a finite free complex $0\to F_e\to\cdots\to F_0$ with differentials $d_i$ and $n_i=\operatorname{rank}(F_i)$. Assume $R$ Noetherian local. The rank of a differential is the largest size of a nonzero minor, with the empty minor equal to one. Put $r_i=\sum_{j=i}^e(-1)^{j-i}n_j$.
theorems.statement: Exactness in all positive degrees is equivalent to both conditions for each $1\le i\le e$. The rank of $d_i$ equals $r_i$, and its ideal of $r_i$-minors is the unit ideal or contains an $R$-regular sequence of length $i$.
theorems.proof: Exactness in all positive degrees is equivalent to both conditions for each $1\le i\le e$. The rank of $d_i$ equals $r_i$, and its ideal of $r_i$-minors is the unit ideal or contains an $R$-regular sequence of length $i$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: A hypersurface transverse to a fixed parameter flag
theorems.hypotheses: Over Noetherian local $(R,\mathfrak m)$ let $M$ be Cohen–Macaulay of support dimension $d\ge1$ with regular sequence $f_1,\ldots,f_d$. Assume $g\in\mathfrak m$ and $\dim(\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(g,f_1,\ldots,f_i))=d-i-1$ for $0\le i<d$.
theorems.statement: Then $g$ acts injectively on $M$ and $M/gM$ is Cohen–Macaulay with maximal regular sequence given by $f_1,\ldots,f_{d-1}$.
theorems.proof: Then $g$ acts injectively on $M$ and $M/gM$ is Cohen–Macaulay with maximal regular sequence given by $f_1,\ldots,f_{d-1}$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: A single dimension drop detects a regular element
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be Cohen–Macaulay over Noetherian local $R$, with $g$ in the maximal ideal cutting its support dimension down by exactly one.
theorems.statement: Multiplication by $g$ is injective on $M$, and $M/gM$ is Cohen–Macaulay with depth exactly one less.
theorems.proof: Multiplication by $g$ is injective on $M$, and $M/gM$ is Cohen–Macaulay with depth exactly one less.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Expected codimension detects a regular sequence on a Cohen–Macaulay module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be Cohen–Macaulay of support dimension $d$ over Noetherian local $R$. Suppose $g_1,\ldots,g_c$ are in the maximal ideal and the quotient support has dimension $d-c$.
theorems.statement: The elements form an $M$-regular sequence and can be extended to a maximal one.
theorems.proof: The elements form an $M$-regular sequence and can be extended to a maximal one.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Prime-chain lengths from a full-support Cohen–Macaulay module
theorems.hypotheses: Assume a Noetherian local ring $R$ has a Cohen–Macaulay module with support the entire spectrum.
theorems.statement: Each maximal strict chain of prime ideals has length $\dim(R)$.
theorems.proof: Each maximal strict chain of prime ideals has length $\dim(R)$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Dimension formula from a full-support Cohen–Macaulay module
theorems.hypotheses: Assume a Noetherian local ring $R$ has a Cohen–Macaulay module supported everywhere.
theorems.statement: For every prime $\mathfrak p$, $\dim R=\dim R_{\mathfrak p}+\dim(R/\mathfrak p)$.
theorems.proof: For every prime $\mathfrak p$, $\dim R=\dim R_{\mathfrak p}+\dim(R/\mathfrak p)$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Regular sequences by dimension in a Cohen–Macaulay local ring
theorems.hypotheses: Take $x_1,\ldots,x_c$ in the maximal ideal of a Noetherian Cohen–Macaulay local ring of dimension $d$.
theorems.statement: The sequence is regular exactly when the quotient has dimension $d-c$. In that case it extends to length $d$, and each initial quotient is Cohen–Macaulay of dimension $d-i$.
theorems.proof: The sequence is regular exactly when the quotient has dimension $d-c$. In that case it extends to length $d$, and each initial quotient is Cohen–Macaulay of dimension $d-i$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Equidimensional chains in a Cohen–Macaulay local ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian local and Cohen–Macaulay.
theorems.statement: Every maximal chain of prime ideals has length $\dim(R)$, by applying the full-support result to $M=R$.
theorems.proof: Every maximal chain of prime ideals has length $\dim(R)$, by applying the full-support result to $M=R$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Dimension formula in a Cohen–Macaulay local ring
theorems.hypotheses: Take Noetherian local Cohen–Macaulay $R$ and a prime $\mathfrak p$.
theorems.statement: Then $\dim R=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)+\dim(R/\mathfrak p)$.
theorems.proof: Then $\dim R=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)+\dim(R/\mathfrak p)$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Cohen–Macaulay local rings remain Cohen–Macaulay at all primes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Cohen–Macaulay and local in the Noetherian sense.
theorems.statement: For every $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}(R)$, $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is Cohen–Macaulay.
theorems.proof: For every $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}(R)$, $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is Cohen–Macaulay.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Polynomial extensions preserve Cohen–Macaulayness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian Cohen–Macaulay.
theorems.statement: Every finite-variable polynomial ring $R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ is Noetherian Cohen–Macaulay, by adjoining one variable at a time. This qualification ensures the resulting ring is Noetherian.
theorems.proof: Every finite-variable polynomial ring $R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ is Noetherian Cohen–Macaulay, by adjoining one variable at a time. This qualification ensures the resulting ring is Noetherian.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Depth shift for a first syzygy
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Cohen–Macaulay local of dimension $d$, and $0\to K\to R^n\to M\to0$ exact with $n$ finite.
theorems.statement: Either $M=0$, the depth of $K$ strictly exceeds that of $M$, or both depths equal $d$.
theorems.proof: Either $M=0$, the depth of $K$ strictly exceeds that of $M$, or both depths equal $d$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Resolution by free modules ending in a maximal Cohen–Macaulay syzygy
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian local Cohen–Macaulay of dimension $d$ and $M$ a nonzero finite module of depth $e$.
theorems.statement: After $d-e$ successive finite free surjections the syzygy can be taken maximal Cohen–Macaulay. Equivalently there is an exact resolution starting with a maximal Cohen–Macaulay term and $d-e$ finite free terms before $M$, with $M$ itself used if $e=d$.
theorems.proof: After $d-e$ successive finite free surjections the syzygy can be taken maximal Cohen–Macaulay. Equivalently there is an exact resolution starting with a maximal Cohen–Macaulay term and $d-e$ finite free terms before $M$, with $M$ itself used if $e=d$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Choosing a regular sequence from the source of a local map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a local homomorphism with $B$ Noetherian Cohen–Macaulay and $\sqrt{\mathfrak m_AB}=\mathfrak m_B$.
theorems.statement: Some $\dim(B)$ elements of $\mathfrak m_A$ map to a regular sequence in $B$.
theorems.proof: Some $\dim(B)$ elements of $\mathfrak m_A$ map to a regular sequence in $B$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Catenarity of a ring and its spectrum
theorems.hypotheses: Give $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ its Zariski topology.
theorems.statement: Catenarity of $R$ is equivalent to catenarity of its spectrum. Intervals of primes with inclusion correspond to the intervals of irreducible closed subsets under the reversed order.
theorems.proof: Catenarity of $R$ is equivalent to catenarity of its spectrum. Intervals of primes with inclusion correspond to the intervals of irreducible closed subsets under the reversed order.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Localization preserves catenarity
theorems.hypotheses: Take an arbitrary localization of a catenary ring.
theorems.statement: It is catenary. Moreover any localization of a Noetherian universally catenary ring is universally catenary.
theorems.proof: It is catenary. Moreover any localization of a Noetherian universally catenary ring is universally catenary.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Essentially finite type algebras over universally catenary rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be Noetherian universally catenary and $B$ essentially of finite type over $A$.
theorems.statement: Then $B$ is universally catenary. First pass to a finite type algebra and then localize.
theorems.proof: Then $B$ is universally catenary. First pass to a finite type algebra and then localize.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Stalkwise catenarity
theorems.hypotheses: Take any ring $R$.
theorems.statement: Catenarity can be checked after localization at all primes or just all maximal ideals. For Noetherian $R$ both stalkwise tests also characterize universal catenarity.
theorems.proof: Catenarity can be checked after localization at all primes or just all maximal ideals. For Noetherian $R$ both stalkwise tests also characterize universal catenarity.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Quotients preserve catenarity
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be an ideal of $R$.
theorems.statement: Catenarity of $R$ implies that of $R/I$. For Noetherian $R$, universal catenarity passes to $R/I$ as well.
theorems.proof: Catenarity of $R$ implies that of $R/I$. For Noetherian $R$, universal catenarity passes to $R/I$ as well.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Testing catenarity on irreducible components
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $R$ is Noetherian.
theorems.statement: Catenarity of $R$ is equivalent to catenarity of each $R/\mathfrak p$ for minimal $\mathfrak p$. The same equivalence holds for universal catenarity.
theorems.proof: Catenarity of $R$ is equivalent to catenarity of each $R/\mathfrak p$ for minimal $\mathfrak p$. The same equivalence holds for universal catenarity.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: A full-support Cohen–Macaulay module gives universal catenarity
theorems.hypotheses: Take a Noetherian ring with a Cohen–Macaulay module supported on its entire spectrum.
theorems.statement: Then the ring is universally catenary. Applying this to the regular module includes every Noetherian Cohen–Macaulay ring.
theorems.proof: Then the ring is universally catenary. Applying this to the regular module includes every Noetherian Cohen–Macaulay ring.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: A dimension function tests local catenarity
theorems.hypotheses: Take a Noetherian local ring $A$.
theorems.statement: It is catenary precisely when $\mathfrak p\mapsto\dim(A/\mathfrak p)$ is a dimension function, decreasing by one along each immediate strict specialization.
theorems.proof: It is catenary precisely when $\mathfrak p\mapsto\dim(A/\mathfrak p)$ is a dimension function, decreasing by one along each immediate strict specialization.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Associated graded ring of a regular local ring
theorems.hypotheses: Take regular local $(R,\mathfrak m,k)$ of dimension $d$.
theorems.statement: The associated graded ring of the maximal ideal is isomorphic to the standard graded $k[X_1,\ldots,X_d]$. The variables may be sent to the initial classes of minimal generators.
theorems.proof: The associated graded ring of the maximal ideal is isomorphic to the standard graded $k[X_1,\ldots,X_d]$. The variables may be sent to the initial classes of minimal generators.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Regular parameters in a regular local ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $x_1,\ldots,x_d$ minimally generate the maximal ideal of a regular local ring $R$.
theorems.statement: They form a regular sequence, and the quotient by its first $c$ terms is regular local of dimension $d-c$. In particular $R$ is Cohen–Macaulay.
theorems.proof: They form a regular sequence, and the quotient by its first $c$ terms is regular local of dimension $d-c$. In particular $R$ is Cohen–Macaulay.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Ideals with regular local quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $R$ and $R/I$ both regular local.
theorems.statement: One may choose a minimal generating set of the maximal ideal of $R$ such that an initial segment generates $I$.
theorems.proof: One may choose a minimal generating set of the maximal ideal of $R$ such that an initial segment generates $I$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Lifting freeness modulo a module nonzerodivisor
theorems.hypotheses: Over Noetherian local $R$, take finite $M$ and $x$ in the maximal ideal acting injectively on $M$.
theorems.statement: If $M/xM$ is free over $R/xR$, then $M$ is free over $R$.
theorems.proof: If $M/xM$ is free over $R/xR$, then $M$ is free over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Maximal Cohen–Macaulay modules over a regular local ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be maximal Cohen–Macaulay over regular local $R$.
theorems.statement: Then $M$ is free over $R$.
theorems.proof: Then $M$ is free over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Lifting regularity across a regular sequence
theorems.hypotheses: Take a Noetherian local ring and a regular sequence in its maximal ideal whose quotient is a regular local ring.
theorems.statement: Then the original ring is regular local. This includes the case of one nonzerodivisor.
theorems.proof: Then the original ring is regular local. This includes the case of one nonzerodivisor.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Noetherian directed colimit of regular local rings
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose a directed system of regular local rings has local transition homomorphisms and its colimit $R$ is Noetherian.
theorems.statement: The colimit is regular local.
theorems.proof: The colimit is regular local.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Epimorphisms compose
theorems.hypotheses: Take composable epimorphisms of commutative rings.
theorems.statement: Their composite is an epimorphism, by right cancellation twice.
theorems.proof: Their composite is an epimorphism, by right cancellation twice.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Epimorphisms under base change
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $R\to S$ is an epimorphism and $A$ an $R$-algebra.
theorems.statement: The pushout $A\to A\otimes_R S$ is an epimorphism.
theorems.proof: The pushout $A\to A\otimes_R S$ is an epimorphism.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Right factor of an epimorphism
theorems.hypotheses: For $A\to B\to C$ suppose the composite is an epimorphism.
theorems.statement: Then $B\to C$ is an epimorphism by its cancellation test.
theorems.proof: Then $B\to C$ is an epimorphism by its cancellation test.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Source-stalk criterion for ring epimorphisms
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be arbitrary. Localize $S$ using the complement of a prime of $R$.
theorems.statement: The map is an epimorphism exactly when all $R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak p}$ are epimorphisms. Test the multiplication isomorphism locally.
theorems.proof: The map is an epimorphism exactly when all $R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak p}$ are epimorphisms. Test the multiplication isomorphism locally.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Epimorphisms out of fields
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $k\to S$ is an epimorphism and $k$ is a field.
theorems.statement: Either $S=0$ or the given map is an isomorphism. A nonzero $k$-algebra is faithfully flat.
theorems.proof: Either $S=0$ or the given map is an isomorphism. A nonzero $k$-algebra is faithfully flat.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Spectral and residue effects of an epimorphism
theorems.hypotheses: Take an epimorphism of rings $R\to S$.
theorems.statement: Its spectral map is injective and each induced residue field map is an isomorphism, by applying the field case to the fibres.
theorems.proof: Its spectral map is injective and each induced residue field map is an isomorphism, by applying the field case to the fibres.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A finite matrix test for vanishing in a tensor product
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(x_i)$ generate $M$, $(y_j)$ generate $N$, and take a finitely supported tuple $(m_j)$ in $M$.
theorems.statement: Then $\sum_jm_j\otimes y_j=0$ exactly when a matrix $(a_{ij})$ over $R$ of finite total support satisfies $m_j=\sum_i a_{ij}x_i$ for all $j$ and $\sum_j a_{ij}y_j=0$ for all $i$.
theorems.proof: Then $\sum_jm_j\otimes y_j=0$ exactly when a matrix $(a_{ij})$ over $R$ of finite total support satisfies $m_j=\sum_i a_{ij}x_i$ for all $j$ and $\sum_j a_{ij}y_j=0$ for all $i$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Equalizer of the two tensor-square inclusions
theorems.hypotheses: For $f:R\to S$ choose $g\in S$.
theorems.statement: The equation $g\otimes1=1\otimes g$ holds exactly when $g=\sum_{i,j}a_{ij}y_i z_j$ for finite tuples in $S$ and coefficients in $R$, with each $\sum_i a_{ij}y_i$ and $\sum_j a_{ij}z_j$ in $f(R)$.
theorems.proof: The equation $g\otimes1=1\otimes g$ holds exactly when $g=\sum_{i,j}a_{ij}y_i z_j$ for finite tuples in $S$ and coefficients in $R$, with each $\sum_i a_{ij}y_i$ and $\sum_j a_{ij}z_j$ in $f(R)$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Cardinality bound for a ring epimorphism
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $R\to S$ is an epimorphism.
theorems.statement: Then $|S|\le |R|$. Finite tensor-square witnesses bound the number of distinct possible elements of the target.
theorems.proof: Then $|S|\le |R|$. Finite tensor-square witnesses bound the number of distinct possible elements of the target.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Restriction of scalars for epimorphisms
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings.
theorems.statement: It is an epimorphism exactly when restriction from $S$-modules to $R$-modules is fully faithful, equivalently every $R$-linear map between $S$-modules is already $S$-linear.
theorems.proof: It is an epimorphism exactly when restriction from $S$-modules to $R$-modules is fully faithful, equivalently every $R$-linear map between $S$-modules is already $S$-linear.

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.name: Local, ideal-theoretic and localization tests for purity
theorems.hypotheses: Fix an ideal $I$ of $R$.
theorems.statement: Purity is equivalent to $I\cap J=IJ$ for all ideals, for all finite ideals, or for all principal ideals $J$. Equivalently each finite tuple in $I$ is fixed by multiplication by one element of $I$, and it suffices to test singletons. Other equivalent criteria are $I_{\mathfrak p}=0$ or $R_{\mathfrak p}$ at every prime, $\operatorname{Supp}(I)=\operatorname{Spec}(R)\setminus V(I)$, and $I=\ker(R\to(1+I)^{-1}R)$. Equivalently $R/I$ is a localization as an $R$-algebra, in which case the set $1+I$ suffices.
theorems.proof: Purity is equivalent to $I\cap J=IJ$ for all ideals, for all finite ideals, or for all principal ideals $J$. Equivalently each finite tuple in $I$ is fixed by multiplication by one element of $I$, and it suffices to test singletons. Other equivalent criteria are $I_{\mathfrak p}=0$ or $R_{\mathfrak p}$ at every prime, $\operatorname{Supp}(I)=\operatorname{Spec}(R)\setminus V(I)$, and $I=\ker(R\to(1+I)^{-1}R)$. Equivalently $R/I$ is a localization as an $R$-algebra, in which case the set $1+I$ suffices.

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.name: A pure ideal is determined by its closed subset
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I,J$ be pure ideals of the same ring and suppose $V(I)=V(J)$.
theorems.statement: Then $I=J$ because their stalks agree at every prime.
theorems.proof: Then $I=J$ because their stalks agree at every prime.

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.name: Pure ideals and closed sets stable under generalizations
theorems.hypotheses: Use the Zariski spectrum of any ring $R$.
theorems.statement: The assignment $I\mapsto V(I)$ bijects pure ideals with closed subsets that contain every generalization of each of their points.
theorems.proof: The assignment $I\mapsto V(I)$ bijects pure ideals with closed subsets that contain every generalization of each of their points.

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.name: Projective quotient and idempotent tests for finite pure ideals
theorems.hypotheses: Fix an ideal $I$ of $R$.
theorems.statement: Finite generation and purity together are equivalent to generation by a single idempotent. They are also equivalent to purity with $V(I)$ open, or to projectivity of $R/I$ as an $R$-module.
theorems.proof: Finite generation and purity together are equivalent to generation by a single idempotent. They are also equivalent to purity with $V(I)$ open, or to projectivity of $R/I$ as an $R$-module.

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.name: A topological characterization of finite-flat projectivity
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be an arbitrary ring.
theorems.statement: Every finite flat $R$-module is finite locally free exactly when every closed subset of $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ stable under generalization is open.
theorems.proof: Every finite flat $R$-module is finite locally free exactly when every closed subset of $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ stable under generalization is open.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Schanuel’s lemma
theorems.hypotheses: Let $P\to M$ and $Q\to M$ be surjections from projectives with kernels $K,L$.
theorems.statement: There is an isomorphism $K\oplus Q\simeq P\oplus L$, compatible with an isomorphism between the two stabilized presentations inducing the identity on $M$. Split the two projections of the fibre product.
theorems.proof: There is an isomorphism $K\oplus Q\simeq P\oplus L$, compatible with an isomorphism between the two stabilized presentations inducing the identity on $M$. Split the two projections of the fibre product.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Projective dimension from a syzygy
theorems.hypotheses: For a module $M$, set its zeroth syzygy equal to $M$. The first is the kernel of a projective surjection and higher ones are formed recursively. Fix $d\ge0$.
theorems.statement: Projective dimension at most $d$ is equivalent to admitting a projective resolution of length at most $d$, and to the $d$th syzygy being projective in some or every projective resolution.
theorems.proof: Projective dimension at most $d$ is equivalent to admitting a projective resolution of length at most $d$, and to the $d$th syzygy being projective in some or every projective resolution.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Free resolutions of bounded length over a local ring
theorems.hypotheses: $R$ is local, $M$ arbitrary and $d$ nonnegative.
theorems.statement: Projective dimension at most $d$ is equivalent to existence of a free resolution of length at most $d$, since all projectives are free over a local ring.
theorems.proof: Projective dimension at most $d$ is equivalent to existence of a free resolution of length at most $d$, since all projectives are free over a local ring.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Finite projective resolutions over a Noetherian ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be finite over Noetherian $R$ and $d$ nonnegative.
theorems.statement: One has projective dimension at most $d$ exactly when there is a resolution of length at most $d$ by finite projectives. Finite syzygies can be chosen at every step.
theorems.proof: One has projective dimension at most $d$ exactly when there is a resolution of length at most $d$ by finite projectives. Finite syzygies can be chosen at every step.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Bounded finite free resolutions in the local Noetherian case
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be finite over Noetherian local $R$ and $d$ nonnegative.
theorems.statement: Projective dimension at most $d$ is equivalent to having a finite free resolution of length at most $d$.
theorems.proof: Projective dimension at most $d$ is equivalent to having a finite free resolution of length at most $d$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Ext characterization of a projective dimension bound
theorems.hypotheses: Take an $R$-module $M$ and $n\ge0$.
theorems.statement: The bound $\operatorname{pd}_R(M)\le n$ holds exactly when $\operatorname{Ext}^{n+1}_R(M,N)=0$ for every $N$, equivalently when all such Ext groups in degrees above $n$ vanish.
theorems.proof: The bound $\operatorname{pd}_R(M)\le n$ holds exactly when $\operatorname{Ext}^{n+1}_R(M,N)=0$ for every $N$, equivalently when all such Ext groups in degrees above $n$ vanish.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Projective dimension estimates in a short exact sequence
theorems.hypotheses: Let $0\to L\to M\to N\to0$ be exact and $n\ge0$. Write $a,b,c$ for the respective projective dimensions.
theorems.statement: If $b\le n$ and $c\le n+1$ then $a\le n$. If $a,c\le n$ then $b\le n$. If $a\le n$ and $b\le n+1$ then $c\le n+1$.
theorems.proof: If $b\le n$ and $c\le n+1$ then $a\le n$. If $a,c\le n$ then $b\le n$. If $a\le n$ and $b\le n+1$ then $c\le n+1$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: A well-ordered filtration preserves a projective dimension bound
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be the union of submodules $M_e$ well-ordered by inclusion, and assume each $M_e/\bigcup_{e'<e}M_{e'}$ has projective dimension at most $n$.
theorems.statement: Then $\operatorname{pd}_R(M)\le n$.
theorems.proof: Then $\operatorname{pd}_R(M)\le n$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Cyclic modules test global dimension
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $n\ge0$ for a ring $R$.
theorems.statement: Global dimension at most $n$ is equivalent to projective dimension at most $n$ for all finite modules, and also to the same bound just for all cyclic modules $R/I$.
theorems.proof: Global dimension at most $n$ is equivalent to projective dimension at most $n$ for all finite modules, and also to the same bound just for all cyclic modules $R/I$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Finite free resolutions over a regular local ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be regular local of dimension $d$ and $M$ nonzero finite of depth $e$.
theorems.statement: There exists a resolution of $M$ by finite free modules of length at most $d-e$. In particular every $R$-module has projective dimension at most $d$.
theorems.proof: There exists a resolution of $M$ by finite free modules of length at most $d-e$. In particular every $R$-module has projective dimension at most $d$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Global dimension at maximal ideals
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian and $n\ge0$.
theorems.statement: Global dimension is at most $n$ exactly when all localizations $R_{\mathfrak m}$ at maximal ideals have global dimension at most $n$. The bound is uniform in $\mathfrak m$.
theorems.proof: Global dimension is at most $n$ exactly when all localizations $R_{\mathfrak m}$ at maximal ideals have global dimension at most $n$. The bound is uniform in $\mathfrak m$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Embedding dimension bounds the projective dimension of the residue field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,k)$ be Noetherian local.
theorems.statement: One has $\operatorname{pd}_R(k)\ge\dim_k(\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2)$, allowing infinite projective dimension.
theorems.proof: One has $\operatorname{pd}_R(k)\ge\dim_k(\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2)$, allowing infinite projective dimension.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Finite residue-field projective dimension is bounded by Krull dimension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,k)$ be Noetherian local with $\operatorname{pd}_R(k)=n<\infty$.
theorems.statement: Then $n\le\dim(R)$.
theorems.proof: Then $n\le\dim(R)$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Homological characterizations of regular local rings
theorems.hypotheses: For Noetherian local $(R,\mathfrak m,k)$ consider the residue field as an $R$-module.
theorems.statement: Finite projective dimension of $k$, finite global dimension of $R$ and regularity of $R$ are equivalent. When they hold the global dimension equals both $\dim R$ and $\dim_k\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$.
theorems.proof: Finite projective dimension of $k$, finite global dimension of $R$ and regularity of $R$ are equivalent. When they hold the global dimension equals both $\dim R$ and $\dim_k\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Regularity descends along flat local maps
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)\to S$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Assume $S$ regular and the map flat.
theorems.statement: Then $R$ is regular local.
theorems.proof: Then $R$ is regular local.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Regular base and regular closed fibre
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)\to S$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Assume $R$ regular, the map flat, and $S/\mathfrak mS$ regular.
theorems.statement: Then $S$ is regular local.
theorems.proof: Then $S$ is regular local.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Cohen–Macaulayness with zero-dimensional closed fibre
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)\to S$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Assume $R$ Cohen–Macaulay and either $S$ finite flat over $R$, or $S$ flat over $R$ with $\dim S\le\dim R$.
theorems.statement: Then $S$ is Cohen–Macaulay and $\dim S=\dim R$.
theorems.proof: Then $S$ is Cohen–Macaulay and $\dim S=\dim R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Dimension inequality and the catenary dimension formula
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\subseteq S$ be domains with $R$ Noetherian and $S$ finite type over $R$. Choose $\mathfrak q\subset S$ over $\mathfrak p\subset R$. Write $t$ for the transcendence degree of the fraction-field extension.
theorems.statement: Then $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\kappa(\mathfrak q)\le\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)+t$. Equality holds if $R$ is universally catenary.
theorems.proof: Then $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\kappa(\mathfrak q)\le\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)+t$. Equality holds if $R$ is universally catenary.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Height-one fibres for a generically finite extension
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $A\subseteq B$ domains, $A$ Noetherian, $B$ finite type over $A$, with finite fraction-field extension. Let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ have height one.
theorems.statement: There are finitely many primes of $B$ over $\mathfrak p$, possibly none, and each has height one.
theorems.proof: There are finitely many primes of $B$ over $\mathfrak p$, possibly none, and each has height one.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Maximal localizations of affine space
theorems.hypotheses: Take a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ for a field $k$.
theorems.statement: Its local ring is regular of dimension $n$. The ideal $\mathfrak m$ is generated by $n$ elements in the polynomial ring itself.
theorems.proof: Its local ring is regular of dimension $n$. The ideal $\mathfrak m$ is generated by $n$ elements in the polynomial ring itself.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Global dimension of a polynomial ring over a field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$.
theorems.statement: It is regular, of global dimension $n$, and each localization at a maximal ideal has dimension $n$.
theorems.proof: It is regular, of global dimension $n$, and each localization at a maximal ideal has dimension $n$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Lengths of saturated prime intervals in affine space
theorems.hypotheses: Take $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak q$ in a finite-variable polynomial ring over a field.
theorems.statement: Each maximal prime chain from $\mathfrak p$ to $\mathfrak q$ has length $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)-\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)$.
theorems.proof: Each maximal prime chain from $\mathfrak p$ to $\mathfrak q$ has length $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)-\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Equidimensional prime chains in an affine domain
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be a finite type domain over a field.
theorems.statement: Each localization at a maximal ideal has dimension $\dim S$, and all maximal chains of prime ideals in $S$ have that length.
theorems.proof: Each localization at a maximal ideal has dimension $\dim S$, and all maximal chains of prime ideals in $S$ have that length.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Computing topological dimension at an affine point
theorems.hypotheses: Let $x$ correspond to $\mathfrak p$ in the spectrum $X$ of a finite type $k$-algebra. Here $\dim_x X$ is the infimum of dimensions of open neighbourhoods.
theorems.statement: It equals the largest dimension among irreducible components containing $x$, and the minimum of $\dim S_{\mathfrak m}$ over maximal ideals containing $\mathfrak p$.
theorems.proof: It equals the largest dimension among irreducible components containing $x$, and the minimum of $\dim S_{\mathfrak m}$ over maximal ideals containing $\mathfrak p$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Dimension at a closed point of an affine variety
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be finite type over a field and let $x$ correspond to a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$.
theorems.statement: Then $\dim_x\operatorname{Spec}(S)=\dim S_{\mathfrak m}$.
theorems.proof: Then $\dim_x\operatorname{Spec}(S)=\dim S_{\mathfrak m}$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Equidimensional summands of a Cohen–Macaulay algebra over a field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be finite type over a field and Cohen–Macaulay.
theorems.statement: Its spectrum decomposes into a finite disjoint union of clopen pure-dimensional pieces. On the piece of dimension $d$ all maximal ideals have height $d$.
theorems.proof: Its spectrum decomposes into a finite disjoint union of clopen pure-dimensional pieces. On the piece of dimension $d$ all maximal ideals have height $d$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Separating finitely many monomials by a positive weight
theorems.hypotheses: Take a finite nonempty set of exponent vectors $\nu\in\mathbf N^n$.
theorems.statement: Positive weights $e_i$ can be chosen successively sufficiently large relative to the weights on their right so that $\sum e_i\nu_i$ are distinct for distinct vectors. This is also obtained by radix encoding with a base larger than every exponent.
theorems.proof: Positive weights $e_i$ can be chosen successively sufficiently large relative to the weights on their right so that $\sum e_i\nu_i$ are distinct for distinct vectors. This is also obtained by radix encoding with a base larger than every exponent.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A triangular substitution with scalar leading coefficient
theorems.hypotheses: Let $g\in R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ be nonconstant and take $e_n=1$, with earlier positive weights successively sufficiently large.
theorems.statement: Substituting $x_i+x_n^{e_i}$ for each $x_i$ with $i<n$ makes the highest $x_n$-term have positive degree and leading coefficient one of the nonzero scalar coefficients of $g$.
theorems.proof: Substituting $x_i+x_n^{e_i}$ for each $x_i$ with $i<n$ makes the highest $x_n$-term have positive degree and leading coefficient one of the nonzero scalar coefficients of $g$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: One polynomial relation removes one algebra generator up to finiteness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/I$ with $I$ nonzero and proper and $k$ a field.
theorems.statement: There are $n-1$ polynomials $y_i$ such that $S$ is finite over the subalgebra generated by their images. They may be chosen with coefficients in the image of $\mathbf Z$.
theorems.proof: There are $n-1$ polynomials $y_i$ such that $S$ is finite over the subalgebra generated by their images. They may be chosen with coefficients in the image of $\mathbf Z$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Noether normalization over an arbitrary field
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $S=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/I$ is nonzero over a field $k$.
theorems.statement: If $r=\dim S$, there exist $r$ algebraically independent elements in $S$ such that $S$ is finite over their polynomial subalgebra. Their representatives in the chosen polynomial ring may have coefficients in the image of $\mathbf Z$.
theorems.proof: If $r=\dim S$, there exist $r$ algebraically independent elements in $S$ such that $S$ is finite over their polynomial subalgebra. Their representatives in the chosen polynomial ring may have coefficients in the image of $\mathbf Z$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Noether normalization near a chosen point
theorems.hypotheses: Take $x$ in the spectrum of a finite type $k$-algebra $S$ and put $d=\dim_x\operatorname{Spec}(S)$.
theorems.statement: There is a principal neighbourhood $D(g)$ of $x$ with $\dim S_g=d$ admitting a finite injective map $k[y_1,\ldots,y_d]\to S_g$.
theorems.proof: There is a principal neighbourhood $D(g)$ of $x$ with $\dim S_g=d$ admitting a finite injective map $k[y_1,\ldots,y_d]\to S_g$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Noether normalization adapted to a prime of affine space
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathfrak q$ be a prime in $k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ and $r=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(\mathfrak q)$.
theorems.statement: There exists a finite ring map $k[y_1,\ldots,y_n]\to k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ whose inverse image of $\mathfrak q$ is exactly $(y_{r+1},\ldots,y_n)$.
theorems.proof: There exists a finite ring map $k[y_1,\ldots,y_n]\to k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ whose inverse image of $\mathfrak q$ is exactly $(y_{r+1},\ldots,y_n)$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Noether normalization over a domain after localization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be injective of finite type with $R$ a domain.
theorems.statement: It factors through injections $R\to R[y_1,\ldots,y_d]\to B\to S$ with $B$ finite over the polynomial ring and $B_f\simeq S_f$ for some nonzero $f\in R$.
theorems.proof: It factors through injections $R\to R[y_1,\ldots,y_d]\to B\to S$ with $B$ finite over the polynomial ring and $B_f\simeq S_f$ for some nonzero $f\in R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Dimension of an affine domain equals transcendence degree
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be a finite type domain over a field $k$, with fraction field $K$.
theorems.statement: Then $\dim S=\operatorname{trdeg}_k K$. Every maximal localization has this same dimension.
theorems.proof: Then $\dim S=\operatorname{trdeg}_k K$. Every maximal localization has this same dimension.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Residue transcendence degree decreases under strict specialization
theorems.hypotheses: Take a strict inclusion of primes $\mathfrak q\subsetneq\mathfrak q'$ in a finite type $k$-algebra.
theorems.statement: Then $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(\mathfrak q')<\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(\mathfrak q)$.
theorems.proof: Then $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(\mathfrak q')<\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(\mathfrak q)$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Height plus residue transcendence degree at a point
theorems.hypotheses: Let $x$ correspond to $\mathfrak p$ in $X=\operatorname{Spec}(S)$ for a finite type $k$-algebra. Use neighbourhood dimension at $x$.
theorems.statement: Then $\dim_x X=\dim S_{\mathfrak p}+\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.
theorems.proof: Then $\dim_x X=\dim S_{\mathfrak p}+\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Local dimension drop under a closed immersion
theorems.hypotheses: For a surjection $T\to S$ of finite type $k$-algebras, take corresponding points $y,x$ with primes $\mathfrak q,\mathfrak p$.
theorems.statement: Then $\dim_y\operatorname{Spec}(T)-\dim_x\operatorname{Spec}(S)=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)-\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)$ because the residue fields agree.
theorems.proof: Then $\dim_y\operatorname{Spec}(T)-\dim_x\operatorname{Spec}(S)=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)-\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)$ because the residue fields agree.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Krull dimension under field extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be a finite type $k$-algebra and $K/k$ any field extension.
theorems.statement: The Krull dimensions of $S$ and $K\otimes_k S$ are equal.
theorems.proof: The Krull dimensions of $S$ and $K\otimes_k S$ are equal.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Topological dimension at a point under field extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be finite type over $k$, and $x_K\in\operatorname{Spec}(K\otimes_k S)$ over $x\in\operatorname{Spec}(S)$ for an extension $K/k$.
theorems.statement: The neighbourhood dimensions agree at $x_K$ and $x$. Individual heights of the corresponding primes can differ.
theorems.proof: The neighbourhood dimensions agree at $x_K$ and $x$. Individual heights of the corresponding primes can differ.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Compensating changes of height and residue transcendence degree
theorems.hypotheses: Put $A=K\otimes_k S$ for a finite type $k$-algebra $S$ and field extension $K/k$. Let $\mathfrak Q$ lie over $\mathfrak q$.
theorems.statement: The dimension of the local fibre ring at $\mathfrak Q$ equals $\dim A_{\mathfrak Q}-\dim S_{\mathfrak q}$ and $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(\mathfrak q)-\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(\mathfrak Q)$. For each $\mathfrak q$ a point above it can be chosen with this number zero.
theorems.proof: The dimension of the local fibre ring at $\mathfrak Q$ equals $\dim A_{\mathfrak Q}-\dim S_{\mathfrak q}$ and $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(\mathfrak q)-\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(\mathfrak Q)$. For each $\mathfrak q$ a point above it can be chosen with this number zero.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Hilbert polynomial and the dimension of a standard graded algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S_0=k$ be a field and $S$ generated by finitely many degree-one elements. Let $P(d)=\dim_k S_d$ for large $d$, extending to a polynomial with convention $\deg(0)=-1$.
theorems.statement: The irrelevant ideal $\mathfrak m=S_+$ is maximal and contains all minimal primes, which are homogeneous. The local ring at $\mathfrak m$ has the same Hilbert function as $S$, and $\dim S=\dim_{\mathfrak m}\operatorname{Spec}(S)=1+\deg P$.
theorems.proof: The irrelevant ideal $\mathfrak m=S_+$ is maximal and contains all minimal primes, which are homogeneous. The local ring at $\mathfrak m$ has the same Hilbert function as $S$, and $\dim S=\dim_{\mathfrak m}\operatorname{Spec}(S)=1+\deg P$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Generic freeness over a Noetherian domain
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a Noetherian domain, $S$ a finite type $R$-algebra and $M$ a finite $S$-module.
theorems.statement: Some nonzero $f\in R$ makes $M_f$ free over $R_f$. Its free rank need not be finite.
theorems.proof: Some nonzero $f\in R$ makes $M_f$ free over $R_f$. Its free rank need not be finite.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Generic freeness for finitely presented data
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a domain, $S$ a finitely presented $R$-algebra and $M$ a finitely presented $S$-module.
theorems.statement: Then $M_f$ is free over $R_f$ for some nonzero $f\in R$. No Noetherian hypothesis on $R$ is needed.
theorems.proof: Then $M_f$ is free over $R_f$ for some nonzero $f\in R$. No Noetherian hypothesis on $R$ is needed.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Generic freeness and presentation over an arbitrary domain
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a domain, $S$ a finite type $R$-algebra, and $M$ finite over $S$.
theorems.statement: For one nonzero $f\in R$ both $S_f$ and $M_f$ are free over $R_f$, while $S_f$ is finitely presented as an $R_f$-algebra and $M_f$ finitely presented over $S_f$.
theorems.proof: For one nonzero $f\in R$ both $S_f$ and $M_f$ are free over $R_f$, while $S_f$ is finitely presented as an $R_f$-algebra and $M_f$ finitely presented over $S_f$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: The generic freeness and presentation locus in an exact sequence
theorems.hypotheses: For $R\to S$ write $U(M)$ for the union of the $D(f)$ where $S_f,M_f$ are $R_f$-free, $S_f$ is an $R_f$-algebra of finite presentation and $M_f$ is finitely presented over $S_f$. Take an exact sequence $0\to L\to M\to N\to0$.
theorems.statement: Then $U(L)\cap U(N)\subseteq U(M)$. The sequence splits as modules over the localized base wherever its quotient is free there.
theorems.proof: Then $U(L)\cap U(N)\subseteq U(M)$. The sequence splits as modules over the localized base wherever its quotient is free there.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Restriction of the generic freeness and presentation locus
theorems.hypotheses: Write $U(M)$ for the union of principal opens where the algebra and module are base-free and respectively finitely presented as algebra and module. Let $f\in R$.
theorems.statement: For the data localized at $f$, this locus is $D(f)\cap U(M)$ inside $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$.
theorems.proof: For the data localized at $f$, this locus is $D(f)\cap U(M)$ inside $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Density of the generic freeness and presentation locus is local on a dense open
theorems.hypotheses: Let $U(M)$ denote the locus defined by local base-freeness of $S,M$ and their finite presentations as algebra and module. Suppose a dense open of $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ is covered by $D(f_i)$ where the corresponding locus of the localized data is dense in each $D(f_i)$.
theorems.statement: Then $U(M)$ is dense in the whole spectrum.
theorems.proof: Then $U(M)$ is dense in the whole spectrum.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Generic freeness over a reduced base
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be reduced, $S$ finite type over $R$, and $M$ finite over $S$.
theorems.statement: On a dense open of $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ each point has a principal neighbourhood $D(f)$ where $S_f,M_f$ are free over $R_f$, $S_f$ is a finitely presented $R_f$-algebra and $M_f$ a finitely presented $S_f$-module.
theorems.proof: On a dense open of $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ each point has a principal neighbourhood $D(f)$ where $S_f,M_f$ are free over $R_f$, $S_f$ is a finitely presented $R_f$-algebra and $M_f$ a finitely presented $S_f$-module.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: A one-dimensional birational local overring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a Noetherian local domain other than a field, with fraction field $K$.
theorems.statement: There exists a one-dimensional Noetherian local overring in $K$ dominating $R$ and essentially of finite type over $R$.
theorems.proof: There exists a one-dimensional Noetherian local overring in $K$ dominating $R$ and essentially of finite type over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Four alternatives for a Noetherian local ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be Noetherian local.
theorems.statement: Exactly one alternative holds. It is Artinian, regular of dimension one, or of depth at least two, or it admits a finite nonisomorphic map $R\to B$ with $B\ne0$, kernel and cokernel killed by a power of $\mathfrak m$, and $\mathfrak m\notin\operatorname{Ass}_R(B)$.
theorems.proof: Exactly one alternative holds. It is Artinian, regular of dimension one, or of depth at least two, or it admits a finite nonisomorphic map $R\to B$ with $B\ne0$, kernel and cokernel killed by a power of $\mathfrak m$, and $\mathfrak m\notin\operatorname{Ass}_R(B)$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: A finite modification in dimension one
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,k)$ be a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring of embedding dimension greater than one.
theorems.statement: Some finite map $R\to B$ is not an isomorphism, has kernel and cokernel killed by a power of $\mathfrak m$, and satisfies $\mathfrak m\notin\operatorname{Ass}_R(B)$.
theorems.proof: Some finite map $R\to B$ is not an isomorphism, has kernel and cokernel killed by a power of $\mathfrak m$, and satisfies $\mathfrak m\notin\operatorname{Ass}_R(B)$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Repeated modification of a nonreduced double line
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R=k[[x,y]]/(y^2)$ over a field $k$.
theorems.statement: This one-dimensional Cohen–Macaulay ring embeds finitely into $k[[x,z]]/(z^2)$ by $y\mapsto xz$. The extension adjoins $y/x$, and iteration adjoins $y/x^n$ in the total quotient ring.
theorems.proof: This one-dimensional Cohen–Macaulay ring embeds finitely into $k[[x,z]]/(z^2)$ by $y\mapsto xz$. The extension adjoins $y/x$, and iteration adjoins $y/x^n$ in the total quotient ring.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: A domain with nonreduced completion
theorems.hypotheses: Take $k$ of characteristic $p$ with $[k:k^p]$ infinite. Inside $k[[x]]$, let $A$ consist of series with all coefficients in a single finite extension of $k^p$ inside $k$, depending on the series. Choose $f\in k[[x]]\setminus A$.
theorems.statement: The ring $A$ is a DVR with completion $k[[x]]$ and infinite purely inseparable extension on taking fraction fields. The finite algebra $A[f]$ is a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain with nonreduced completion. Indeed $f^p\in A$, and $f$ belongs to the completed coefficient ring.
theorems.proof: The ring $A$ is a DVR with completion $k[[x]]$ and infinite purely inseparable extension on taking fraction fields. The finite algebra $A[f]$ is a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain with nonreduced completion. Indeed $f^p\in A$, and $f$ belongs to the completed coefficient ring.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Bounding a quotient length in rank at most r
theorems.hypotheses: For a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain $R$ with fraction field $K$, let $M\subseteq K^r$ be any submodule and choose nonzero $x\in R$.
theorems.statement: Then $\ell_R(M/xM)\le r\ell_R(R/xR)<\infty$, even without finite generation of $M$.
theorems.proof: Then $\ell_R(M/xM)\le r\ell_R(R/xR)<\infty$, even without finite generation of $M$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Closed fibres of an algebra in a finite extension of fraction fields
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $R\subseteq S$ are domains, $R$ is Noetherian local of dimension one and their fraction fields form a finite extension.
theorems.statement: All primes of $S$ over the maximal ideal of $R$ are maximal, there are finitely many, and their residue extensions are finite. The algebra need not be finite type.
theorems.proof: All primes of $S$ over the maximal ideal of $R$ are maximal, there are finitely many, and their residue extensions are finite. The algebra need not be finite type.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Finite length of torsion quotients in dimension one
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a Noetherian domain of dimension one and $M$ any submodule of $\operatorname{Frac}(R)^r$ for finite $r$.
theorems.statement: For each nonzero $x\in R$, $M/xM$ has finite length over $R$.
theorems.proof: For each nonzero $x\in R$, $M/xM$ has finite length over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Krull–Akizuki theorem
theorems.hypotheses: Take a one-dimensional Noetherian domain $R$ and a finite field extension $L/\operatorname{Frac}(R)$.
theorems.statement: Every intermediate ring $R\subseteq A\subseteq L$ is Noetherian. Finiteness as an $R$-module is not part of the conclusion.
theorems.proof: Every intermediate ring $R\subseteq A\subseteq L$ is Noetherian. Finiteness as an $R$-module is not part of the conclusion.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Dominating DVR with prescribed finitely generated fraction field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a Noetherian local domain other than a field and $L/\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ a finitely generated field extension.
theorems.statement: There is a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $L$ dominating $R$.
theorems.proof: There is a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $L$ dominating $R$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Existence of factorizations from ACC on principal ideals
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose the domain $R$ satisfies the ascending chain condition on principal ideals.
theorems.statement: Every nonzero nonunit of $R$ is a finite product of irreducibles. Continued strict factorization would otherwise give a strictly increasing chain of principal ideals.
theorems.proof: Every nonzero nonunit of $R$ is a finite product of irreducibles. Continued strict factorization would otherwise give a strictly increasing chain of principal ideals.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Primeness of irreducibles detects unique factorization
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose each nonzero nonunit of a domain has a factorization into irreducibles.
theorems.statement: The domain is a UFD exactly when each irreducible element is prime. Primeness allows cancellation up to associates in any two factorizations.
theorems.proof: The domain is a UFD exactly when each irreducible element is prime. Primeness allows cancellation up to associates in any two factorizations.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Nagata’s localization test for unique factorization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $U$ be a multiplicative set generated by prime elements of a domain $A$.
theorems.statement: An irreducible $x$ remains irreducible or becomes a unit. It is prime in $A$ exactly when its image is prime or a unit. Thus $A$ is a UFD exactly when factorization into irreducibles exists in $A$ and $U^{-1}A$ is a UFD.
theorems.proof: An irreducible $x$ remains irreducible or becomes a unit. It is prime in $A$ exactly when its image is prime or a unit. Thus $A$ is a UFD exactly when factorization into irreducibles exists in $A$ and $U^{-1}A$ is a UFD.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: ACC on principal ideals in a UFD
theorems.hypotheses: Assume the ring is a unique factorization domain.
theorems.statement: An ascending chain of principal ideals stabilizes. A proper divisibility step between nonzero generators decreases the total number of irreducible factors.
theorems.proof: An ascending chain of principal ideals stabilizes. A proper divisibility step between nonzero generators decreases the total number of irreducible factors.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: ACC on principal ideals of a polynomial ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a domain with ACC on principal ideals.
theorems.statement: A polynomial ring over $R$ also satisfies ACC on principal ideals. In an ascending chain the total degree of nonzero generators eventually stabilizes, leaving only scalar factors.
theorems.proof: A polynomial ring over $R$ also satisfies ACC on principal ideals. In an ascending chain the total degree of nonzero generators eventually stabilizes, leaving only scalar factors.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Polynomial algebras over a UFD
theorems.hypotheses: Take a unique factorization domain $R$.
theorems.statement: A polynomial ring over $R$ is a UFD. In particular every $k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ over a field is a UFD.
theorems.proof: A polynomial ring over $R$ is a UFD. In particular every $k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ over a field is a UFD.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Factors of a principal ideal generated by a nonzerodivisor
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I,J$ be nonzero ideals with $IJ=fA$ for a nonzerodivisor $f$ of $A$.
theorems.statement: Both $I$ and $J$ are finite ideals and finite locally free $A$-modules of rank one.
theorems.proof: Both $I$ and $J$ are finite ideals and finite locally free $A$-modules of rank one.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Integral closure in a finite extension over a one-dimensional domain
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a Noetherian domain of dimension one and $L/\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ finite. Write $B$ for its integral closure in $L$.
theorems.statement: Then $B$ is Dedekind. The map $\operatorname{Spec}(B)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ is surjective with finite fibres and finite residue field extensions.
theorems.proof: Then $B$ is Dedekind. The map $\operatorname{Spec}(B)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ is surjective with finite fibres and finite residue field extensions.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Six tests for an isolated point over a field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be a finite type $k$-algebra over a field. Put $F=\operatorname{Spec}S$ and fix $x\in F$.
theorems.statement: The following conditions are equivalent at $x$. It is isolated. Its local ring is finite over the base field. A principal open in the fibre is the singleton $\{x\}$. The dimension of the fibre at $x$ is zero. Its local ring has dimension zero and $x$ is closed, equivalently the local ring has dimension zero and the residue extension is finite. In this case its local ring is a direct product factor of $S$ and is the localization at any principal singleton neighbourhood.
theorems.proof: The following conditions are equivalent at $x$. It is isolated. Its local ring is finite over the base field. A principal open in the fibre is the singleton $\{x\}$. The dimension of the fibre at $x$ is zero. Its local ring has dimension zero and $x$ is closed, equivalently the local ring has dimension zero and the residue extension is finite. In this case its local ring is a direct product factor of $S$ and is the localization at any principal singleton neighbourhood.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Isolated points and six fibre tests
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be finite type, let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ lie over $\mathfrak p\subset R$, and let $x$ be the corresponding point of the fibre $F=\operatorname{Spec}(S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$.
theorems.statement: The following conditions are equivalent at $x$. It is isolated. Its local ring is finite over the base field. A principal open in the fibre is the singleton $\{x\}$. The dimension of the fibre at $x$ is zero. Its local ring has dimension zero and $x$ is closed, equivalently the local ring has dimension zero and the residue extension is finite.
theorems.proof: The following conditions are equivalent at $x$. It is isolated. Its local ring is finite over the base field. A principal open in the fibre is the singleton $\{x\}$. The dimension of the fibre at $x$ is zero. Its local ring has dimension zero and $x$ is closed, equivalently the local ring has dimension zero and the residue extension is finite.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Quasi-finiteness above one base point
theorems.hypotheses: Take a finite type map $R\to S$ and a prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R$.
theorems.statement: Quasi-finiteness at all points above $\mathfrak p$ is equivalent both to finite dimension of the fibre algebra over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and to finiteness of its prime spectrum as a set.
theorems.proof: Quasi-finiteness at all points above $\mathfrak p$ is equivalent both to finite dimension of the fibre algebra over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and to finiteness of its prime spectrum as a set.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Localizing source and base around a quasi-finite point
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be finite type, let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ lie over $\mathfrak p\subset R$, and let $x$ be the corresponding point of the fibre $F=\operatorname{Spec}(S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$. Choose $f\notin\mathfrak p$ and $g\notin\mathfrak q$.
theorems.statement: Quasi-finiteness at $\mathfrak q$ is equivalent to quasi-finiteness of $R_f\to S_{fg}$ at its image prime.
theorems.proof: Quasi-finiteness at $\mathfrak q$ is equivalent to quasi-finiteness of $R_f\to S_{fg}$ at its image prime.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Quasi-finiteness after base change and quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Take a compatible square from a finite type map $R\to S$ to $R'\to S'$ with $S\otimes_R R'\to S'$ surjective. Fix $\mathfrak q'$ over $\mathfrak q$.
theorems.statement: Quasi-finiteness of $R\to S$ at $\mathfrak q$ gives quasi-finiteness of $R'\to S'$ at $\mathfrak q'$.
theorems.proof: Quasi-finiteness of $R\to S$ at $\mathfrak q$ gives quasi-finiteness of $R'\to S'$ at $\mathfrak q'$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Composition of quasi-finite maps
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $A\to B$ and $B\to C$ are quasi-finite.
theorems.statement: Then $A\to C$ is quasi-finite.
theorems.proof: Then $A\to C$ is quasi-finite.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Base change of the quasi-finite locus
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be finite type, $R\to B$ arbitrary and $T=S\otimes_R B$.
theorems.statement: The quasi-finite locus of $B\to T$ is the inverse image of that of $R\to S$. In particular quasi-finiteness ascends under every base change and descends if $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is surjective.
theorems.proof: The quasi-finite locus of $B\to T$ is the inverse image of that of $R\to S$. In particular quasi-finiteness ascends under every base change and descends if $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is surjective.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Quasi-finiteness from a finite type composite
theorems.hypotheses: For $A\to B\to C$ suppose $A\to C$ is finite type and quasi-finite at $\mathfrak r\subset C$.
theorems.statement: Then $B\to C$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak r$.
theorems.proof: Then $B\to C$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak r$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Finiteness near a minimal prime with a finite fibre
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be finite type over $R$ and $\mathfrak p$ a minimal prime of $R$ with finitely many primes above it.
theorems.statement: For some $g\notin\mathfrak p$ the algebra $S_g$ is finite over $R_g$.
theorems.proof: For some $g\notin\mathfrak p$ the algebra $S_g$ is finite over $R_g$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Making an element integral with a leading coefficient
theorems.hypotheses: Let $t\in S$ satisfy $\sum_{i=0}^n a_it^i=0$ over $R$ with $n\geq1$.
theorems.statement: The product $a_nt$ is integral over $R$.
theorems.proof: The product $a_nt$ is integral over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Integral remainder after polynomial subtraction
theorems.hypotheses: For $\phi:R[X]\to S$ take $t$ integral over $R[X]$ and monic $P$ with $t\phi(P)\in\phi(R[X])$.
theorems.statement: Some $Q\in R[X]$ makes $t-\phi(Q)$ integral over $R$.
theorems.proof: Some $Q\in R[X]$ makes $t-\phi(Q)$ integral over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Clearing a leading coefficient before polynomial subtraction
theorems.hypotheses: For $\phi:R[X]\to S$ let $t$ be integral over $R[X]$ and $P=\sum_{i=0}^d a_iX^i$ with $t\phi(P)\in\phi(R[X])$.
theorems.statement: There exist $n\geq0$ and $Q\in R[X]$ such that $\phi(a_d)^nt-\phi(Q)$ is integral over $R$.
theorems.proof: There exist $n\geq0$ and $Q\in R[X]$ such that $\phi(a_d)^nt-\phi(Q)$ is integral over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Leading coefficient in the conductor
