theorems.hypotheses: Let $\phi:R[X]\to S$ be finite with the image of $R$ integrally closed in $S$. Let $J=\{s\in S\mid sS\subseteq\phi(R[X])\}$ and write $P=\sum_{i=0}^d a_iX^i$. Suppose $u\phi(P)\in J$.
theorems.statement: For some $n\geq0$, $u\phi(a_d)^n\in J$.
theorems.proof: For some $n\geq0$, $u\phi(a_d)^n\in J$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: All coefficients in the radical of the conductor
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\phi:R[X]\to S$ be finite with the image of $R$ integrally closed in $S$. Let $J=\{s\in S\mid sS\subseteq\phi(R[X])\}$ and write $P=\sum_{i=0}^d a_iX^i$. Suppose $u\phi(P)\in\sqrt J$.
theorems.statement: Each $u\phi(a_i)$ lies in $\sqrt J$.
theorems.proof: Each $u\phi(a_i)$ lies in $\sqrt J$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: No quasi-finite points over a transcendental direction
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\subseteq S$ be domains and $x\in S$ strongly transcendental over $R$, with $S$ finite over $R[x]$.
theorems.statement: The map $R\to S$ has empty quasi-finite locus.
theorems.proof: The map $R\to S$ has empty quasi-finite locus.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Zariski’s Main Theorem in one variable
theorems.hypotheses: For $S=R[X]/I$, take $\mathfrak q$ a quasi-finite point over $R$, and let $C$ be the integral closure of the image of $R$ in $S$.
theorems.statement: Some $g\in C\setminus\mathfrak q$ makes $C_g\to S_g$ an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: Some $g\in C\setminus\mathfrak q$ makes $C_g\to S_g$ an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Zariski’s Main Theorem for a finite type algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be a finite type $R$-algebra, $C$ the integral closure of the image of $R$ in $S$, and $\mathfrak q$ a quasi-finite point.
theorems.statement: There is $g\in C\setminus\mathfrak q$ with $C_g\cong S_g$ by the inclusion.
theorems.proof: There is $g\in C\setminus\mathfrak q$ with $C_g\cong S_g$ by the inclusion.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Length inequality over a one-dimensional local domain
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\subset B$ be finite type between domains with $A$ local Noetherian of dimension one and finite fraction extension $L/K$. Choose $0\ne x\in\mathfrak m_A$.
theorems.statement: The ring $B$ is semilocal. The sum of $\operatorname{ord}_{B_{\mathfrak n}}(x)[\kappa(\mathfrak n):\kappa(\mathfrak m_A)]$ over maximal ideals above the closed point is at most $[L:K]\operatorname{ord}_A(x)$, with equality precisely when $B$ is finite. Orders are lengths of principal quotients. If $B$ is a field its closed fibre is empty and the sum is zero.
theorems.proof: The ring $B$ is semilocal. The sum of $\operatorname{ord}_{B_{\mathfrak n}}(x)[\kappa(\mathfrak n):\kappa(\mathfrak m_A)]$ over maximal ideals above the closed point is at most $[L:K]\operatorname{ord}_A(x)$, with equality precisely when $B$ is finite. Orders are lengths of principal quotients. If $B$ is a field its closed fibre is empty and the sum is zero.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite-algebra presentation of an essentially finite type local algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)\to(S,\mathfrak n)$ be a local homomorphism. Assume the map essentially finite type, the residue extension finite and $\dim(S/\mathfrak mS)=0$.
theorems.statement: Then $S$ is a localization of a finite $R$-algebra.
theorems.proof: Then $S$ is a localization of a finite $R$-algebra.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A completed quasi-finite stalk splits from the completed base change
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be finite type, let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ lie over $\mathfrak p\subset R$, and let $x$ be the corresponding point of the fibre $F=\operatorname{Spec}(S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$. Suppose $R$ Noetherian and the map quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$.
theorems.statement: There is a decomposition $\widehat{R_{\mathfrak p}}\otimes_R S\cong\widehat{S_{\mathfrak q}}\times B$ as algebras over the completed base stalk.
theorems.proof: There is a decomposition $\widehat{R_{\mathfrak p}}\otimes_R S\cong\widehat{S_{\mathfrak q}}\times B$ as algebras over the completed base stalk.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite type descends under faithful flatness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be any ring map and $R\to R'$ faithfully flat. Set $S'=S\otimes_R R'$.
theorems.statement: Finite type of $R\to S$ is equivalent to finite type of $R'\to S'$.
theorems.proof: Finite type of $R\to S$ is equivalent to finite type of $R'\to S'$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite presentation descends under faithful flatness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be any ring map and $R\to R'$ faithfully flat. Set $S'=S\otimes_R R'$.
theorems.statement: Finite presentation of $R\to S$ is equivalent to finite presentation of $R'\to S'$.
theorems.proof: Finite presentation of $R\to S$ is equivalent to finite presentation of $R'\to S'$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Lifting a module from a localization of a quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Take $B=U^{-1}(R/I)$ for an ideal $I$ and a multiplicative set $U$.
theorems.statement: Every finite $B$-module comes from a finite $R$-module by tensor with $B$. Every finitely presented $B$-module comes in the same way from a finitely presented $R$-module.
theorems.proof: Every finite $B$-module comes from a finite $R$-module by tensor with $B$. Every finitely presented $B$-module comes in the same way from a finitely presented $R$-module.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A finite model of a localized module with a map to the original
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be an $R$-module and $U$ multiplicative. Suppose $U^{-1}M$ finite or finitely presented over $U^{-1}R$.
theorems.statement: There is an $R$-module $N$ with the corresponding finiteness and a map $N\to M$ that becomes an isomorphism after inverting $U$.
theorems.proof: There is an $R$-module $N$ with the corresponding finiteness and a map $N\to M$ that becomes an isomorphism after inverting $U$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A finite model of a stalk with a map to the original module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be an $R$-module and $\mathfrak p$ a prime with $M_{\mathfrak p}$ finite or finitely presented.
theorems.statement: There is a correspondingly finite or finitely presented $N$ over $R$ and $N\to M$ inducing an isomorphism at $\mathfrak p$.
theorems.proof: There is a correspondingly finite or finitely presented $N$ over $R$ and $N\to M$ inducing an isomorphism at $\mathfrak p$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Splitting a base component from an isomorphism of local rings
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $R\to S$ finitely presented and $R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$ an isomorphism at a prime over $\mathfrak p$.
theorems.statement: There exist $f\notin\mathfrak p$ and an $R_f$-algebra $C$ with $S_f\cong R_f\times C$.
theorems.proof: There exist $f\notin\mathfrak p$ and an $R_f$-algebra $C$ with $S_f\cong R_f\times C$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Spreading an isomorphism of local algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S,T$ be finitely presented $R$-algebras with $S_{\mathfrak q}\cong T_{\mathfrak r}$ as $R$-algebras.
theorems.statement: For some $f\notin\mathfrak q$, $g\notin\mathfrak r$, the principal localizations $S_f,T_g$ are isomorphic over $R$.
theorems.proof: For some $f\notin\mathfrak q$, $g\notin\mathfrak r$, the principal localizations $S_f,T_g$ are isomorphic over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite type detected modulo a nilpotent ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $I\subset R$ nilpotent and $S/IS$ finite type over $R/I$.
theorems.statement: Then $S$ is finite type over $R$.
theorems.proof: Then $S$ is finite type over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Surjectivity detected modulo a locally nilpotent ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Take an $R$-algebra map $S\to T$ with $T$ finite type over $R$. Suppose $I\subset R$ locally nilpotent and $S\to T/IT$ surjective.
theorems.statement: The homomorphism $S\to T$ is surjective.
theorems.proof: The homomorphism $S\to T$ is surjective.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A local isomorphism from a surjection and a flat quotient test
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S\to T$ be a surjective $R$-algebra map with $S$ finite type, $T$ finitely presented over $R$. At $\mathfrak q\supseteq IS$ assume $T_{\mathfrak q}$ is $R$-flat and $S_{\mathfrak q}/IS_{\mathfrak q}\to T_{\mathfrak q}/IT_{\mathfrak q}$ an isomorphism.
theorems.statement: Some $g\notin\mathfrak q$ gives $S_g\cong T_g$ via the given map.
theorems.proof: Some $g\notin\mathfrak q$ gives $S_g\cong T_g$ via the given map.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Isomorphism criterion after locally nilpotent reduction
theorems.hypotheses: For $I\subset R$ locally nilpotent, let $S\to T$ induce an isomorphism modulo $I$, with $S$ of finite type and $T$ flat of finite presentation over $R$.
theorems.statement: Then $S\to T$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: Then $S\to T$ is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Canonical filtered presentation of any algebra
theorems.hypotheses: For an $R$-algebra $A$ consider finitely presented $R$-algebras equipped with maps to $A$, and maps compatible with these.
theorems.statement: This category is filtered and the colimit of its source algebras is $A$.
theorems.proof: This category is filtered and the colimit of its source algebras is $A$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Directed presentation by finitely presented algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Take any $R$-algebra $A$.
theorems.statement: It is a directed colimit of finitely presented $R$-algebras, with surjective transitions available when $A$ is finite type.
theorems.proof: It is a directed colimit of finitely presented $R$-algebras, with surjective transitions available when $A$ is finite type.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Detecting presentation as a filtered colimit from a prescribed class
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a set of finitely presented $R$-algebras $\mathcal E$ and an $R$-algebra $B$.
theorems.statement: The algebra $B$ is a filtered colimit of objects of $\mathcal E$ precisely when every map from a finitely presented $R$-algebra into $B$ factors through an object of $\mathcal E$.
theorems.proof: The algebra $B$ is a filtered colimit of objects of $\mathcal E$ precisely when every map from a finitely presented $R$-algebra into $B$ factors through an object of $\mathcal E$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite-stage detection of module maps
theorems.hypotheses: Work with module maps over $A$ and a directed colimit $R=\operatorname{colim}R_i$ of $A$-algebras. Use the corresponding scalar extensions throughout.
theorems.statement: Equality after base change of two maps descends to some stage if the source is finitely generated. Surjectivity descends if the target is finitely generated. A map after base change lifts to some stage when the source is finitely presented. For a given map with finitely generated source and finitely presented target, becoming an isomorphism at the colimit implies becoming one at some stage.
theorems.proof: Equality after base change of two maps descends to some stage if the source is finitely generated. Surjectivity descends if the target is finitely generated. A map after base change lifts to some stage when the source is finitely presented. For a given map with finitely generated source and finitely presented target, becoming an isomorphism at the colimit implies becoming one at some stage.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite-stage detection of algebra maps
theorems.hypotheses: Work with algebra maps over $A$ and a directed colimit $R=\operatorname{colim}R_i$ of $A$-algebras. Use the corresponding scalar extensions throughout.
theorems.statement: Equality after base change of two maps descends to some stage if the source is finitely generated. Surjectivity descends if the target is finitely generated. A map after base change lifts to some stage when the source is finitely presented. For a given map with finitely generated source and finitely presented target, becoming an isomorphism at the colimit implies becoming one at some stage.
theorems.proof: Equality after base change of two maps descends to some stage if the source is finitely generated. Surjectivity descends if the target is finitely generated. A map after base change lifts to some stage when the source is finitely presented. For a given map with finitely generated source and finitely presented target, becoming an isomorphism at the colimit implies becoming one at some stage.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: The category of finitely presented modules over a directed colimit
theorems.hypotheses: Write $R=\operatorname{colim}_i R_i$ for a directed colimit of rings.
theorems.statement: A finitely presented object descends to a finitely presented object at some stage. Between two such models a morphism over $R$ descends after advancing the stage. Two stage maps equal over $R$ are equal at a later stage. This identifies the category of finitely presented modules with the filtered colimit of the stage categories.
theorems.proof: A finitely presented object descends to a finitely presented object at some stage. Between two such models a morphism over $R$ descends after advancing the stage. Two stage maps equal over $R$ are equal at a later stage. This identifies the category of finitely presented modules with the filtered colimit of the stage categories.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: The category of finitely presented algebras over a directed colimit
theorems.hypotheses: Write $R=\operatorname{colim}_i R_i$ for a directed colimit of rings.
theorems.statement: A finitely presented object descends to a finitely presented object at some stage. Between two such models a morphism over $R$ descends after advancing the stage. Two stage maps equal over $R$ are equal at a later stage. This identifies the category of finitely presented algebras with the filtered colimit of the stage categories.
theorems.proof: A finitely presented object descends to a finitely presented object at some stage. Between two such models a morphism over $R$ descends after advancing the stage. Two stage maps equal over $R$ are equal at a later stage. This identifies the category of finitely presented algebras with the filtered colimit of the stage categories.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Approximating arbitrary local homomorphisms
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)\to(S,\mathfrak n)$ be a local homomorphism.
theorems.statement: A local model exists for every such map. A local model consists of a directed system of local homomorphisms $R_i\to S_i$, with $R_i$ essentially of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ and $S_i$ essentially of finite type over $R_i$, whose colimit is the specified local map $R\to S$.
theorems.proof: A local model exists for every such map. A local model consists of a directed system of local homomorphisms $R_i\to S_i$, with $R_i$ essentially of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ and $S_i$ essentially of finite type over $R_i$, whose colimit is the specified local map $R\to S$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Approximating essentially finite type local maps
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)\to(S,\mathfrak n)$ be a local homomorphism. Assume $S$ essentially of finite type over $R$. A local model consists of a directed system of local homomorphisms $R_i\to S_i$, with $R_i$ essentially of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ and $S_i$ essentially of finite type over $R_i$, whose colimit is the specified local map $R\to S$.
theorems.statement: A model exists with every transition $S_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j\to S_j$ a localization of a quotient.
theorems.proof: A model exists with every transition $S_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j\to S_j$ a localization of a quotient.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Approximating essentially finitely presented local maps
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)\to(S,\mathfrak n)$ be a local homomorphism. Assume $S$ essentially finitely presented over $R$. A local model consists of a directed system of local homomorphisms $R_i\to S_i$, with $R_i$ essentially of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ and $S_i$ essentially of finite type over $R_i$, whose colimit is the specified local map $R\to S$.
theorems.statement: A model exists in which each $S_j$ for $j\geq i$ is a prime localization of $S_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j$.
theorems.proof: A model exists in which each $S_j$ for $j\geq i$ is a prime localization of $S_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A local model with the wrong transition maps
theorems.hypotheses: Over $\mathbf F_2$ let $R$ be the origin localization of $\mathbf F_2[z,y_1,y_2,\ldots]/(y_i^2-zy_{i+1})$ and $S=R/zR$. Let $R_n$ use the first $n$ variables and first $n-1$ relations.
theorems.statement: The quotients $S_n=R_n/(z,y_n^2)$ approximate $S$ but the base-changed transitions kill $y_{n+1}^2$ and are not localizations. In contrast $R_n/zR_n$ gives base-change isomorphisms.
theorems.proof: The quotients $S_n=R_n/(z,y_n^2)$ approximate $S$ but the base-changed transitions kill $y_{n+1}^2$ and are not localizations. In contrast $R_n/zR_n$ gives base-change isomorphisms.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Local approximation of a finitely presented module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)\to(S,\mathfrak n)$ be a local homomorphism. Assume $R\to S$ essentially finitely presented and $M$ finitely presented over $S$. A local model consists of a directed system of local homomorphisms $R_i\to S_i$, with $R_i$ essentially of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ and $S_i$ essentially of finite type over $R_i$, whose colimit is the specified local map $R\to S$.
theorems.statement: Such a model with module data exists satisfying the following conditions. In a local model require each $S_j$ for $j\geq i$ to be a prime localization of $S_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j$. Model modules $M_i$ are finite over $S_i$ with $M_i\otimes_{S_i} S_j\cong M_j$ and colimit $M$.
theorems.proof: Such a model with module data exists satisfying the following conditions. In a local model require each $S_j$ for $j\geq i$ to be a prime localization of $S_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j$. Model modules $M_i$ are finite over $S_i$ with $M_i\otimes_{S_i} S_j\cong M_j$ and colimit $M$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite type approximation of an arbitrary ring map
theorems.hypotheses: Take any homomorphism $R\to S$.
theorems.statement: The following approximation always exists. Use a directed system $R_i\to S_i$ with colimit $R\to S$, each $R_i$ of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ and each $S_i$ of finite type over $R_i$.
theorems.proof: The following approximation always exists. Use a directed system $R_i\to S_i$ with colimit $R\to S$, each $R_i$ of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ and each $S_i$ of finite type over $R_i$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite algebra approximations of an integral map
theorems.hypotheses: Take $R\to S$ integral. Use a directed system $R_i\to S_i$ with colimit $R\to S$, each $R_i$ of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ and each $S_i$ of finite type over $R_i$.
theorems.statement: A model exists with every $S_i$ finite over $R_i$.
theorems.proof: A model exists with every $S_i$ finite over $R_i$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite type approximation with quotient transitions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be finite type over $R$. Use a directed system $R_i\to S_i$ with colimit $R\to S$, each $R_i$ of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ and each $S_i$ of finite type over $R_i$.
theorems.statement: The system can be chosen with each $S_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j\to S_j$ surjective for $j\geq i$.
theorems.proof: The system can be chosen with each $S_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j\to S_j$ surjective for $j\geq i$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite type approximation with cartesian transitions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be finitely presented over $R$. Use a directed system $R_i\to S_i$ with colimit $R\to S$, each $R_i$ of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ and each $S_i$ of finite type over $R_i$.
theorems.statement: Each transition $S_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j\to S_j$ may be taken to be an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: Each transition $S_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j\to S_j$ may be taken to be an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Joint approximation of a finitely presented algebra and module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ and the $S$-module $M$ both be finitely presented. Use a directed system $R_i\to S_i$ with colimit $R\to S$, each $R_i$ of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ and each $S_i$ of finite type over $R_i$.
theorems.statement: One may require $S_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j\cong S_j$ and finite $S_i$-modules $M_i$ with $M_i\otimes_{S_i}S_j\cong M_j$ and colimit $M$. In particular $M=M_i\otimes_{R_i}R$ at every stage.
theorems.proof: One may require $S_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j\cong S_j$ and finite $S_i$-modules $M_i$ with $M_i\otimes_{S_i}S_j\cong M_j$ and colimit $M$. In particular $M=M_i\otimes_{R_i}R$ at every stage.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Flatness from a parameter system remaining regular
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a map of Noetherian local rings with $R$ regular local and one regular parameter system of $R$ mapping to a regular sequence in $S$.
theorems.statement: The map is flat.
theorems.proof: The map is flat.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Flatness achieved at a finite local model
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)\to(S,\mathfrak n)$ be a local homomorphism. Let $S$ be essentially finitely presented over $R$, $M$ finitely presented over $S$ and flat over $R$. A local model consists of a directed system of local homomorphisms $R_i\to S_i$, with $R_i$ essentially of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ and $S_i$ essentially of finite type over $R_i$, whose colimit is the specified local map $R\to S$. In a local model require each $S_j$ for $j\geq i$ to be a prime localization of $S_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j$. Model modules $M_i$ are finite over $S_i$ with $M_i\otimes_{S_i} S_j\cong M_j$ and colimit $M$.
theorems.statement: In any such system there is a stage with $M_i$ flat over $R_i$.
theorems.proof: In any such system there is a stage with $M_i$ flat over $R_i$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Lifting an injection from the closed fibre
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)\to(S,\mathfrak n)$ be a local homomorphism. Let $S$ be essentially finitely presented over $R$ and $u:M\to N$ a map of finitely presented $S$-modules with $N$ flat over $R$ and the reduction of $u$ modulo $\mathfrak m$ injective.
theorems.statement: Then $u$ is injective and its cokernel is flat over $R$.
theorems.proof: Then $u$ is injective and its cokernel is flat over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Nonzerodivisor on the closed fibre of a flat local family
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)\to(S,\mathfrak n)$ be a local homomorphism. Assume the map flat and essentially finitely presented, and the image of $f\in S$ a nonzerodivisor modulo $\mathfrak mS$.
theorems.statement: The element $f$ is a nonzerodivisor in $S$ and $S/fS$ is flat over $R$.
theorems.proof: The element $f$ is a nonzerodivisor in $S$ and $S/fS$ is flat over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Regular sequences lift in a flat local family
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)\to(S,\mathfrak n)$ be a local homomorphism. Assume the map flat and essentially finitely presented and the images of $f_1,\ldots,f_c$ form a regular sequence in $S/\mathfrak mS$.
theorems.statement: The tuple is regular in $S$ and every successive quotient of $S$ by an initial segment is flat over $R$.
theorems.proof: The tuple is regular in $S$ and every successive quotient of $S$ by an initial segment is flat over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Flatness modulo a proper ideal in an essentially finitely presented local family
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)\to(S,\mathfrak n)$ be a local homomorphism. Assume the map essentially finitely presented, $M$ finitely presented over $S$, and $I\subsetneq R$. Suppose $\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(M,R/I)=0$ and $M/IM$ is $R/I$-flat.
theorems.statement: The module $M$ is flat over $R$.
theorems.proof: The module $M$ is flat over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Fibre criterion for flatness in a local tower
theorems.hypotheses: Take local maps $R\to S\to T$ with $T$ essentially finitely presented over $R$ and $S$ essentially of finite presentation over $R$. Assume $M\ne0$ finitely presented over $T$ and flat over $R$, with $M/\mathfrak m_RM$ flat over $S/\mathfrak m_RS$.
theorems.statement: Then $M$ is flat over $S$, and $S$ is flat and essentially finitely presented over $R$.
theorems.proof: Then $M$ is flat over $S$, and $S$ is flat and essentially finitely presented over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Fibre criterion upgrades essential finite type to finite presentation
theorems.hypotheses: Take local maps $R\to S\to T$ with $T$ essentially finitely presented over $R$ and $S$ essentially of finite type over $R$. Assume $M\ne0$ finitely presented over $T$ and flat over $R$, with $M/\mathfrak m_RM$ flat over $S/\mathfrak m_RS$.
theorems.statement: Then $M$ is flat over $S$, and $S$ is flat and essentially finitely presented over $R$.
theorems.proof: Then $M$ is flat over $S$, and $S$ is flat and essentially finitely presented over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Fibre criterion for flatness over a locally nilpotent ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Take $R\to S\to T$ with $S$ finite type and $T$ finitely presented over $R$. Let $I$ be locally nilpotent in $R$ and $M$ finitely presented over $T$, flat over $R$, with $M/IM$ flat over $S/IS$.
theorems.statement: Then $M$ is $S$-flat. Wherever $M\otimes_S\kappa(\mathfrak q)\ne0$, $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat and essentially finitely presented over $R$.
theorems.proof: Then $M$ is $S$-flat. Wherever $M\otimes_S\kappa(\mathfrak q)\ne0$, $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat and essentially finitely presented over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Expected dimension of an intersection in a Cohen–Macaulay algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be equidimensional Cohen–Macaulay of dimension $d$ and finite type over a field. Suppose a nonempty $V(f_1,\ldots,f_i)$ has dimension at most $d-i$.
theorems.statement: Its dimension is $d-i$, and at each prime in it the tuple is a regular sequence. For the empty locus the local conclusion is vacuous.
theorems.proof: Its dimension is $d-i$, and at each prime in it the tuple is a regular sequence. For the empty locus the local conclusion is vacuous.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Openness of regular-sequence behaviour on fibres
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be finite type with all fibres equidimensional Cohen–Macaulay of dimension $d$. Fix $f_1,\ldots,f_i\in S$.
theorems.statement: Inside their zero locus the points where the tuple is regular in the local fibre ring form a relatively open subset.
theorems.proof: Inside their zero locus the points where the tuple is regular in the local fibre ring form a relatively open subset.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Openness of fibrewise exactness of a finite free complex
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian and $R\to S$ flat and finite type with Cohen–Macaulay fibres of dimension $d$. Let $F_e\to\cdots\to F_0$ be a finite complex of finite free $S$-modules.
theorems.statement: The locus where the localized fibre complex is exact in positive degrees is open in $\operatorname{Spec}S$.
theorems.proof: The locus where the localized fibre complex is exact in positive degrees is open in $\operatorname{Spec}S$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Openness of the relative flat locus
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be finitely presented and $M$ finitely presented over $S$.
theorems.statement: The set of primes of $S$ with $M_{\mathfrak q}$ flat over $R$ is open in $\operatorname{Spec}S$.
theorems.proof: The set of primes of $S$ with $M_{\mathfrak q}$ flat over $R$ is open in $\operatorname{Spec}S$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Flatness for quasi-finite polynomial coordinates
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be finite type over $k$ and let $k[y_1,\ldots,y_d]\to S$ be quasi-finite.
theorems.statement: At $\mathfrak q$, flatness of $S_{\mathfrak q}$ over the polynomial ring is equivalent to $S_{\mathfrak q}$ being Cohen–Macaulay and $\dim_{\mathfrak q}(S/k)=d$.
theorems.proof: At $\mathfrak q$, flatness of $S_{\mathfrak q}$ over the polynomial ring is equivalent to $S_{\mathfrak q}$ being Cohen–Macaulay and $\dim_{\mathfrak q}(S/k)=d$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Openness of the Cohen–Macaulay locus over a field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be a finite type algebra over a field $k$.
theorems.statement: The set of primes $\mathfrak q$ with $S_{\mathfrak q}$ Cohen–Macaulay is open.
theorems.proof: The set of primes $\mathfrak q$ with $S_{\mathfrak q}$ Cohen–Macaulay is open.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Density of the Cohen–Macaulay locus over a field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be a finite type algebra over a field $k$.
theorems.statement: The Cohen–Macaulay locus in $\operatorname{Spec}S$ is dense and open.
theorems.proof: The Cohen–Macaulay locus in $\operatorname{Spec}S$ is dense and open.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Open constant fibre-dimension strata on the Cohen–Macaulay locus
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be flat and finitely presented and $d\geq0$.
theorems.statement: The locus of points where the local fibre ring is Cohen–Macaulay and $\dim_{\mathfrak q}(S/R)=d$ is open.
theorems.proof: The locus of points where the local fibre ring is Cohen–Macaulay and $\dim_{\mathfrak q}(S/R)=d$ is open.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Fibrewise density of the relative Cohen–Macaulay locus
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be flat and finitely presented.
theorems.statement: The points where the local fibre ring is Cohen–Macaulay form an open set dense in every fibre.
theorems.proof: The points where the local fibre ring is Cohen–Macaulay form an open set dense in every fibre.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Cohen–Macaulayness at corresponding primes under field extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be finite type over $k$, let $K/k$ be a field extension and fix $\mathfrak q'$ of $S\otimes_k K$ over $\mathfrak q$.
theorems.statement: The local rings $S_{\mathfrak q}$ and $(S\otimes_k K)_{\mathfrak q'}$ are Cohen–Macaulay simultaneously.
theorems.proof: The local rings $S_{\mathfrak q}$ and $(S\otimes_k K)_{\mathfrak q'}$ are Cohen–Macaulay simultaneously.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Arbitrary base change of the relative Cohen–Macaulay locus
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be finite type and $R\to B$ any map.
theorems.statement: The relative Cohen–Macaulay locus of $B\to S\otimes_R B$ is exactly the inverse image of the relative locus of $R\to S$.
theorems.proof: The relative Cohen–Macaulay locus of $B\to S\otimes_R B$ is exactly the inverse image of the relative locus of $R\to S$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Decomposition of a flat algebra with Cohen–Macaulay fibres by dimension
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $R\to S$ is flat, finitely presented and has Cohen–Macaulay fibres.
theorems.statement: There is a finite product decomposition into $S_d$, each flat finitely presented with Cohen–Macaulay fibres, with every nonempty fibre of $S_d$ equidimensional of dimension $d$.
theorems.proof: There is a finite product decomposition into $S_d$, each flat finitely presented with Cohen–Macaulay fibres, with every nonempty fibre of $S_d$ equidimensional of dimension $d$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Functorial square for Kähler differentials
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$, $R'\to S'$ be connected by compatible maps $\psi:R\to R'$, $\phi:S\to S'$.
theorems.statement: The induced $\phi$-linear map on differentials sends $ds$ to $d\phi(s)$ and induces an $S'$-linear map $S'\otimes_S\Omega_{S/R}\to\Omega_{S'/R'}$.
theorems.proof: The induced $\phi$-linear map on differentials sends $ds$ to $d\phi(s)$ and induces an $S'$-linear map $S'\otimes_S\Omega_{S/R}\to\Omega_{S'/R'}$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Functorial presentation of the relations on differentials
theorems.hypotheses: Take a compatible square of algebras from $R\to S$ to $R'\to S'$, with horizontal maps $\psi,\phi$.
theorems.statement: The free module on differential generators maps $[a]\mapsto[\phi(a)]$. Relations for sums and products go to the corresponding relations for the image elements, and coefficient relations $[r]$ map to $[\psi(r)]$. This induces the canonical map between the presented differential modules.
theorems.proof: The free module on differential generators maps $[a]\mapsto[\phi(a)]$. Relations for sums and products go to the corresponding relations for the image elements, and coefficient relations $[r]$ map to $[\psi(r)]$. This induces the canonical map between the presented differential modules.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Exterior derivative on elementary differential forms
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to B$ be a ring map, $b_0,\ldots,b_p\in B$.
theorems.statement: The de Rham differential is given by $d(b_0\,db_1\wedge\cdots\wedge db_p)=db_0\wedge db_1\wedge\cdots\wedge db_p$.
theorems.proof: The de Rham differential is given by $d(b_0\,db_1\wedge\cdots\wedge db_p)=db_0\wedge db_1\wedge\cdots\wedge db_p$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Canonical polynomial presentation of any algebra
theorems.hypotheses: For an $R$-algebra $S$, let $R[S]$ be polynomial on its underlying set.
theorems.statement: The evaluation homomorphism $[s]\mapsto s$ surjects onto $S$ functorially.
theorems.proof: The evaluation homomorphism $[s]\mapsto s$ surjects onto $S$ functorially.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Canonical two-term naive cotangent complex
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I=\ker(R[S]\to S)$ for the canonical polynomial presentation $P=R[S]$.
theorems.statement: The complex is $I/I^2\to\Omega_{P/R}\otimes_P S$ in homological degrees one and zero, with differential induced by $d$.
theorems.proof: The complex is $I/I^2\to\Omega_{P/R}\otimes_P S$ in homological degrees one and zero, with differential induced by $d$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Functoriality square of the naive cotangent complex
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a commutative square from $R\to S$ to $R'\to S'$.
theorems.statement: The canonical polynomial presentations and their kernels give the functorial map $\mathrm{NL}_{S/R}\to\mathrm{NL}_{S'/R'}$ linear over the target map $S\to S'$.
theorems.proof: The canonical polynomial presentations and their kernels give the functorial map $\mathrm{NL}_{S/R}\to\mathrm{NL}_{S'/R'}$ linear over the target map $S\to S'$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Naive cotangent complex for a polynomial algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $B$ be polynomial over $A$.
theorems.statement: The naive complex is homotopy equivalent to $\Omega_{B/A}$ in degree zero.
theorems.proof: The naive complex is homotopy equivalent to $\Omega_{B/A}$ in degree zero.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Jacobi–Zariski sequence for the naive cotangent complex
theorems.hypotheses: Take $A\to B\to C$ and compatible polynomial presentations with kernels $I,J,K$ for $B/A,C/B,C/A$.
theorems.statement: The conormal row $(I/I^2)\otimes_B C\to K/K^2\to J/J^2\to0$ maps to the short exact row for polynomial differentials. This gives $H_1(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_B C)\to H_1(L_{C/A})\to H_1(L_{C/B})\to\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_B C\to\Omega_{C/A}\to\Omega_{C/B}\to0$. If $\operatorname{Tor}_i^B(\Omega_{B/A},C)=0$ for $i=1,2$, its first term identifies with $H_1(L_{B/A})\otimes_B C$.
theorems.proof: The conormal row $(I/I^2)\otimes_B C\to K/K^2\to J/J^2\to0$ maps to the short exact row for polynomial differentials. This gives $H_1(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_B C)\to H_1(L_{C/A})\to H_1(L_{C/B})\to\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_B C\to\Omega_{C/A}\to\Omega_{C/B}\to0$. If $\operatorname{Tor}_i^B(\Omega_{B/A},C)=0$ for $i=1,2$, its first term identifies with $H_1(L_{B/A})\otimes_B C$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A canonical null homotopy in cotangent transitivity
theorems.hypotheses: Take maps $A\to B\xrightarrow{\phi} C$. Put $J=\ker(B[C]\to C)$.
theorems.statement: The composite $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\to\mathrm{NL}_{C/A}\to\mathrm{NL}_{C/B}$ is null homotopic. The homotopy sends $d[b]$ to the class of $[\phi(b)]-b$ in $J/J^2$.
theorems.proof: The composite $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\to\mathrm{NL}_{C/A}\to\mathrm{NL}_{C/B}$ is null homotopic. The homotopy sends $d[b]$ to the class of $[\phi(b)]-b$ in $J/J^2$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Naive cotangent complex of a surjection
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\twoheadrightarrow B$ have kernel $I$.
theorems.statement: Its naive cotangent complex is homotopy equivalent to $I/I^2$ in homological degree one.
theorems.proof: Its naive cotangent complex is homotopy equivalent to $I/I^2$ in homological degree one.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Conormal sequence for compatible surjections
theorems.hypotheses: Take $A\to B\to C$ with composite surjective, and write $I=\ker(A\to C)$, $J=\ker(B\to C)$.
theorems.statement: One has an exact sequence $I/I^2\to J/J^2\to\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_B C\to0$.
theorems.proof: One has an exact sequence $I/I^2\to J/J^2\to\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_B C\to0$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Directed colimits of naive cotangent complexes
theorems.hypotheses: Take a directed system $R_i\to S_i$ with colimit $R\to S$.
theorems.statement: The canonical complex $\mathrm{NL}_{S/R}$ identifies with $\operatorname{colim}_i\mathrm{NL}_{S_i/R_i}$.
theorems.proof: The canonical complex $\mathrm{NL}_{S/R}$ identifies with $\operatorname{colim}_i\mathrm{NL}_{S_i/R_i}$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Localization in the source of the naive cotangent complex
theorems.hypotheses: Let $U$ be multiplicative in $A$, and $U^{-1}A\to B$ a homomorphism.
theorems.statement: The map $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\to\mathrm{NL}_{B/U^{-1}A}$ is a homotopy equivalence.
theorems.proof: The map $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\to\mathrm{NL}_{B/U^{-1}A}$ is a homotopy equivalence.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Principal target localization of the naive cotangent complex
theorems.hypotheses: Let $P\to S$ be a polynomial presentation of an $R$-algebra with kernel $I$ and $h\mapsto g\in S$. Present $S_g$ by $P[X]/(I,hX-1)$.
theorems.statement: The conormal and differential terms of the localized presentation split as the original localized terms plus rank-one summands generated respectively by $hX-1$ and $dX$. In the complex one may change the splitting to obtain the contractible additional summand $[S_g\xrightarrow{g}S_g]$. Thus principal localization gives a homotopy equivalence.
theorems.proof: The conormal and differential terms of the localized presentation split as the original localized terms plus rank-one summands generated respectively by $hX-1$ and $dX$. In the complex one may change the splitting to obtain the contractible additional summand $[S_g\xrightarrow{g}S_g]$. Thus principal localization gives a homotopy equivalence.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Arbitrary target localization of the naive cotangent complex
theorems.hypotheses: For $A\to B$ and $U$ multiplicative in $B$, set $C=U^{-1}B$.
theorems.statement: The map $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_B C\to\mathrm{NL}_{C/A}$ is a quasi-isomorphism.
theorems.proof: The map $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_B C\to\mathrm{NL}_{C/A}$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Stable isomorphism from two homotopy-equivalent two-term complexes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $[A_1\to A_0]$ and $[B_1\to B_0]$ be complexes of modules with mutually inverse maps up to homotopy.
theorems.statement: Then $A_1\oplus B_0\cong B_1\oplus A_0$.
theorems.proof: Then $A_1\oplus B_0\cong B_1\oplus A_0$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Stable conormal isomorphism at a principal localization
theorems.hypotheses: For finite type $R\to S$ choose polynomial presentations in $n,m$ variables for $S,S_g$ with kernels $I,J$, respectively.
theorems.statement: There is an $S_g$-linear isomorphism $(I/I^2)_g\oplus S_g^m\cong J/J^2\oplus S_g^n$.
theorems.proof: There is an $S_g$-linear isomorphism $(I/I^2)_g\oplus S_g^m\cong J/J^2\oplus S_g^n$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Principal localization of complete intersections over a field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be a finite type algebra over a field $k$.
theorems.statement: If $S$ is a global complete intersection, so is $S_g$. If $S$ is a local complete intersection, so is $S_g$.
theorems.proof: If $S$ is a global complete intersection, so is $S_g$. If $S$ is a local complete intersection, so is $S_g$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Cohen–Macaulayness of a local complete intersection over a field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be a finite type algebra over a field $k$. Assume $S$ a local complete intersection.
theorems.statement: The ring $S$ is Cohen–Macaulay.
theorems.proof: The ring $S$ is Cohen–Macaulay.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Five presentation tests for a complete intersection point
theorems.hypotheses: Write $S=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/I=P/I$ with $k$ a field. Let $\mathfrak q'\subset P$ correspond to $\mathfrak q\subset S$, and $c=\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak q'-\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak q$.
theorems.statement: A global complete intersection neighbourhood exists exactly when $I_{\mathfrak q'}$ has $c$ generators, or when its conormal at $\mathfrak q$ has $c$ generators, or when that conormal is free of rank $c$, or when the localized ideal is generated by a regular sequence. In this situation any $c$ lifts of generators modulo $\mathfrak q'I_{\mathfrak q'}$ form a regular sequence.
theorems.proof: A global complete intersection neighbourhood exists exactly when $I_{\mathfrak q'}$ has $c$ generators, or when its conormal at $\mathfrak q$ has $c$ generators, or when that conormal is free of rank $c$, or when the localized ideal is generated by a regular sequence. In this situation any $c$ lifts of generators modulo $\mathfrak q'I_{\mathfrak q'}$ form a regular sequence.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Invariance of the regular local presentation test
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B\to C$ be local surjections with $A,B$ regular local.
theorems.statement: For either regular source, generation of the kernel by a regular sequence is equivalent to generation by the dimension drop many elements. All four resulting conditions are equivalent.
theorems.proof: For either regular source, generation of the kernel by a regular sequence is equivalent to generation by the dimension drop many elements. All four resulting conditions are equivalent.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Complete intersections for essentially finite type local field algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be local essentially of finite type over a field $k$.
theorems.statement: The complete intersection condition is equivalent to regular-sequence generation of the kernel for every regular local essentially finitely presented source surjecting onto $S$, and to dimension-drop many generators for one such source. It is also equivalent to $S$ being a prime localization of a global, or of a local, complete intersection over $k$.
theorems.proof: The complete intersection condition is equivalent to regular-sequence generation of the kernel for every regular local essentially finitely presented source surjecting onto $S$, and to dimension-drop many generators for one such source. It is also equivalent to $S$ being a prime localization of a global, or of a local, complete intersection over $k$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Complete intersections at a prime and on a neighbourhood
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be a finite type algebra over a field $k$. Fix $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}S$.
theorems.statement: The stalk is a complete intersection over $k$ exactly when some principal neighbourhood is a local complete intersection, equivalently a global complete intersection, or equivalently the codimension and conormal criteria of Tag 00SC hold for any polynomial presentation.
theorems.proof: The stalk is a complete intersection over $k$ exactly when some principal neighbourhood is a local complete intersection, equivalently a global complete intersection, or equivalently the codimension and conormal criteria of Tag 00SC hold for any polynomial presentation.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Detecting the local complete intersection property at maximal ideals
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be a finite type algebra over a field $k$.
theorems.statement: Being a local complete intersection over $k$ is equivalent to the corresponding local complete intersection property for all local rings, or just all localizations at maximal ideals.
theorems.proof: Being a local complete intersection over $k$ is equivalent to the corresponding local complete intersection property for all local rings, or just all localizations at maximal ideals.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Complete intersections at corresponding points under field extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be a finite type algebra over a field $k$. Let $K/k$ be a field extension, and $\mathfrak q'$ a prime of $S\otimes_k K$ above $\mathfrak q$.
theorems.statement: The stalk at $\mathfrak q$ is a complete intersection over $k$ if and only if the stalk at $\mathfrak q'$ is one over $K$.
theorems.proof: The stalk at $\mathfrak q$ is a complete intersection over $k$ if and only if the stalk at $\mathfrak q'$ is one over $K$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Field base change of local complete intersection algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be a finite type algebra over a field $k$. Let $K/k$ be a field extension.
theorems.statement: The algebra $S$ is a local complete intersection over $k$ exactly when $S\otimes_k K$ is one over $K$.
theorems.proof: The algebra $S$ is a local complete intersection over $k$ exactly when $S\otimes_k K$ is one over $K$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Descent of a regular-sequence kernel in a local square
theorems.hypotheses: Take a commutative square from $R\to S$ to $A=R/I\to B=S/J$ of local rings, with both horizontal maps flat. Assume $R$ and $S/\mathfrak m_R S$ regular local and both $J$ and its image in that closed fibre generated by regular sequences.
theorems.statement: Then $I$ is generated by a regular sequence.
theorems.proof: Then $I$ is generated by a regular sequence.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Arbitrary base change of a syntomic algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be syntomic and $R\to A$ arbitrary.
theorems.statement: The map $A\to S\otimes_R A$ is syntomic.
theorems.proof: The map $A\to S\otimes_R A$ is syntomic.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Gluing syntomicity on a principal cover
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $g_1,\ldots,g_m$ generate the unit ideal of $S$, with $R\to S_{g_i}$ syntomic for each $i$.
theorems.statement: Then $R\to S$ is syntomic.
theorems.proof: Then $R\to S$ is syntomic.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A presentation with a basis of conormal equations
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $S$ finitely presented over $R$ and some finite polynomial presentation $P/I$ has free conormal $I/I^2$.
theorems.statement: There is a finite polynomial presentation with the defining equations giving a basis of the new conormal module.
theorems.proof: There is a finite polynomial presentation with the defining equations giving a basis of the new conormal module.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Universal factorization into two prescribed degrees
theorems.hypotheses: For $n,m\geq1$ take the coefficient map classifying a monic polynomial as the product of two monic factors of degrees $n,m$ over $\mathbf Z$.
theorems.statement: This is a finite relative global complete intersection. Its fibres have dimension zero, and the coefficients of both universal factors are integral over the universal coefficient ring.
theorems.proof: This is a finite relative global complete intersection. Its fibres have dimension zero, and the coefficients of both universal factors are integral over the universal coefficient ring.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Ordered roots of the universal monic polynomial
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R=\mathbf Z[a_1,\ldots,a_n]$ act on $S=\mathbf Z[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ via the elementary symmetric functions.
theorems.statement: The map is a relative global complete intersection and finite free of rank $n!$, hence faithfully flat. A basis consists of $\prod_i x_i^{e_i}$ with $0\le e_i\le n-i$.
theorems.proof: The map is a relative global complete intersection and finite free of rank $n!$, hence faithfully flat. A basis consists of $\prod_i x_i^{e_i}$ with $0\le e_i\le n-i$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Base change and principal localization of relative global complete intersections
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $S=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ with the displayed presentation a relative global complete intersection.
theorems.statement: Every base change of this presentation is a relative global complete intersection. Inverting $g\in S$ is presented by adding one variable $X$ and the equation $hX-1$, with $h$ lifting $g$. Inverting a base element already invertible in $S$ also preserves the condition on the displayed presentation.
theorems.proof: Every base change of this presentation is a relative global complete intersection. Inverting $g\in S$ is presented by adding one variable $X$ and the equation $hX-1$, with $h$ lifting $g$. Inverting a base element already invertible in $S$ also preserves the condition on the displayed presentation.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Extending an expected-dimension presentation near a fibre
theorems.hypotheses: Write $S=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ and put $d=n-c$.
theorems.statement: If all fibres above $V(I)$ have dimension $d$, a localization at some $g\equiv1\bmod IS$ gives a relative global complete intersection by adjoining an inverse. If just one fibre has dimension $d$, take $g$ a unit on that fibre. If the relative dimension at $\mathfrak q$ is $d$, take $g\notin\mathfrak q$.
theorems.proof: If all fibres above $V(I)$ have dimension $d$, a localization at some $g\equiv1\bmod IS$ gives a relative global complete intersection by adjoining an inverse. If just one fibre has dimension $d$, take $g$ a unit on that fibre. If the relative dimension at $\mathfrak q$ is $d$, take $g\notin\mathfrak q$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Noetherian approximation of relative global complete intersection equations
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $S=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ with the displayed presentation a relative global complete intersection.
theorems.statement: All equations can be defined over one finite type $\mathbf Z$-subalgebra $R_0\subset R$ with the same presentation a relative global complete intersection there.
theorems.proof: All equations can be defined over one finite type $\mathbf Z$-subalgebra $R_0\subset R$ with the same presentation a relative global complete intersection there.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Regularity, flat intermediate quotients and conormal bases
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $S=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ with the displayed presentation a relative global complete intersection.
theorems.statement: At every prime of the polynomial algebra containing the defining ideal, the displayed tuple is regular and every quotient by an initial segment there is flat over $R$. Globally the classes of the equations form an $S$-basis of the conormal.
theorems.proof: At every prime of the polynomial algebra containing the defining ideal, the displayed tuple is regular and every quotient by an initial segment there is flat over $R$. Globally the classes of the equations form an $S$-basis of the conormal.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Relative global complete intersections are syntomic
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $S=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ with the displayed presentation a relative global complete intersection.
theorems.statement: The algebra $S$ is syntomic, in particular flat over $R$.
theorems.proof: The algebra $S$ is syntomic, in particular flat over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Splitting a monic polynomial by a syntomic finite free extension
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a monic polynomial $P$ of degree $n$ over $R$.
theorems.statement: A syntomic finite free faithfully flat extension $R\subseteq B$ admits a factorization of $P$ as a product of $n$ monic linear factors.
theorems.proof: A syntomic finite free faithfully flat extension $R\subseteq B$ admits a factorization of $P$ as a product of $n$ monic linear factors.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Three tests for a syntomic neighbourhood
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathfrak q$ of $S$ lie over $\mathfrak p$ of $R$.
theorems.statement: A syntomic principal neighbourhood exists exactly when a relative global complete intersection neighbourhood exists, or equivalently when finite presentation holds on a neighbourhood, $R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat, and the local fibre is a complete intersection over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.
theorems.proof: A syntomic principal neighbourhood exists exactly when a relative global complete intersection neighbourhood exists, or equivalently when finite presentation holds on a neighbourhood, $R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat, and the local fibre is a complete intersection over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Projectivity of the conormal on a syntomic principal open
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/I$ with $I$ finitely generated and $S_g$ syntomic over $R$.
theorems.statement: The module $(I/I^2)_g$ is finite projective over $S_g$.
theorems.proof: The module $(I/I^2)_g$ is finite projective over $S_g$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Composition for syntomic and relative global complete intersection algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Take a pair of composable maps, both syntomic, or both relative global complete intersections.
theorems.statement: The composite satisfies the respective condition.
theorems.proof: The composite satisfies the respective condition.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Local lifting of a syntomic algebra through a quotient of the base
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R/I\to B$ be syntomic.
theorems.statement: A principal open cover of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ exists on which every localized algebra lifts to a relative global complete intersection over $R$.
theorems.proof: A principal open cover of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ exists on which every localized algebra lifts to a relative global complete intersection over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Principal localizations of a smooth ring map
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $R\to S$ smooth.
theorems.statement: Then $S_g$ is smooth over $R$ for every $g\in S$. If $f\in R$ already acts invertibly on $S$, the map $R_f\to S$ is smooth.
theorems.proof: Then $S_g$ is smooth over $R$ for every $g\in S$. If $f\in R$ already acts invertibly on $S$, the map $R_f\to S$ is smooth.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Smooth algebras over fields are local complete intersections
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be smooth over a field $k$.
theorems.statement: Then $S$ is a local complete intersection over $k$.
theorems.proof: Then $S$ is a local complete intersection over $k$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Conormal and differential bases in a standard smooth presentation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ have invertible Jacobian minor in the first $c$ variables.
theorems.statement: The map is smooth and a relative global complete intersection. The conormal has basis the equation classes and $\Omega_{S/R}$ has basis $dx_{c+1},\ldots,dx_n$. Standard smoothness persists under base change, principal localization of the target and localization of the base at an element already invertible in the target.
theorems.proof: The map is smooth and a relative global complete intersection. The conormal has basis the equation classes and $\Omega_{S/R}$ has basis $dx_{c+1},\ldots,dx_n$. Standard smoothness persists under base change, principal localization of the target and localization of the base at an element already invertible in the target.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A standard smooth chart cut out by a Jacobian minor
theorems.hypotheses: In a polynomial algebra over $R$ choose $c$ equations and the determinant $h$ of their partial derivatives with respect to the first $c$ variables.
theorems.statement: Adjoin a variable $z$ and the equation $zh-1$. The resulting algebra is standard smooth, using the variables $x_1,\ldots,x_c,z$ for the enlarged Jacobian minor.
theorems.proof: Adjoin a variable $z$ and the equation $zh-1$. The resulting algebra is standard smooth, using the variables $x_1,\ldots,x_c,z$ for the enlarged Jacobian minor.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Composition of standard smooth presentations
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B\to C$ be standard smooth maps.
theorems.statement: The composite is standard smooth.
theorems.proof: The composite is standard smooth.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Standard smooth charts of a smooth algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be smooth.
theorems.statement: There is a principal open cover on the target by standard smooth $R$-algebras. In particular the map is syntomic.
theorems.proof: There is a principal open cover on the target by standard smooth $R$-algebras. In particular the map is syntomic.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Cotangent criterion at a point of a finitely presented algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $\mathfrak q$ in a finitely presented $R$-algebra $S$.
theorems.statement: Smoothness at $\mathfrak q$ is equivalent to $H_1(L_{S/R})_{\mathfrak q}=0$ and $\Omega_{S/R,\mathfrak q}$ finite free. Under the same vanishing, projectivity or flatness of the localized differential module are equivalent tests.
theorems.proof: Smoothness at $\mathfrak q$ is equivalent to $H_1(L_{S/R})_{\mathfrak q}=0$ and $\Omega_{S/R,\mathfrak q}$ finite free. Under the same vanishing, projectivity or flatness of the localized differential module are equivalent tests.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Smoothness detected at all target primes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be any ring map.
theorems.statement: It is smooth exactly when it is smooth at every prime of $S$.
theorems.proof: It is smooth exactly when it is smooth at every prime of $S$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Composition of smooth ring maps
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B\to C$ be smooth maps.
theorems.statement: Then $A\to C$ is smooth.
theorems.proof: Then $A\to C$ is smooth.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Smoothness of a finite product of algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S=B\times C$ be a product of two $R$-algebras.
theorems.statement: The algebra $S$ is smooth over $R$ exactly when $B$ and $C$ are both smooth over $R$.
theorems.proof: The algebra $S$ is smooth over $R$ exactly when $B$ and $C$ are both smooth over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Jacobian criterion on a relative global complete intersection
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $S=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ with the displayed presentation a relative global complete intersection.
theorems.statement: At $\mathfrak q\subset S$, smoothness is equivalent to some $c$-rowed Jacobian minor being outside $\mathfrak q$.
theorems.proof: At $\mathfrak q\subset S$, smoothness is equivalent to some $c$-rowed Jacobian minor being outside $\mathfrak q$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Flat base change of the smooth locus
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $R\to S$ finitely presented and $R\to B$ flat.
theorems.statement: The smooth locus of $B\to S\otimes_R B$ is precisely the inverse image of the smooth locus over $R$.
theorems.proof: The smooth locus of $B\to S\otimes_R B$ is precisely the inverse image of the smooth locus over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Smoothness at corresponding points after field extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be a finite type algebra over a field $k$. For an extension $K/k$ take a prime $\mathfrak q'$ of $S\otimes_k K$ over $\mathfrak q$.
theorems.statement: Smoothness over $k$ at $\mathfrak q$ is equivalent to smoothness over $K$ at $\mathfrak q'$.
theorems.proof: Smoothness over $k$ at $\mathfrak q$ is equivalent to smoothness over $K$ at $\mathfrak q'$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Standard smooth lifts on a principal cover
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R/I\to B$ be smooth, for any ideal $I$ of $R$.
theorems.statement: On some principal open cover of $\operatorname{Spec}B$, each localized algebra is the reduction of a standard smooth $R$-algebra.
theorems.proof: On some principal open cover of $\operatorname{Spec}B$, each localized algebra is the reduction of a standard smooth $R$-algebra.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Arbitrary base change of formally smooth rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be formally smooth and $R\to B$ arbitrary.
theorems.statement: The algebra $S\otimes_R B$ is formally smooth over $B$.
theorems.proof: The algebra $S\otimes_R B$ is formally smooth over $B$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Composition preserves formal smoothness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B\to C$ be formally smooth ring maps.
theorems.statement: The composite is formally smooth.
theorems.proof: The composite is formally smooth.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Formal smoothness of a polynomial ring
theorems.hypotheses: Take any set of polynomial variables over $R$.
theorems.statement: The polynomial algebra is formally smooth over $R$.
theorems.proof: The polynomial algebra is formally smooth over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Testing formal smoothness by a polynomial presentation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $P\to S$ be a surjection of $R$-algebras with kernel $J$ and $P$ polynomial over $R$.
theorems.statement: Formal smoothness of $S$ over $R$ is equivalent to the existence of an $R$-algebra section of $P/J^2\to S$.
theorems.proof: Formal smoothness of $S$ over $R$ is equivalent to the existence of an $R$-algebra section of $P/J^2\to S$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Testing formal smoothness by a formally smooth presentation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $P\to S$ be a surjection of $R$-algebras with kernel $J$ and $P$ formally smooth over $R$.
theorems.statement: Formal smoothness of $S$ over $R$ is equivalent to the existence of an $R$-algebra section of $P/J^2\to S$.
theorems.proof: Formal smoothness of $S$ over $R$ is equivalent to the existence of an $R$-algebra section of $P/J^2\to S$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Split conormal sequence detects formal smoothness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $P\to S$ be a polynomial presentation over $R$ with kernel $J$.
theorems.statement: Formal smoothness is equivalent to split exactness of $0\to J/J^2\to\Omega_{P/R}\otimes_P S\to\Omega_{S/R}\to0$.
theorems.proof: Formal smoothness is equivalent to split exactness of $0\to J/J^2\to\Omega_{P/R}\otimes_P S\to\Omega_{S/R}\to0$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Formal smoothness via sections, conormals and the naive complex
theorems.hypotheses: Allow surjections $P\to S$ with $P$ formally smooth over $R$, and denote the kernel by $J$.
theorems.statement: Formal smoothness of $S/R$ is equivalent to having a section of $P/J^2\to S$ for some such presentation, or for all. Split exactness of the conormal sequence for some or for all is equivalent as well. Intrinsically the tests are $H_1(\mathrm{NL}_{S/R})=0$ and projectivity of $\Omega_{S/R}$.
theorems.proof: Formal smoothness of $S/R$ is equivalent to having a section of $P/J^2\to S$ for some such presentation, or for all. Split exactness of the conormal sequence for some or for all is equivalent as well. Intrinsically the tests are $H_1(\mathrm{NL}_{S/R})=0$ and projectivity of $\Omega_{S/R}$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Split transitivity sequence for a terminal formally smooth map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B\to C$ have $B\to C$ formally smooth.
theorems.statement: There is a split short exact sequence $0\to C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/A}\to\Omega_{C/A}\to\Omega_{C/B}\to0$.
theorems.proof: There is a split short exact sequence $0\to C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/A}\to\Omega_{C/A}\to\Omega_{C/B}\to0$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Split conormal sequence for a formally smooth quotient algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to C$ be formally smooth and factor through $B\twoheadrightarrow C$ with kernel $J$.
theorems.statement: The sequence $0\to J/J^2\to\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_B C\to\Omega_{C/A}\to0$ is split exact.
theorems.proof: The sequence $0\to J/J^2\to\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_B C\to\Omega_{C/A}\to0$ is split exact.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Conormal comparison with a formally smooth first map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B\to C$ have surjective composite and formally smooth first map. Write $I,J$ for the kernels of $A\to C,B\to C$.
theorems.statement: The sequence $0\to I/I^2\to J/J^2\to\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_B C\to0$ is split exact.
theorems.proof: The sequence $0\to I/I^2\to J/J^2\to\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_B C\to0$ is split exact.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Formal smoothness lifts across a square-zero base ideal under flatness
theorems.hypotheses: Take $I\subset R$ with $I^2=0$, $R\to S$ flat, and $R/I\to S/IS$ formally smooth.
theorems.statement: Then $R\to S$ is formally smooth.
theorems.proof: Then $R\to S$ is formally smooth.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Reduced conormal sequence in the square-zero lifting proof
theorems.hypotheses: Under the square-zero, flatness and formal smoothness hypotheses of Tag 031L choose a polynomial presentation $P\to S$ with kernel $J$.
theorems.statement: The reduced sequence $0\to J/(IJ+J^2)\to\Omega_{P/R}\otimes_P S/IS\to\Omega_{S/R}\otimes_S S/IS\to0$ is split exact.
theorems.proof: The reduced sequence $0\to J/(IJ+J^2)\to\Omega_{P/R}\otimes_P S/IS\to\Omega_{S/R}\otimes_S S/IS\to0$ is split exact.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Smooth maps have Noetherian models inside the base
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $R\to S$ is smooth.
theorems.statement: There exists a finite type $\mathbf Z$-subalgebra $R_0\subseteq R$ and a smooth $R_0$-algebra $S_0$ with $S_0\otimes_{R_0}R\cong S$.
theorems.proof: There exists a finite type $\mathbf Z$-subalgebra $R_0\subseteq R$ and a smooth $R_0$-algebra $S_0$ with $S_0\otimes_{R_0}R\cong S$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Smooth algebras descend along filtered colimits
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A=\operatorname{colim} A_i$ be filtered and $B$ smooth over $A$.
theorems.statement: Some $A_i$ admits a smooth $B_i$ whose base change is $B$.
theorems.proof: Some $A_i$ admits a smooth $B_i$ whose base change is $B$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Faithfully flat descent of formal smoothness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be any ring map and $R\to R'$ faithfully flat. Set $S'=S\otimes_R R'$.
theorems.statement: The map $R\to S$ is formally smooth if and only if $R'\to S'$ is formally smooth.
theorems.proof: The map $R\to S$ is formally smooth if and only if $R'\to S'$ is formally smooth.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Lifting a smooth algebra across a locally nilpotent ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be smooth and $S\to A/I$ an $R$-algebra map for a locally nilpotent ideal $I$ in the $R$-algebra $A$.
theorems.statement: There exists an $R$-algebra lift $S\to A$.
theorems.proof: There exists an $R$-algebra lift $S\to A$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Differential transitivity for a terminal smooth map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B\to C$ have $B\to C$ smooth.
theorems.statement: The sequence $0\to C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/A}\to\Omega_{C/A}\to\Omega_{C/B}\to0$ is exact.
theorems.proof: The sequence $0\to C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/A}\to\Omega_{C/A}\to\Omega_{C/B}\to0$ is exact.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Split conormal sequence for a smooth quotient algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to C$ be smooth and factor through $B\twoheadrightarrow C$ with kernel $J$.
theorems.statement: The sequence $0\to J/J^2\to\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_B C\to\Omega_{C/A}\to0$ splits.
theorems.proof: The sequence $0\to J/J^2\to\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_B C\to\Omega_{C/A}\to0$ splits.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Conormal comparison for a smooth first map
theorems.hypotheses: Take $A\to B\to C$ with $A\to B$ smooth and $A\to C$ surjective. Write $I,J$ for the kernels of maps to $C$.
theorems.statement: One has $0\to I/I^2\to J/J^2\to\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_B C\to0$ exact.
theorems.proof: One has $0\to I/I^2\to J/J^2\to\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_B C\to0$ exact.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Formal neighbourhood of a section of a smooth algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be smooth with an $R$-algebra retraction $S\to R$ of kernel $I$.
theorems.statement: The conormal $I/I^2$ is finite locally free over $R$. If it is free of rank $d$, the $I$-adic completion of $S$ is a formal power series algebra in $d$ variables over $R$.
theorems.proof: The conormal $I/I^2$ is finite locally free over $R$. If it is free of rank $d$, the $I$-adic completion of $S$ is a formal power series algebra in $d$ variables over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Cotangent-space dimension at a closed point over an algebraically closed field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be algebraically closed, $S$ finite type, and $\mathfrak m$ maximal.
theorems.statement: The dimensions over $\kappa(\mathfrak m)$ of $\Omega_{S/k}\otimes\kappa(\mathfrak m)$ and $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ agree.
theorems.proof: The dimensions over $\kappa(\mathfrak m)$ of $\Omega_{S/k}\otimes\kappa(\mathfrak m)$ and $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ agree.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Equivalent smoothness tests at a closed point over an algebraically closed field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be algebraically closed, $S$ finite type and $\mathfrak m$ maximal. Let $e$ be the dimension of the differential fibre and $d=\dim S_{\mathfrak m}$.
theorems.statement: Regularity of the stalk, smoothness at the point, $e\leq d$, and $e=d$ are equivalent.
theorems.proof: Regularity of the stalk, smoothness at the point, $e\leq d$, and $e=d$ are equivalent.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Differential dimension criterion at any point over a field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be a finite type algebra over a field $k$. Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}S$, let $x$ correspond to $\mathfrak q$, and $e=\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak q)}(\Omega_{S/k}\otimes_S\kappa(\mathfrak q))$.
theorems.statement: Smoothness at $x$ is equivalent to $e\leq\dim_x X$ and to $e=\dim_x X$. At such a point the local ring is regular.
theorems.proof: Smoothness at $x$ is equivalent to $e\leq\dim_x X$ and to $e=\dim_x X$. At such a point the local ring is regular.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Conormal injection for a separably generated residue extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a Noetherian local $k$-algebra with $\kappa/k$ finitely generated and separable.
theorems.statement: The differential gives an injection $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\hookrightarrow\Omega_{R/k}\otimes_R\kappa$.
theorems.proof: The differential gives an injection $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\hookrightarrow\Omega_{R/k}\otimes_R\kappa$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Regularity detects smoothness at a separable residue extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be a finite type algebra over a field $k$. Assume $\kappa(\mathfrak q)/k$ separable.
theorems.statement: Smoothness at $\mathfrak q$ is equivalent to regularity of $S_{\mathfrak q}$.
theorems.proof: Smoothness at $\mathfrak q$ is equivalent to regularity of $S_{\mathfrak q}$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Nonzerodivisor detected by a differential in characteristic zero
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a map of $\mathbf Q$-algebras with $S\ne0$ and $df$ the basis of a free direct summand $S\,df$ of $\Omega_{S/R}$.
theorems.statement: The element $f$ is not nilpotent. If $S$ is Noetherian local, $f$ is a nonzerodivisor.
theorems.proof: The element $f$ is not nilpotent. If $S$ is Noetherian local, $f$ is a nonzerodivisor.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Regularity, smoothness and locally free differentials in characteristic zero
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be a finite type algebra over a field $k$. Suppose $k$ has characteristic zero and fix $\mathfrak q\subset S$.
theorems.statement: Smoothness at $\mathfrak q$, regularity of $S_{\mathfrak q}$, and freeness of the localized differential module are equivalent.
theorems.proof: Smoothness at $\mathfrak q$, regularity of $S_{\mathfrak q}$, and freeness of the localized differential module are equivalent.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Failures of differential and regularity criteria in characteristic p
theorems.hypotheses: In characteristic $p>0$ consider the algebras in the source examples.
theorems.statement: The algebra $\mathbf F_p[x]/(x^p)$ has free differentials but is not smooth. For $p>2$ over $k=\mathbf F_p(t)$ take $S=k[x,y]/(x^p+y^2+t)$. At the prime $(y,x^p+t)$ the local ring is regular but its differential fibre has dimension two while the curve has dimension one, so it is not smooth.
theorems.proof: The algebra $\mathbf F_p[x]/(x^p)$ has free differentials but is not smooth. For $p>2$ over $k=\mathbf F_p(t)$ take $S=k[x,y]/(x^p+y^2+t)$. At the prime $(y,x^p+t)$ the local ring is regular but its differential fibre has dimension two while the curve has dimension one, so it is not smooth.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Generic smoothness and the fraction field extension
theorems.hypotheses: Take a finite type inclusion $R\subset S$ of domains.
theorems.statement: Smoothness at the generic point of $S$ is equivalent to separability of $\operatorname{Frac}(S)/\operatorname{Frac}(R)$.
theorems.proof: Smoothness at the generic point of $S$ is equivalent to separability of $\operatorname{Frac}(S)/\operatorname{Frac}(R)$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Artinian lifting tests at a smooth point
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be finite type over Noetherian $R$ and fix $\mathfrak q\subset S$. Consider local $R$-algebra surjections $B'\to B$ with square-zero kernel and maps $S\to B$ carrying the closed point to $\mathfrak q$.
theorems.statement: Smoothness there is equivalent to existence of lifts $S\to B'$ for every such square. Testing only small extensions suffices, even with the further condition that the residue map at $\mathfrak q$ be an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: Smoothness there is equivalent to existence of lifts $S\to B'$ for every such square. Testing only small extensions suffices, even with the further condition that the residue map at $\mathfrak q$ be an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Localized conormal differential in the Artinian lifting test
theorems.hypotheses: Present $S=P/I$ by a finite polynomial algebra over Noetherian $R$, and let $\mathfrak q'\subset P$ lift $\mathfrak q$.
theorems.statement: At the chosen point the map tested in the proof is $I_{\mathfrak q'}/I_{\mathfrak q'}^2\to S_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{P_{\mathfrak q'}}\Omega_{P_{\mathfrak q'}/R}$, induced by $d$. A split injection gives the local smoothness criterion.
theorems.proof: At the chosen point the map tested in the proof is $I_{\mathfrak q'}/I_{\mathfrak q'}^2\to S_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{P_{\mathfrak q'}}\Omega_{P_{\mathfrak q'}/R}$, induced by $d$. A split injection gives the local smoothness criterion.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A square invertible Jacobian presentation for every étale algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $R\to S$ étale.
theorems.statement: There is a presentation with as many variables as equations and Jacobian determinant invertible in $S$. In particular the algebra is standard smooth.
theorems.proof: There is a presentation with as many variables as equations and Jacobian determinant invertible in $S$. In particular the algebra is standard smooth.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Permanence, descent to a finite stage and local tests for étale algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Use étale homomorphisms of commutative rings. The flat locus-comparison assertion assumes a finitely presented initial algebra.
theorems.statement: Principal localizations are étale. Composition and arbitrary base change preserve étaleness, which glues on principal covers and is equivalent for a product algebra to étaleness of both factors. Étale maps are syntomic and flat. Under flat base change of a finitely presented map the étale locus pulls back exactly. Over a field and for finite type algebras, vanishing of differentials is equivalent to étaleness. An étale algebra descends to a finite type $\mathbf Z$-subalgebra of the base and to a stage of any filtered base presentation. An étale algebra over a localization of the base is the localization of an étale algebra over the original base.
theorems.proof: Principal localizations are étale. Composition and arbitrary base change preserve étaleness, which glues on principal covers and is equivalent for a product algebra to étaleness of both factors. Étale maps are syntomic and flat. Under flat base change of a finitely presented map the étale locus pulls back exactly. Over a field and for finite type algebras, vanishing of differentials is equivalent to étaleness. An étale algebra descends to a finite type $\mathbf Z$-subalgebra of the base and to a stage of any filtered base presentation. An étale algebra over a localization of the base is the localization of an étale algebra over the original base.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Maximal ideal and residue field of an étale stalk
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be étale at $\mathfrak q$ above $\mathfrak p$.
theorems.statement: The maximal ideal of $S_{\mathfrak q}$ equals $\mathfrak p S_{\mathfrak q}$ and the extension $\kappa(\mathfrak q)/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is finite separable.
theorems.proof: The maximal ideal of $S_{\mathfrak q}$ equals $\mathfrak p S_{\mathfrak q}$ and the extension $\kappa(\mathfrak q)/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is finite separable.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Maps between étale algebras over the same base
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ and $T$ both be étale over $R$.
theorems.statement: Every $R$-algebra homomorphism $S\to T$ is étale.
theorems.proof: Every $R$-algebra homomorphism $S\to T$ is étale.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Surjective flat maps of finite presentation are idempotent localizations
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $R\to S$ is surjective, flat and finitely presented.
theorems.statement: For some idempotent $e\in R$ there is an $R$-algebra isomorphism $S\cong R_e$.
theorems.proof: For some idempotent $e\in R$ there is an $R$-algebra isomorphism $S\cong R_e$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Lifting an étale algebra from a quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be any ideal of $R$ and $B$ an étale $R/I$-algebra.
theorems.statement: There is an étale $R$-algebra $S$ with $B\cong S/IS$ over $R/I$.
