theorems.proof: There is an étale $R$-algebra $S$ with $B\cong S/IS$ over $R/I$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Étaleness of a compatible square-zero thickening
theorems.hypotheses: Take compatible surjections $A'\to A$ and $B'\to B$ with square-zero kernels $I,J$, where $A\to B$ is étale and the natural map $I\otimes_A B\to J$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.statement: Then $A'\to B'$ is étale.
theorems.proof: Then $A'\to B'$ is étale.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Étale locus of universal polynomial factorization
theorems.hypotheses: On the map multiplying two universal monic polynomials $g,h$ of fixed positive degrees, let $\Delta$ be their resultant.
theorems.statement: At a target prime étaleness is equivalent to invertibility of $\Delta$ in the stalk, equivalently to coprimality of the residual factors. The Jacobian is the Sylvester determinant up to ordering and sign.
theorems.proof: At a target prime étaleness is equivalent to invertibility of $\Delta$ in the stalk, equivalently to coprimality of the residual factors. The Jacobian is the Sylvester determinant up to ordering and sign.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Étale lifting of coprime residual polynomial factors
theorems.hypotheses: Let a monic $f\in R[X]$ have a chosen factorization into coprime monic factors in $\kappa(\mathfrak p)[X]$.
theorems.statement: After étale extension at a point above $\mathfrak p$ with identical residue field, there exists a factorization lifting both chosen factors and generating the unit ideal in the new polynomial ring. Arbitrary leading coefficients can be recovered by lifting their reciprocal units after shrinking.
theorems.proof: After étale extension at a point above $\mathfrak p$ with identical residue field, there exists a factorization lifting both chosen factors and generating the unit ideal in the new polynomial ring. Arbitrary leading coefficients can be recovered by lifting their reciprocal units after shrinking.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Permanence and composition boundary for standard étale algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Use a presentation $R[X]_g/(f)$ with $f$ monic and $f'$ invertible in the quotient.
theorems.statement: It is étale. Standard étaleness persists under arbitrary base change and principal localization of the target. Two composable standard étale maps may have a composite admitting no standard étale presentation.
theorems.proof: It is étale. Standard étaleness persists under arbitrary base change and principal localization of the target. Two composable standard étale maps may have a composite admitting no standard étale presentation.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Realization of prescribed finite separable residue extension
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R$ and a finite separable extension $L/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.
theorems.statement: Some étale $R$-algebra has a point over $\mathfrak p$ realizing exactly this residue extension.
theorems.proof: Some étale $R$-algebra has a point over $\mathfrak p$ realizing exactly this residue extension.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite faithfully flat cover splitting a standard étale map locally
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $R\to S$ standard étale.
theorems.statement: There is a finite projective faithfully flat $R$-algebra $T$ such that for each pair of primes $\mathfrak q$ of $S$ and $\mathfrak t$ of $T$ over the same base prime, some principal neighbourhood of $\mathfrak t$ admits a factorization through $S$ taking $\mathfrak t$ to $\mathfrak q$.
theorems.proof: There is a finite projective faithfully flat $R$-algebra $T$ such that for each pair of primes $\mathfrak q$ of $S$ and $\mathfrak t$ of $T$ over the same base prime, some principal neighbourhood of $\mathfrak t$ admits a factorization through $S$ taking $\mathfrak t$ to $\mathfrak q$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite faithfully flat and Zariski refinement of an étale cover
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $R\to S$ étale and surjective on spectra.
theorems.statement: There is a finite projective faithfully flat $R$-algebra $T$ and a principal cover of its spectrum such that the structure map to each localized algebra factors through $S$.
theorems.proof: There is a finite projective faithfully flat $R$-algebra $T$ and a principal cover of its spectrum such that the structure map to each localized algebra factors through $S$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Clearing an integral model to make a map finite near a fibre
theorems.hypotheses: Take $R\to C\to S$, with $C$ integral and $S$ finite type over $R$. Suppose $C_g\cong S_g$ via the given map and $g$ invertible in $C\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.
theorems.statement: There exists $f\notin\mathfrak p$ such that $S_f$ is finite over $R_f$.
theorems.proof: There exists $f\notin\mathfrak p$ such that $S_f$ is finite over $R_f$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Splitting one quasi-finite point by an étale neighbourhood
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be finite type, let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ lie over $\mathfrak p\subset R$, and let $x$ be the corresponding point of the fibre $F=\operatorname{Spec}(S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$. Assume quasi-finiteness at $\mathfrak q$.
theorems.statement: An étale base neighbourhood $(R',\mathfrak p')$ preserving the residue field gives $R'\otimes_R S=A\times B$. The finite $R'$-algebra $A$ has precisely one point over $\mathfrak p'$, lying over $\mathfrak q$. No point of $B$ lies over both selected points.
theorems.proof: An étale base neighbourhood $(R',\mathfrak p')$ preserving the residue field gives $R'\otimes_R S=A\times B$. The finite $R'$-algebra $A$ has precisely one point over $\mathfrak p'$, lying over $\mathfrak q$. No point of $B$ lies over both selected points.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Splitting all quasi-finite points above a fibre without residue extension
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a finite type $R$-algebra $S$ and a base prime $\mathfrak p$.
theorems.statement: After étale base change at $\mathfrak p'$ with identical residue field, the algebra splits as finitely many finite factors and a remaining factor. Each finite factor has exactly one point above $\mathfrak p'$. The remaining algebra is quasi-finite at no point above $\mathfrak p'$.
theorems.proof: After étale base change at $\mathfrak p'$ with identical residue field, the algebra splits as finitely many finite factors and a remaining factor. Each finite factor has exactly one point above $\mathfrak p'$. The remaining algebra is quasi-finite at no point above $\mathfrak p'$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Splitting a fibre with purely inseparable residual extensions
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a finite type $R$-algebra $S$ and a base prime $\mathfrak p$.
theorems.statement: After étale base change at some point $\mathfrak p'$ the algebra splits into finite factors, each with a unique point above $\mathfrak p'$ of finite purely inseparable residue extension, and a remaining factor with no quasi-finite points above $\mathfrak p'$.
theorems.proof: After étale base change at some point $\mathfrak p'$ the algebra splits into finite factors, each with a unique point above $\mathfrak p'$ of finite purely inseparable residue extension, and a remaining factor with no quasi-finite points above $\mathfrak p'$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Lindel’s common infinitesimal quotients
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a local map of local rings, with $S$ a localization of an étale $R$-algebra. Assume the residue field map is an isomorphism.
theorems.statement: There is $t\in\mathfrak m_R$ for which all $R/t^nR\to S/t^nS$, $n\ge1$, are isomorphisms.
theorems.proof: There is $t\in\mathfrak m_R$ for which all $R/t^nR\to S/t^nS$, $n\ge1$, are isomorphisms.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite faithfully flat factorization at the maximal primes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a local map of local rings, with $S$ a localization of an étale $R$-algebra.
theorems.statement: There exists a finite, finitely presented, faithfully flat $R$-algebra $C$ such that for each maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ of $C$, the map $R\to C_{\mathfrak n}$ factors through $S$.
theorems.proof: There exists a finite, finitely presented, faithfully flat $R$-algebra $C$ such that for each maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ of $C$, the map $R\to C_{\mathfrak n}$ factors through $S$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Integral coefficients after multiplication by the derivative
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f\in R[X]$ be monic, $B$ an $R$-algebra and $h\in B[X]/(f)$ integral over $R$.
theorems.statement: The class $f'h$ has a polynomial representative all of whose coefficients in $B$ are integral over $R$.
theorems.proof: The class $f'h$ has a polynomial representative all of whose coefficients in $B$ are integral over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Integral closure commutes with étale base change
theorems.hypotheses: Take $R\to B$, write $C$ for the integral closure of $R$ in $B$, and suppose $S/R$ is étale.
theorems.statement: Inside $S\otimes_R B$, the integral closure of $S$ is canonically $S\otimes_R C$.
theorems.proof: Inside $S\otimes_R B$, the integral closure of $S$ is canonically $S\otimes_R C$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Integral closure commutes with smooth base change
theorems.hypotheses: Take $R\to B$, write $C$ for the integral closure of $R$ in $B$, and suppose $S/R$ is smooth.
theorems.statement: Inside $S\otimes_R B$, the integral closure of $S$ is canonically $S\otimes_R C$.
theorems.proof: Inside $S\otimes_R B$, the integral closure of $S$ is canonically $S\otimes_R C$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Integral closure commutes with a filtered colimit of smooth algebras over the source base change
theorems.hypotheses: Take $R\to B$, write $C$ for the integral closure of $R$ in $B$, and suppose $S/R$ is a filtered colimit of smooth algebras over the source.
theorems.statement: Inside $S\otimes_R B$, the integral closure of $S$ is canonically $S\otimes_R C$.
theorems.proof: Inside $S\otimes_R B$, the integral closure of $S$ is canonically $S\otimes_R C$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Cyclotomic interpolation after inverting the prime
theorems.hypotheses: For a prime $p$ put $R=\mathbf Z[1/p]$ and $S=R[\zeta_p]$ with $\zeta_p$ a primitive $p$th root of unity.
theorems.statement: The $p$ powers $\zeta_p^j$ have pairwise unit differences in $S$. At each root the derivative of $X^p-1$ is a unit and is the product of its differences from all other roots. In particular, any $d<p$ of them give a unit Vandermonde determinant.
theorems.proof: The $p$ powers $\zeta_p^j$ have pairwise unit differences in $S$. At each root the derivative of $X^p-1$ is a unit and is the product of its differences from all other roots. In particular, any $d<p$ of them give a unit Vandermonde determinant.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Base change of a formally unramified map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be formally unramified and $R\to A$ any map.
theorems.statement: The map $A\to A\otimes_R S$ is formally unramified.
theorems.proof: The map $A\to A\otimes_R S$ is formally unramified.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Directed colimits of formally unramified algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(S_i)$ be a directed system of formally unramified algebras over a fixed $R$.
theorems.statement: The map $R\to\operatorname{colim}_i S_i$ is formally unramified.
theorems.proof: The map $R\to\operatorname{colim}_i S_i$ is formally unramified.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Base change of a formally étale map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be formally étale and $R\to A$ any map.
theorems.statement: The map $A\to A\otimes_R S$ is formally étale.
theorems.proof: The map $A\to A\otimes_R S$ is formally étale.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Directed colimits of formally étale algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(S_i)$ be a directed system of formally étale algebras over a fixed $R$.
theorems.statement: The map $R\to\operatorname{colim}_i S_i$ is formally étale.
theorems.proof: The map $R\to\operatorname{colim}_i S_i$ is formally étale.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Testing formal unramifiedness on local rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be any map and write $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap R$ for each target prime.
theorems.statement: The map is formally unramified exactly when every $R\to S_{\mathfrak q}$ is, equivalently when every $R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$ is.
theorems.proof: The map is formally unramified exactly when every $R\to S_{\mathfrak q}$ is, equivalently when every $R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$ is.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Localizing formally unramified maps
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be formally unramified.
theorems.statement: For multiplicative sets $U\subset R$ and $V\subset S$, both $U^{-1}R\to U^{-1}S$ and $R\to V^{-1}S$ are formally unramified.
theorems.proof: For multiplicative sets $U\subset R$ and $V\subset S$, both $U^{-1}R\to U^{-1}S$ and $R\to V^{-1}S$ are formally unramified.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Infinitesimal quotients of a formally étale algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be formally étale and $J\subset S$ with $R\to S/J$ surjective of kernel $I$.
theorems.statement: For each $n\ge1$ one has $R/I^n\simeq S/J^n$. The induced homomorphism of associated graded rings is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: For each $n\ge1$ one has $R/I^n\simeq S/J^n$. The induced homomorphism of associated graded rings is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Infinitesimal diagonal neighbourhoods under formally étale extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S\to T$ be ring maps with $S\to T$ formally étale.
theorems.statement: For $J_S=\ker(S\otimes_R S\to S)$ and $J_T$ defined similarly, $T\otimes_S((S\otimes_R S)/J_S^{k+1})\cong (T\otimes_R T)/J_T^{k+1}$ for $k\ge0$. In particular $T\otimes_S\Omega_{S/R}\cong\Omega_{T/R}$.
theorems.proof: For $J_S=\ker(S\otimes_R S\to S)$ and $J_T$ defined similarly, $T\otimes_S((S\otimes_R S)/J_S^{k+1})\cong (T\otimes_R T)/J_T^{k+1}$ for $k\ge0$. In particular $T\otimes_S\Omega_{S/R}\cong\Omega_{T/R}$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Principal parts and extension of differential operators
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S\to T$ be ring maps with $S\to T$ formally étale. Write $M_T=T\otimes_S M$ for scalar extension of each $S$-module.
theorems.statement: For $k\ge0$ there is a canonical isomorphism $T\otimes_S P^k_{S/R}(M)\cong P^k_{T/R}(M_T)$. Every $R$-linear differential operator $M\to N$ of order at most $k$ extends uniquely to one $M_T\to N_T$ of order at most $k$.
theorems.proof: For $k\ge0$ there is a canonical isomorphism $T\otimes_S P^k_{S/R}(M)\cong P^k_{T/R}(M_T)$. Every $R$-linear differential operator $M\to N$ of order at most $k$ extends uniquely to one $M_T\to N_T$ of order at most $k$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Composition of extended differential operators
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S\to T$ be ring maps with $S\to T$ formally étale.
theorems.statement: Extension to $T$ of finite-order $R$-linear differential operators between $S$-modules respects composition. Thus $T\otimes_S M$ carries the induced action of $\operatorname{Diff}_{S/R}(M,M)$.
theorems.proof: Extension to $T$ of finite-order $R$-linear differential operators between $S$-modules respects composition. Thus $T\otimes_S M$ carries the induced action of $\operatorname{Diff}_{S/R}(M,M)$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Permanence, local tests and descent models for unramified maps
theorems.hypotheses: Use finite type for unramified maps and finite presentation for G-unramified maps. Let $\mathfrak q$ lie over $\mathfrak p$.
theorems.statement: Both classes are closed under composition and base change, contain principal localizations and étale maps, and can be tested on principal covers or at every target prime. All quotients are unramified and quotients by finite ideals are G-unramified. Under the respective finiteness assumption, local vanishing of $\Omega_{S/R}$ can be tested at the stalk, over its residue field, or after passage to the fibre over $\mathfrak p$ by either test. G-unramified algebras descend by base change from a G-unramified algebra over a finite-type $\mathbf Z$-algebra. An unramified algebra is a quotient of a base change of such a finite-base unramified model.
theorems.proof: Both classes are closed under composition and base change, contain principal localizations and étale maps, and can be tested on principal covers or at every target prime. All quotients are unramified and quotients by finite ideals are G-unramified. Under the respective finiteness assumption, local vanishing of $\Omega_{S/R}$ can be tested at the stalk, over its residue field, or after passage to the fibre over $\mathfrak p$ by either test. G-unramified algebras descend by base change from a G-unramified algebra over a finite-type $\mathbf Z$-algebra. An unramified algebra is a quotient of a base change of such a finite-base unramified model.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: The diagonal of an unramified map is cut out by an idempotent
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be unramified and $T=S\otimes_R S$.
theorems.statement: For some idempotent $e\in T$, multiplication $T\to S$ identifies with localization $T\to T_e$.
theorems.proof: For some idempotent $e\in T$, multiplication $T\to S$ identifies with localization $T\to T_e$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Étale coordinates on a finite-type algebra over a field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field and let $k[X_1,\ldots,X_n]\to A$ be of finite type, sending $X_i$ to $a_i$.
theorems.statement: The map is étale exactly when every maximal localization of $A$ has dimension $n$ and the differentials $d a_1,\ldots,d a_n$ span $\Omega_{A/k}$.
theorems.proof: The map is étale exactly when every maximal localization of $A$ has dimension $n$ and the differentials $d a_1,\ldots,d a_n$ span $\Omega_{A/k}$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Local quotient of a standard étale algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}S$ contract to $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R$. Assume unramifiedness at $\mathfrak q$.
theorems.statement: For some $g\notin\mathfrak q$, $S_g$ is a quotient of a standard étale $R$-algebra.
theorems.proof: For some $g\notin\mathfrak q$, $S_g$ is a quotient of a standard étale $R$-algebra.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: A closed factor after étale base change at one point
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}S$ contract to $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R$. Assume $S$ of finite type and unramified at $\mathfrak q$.
theorems.statement: There exist an étale $R\to R'$, a prime $\mathfrak p'$ over $\mathfrak p$, and $R'\otimes_R S=A\times B$ with $R'\twoheadrightarrow A$ and $\mathfrak p'A$ a prime over both $\mathfrak q$ and $\mathfrak p'$.
theorems.proof: There exist an étale $R\to R'$, a prime $\mathfrak p'$ over $\mathfrak p$, and $R'\otimes_R S=A\times B$ with $R'\twoheadrightarrow A$ and $\mathfrak p'A$ a prime over both $\mathfrak q$ and $\mathfrak p'$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Separating all unramified fibre points after étale base change
theorems.hypotheses: Fix an unramified $R\to S$ and $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R$.
theorems.statement: There exist an étale $R'$ with a prime $\mathfrak p'$ over $\mathfrak p$ and a decomposition $R'\otimes_R S=A_1\times\cdots\times A_n\times B$. Each $A_i$ is a quotient of $R'$, each $\mathfrak p'A_i$ is prime over $\mathfrak p'$, and $B$ has empty fibre there.
theorems.proof: There exist an étale $R'$ with a prime $\mathfrak p'$ over $\mathfrak p$ and a decomposition $R'\otimes_R S=A_1\times\cdots\times A_n\times B$. Each $A_i$ is a quotient of $R'$, each $\mathfrak p'A_i$ is prime over $\mathfrak p'$, and $B$ has empty fibre there.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Uniqueness of a lift of a simple residue root
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,k)$ be a local ring.
theorems.statement: If $f(a)=f(b)=0$ for $f\in R[T]$, $a-b\in\mathfrak m$, and $f'(a)$ is a unit, then $a=b$. This uniqueness holds over every local ring.
theorems.proof: If $f(a)=f(b)=0$ for $f\in R[T]$, $a-b\in\mathfrak m$, and $f'(a)$ is a unit, then $a=b$. This uniqueness holds over every local ring.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Finite extensions and quasi-finite fibres over a henselian ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,k)$ be a local ring. Assume $R$ henselian.
theorems.statement: Each finite algebra is a finite product of henselian local rings finite over $R$, with local structure maps on these factors. If $S$ is of finite type and quasi-finite at a closed-fibre prime $\mathfrak q$, then $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is henselian and finite over $R$. This holds at each such prime for a quasi-finite algebra.
theorems.proof: Each finite algebra is a finite product of henselian local rings finite over $R$, with local structure maps on these factors. If $S$ is of finite type and quasi-finite at a closed-fibre prime $\mathfrak q$, then $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is henselian and finite over $R$. This holds at each such prime for a quasi-finite algebra.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Splitting the quasi-finite part over a henselian local ring
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $(R,\mathfrak m,k)$ henselian and $S$ a finite-type $R$-algebra.
theorems.statement: One has $S=A_1\times\cdots\times A_n\times B$, the $A_i$ finite local over $R$ and $B/R$ nowhere quasi-finite above $\mathfrak m$.
theorems.proof: One has $S=A_1\times\cdots\times A_n\times B$, the $A_i$ finite local over $R$ and $B/R$ nowhere quasi-finite above $\mathfrak m$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Splitting the quasi-finite part over a strictly henselian local ring
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $(R,\mathfrak m,k)$ strictly henselian and $S$ a finite-type $R$-algebra.
theorems.statement: One has $S=A_1\times\cdots\times A_n\times B$, the $A_i$ finite local over $R$ and $B/R$ nowhere quasi-finite above $\mathfrak m$. Every residue field extension $k\subset\kappa(A_i)$ is finite purely inseparable.
theorems.proof: One has $S=A_1\times\cdots\times A_n\times B$, the $A_i$ finite local over $R$ and $B/R$ nowhere quasi-finite above $\mathfrak m$. Every residue field extension $k\subset\kappa(A_i)$ is finite purely inseparable.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Finite étale algebras over a henselian local ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,k)$ be henselian local.
theorems.statement: Reduction $S\mapsto S/\mathfrak mS$ is an equivalence from finite étale $R$-algebras to finite étale $k$-algebras.
theorems.proof: Reduction $S\mapsto S/\mathfrak mS$ is an equivalence from finite étale $R$-algebras to finite étale $k$-algebras.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Unramified algebras over a strictly henselian local ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,k)$ be strictly henselian local and $S/R$ unramified.
theorems.statement: The algebra is a finite product of quotients of $R$ and one additional algebra having empty closed fibre.
theorems.proof: The algebra is a finite product of quotients of $R$ and one additional algebra having empty closed fibre.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Lifting a residue embedding from an étale algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $R\to T$ with $T$ henselian local. Let $A/R$ be étale, $\mathfrak q$ above $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m_T\cap R$, and $\kappa(\mathfrak q)\to\kappa(T)$ an embedding over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.
theorems.statement: There is exactly one $R$-map $A\to T$ inducing that residue embedding and contracting $\mathfrak m_T$ to $\mathfrak q$.
theorems.proof: There is exactly one $R$-map $A\to T$ inducing that residue embedding and contracting $\mathfrak m_T$ to $\mathfrak q$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Lifting a residue embedding from an ind-étale algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $R\to T$ with $T$ henselian local. Let $A/R$ be ind-étale, $\mathfrak q$ above $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m_T\cap R$, and $\kappa(\mathfrak q)\to\kappa(T)$ an embedding over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.
theorems.statement: There is exactly one $R$-map $A\to T$ inducing that residue embedding and contracting $\mathfrak m_T$ to $\mathfrak q$.
theorems.proof: There is exactly one $R$-map $A\to T$ inducing that residue embedding and contracting $\mathfrak m_T$ to $\mathfrak q$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Solutions of étale systems over strictly henselian local rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be local between strictly henselian local rings. Suppose $R[X_1,\ldots,X_n]/(P_1,\ldots,P_n)$ is étale over $R$.
theorems.statement: Sending each coordinate to $S$ gives a bijection from the simultaneous roots in $R^n$ to those in $S^n$.
theorems.proof: Sending each coordinate to $S$ gives a bijection from the simultaneous roots in $R^n$ to those in $S^n$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Decomposition of countably generated Mittag–Leffler modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be henselian local, and $M$ a countably generated Mittag–Leffler module over $R$.
theorems.statement: The module $M$ splits as a direct sum of finitely presented $R$-modules.
theorems.proof: The module $M$ splits as a direct sum of finitely presented $R$-modules.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Base change of ind-étale algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A/R$ be ind-étale and $R\to T$ any map.
theorems.statement: The algebra $T\otimes_R A$ is ind-étale over $T$.
theorems.proof: The algebra $T\otimes_R A$ is ind-étale over $T$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Composition of ind-étale maps
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose both maps $A\to B\to C$ are ind-étale.
theorems.statement: Then $A\to C$ is ind-étale.
theorems.proof: Then $A\to C$ is ind-étale.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Filtered colimits of ind-étale algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Take a filtered diagram of ind-étale algebras over fixed $R$.
theorems.statement: Its colimit is ind-étale over $R$.
theorems.proof: Its colimit is ind-étale over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Directed colimits of ind-étale arrows
theorems.hypotheses: Take a directed system of arrows $R_i\to A_i$, all ind-étale.
theorems.statement: The map $\operatorname{colim} R_i\to\operatorname{colim} A_i$ is ind-étale.
theorems.proof: The map $\operatorname{colim} R_i\to\operatorname{colim} A_i$ is ind-étale.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Maps between ind-étale algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $A,B$ are ind-étale over $R$, and $A\to B$ is an $R$-map.
theorems.statement: Then $B$ is ind-étale over $A$.
theorems.proof: Then $B$ is ind-étale over $A$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Uniqueness of a henselian ind-étale algebra over a marked residue field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S,T$ be henselian local ind-étale $R$-algebras with identifications of their residue fields with the same $R$-algebra field $K$.
theorems.statement: There is a unique $R$-algebra isomorphism $S\to T$ respecting the maps to $K$.
theorems.proof: There is a unique $R$-algebra isomorphism $S\to T$ respecting the maps to $K$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Filtered local colimits of henselian rings
theorems.hypotheses: Take a filtered diagram of local rings with local transition maps.
theorems.statement: If all terms are henselian the colimit is henselian. If all are strictly henselian its residue field is separably closed and the colimit is strictly henselian.
theorems.proof: If all terms are henselian the colimit is henselian. If all are strictly henselian its residue field is separably closed and the colimit is strictly henselian.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Constructing strict henselization from finite separable residue extensions
theorems.hypotheses: Choose a separable closure $k^{\mathrm{sep}}$ of the residue field of $R$.
theorems.statement: The strict henselization is the filtered union of the finite étale local extensions of $R^h$ corresponding to finite intermediate fields $k\subset l\subset k^{\mathrm{sep}}$. Transition embeddings are specified by the residue inclusions.
theorems.proof: The strict henselization is the filtered union of the finite étale local extensions of $R^h$ corresponding to finite intermediate fields $k\subset l\subset k^{\mathrm{sep}}$. Transition embeddings are specified by the residue inclusions.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Lifting a pointed étale neighbourhood into a henselization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a local map of local rings with residue map $k\to l$. Take $A/R$ étale with prime $\mathfrak q$ over $\mathfrak m_R$ and residue field $k$.
theorems.statement: A unique $R$-map $A\to S^h$ contracts its maximal ideal to $\mathfrak q$.
theorems.proof: A unique $R$-map $A\to S^h$ contracts its maximal ideal to $\mathfrak q$.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Functoriality of henselization for local homomorphisms
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a local map of local rings with residue map $k\to l$.
theorems.statement: There is a unique local map $R^h\to S^h$ over the given homomorphism.
theorems.proof: There is a unique local map $R^h\to S^h$ over the given homomorphism.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Lifting a marked étale point to a strict henselization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a local map of local rings with residue map $k\to l$. Choose $l^{\mathrm{sep}}$ and an étale $A/R$, $\mathfrak q$ over $\mathfrak m_R$, with an embedding $\kappa(\mathfrak q)\to l^{\mathrm{sep}}$ over $k$.
theorems.statement: There is a unique $R$-map $A\to S^{\mathrm{sh}}$ contracting the maximal ideal to $\mathfrak q$ and inducing the specified embedding.
theorems.proof: There is a unique $R$-map $A\to S^{\mathrm{sh}}$ contracting the maximal ideal to $\mathfrak q$ and inducing the specified embedding.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Functoriality of strict henselization with marked residue closures
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a local map of local rings with residue map $k\to l$. Choose separable closures and an embedding $k^{\mathrm{sep}}\to l^{\mathrm{sep}}$ extending the residue map.
theorems.statement: This embedding is induced by a unique local map $R^{\mathrm{sh}}\to S^{\mathrm{sh}}$ over the given map.
theorems.proof: This embedding is induced by a unique local map $R^{\mathrm{sh}}\to S^{\mathrm{sh}}$ over the given map.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Pointed étale colimit presenting the henselization
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R$ and consider pointed étale $R$-algebras $(C,\mathfrak r)$ above $\mathfrak p$, where the residue map at the marked point is an isomorphism.
theorems.statement: The category of these neighbourhoods is filtered and both $\operatorname{colim} C$ and $\operatorname{colim} C_{\mathfrak r}$ canonically give the henselization of $R_{\mathfrak p}$.
theorems.proof: The category of these neighbourhoods is filtered and both $\operatorname{colim} C$ and $\operatorname{colim} C_{\mathfrak r}$ canonically give the henselization of $R_{\mathfrak p}$.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Pointed étale colimit presenting the strict henselization
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R$ and consider pointed étale $R$-algebras $(C,\mathfrak r)$ above $\mathfrak p$, where each residue field is equipped with a compatible embedding in a fixed separable closure of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.
theorems.statement: The category of these neighbourhoods is filtered and both $\operatorname{colim} C$ and $\operatorname{colim} C_{\mathfrak r}$ canonically give the strict henselization of $R_{\mathfrak p}$.
theorems.proof: The category of these neighbourhoods is filtered and both $\operatorname{colim} C$ and $\operatorname{colim} C_{\mathfrak r}$ canonically give the strict henselization of $R_{\mathfrak p}$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Henselization after a change to the henselian base
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}S$ lie over $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R$, and write $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$, $B=S_{\mathfrak q}$.
theorems.statement: There is exactly one prime of $A^h\otimes_R S$ above both $\mathfrak m_{A^h}$ and $\mathfrak q$. Henselizing at that prime gives $B^h$ compatibly with the canonical local map.
theorems.proof: There is exactly one prime of $A^h\otimes_R S$ above both $\mathfrak m_{A^h}$ and $\mathfrak q$. Henselizing at that prime gives $B^h$ compatibly with the canonical local map.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Strict henselization after strict henselian base change
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}S$ lie over $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R$, and write $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$, $B=S_{\mathfrak q}$. Choose compatible embeddings of the two separable residue closures.
theorems.statement: The strict henselization of $A^{\mathrm{sh}}\otimes_R S$ at the prime and geometric point determined by those choices identifies with $B^{\mathrm{sh}}$.
theorems.proof: The strict henselization of $A^{\mathrm{sh}}\otimes_R S$ at the prime and geometric point determined by those choices identifies with $B^{\mathrm{sh}}$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Comparing strict and ordinary henselizations over equal residue fields
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}S$ lie over $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R$, and write $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$, $B=S_{\mathfrak q}$. Suppose the residue map is an isomorphism and use the same separable closure on both sides.
theorems.statement: One has $B^{\mathrm{sh}}\cong B^h\otimes_{A^h} A^{\mathrm{sh}}$.
theorems.proof: One has $B^{\mathrm{sh}}\cong B^h\otimes_{A^h} A^{\mathrm{sh}}$.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Passing henselization through a local quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Take a local ring $R$, an ideal $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_R$ and compatible residue choices.
theorems.statement: The quotient $R^{h}/IR^{h}$ gives the henselization of $R/I$.
theorems.proof: The quotient $R^{h}/IR^{h}$ gives the henselization of $R/I$.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Passing strict henselization through a local quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Take a local ring $R$, an ideal $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_R$ and compatible residue choices.
theorems.statement: The quotient $R^{\mathrm{sh}}/IR^{\mathrm{sh}}$ gives the strict henselization of $R/I$.
theorems.proof: The quotient $R^{\mathrm{sh}}/IR^{\mathrm{sh}}$ gives the strict henselization of $R/I$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Finiteness after henselization at a quasi-finite point
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}S$ lie over $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R$, and write $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$, $B=S_{\mathfrak q}$. Suppose $R\to S$ quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$.
theorems.statement: The ring $B^h$ is the localization of $A^h\otimes_A B$ at the prime generated by $\mathfrak q$. The map $A^h\to B^h$ is finite.
theorems.proof: The ring $B^h$ is the localization of $A^h\otimes_A B$ at the prime generated by $\mathfrak q$. The map $A^h\to B^h$ is finite.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Finite strict henselization at a quasi-finite point
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}S$ lie over $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R$, and write $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$, $B=S_{\mathfrak q}$. Suppose quasi-finiteness at $\mathfrak q$. Choose a separable closure $l^s$ of $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ and its subfield $k^s$ of elements separable algebraic over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.
theorems.statement: The ring $B^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is the localization of $A^{\mathrm{sh}}\otimes_A B$ at the kernel of its residue map into $l^s$. The induced local map of strict henselizations is finite and $l^s/k^s$ is finite purely inseparable.
theorems.proof: The ring $B^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is the localization of $A^{\mathrm{sh}}\otimes_A B$ at the kernel of its residue map into $l^s$. The induced local map of strict henselizations is finite and $l^s/k^s$ is finite purely inseparable.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Local tensor products with an integral factor
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B,C$ be local maps of local rings. Assume $C/A$ integral and at least one of the two residue extensions purely inseparable.
theorems.statement: The ring $B\otimes_A C$ is local and both structure maps into it are local.
theorems.proof: The ring $B\otimes_A C$ is local and both structure maps into it are local.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Strict henselian base change for quasi-finite or integral algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Let $B,C$ be $A$-algebras and fix $B\otimes_A C\to k$ into a separably closed field. Take localizations and strict henselizations at the induced geometric points. Assume $B/A$ quasi-finite at the marked point, or $B$ a filtered colimit of quasi-finite $A$-algebras, or the analogous condition on the marked localizations, or $B/A$ integral.
theorems.statement: The canonical map $B^{\mathrm{sh}}\otimes_{A^{\mathrm{sh}}} C^{\mathrm{sh}}\to(B\otimes_A C)^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: The canonical map $B^{\mathrm{sh}}\otimes_{A^{\mathrm{sh}}} C^{\mathrm{sh}}\to(B\otimes_A C)^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Height-one intersection and absence of embedded primes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a Noetherian normal domain with fraction field $K$.
theorems.statement: Inside $K$, $R=\bigcap_{\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p=1}R_{\mathfrak p}$. For $0\ne a\in R$ or $0\ne x\in K$, the quotients by $aR$ and by $R\cap xR$ respectively have only associated primes of height one and no embedded primes.
theorems.proof: Inside $K$, $R=\bigcap_{\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p=1}R_{\mathfrak p}$. For $0\ne a\in R$ or $0\ne x\in K$, the quotients by $aR$ and by $R\cap xR$ respectively have only associated primes of height one and no embedded primes.

theorems.subject: field-element
theorems.name: Kernel of the differential over a perfect positive-characteristic field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K/k$ extend a perfect field of characteristic $p>0$ and $a\in K$.
theorems.statement: One has $da=0$ in $\Omega_{K/k}$ exactly when $a\in K^p$.
theorems.proof: One has $da=0$ in $\Omega_{K/k}$ exactly when $a\in K^p$.

theorems.subject: field-family
theorems.name: Degree after adjoining roots of differentially independent elements
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ have characteristic $p>0$ and suppose $da_1,\ldots,da_n$ are linearly independent in $\Omega_{k/\mathbf F_p}$.
theorems.statement: The extension $k(a_1^{1/p},\ldots,a_n^{1/p})/k$ has degree $p^n$.
theorems.proof: The extension $k(a_1^{1/p},\ldots,a_n^{1/p})/k$ has degree $p^n$.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Complete-intersection approximations to arbitrary field extensions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K/k$ be any extension.
theorems.statement: It is a filtered colimit of global complete intersection $k$-algebras. If $K/k$ is separable, it is also a filtered colimit of smooth $k$-algebras.
theorems.proof: It is a filtered colimit of global complete intersection $k$-algebras. If $K/k$ is separable, it is also a filtered colimit of smooth $k$-algebras.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Flat local extension with prescribed residue extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,k)$ be local and $K/k$ any field extension.
theorems.statement: There exists a flat local $R\to T$ with $\mathfrak m_T=\mathfrak mT$ and residue field $K$ over $k$.
theorems.proof: There exists a flat local $R\to T$ with $\mathfrak m_T=\mathfrak mT$ and residue field $K$ over $k$.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Realizing separable algebraic residue extensions by local finite étale stages
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,k)$ be local and $K/k$ separable algebraic.
theorems.statement: There is a directed system of finite étale local extensions of $R$ whose colimit has residue field $K$ compatibly over $k$.
theorems.proof: There is a directed system of finite étale local extensions of $R$ whose colimit has residue field $K$ compatibly over $k$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Finite free realization of a prescribed finite residue extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $L/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ a finite field extension.
theorems.statement: There exists a finite free $R$-algebra $S$ with $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak pS$ prime and whose extension of residue fields at $\mathfrak q$ is isomorphic to $L/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.
theorems.proof: There exists a finite free $R$-algebra $S$ with $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak pS$ prime and whose extension of residue fields at $\mathfrak q$ is isomorphic to $L/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Small flat subalgebras form a cofinal system
theorems.hypotheses: Let $B$ be a flat $A$-algebra and $\kappa=\max(|A|,\aleph_0)$.
theorems.statement: The flat $A$-subalgebras of $B$ of size at most $\kappa$ form a filtered family with union $B$. When $B/A$ is faithfully flat each such subalgebra is faithfully flat over $A$.
theorems.proof: The flat $A$-subalgebras of $B$ of size at most $\kappa$ form a filtered family with union $B$. When $B/A$ is faithfully flat each such subalgebra is faithfully flat over $A$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Quotients and finite algebras of a complete Noetherian local ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian complete local.
theorems.statement: Every nonzero quotient is Noetherian complete local. Every finite algebra is a finite product of Noetherian complete local rings, allowing the empty product for the zero algebra.
theorems.proof: Every nonzero quotient is Noetherian complete local. Every finite algebra is a finite product of Noetherian complete local rings, allowing the empty product for the zero algebra.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Existence of Cohen rings for arbitrary positive-characteristic residue fields
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$.
theorems.statement: There exists a complete discrete valuation ring $\Lambda$ with uniformizer $p$ and residue field isomorphic to $k$.
theorems.proof: There exists a complete discrete valuation ring $\Lambda$ with uniformizer $p$ and residue field isomorphic to $k$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Formal smoothness of truncated Cohen rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\Lambda$ be a Cohen ring of residue characteristic $p$ and $n\ge1$.
theorems.statement: The map $\mathbf Z/p^n\mathbf Z\to\Lambda/p^n\Lambda$ is formally smooth.
theorems.proof: The map $\mathbf Z/p^n\mathbf Z\to\Lambda/p^n\Lambda$ is formally smooth.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Regular complete local presentations over a field or Cohen ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $d\ge0$.
theorems.statement: Power series in $d$ variables form a regular complete Noetherian local ring of dimension $d$ over a field and of dimension $d+1$ over a Cohen ring. Every complete Noetherian local ring is a quotient of a regular local ring of one of these forms.
theorems.proof: Power series in $d$ variables form a regular complete Noetherian local ring of dimension $d$ over a field and of dimension $d+1$ over a Cohen ring. Every complete Noetherian local ring is a quotient of a regular local ring of one of these forms.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Equicharacteristic regular complete local power-series structure
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be complete Noetherian regular local and contain $\mathbf F_p$ or $\mathbf Q$.
theorems.statement: As a ring $R$ is a formal power-series ring over its residue field. Given $k\to R$ inducing the residue isomorphism, the presentation may be taken as an isomorphism of $k$-algebras.
theorems.proof: As a ring $R$ is a formal power-series ring over its residue field. Given $k\to R$ inducing the residue isomorphism, the presentation may be taken as an isomorphism of $k$-algebras.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Finite regular power-series subring of a complete local domain
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a Noetherian complete local domain.
theorems.statement: There exists a regular complete local subring $R_0$ over which $R$ is finite with identical residue field. The subring is a power-series ring in finitely many variables over a field or a Cohen ring.
theorems.proof: There exists a regular complete local subring $R_0$ over which $R$ is finite with identical residue field. The subring is a power-series ring in finitely many variables over a field or a Cohen ring.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Localization of Japanese and N-1 domains
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a domain and localize at a multiplicative set avoiding zero.
theorems.statement: If $R$ is N-1 its localization is N-1. If it is N-2 its localization is N-2.
theorems.proof: If $R$ is N-1 its localization is N-1. If it is N-2 its localization is N-2.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Finite principal-cover tests for N-1 and N-2
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a domain and let the finite family $f_i$ generate the unit ideal. Discard empty principal opens.
theorems.statement: If each $R_{f_i}$ is N-1, then $R$ is N-1. The same local test applies to N-2.
theorems.proof: If each $R_{f_i}$ is N-1, then $R$ is N-1. The same local test applies to N-2.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Quasi-finite domain extensions of a Noetherian Japanese domain
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\subset S$ be a quasi-finite extension of domains, and assume $R$ Noetherian and N-2.
theorems.statement: Then $S$ is N-2. This applies in particular to finite extensions of domains.
theorems.proof: Then $S$ is N-2. This applies in particular to finite extensions of domains.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Recovering N-1 from a Laurent polynomial algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a Noetherian domain with fraction field $K$.
theorems.statement: If $R[Z,Z^{-1}]$ has finite normalization in its fraction field then $R$ has finite normalization in $K$.
theorems.proof: If $R[Z,Z^{-1}]$ has finite normalization in its fraction field then $R$ has finite normalization in $K$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Normalization in a derivation-detected purely inseparable extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a Noetherian domain with fraction field $K$. Assume $R$ normal, $\operatorname{char}K=p>0$, and $D(a)\ne0$ for $a\in K$ under the extension of a derivation $D:R\to R$.
theorems.statement: The algebra $K[X]/(X^p-a)$ is a field and the integral closure of $R$ in it is finite over $R$.
theorems.proof: The algebra $K[X]/(X^p-a)$ is a field and the integral closure of $R$ in it is finite over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Polynomial extension of N-1 and N-2 domains
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a Noetherian domain with fraction field $K$.
theorems.statement: The polynomial ring $R[X]$ is N-1 if $R$ is N-1, and is N-2 if $R$ is N-2.
theorems.proof: The polynomial ring $R[X]$ is N-1 if $R$ is N-1, and is N-2 if $R$ is N-2.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Tate’s completeness criterion for a Japanese domain
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a Noetherian domain with fraction field $K$. Assume $R$ normal, $R\simeq\lim R/x^nR$ by the canonical map, and $R/xR$ a Japanese domain.
theorems.statement: Then $R$ is Japanese.
theorems.proof: Then $R$ is Japanese.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Formal power series over a Noetherian Japanese domain
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $R$ is Noetherian, a domain and N-2.
theorems.statement: The ring $R[[X]]$ is again a Noetherian Japanese domain.
theorems.proof: The ring $R[[X]]$ is again a Noetherian Japanese domain.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite integral closure inside a reduced essentially finite-type algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Nagata and $S$ a reduced algebra essentially of finite type over $R$.
theorems.statement: The subalgebra of elements of $S$ integral over $R$ is a finite $R$-module.
theorems.proof: The subalgebra of elements of $S$ integral over $R$ is a finite $R$-module.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Universally Japanese algebras essentially of finite type
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $R$ universally Japanese and $S/R$ essentially of finite type.
theorems.statement: The ring $S$ is universally Japanese.
theorems.proof: The ring $S$ is universally Japanese.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Quasi-finite algebras over a Nagata ring
theorems.hypotheses: Take a quasi-finite map $R\to S$ with $R$ Nagata.
theorems.statement: The target is Nagata. In particular this applies to every finite algebra.
theorems.proof: The target is Nagata. In particular this applies to every finite algebra.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Arbitrary localization of a Nagata ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Nagata and $U$ multiplicative in $R$.
theorems.statement: Then $U^{-1}R$ is Nagata.
theorems.proof: Then $U^{-1}R$ is Nagata.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Principal-cover tests for Nagata and universally Japanese rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f_1,\ldots,f_n$ generate the unit ideal of $R$.
theorems.statement: If all $R_{f_i}$ are universally Japanese so is $R$. If they are all Nagata then $R$ is Nagata.
theorems.proof: If all $R_{f_i}$ are universally Japanese so is $R$. If they are all Nagata then $R$ is Nagata.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Finite-type algebras over the standard classes of Nagata rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a field, a Noetherian complete local ring, $\mathbf Z$, or a Dedekind domain with characteristic-zero fraction field.
theorems.statement: The ring and all its finite-type algebras are Nagata and universally Japanese.
theorems.proof: The ring and all its finite-type algebras are Nagata and universally Japanese.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Lifting pth roots out of the completion of a Nagata local domain
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a Noetherian local Nagata domain of fraction-field characteristic $p>0$ and take $a\in A$.
theorems.statement: If $a$ is a $p$th power in $\widehat A$, it is already a $p$th power in $A$.
theorems.proof: If $a$ is a $p$th power in $\widehat A$, it is already a $p$th power in $A$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Universal catenarity need not descend along étale maps
theorems.hypotheses: Take the finite two-branch example of Stacks 02JE and the local étale neighbourhood from the cited remark.
theorems.statement: The target is universally catenary while its local Noetherian source fails universal catenarity.
theorems.proof: The target is universally catenary while its local Noetherian source fails universal catenarity.

theorems.subject: field-polynomial
theorems.name: Field obtained from an irreducible polynomial
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F$ be a field and let $P\in F[T]$ be irreducible.
theorems.statement: The quotient $F[T]/(P)$ is a field. The inclusion of constants makes it an extension of $F$. In particular $\mathbf R[T]/(T^2+1)\cong\mathbf C$.
theorems.proof: The ideal of an irreducible polynomial in the principal ideal domain $F[T]$ is maximal. A nonzero constant is a unit and cannot belong to this ideal.

theorems.subject: field
theorems.name: Fractions in a rational function field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F$ be a field and let $T$ be an indeterminate.
theorems.statement: The elements of $F(T)$ have representatives $P/Q$ with $P,Q\in F[T]$ and $Q\ne0$. Equality of two representatives is equivalent to $PQ'=P'Q$.
theorems.proof: Apply the fraction-field construction to the polynomial domain $F[T]$.

theorems.subject: field
theorems.name: Characteristics of the rational and finite prime fields
theorems.hypotheses: Take the rational field $\mathbf Q$ and the field $\mathbf F_p$ for a prime $p$.
theorems.statement: Their characteristics are $0$ and $p$, respectively.
theorems.proof: The canonical homomorphism from $\mathbf Z$ has zero kernel for $\mathbf Q$ and kernel $p\mathbf Z$ for $\mathbf F_p$.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: A polynomial residue class generates a field extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $P$ be irreducible in $F[T]$ for a field $F$, and write $a$ for the class of $T$ in $E=F[T]/(P)$.
theorems.statement: The constants give an inclusion $F\hookrightarrow E$ and $E=F(a)$.
theorems.proof: The quotient is a field and every residue class is a polynomial in $a$ with coefficients in $F$.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: The constant-field embedding for meromorphic functions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a nonempty connected Riemann surface.
theorems.statement: Taking constant functions embeds $\mathbf C$ as a subfield of the field $\mathbf C(X)$ of meromorphic functions.
theorems.proof: Constant functions are holomorphic, and distinct constants define distinct functions on the nonempty surface.

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Finiteness over an intermediate field
theorems.hypotheses: In a tower $F\subseteq E\subseteq K$ of algebraic extensions assume $[K:F]<\infty$.
theorems.statement: The degree $[K:E]$ is finite.
theorems.proof: An $F$-basis of $K$ is also an $E$-spanning set.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Power basis and degree of an irreducible polynomial quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Let $P\in F[T]$ be irreducible of degree $d$ over a field. Let $a$ denote the residue class of $T$ in $E=F[T]/(P)$.
theorems.statement: The elements $1,a,\ldots,a^{d-1}$ form an $F$-basis of $E$, so $[E:F]=d$.
theorems.proof: Division by $P$ gives a unique residue representative of degree less than $d$.
refs: Stacks 09G8 · coefficients of the polynomial relation

theorems.subject: field-polynomial
theorems.name: Leading coefficient in the power-basis relation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $P=\sum_{i=0}^d c_i T^i$ have degree $d>0$ in $F[T]$ and $c_d\ne0$. Write $a=T\bmod P$.
theorems.statement: One has $a^d=-c_d^{-1}\sum_{i=0}^{d-1}c_i a^i$ in $F[T]/(P)$.
theorems.proof: Evaluate the displayed source equation at the residue class $a$ and divide by the nonzero leading coefficient.
refs: Stacks 09G7 · power basis for an irreducible quotient

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: A real annihilating polynomial for every complex number
theorems.hypotheses: Take $z=a+bi\in\mathbf C$, with $a,b\in\mathbf R$.
theorems.statement: The polynomial $T^2-2aT+a^2+b^2$ vanishes at $z$. Thus $\mathbf C/\mathbf R$ is algebraic.
theorems.proof: The polynomial factors over $\mathbf C$ as $(T-z)(T-\bar z)$.

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Transitivity of algebraicity
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F\subseteq E\subseteq L$ be a tower with $E/F$ and $L/E$ algebraic.
theorems.statement: The extension $L/F$ is algebraic.
theorems.proof: For $a\in L$ the coefficients of its minimal polynomial over $E$ generate a finite extension $F'$ of $F$. Then $F'(a)/F'$ and $F'(a)/F$ are finite.

theorems.subject: field-extension-pair
theorems.name: Uniqueness of algebraic closure up to base-field isomorphism
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E$ and $L$ be algebraic closures of the same field $F$.
theorems.statement: There exists an $F$-isomorphism $E\to L$.
theorems.proof: Embed $E$ into $L$ over $F$. Its image is algebraically closed, and $L$ is algebraic over that image, so the embedding is surjective.
refs: Stacks 09GU · embedding in an algebraic closure

theorems.subject: field-polynomial
theorems.name: Frobenius preserves the number of distinct roots
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F$ have characteristic $p>0$, fix an algebraic closure $\overline F$, and let $P\in F[T]$.
theorems.statement: The sets of roots of $P(T^p)$ and $P(T)$ in $\overline F$ are in bijection.
theorems.proof: Frobenius $u\mapsto u^p$ is a bijection on $\overline F$. Its restriction maps the first root set onto the second.

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Embeddings correspond to compatible successive roots
theorems.hypotheses: Take the generating tower $K_i=F(a_1,\ldots,a_i)$ of a finite extension with $K_0=F$, $K_n=K$. Let $P_i$ be the minimal polynomial of $a_i$ over $K_{i-1}$, and fix $\overline F$.
theorems.statement: An $F$-embedding $K\to\overline F$ is uniquely determined by successive choices of roots $b_i$ of the coefficientwise images of $P_i$ under the previously chosen embedding of $K_{i-1}$. Each compatible tuple occurs.
theorems.proof: The presentation $K_i\cong K_{i-1}[T]/(P_i)$ extends the preceding embedding uniquely after specifying the image of $T$.

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Separability detected at every generator in a finite tower
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K_i=F(a_1,\ldots,a_i)$ be a generating tower for a finite extension $K/F$ ending at $K$, with $K_0=F$. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline F$.
theorems.statement: If every $a_i$ is separable over $K_{i-1}$, the number of $F$-embeddings of $K$ into $\overline F$ equals $[K:F]$ and $K/F$ is separable. If some $a_i$ is inseparable over $K_{i-1}$, that number is strictly smaller.
theorems.proof: Compare the product of the numbers of distinct roots of the successive minimal polynomials with the product of their degrees. Equality characterizes separability of a finite extension.

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Transitivity of algebraic separability
theorems.hypotheses: For a tower $F\subseteq E\subseteq L$, assume that $E/F$ and $L/E$ are separable algebraic.
theorems.statement: The extension $L/F$ is separable algebraic.
theorems.proof: Given $a\in L$, the coefficients of its separable minimal polynomial over $E$ lie in a finite separable extension $F'$ of $F$ inside $E$. The minimal polynomial of $a$ over $F'$ divides this separable polynomial. The finite tower criterion applies to $F'(a)/F$.

theorems.subject: field-map
theorems.name: Distinct field embeddings are linearly independent
theorems.hypotheses: Given extensions $K/F$ and $L/F$, let $\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_n:K\to L$ be distinct $F$-embeddings.
theorems.statement: As functions on $K$, the $\sigma_i$ are linearly independent over $L$.
theorems.proof: Apply independence of distinct multiplicative characters to the underlying multiplicative monoid of $K$ and the field $L$.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Separable degree counts embeddings of a finite extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K/F$ be finite with a fixed algebraic closure $\overline F$.
theorems.statement: The number of $F$-embeddings $K\to\overline F$ equals $[K:F]_s$.
theorems.proof: The maximal separable subextension has this many embeddings. Each extends uniquely across the purely inseparable remaining extension, since each required root is unique.
refs: Stacks 030K · separable and purely inseparable tower

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Cyclicity from bounds on every torsion subgroup
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be an abelian group, viewed as a $\mathbf Z$-module. Suppose $nA=0$ for $n\ge1$ and $|\ker(d:A\to A)|\le d$ for every positive divisor $d$ of $n$.
theorems.statement: The group $A$ is cyclic of order dividing $n$. For a finite subgroup of a field's multiplicative group the required bounds follow from the polynomials $T^d-1$.
theorems.proof: The bound with $d=n$ gives finiteness. If two or more nontrivial invariant factors occur, the torsion killed by the smallest factor $e$ has at least $e^2$ elements.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Trace and norm from two coefficients of the minimal polynomial
theorems.hypotheses: Let $L/K$ be finite and $a\in L$ have monic minimal polynomial $P(T)=T^d+c_1T^{d-1}+\cdots+c_d$. Put $e=[L:K(a)]$.
theorems.statement: Then $\operatorname{Tr}_{L/K}(a)=-ec_1$ and $\operatorname{N}_{L/K}(a)=(-1)^{[L:K]}c_d^e$.
theorems.proof: The characteristic polynomial of multiplication by $a$ is $P^e$. Compare the coefficient of degree $[L:K]-1$ and the constant coefficient.
refs: Stacks 0BIG · characteristic polynomial as a power

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Galois extension over an intermediate field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F\subseteq E\subseteq K$ be a tower of algebraic extensions with $K/F$ Galois.
theorems.statement: The extension $K/E$ is Galois.
theorems.proof: Both separability and normality pass from $K/F$ to $K/E$.
refs: Stacks 09H2 · separability over an intermediate field
Stacks 09HN · normality over an intermediate field

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: The normal closure of a finite separable extension is Galois
theorems.hypotheses: Let $L/K$ be finite separable and let $M$ be its normal closure over $K$ inside a fixed algebraic closure.
theorems.statement: The extension $M/K$ is finite Galois.
theorems.proof: The normal closure is generated by conjugates of finitely many separable generators of $L/K$. They remain separable over $K$, and normality holds by construction.

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: The restriction sequence of finite Galois groups
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K\subseteq M\subseteq L$, with $L/K$ and $M/K$ both finite Galois.
theorems.statement: Restriction gives the exact sequence $1\to\operatorname{Gal}(L/M)\to\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)\to\operatorname{Gal}(M/K)\to1$ of finite groups.
theorems.proof: Normality preserves $M$ and gives extensions of its $K$-automorphisms to $L$. The automorphisms fixing $M$ give the kernel.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Universal property of the Krull topology
theorems.hypotheses: Let $L/K$ be Galois, give $L$ the discrete topology, and give $G=\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)$ the coarsest topology making evaluation $G\times L\to L$ continuous. Let $X$ be a topological space.
theorems.statement: A function $u:X\to G$ is continuous exactly when $(x,a)\mapsto u(x)(a)$ is continuous on $X\times L$. In this topology $G$ is a profinite group.
theorems.proof: Continuity on the discrete slices is continuity of every coordinate evaluation. These coordinates generate the Krull topology, which is the inverse limit topology from finite Galois subextensions.
refs: Stacks 0BU2 · inverse system of finite Galois groups

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Continuous surjection onto the group of a Galois subextension
theorems.hypotheses: Take a tower $K\subseteq M\subseteq L$ with $L/K$ and $M/K$ Galois. Give the Galois groups their Krull topologies.
theorems.statement: Restriction $\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)\to\operatorname{Gal}(M/K)$ is a continuous surjective homomorphism.
theorems.proof: Normality allows lifting every $K$-automorphism of $M$. The inverse image of a pointwise stabilizer of a finite subset of $M$ is the pointwise stabilizer of that subset in the larger group.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Galois extensions as unions and Galois groups as inverse limits
theorems.hypotheses: Let $L/K$ be Galois. Order its finite Galois subextensions $L_\lambda/K$ by inclusion and set $G_\lambda=\operatorname{Gal}(L_\lambda/K)$.
theorems.statement: These subextensions form a directed system whose union is $L$. Restriction gives an inverse system of finite groups with surjective transitions and a topological group isomorphism $\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)\cong\varprojlim_\lambda G_\lambda$. Every projection is continuous and surjective.
theorems.proof: Each finite subset of $L$ lies in a finite Galois subextension. Compatible finite restrictions glue to an automorphism of the union. Stabilizers of the finite subextensions give a neighbourhood basis at the identity.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Transcendence degree of the field generated by e and π
theorems.hypotheses: Consider $\mathbf Q(e,\pi)\subset\mathbf R$. Both generators are transcendental over $\mathbf Q$.
theorems.statement: Its transcendence degree is $1$ or $2$. It is $2$ exactly when the two generators are algebraically independent. The source records their algebraic independence as an open question.
theorems.proof: Either generator alone gives a transcendence-degree-one subfield. The two-element generating set bounds the transcendence degree above by two.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Compact Riemann surfaces and one-variable function fields
theorems.hypotheses: Use compact connected Riemann surfaces with nonconstant holomorphic maps, and finitely generated field extensions of $\mathbf C$ of transcendence degree one with $\mathbf C$-embeddings.
theorems.statement: The assignment $X\mapsto\mathbf C(X)$ on objects and pullback on functions is a contravariant equivalence of these categories. Over an algebraically closed field $k$, smooth projective integral curves and nonconstant morphisms have the analogous correspondence with one-variable function fields over $k$.
theorems.proof: The source cites Forster for compact Riemann surfaces. In the algebraic statement, a one-variable function field has a smooth projective model, and field embeddings correspond to dominant rational maps, which extend to morphisms on the smooth proper models.

theorems.subject: ring-presentation
theorems.name: A Jacobian witness at a smooth prime
theorems.hypotheses: Write $A=P/I$ for a finite polynomial presentation with $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$. Suppose $R\to A$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q$.
theorems.statement: After reordering generators and variables, some $a\notin\mathfrak q$ is a multiple of a $c$-minor on the first $c$ equations and $aI\subseteq(f_1,\ldots,f_c)+I^2$ using any lift of $a$ to $P$.
theorems.proof: After reordering generators and variables, some $a\notin\mathfrak q$ is a multiple of a $c$-minor on the first $c$ equations and $aI\subseteq(f_1,\ldots,f_c)+I^2$ using any lift of $a$ to $P$.

theorems.subject: ring-presentation
theorems.name: Jacobian minors and a scalar splitting up to a power
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $A=P/I$, $c$ chosen equations and a scalar $a\in A$. Let $D:A^c\to I/I^2\to\Omega_{P/R}\otimes_PA$ send basis vectors to the differentials of the chosen equations.
theorems.statement: Membership of $a$ in the ideal of $c$-minors of $D$ gives an $A$-linear $v$ with $vD=a\,\mathrm{id}$. Conversely such a $v$ gives membership of $a^c$ in the minors ideal by taking determinants.
theorems.proof: Membership of $a$ in the ideal of $c$-minors of $D$ gives an $A$-linear $v$ with $vD=a\,\mathrm{id}$. Conversely such a $v$ gives membership of $a^c$ in the minors ideal by taking determinants.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Elkik’s description of the singular ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Take $A$ finitely presented over $R$.
theorems.statement: The radical of the ideal generated by the elementary standard elements equals $H_{A/R}$. The strictly standard elements generate an ideal with the same radical.
theorems.proof: The radical of the ideal generated by the elementary standard elements equals $H_{A/R}$. The strictly standard elements generate an ideal with the same radical.

theorems.subject: algebra-element
theorems.name: Standard elements persist after arbitrary base change
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be finitely presented over $R$, and take a homomorphism $R\to T$.
theorems.statement: If $a$ is elementary standard, its image in $A\otimes_R T$ is elementary standard over $T$. The corresponding assertion holds separately for strictly standard elements.
theorems.proof: If $a$ is elementary standard, its image in $A\otimes_R T$ is elementary standard over $T$. The corresponding assertion holds separately for strictly standard elements.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Smooth factorization when the singular ideal becomes the unit ideal
theorems.hypotheses: For $R\to A\to L$ let $A$ be finitely presented over $R$ and $H_{A/R}L=L$.
theorems.statement: The map to $L$ factors as $A\to B\to L$ with $B$ smooth over $R$.
theorems.proof: The map to $L$ factors as $A\to B\to L$ with $B$ smooth over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-presentation
theorems.name: A retract with improved conormal and differential modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a finitely presented $R$-algebra.
theorems.statement: There is a finite type map $A\to C$ with an $A$-algebra retraction. Whenever $R\to A_a$ is lci, $C_a$ is smooth over $A_a$ and has a finite-variable polynomial presentation over $R$ with free conormal module. Wherever $R\to A_a$ is smooth, $\Omega_{C_a/R}$ is free over $C_a$.
theorems.proof: There is a finite type map $A\to C$ with an $A$-algebra retraction. Whenever $R\to A_a$ is lci, $C_a$ is smooth over $A_a$ and has a finite-variable polynomial presentation over $R$ with free conormal module. Wherever $R\to A_a$ is smooth, $\Omega_{C_a/R}$ is free over $C_a$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Lifting smooth and syntomic algebras across any surjection
theorems.hypotheses: Take a surjection $R\to R_0$ with kernel $I$ and an $R_0$-algebra $A_0$.
theorems.statement: If $A_0$ is smooth over $R_0$ there exists a smooth $R$-algebra $A$ with $A/IA\simeq A_0$. The same assertion holds with syntomicity in both places.
theorems.proof: If $A_0$ is smooth over $R_0$ there exists a smooth $R$-algebra $A$ with $A/IA\simeq A_0$. The same assertion holds with syntomicity in both places.

theorems.subject: ring-presentation
theorems.name: Syntomic algebras as retracts of relative complete intersections
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be syntomic over $R$.
theorems.statement: There is a smooth split $A$-algebra $C$ that is a global relative complete intersection over $R$. It admits a presentation on $n$ variables with $c$ equations, flat over $R$, with nonempty fibres of pure dimension $n-c$.
theorems.proof: There is a smooth split $A$-algebra $C$ that is a global relative complete intersection over $R$. It admits a presentation on $n$ variables with $c$ equations, flat over $R$, with nonempty fibres of pure dimension $n-c$.

theorems.subject: ring-presentation
theorems.name: Smooth algebras as retracts of standard smooth algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Take a smooth $R$-algebra $A$.
theorems.statement: There is a smooth $A$-algebra $B$ with an $A$-algebra retraction such that $B$ admits a standard smooth presentation over $R$. In that presentation a square Jacobian minor of size the number of equations is a unit.
theorems.proof: There is a smooth $A$-algebra $B$ with an $A$-algebra retraction such that $B$ admits a standard smooth presentation over $R$. In that presentation a square Jacobian minor of size the number of equations is a unit.

theorems.subject: ring-presentation
theorems.name: Prescribing variables in a standard smooth presentation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be standard smooth over $R$ and fix $n$ distinct elements of $A$.
theorems.statement: A standard smooth presentation can include these elements as the first $n$ coordinate classes, with $c\ge n$ equations and the Jacobian minor for the first $c$ variables invertible.
theorems.proof: A standard smooth presentation can include these elements as the first $n$ coordinate classes, with $c\ge n$ equations and the Jacobian minor for the first $c$ variables invertible.

theorems.subject: algebra-element
theorems.name: Power converses for standard-element tests
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $a$ in a finitely presented $R$-algebra $A$.
theorems.statement: When $A_a$ is smooth with stably free $\Omega_{A_a/R}$, all sufficiently high powers of $a$ are strictly standard in $A$. When $A_a$ is standard smooth, all sufficiently high powers are elementary standard.
theorems.proof: When $A_a$ is smooth with stably free $\Omega_{A_a/R}$, all sufficiently high powers of $a$ are strictly standard in $A$. When $A_a$ is standard smooth, all sufficiently high powers are elementary standard.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Functoriality of the affine Néron blowup
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\subseteq V$ be DVRs of ramification index one with common uniformizer $\pi$. Factor $R\to A\to V$ with $A$ flat of finite type. Write $\mathfrak q=\ker(A\to V)$ and $\mathfrak p$ for the preimage of the maximal ideal of $V$. Let $A'=A[\mathfrak p/\pi]$ with the induced primes $\mathfrak q',\mathfrak p'$.
theorems.statement: For $a\notin\mathfrak p$, the blowup of $A_a$ is $(A')_a$. For a surjection $B\to A$ of flat finite type $R$-algebras with kernel $I$, the blowup of $A$ is the quotient of $B'/IB'$ by its $\pi$-power torsion, using the centre induced on $B$.
theorems.proof: For $a\notin\mathfrak p$, the blowup of $A_a$ is $(A')_a$. For a surjection $B\to A$ of flat finite type $R$-algebras with kernel $I$, the blowup of $A$ is the quotient of $B'/IB'$ by its $\pi$-power torsion, using the centre induced on $B$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Differentials after blowing up a smooth valuation centre
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\subseteq V$ be DVRs of ramification index one with common uniformizer $\pi$. Factor $R\to A\to V$ with $A$ flat of finite type. Write $\mathfrak q=\ker(A\to V)$ and $\mathfrak p$ for the preimage of the maximal ideal of $V$. Let $A'=A[\mathfrak p/\pi]$ with the induced primes $\mathfrak q',\mathfrak p'$. Assume smoothness at $\mathfrak p$ and separability of the residue extension of the DVRs. Put $c=\dim((A/\pi A)_{\mathfrak p})$.
theorems.statement: Then $A'$ is smooth over $R$ at $\mathfrak p'$. There is an exact sequence $0\to\Omega_{A/R}\otimes_AA'_{\mathfrak p'}\to(\Omega_{A'/R})_{\mathfrak p'}\to((A'/\pi A')_{\mathfrak p'})^c\to0$.
theorems.proof: Then $A'$ is smooth over $R$ at $\mathfrak p'$. There is an exact sequence $0\to\Omega_{A/R}\otimes_AA'_{\mathfrak p'}\to(\Omega_{A'/R})_{\mathfrak p'}\to((A'/\pi A')_{\mathfrak p'})^c\to0$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Néron smoothness test via a free differential cokernel
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\subseteq V$ be DVRs of ramification index one with common uniformizer $\pi$. Factor $R\to A\to V$ with $A$ flat of finite type. Write $\mathfrak q=\ker(A\to V)$ and $\mathfrak p$ for the preimage of the maximal ideal of $V$. Let $A'=A[\mathfrak p/\pi]$ with the induced primes $\mathfrak q',\mathfrak p'$. Assume $A$ smooth at $\mathfrak q$, and choose a surjection $B\to A$ of $R$-algebras with kernel $I$, with $B$ smooth over $R$ at the preimage of $\mathfrak p$.
theorems.statement: If the cokernel of $(I/I^2)\otimes_A V\to\Omega_{B/R}\otimes_BV$ is free over $V$, then $A$ is smooth over $R$ at $\mathfrak p$.
theorems.proof: If the cokernel of $(I/I^2)\otimes_A V\to\Omega_{B/R}\otimes_BV$ is free over $V$, then $A$ is smooth over $R$ at $\mathfrak p$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Finite iteration of affine Néron blowups
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\subseteq V$ be DVRs of ramification index one with common uniformizer $\pi$. Factor $R\to A\to V$ with $A$ flat of finite type. Write $\mathfrak q=\ker(A\to V)$ and $\mathfrak p$ for the preimage of the maximal ideal of $V$. Let $A'=A[\mathfrak p/\pi]$ with the induced primes $\mathfrak q',\mathfrak p'$. Assume $A$ smooth at $\mathfrak q$ and the residue extension of the DVRs separable.
theorems.statement: After finitely many blowups at the successive valuation centres the resulting algebra is smooth over $R$ at its centre.
theorems.proof: After finitely many blowups at the successive valuation centres the resulting algebra is smooth over $R$ at its centre.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Ind-smoothness for an extension of DVRs
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $R\subseteq V$ are DVRs of ramification index one and both their residue-field extension and their fraction-field extension are separable.
theorems.statement: Then $V$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $R$-algebras. The field separability assumptions allow extensions of positive transcendence degree.
theorems.proof: Then $V$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $R$-algebras. The field separability assumptions allow extensions of positive transcendence degree.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A first lift across a square-zero ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I^2=0$ in $R$, assume $L/IL$ is ind-smooth over $R/I$, and fix a finitely presented $R$-algebra $A$ mapping to $L$.
theorems.statement: The map factors over $R$ as $A\to B/J\to L$ with $B$ smooth over $R$ and $J$ a finitely generated ideal contained in $IB$.
theorems.proof: The map factors over $R$ as $A\to B/J\to L$ with $B$ smooth over $R$ and $J$ a finitely generated ideal contained in $IB$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Eliminating the remaining square-zero relations
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I^2=0$ in $R$, let $L$ be flat over $R$ with $L/IL$ ind-smooth over $R/I$, and let $B\to L$ be an $R$-algebra map from a smooth algebra. Suppose $J\subseteq IB$ is a finitely generated ideal killed in $L$.
theorems.statement: There is a factorization $B\to B'\to L$ with $B'$ smooth over $R$ such that $J$ already maps to zero in $B'$.
theorems.proof: There is a factorization $B\to B'\to L$ with $B'$ smooth over $R$ such that $J$ already maps to zero in $B'$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Ind-smoothness lifts across a nilpotent base ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $R\to L$ is flat, $I\subseteq R$ is nilpotent and $L/IL$ is ind-smooth over $R/I$.
theorems.statement: Then $L$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $R$-algebras.
theorems.proof: Then $L$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $R$-algebras.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Lifting a finite presentation and its smooth locus from a thickening
theorems.hypotheses: Write $E_T(\pi)$ for the equality $\operatorname{Ann}_T(\pi)=\operatorname{Ann}_T(\pi^2)$. Let $R$ be Noetherian, $R\to L$ a map satisfying $E_R(\pi)$ and $E_L(\pi)$, and $R/\pi^2R\to \bar C\to L/\pi^2L$ a diagram with $\bar C$ finitely presented over $R/\pi^2R$.
theorems.statement: There are a finitely presented $R$-algebra $D\to L$ and a map $\bar C\to D/\pi D$ compatible modulo $\pi$. The map $R\to D$ is smooth off $V(\pi)$ and at each prime in $V(\pi)$ mapping to the smooth locus of $\bar C$ over $R/\pi^2R$. The map $\bar C/\pi\bar C\to D/\pi D$ is smooth at every prime over that same locus.
theorems.proof: There are a finitely presented $R$-algebra $D\to L$ and a map $\bar C\to D/\pi D$ compatible modulo $\pi$. The map $R\to D$ is smooth off $V(\pi)$ and at each prime in $V(\pi)$ mapping to the smooth locus of $\bar C$ over $R/\pi^2R$. The map $\bar C/\pi\bar C\to D/\pi D$ is smooth at every prime over that same locus.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Improving the singular ideal from a fourth-order retraction
theorems.hypotheses: Write $E_T(\pi)$ for the equality $\operatorname{Ann}_T(\pi)=\operatorname{Ann}_T(\pi^2)$. Let $R$ be Noetherian, $A$ finitely presented over $R$ and $A\to L$ given. Assume $E_L(\pi)$, with $\pi\in R$ strictly standard in $A$, and an $R/\pi^4R$-algebra retraction $A/\pi^4A\to R/\pi^4R$ compatible with the map to $L/\pi^4L$.
theorems.statement: There is a factorization $A\to B\to L$ over $R$ with $B$ finitely presented and $\operatorname{Ann}_R(\operatorname{Ann}_R(\pi^2)/\operatorname{Ann}_R(\pi))B\subseteq H_{B/R}$.
theorems.proof: There is a factorization $A\to B\to L$ over $R$ with $B$ finitely presented and $\operatorname{Ann}_R(\operatorname{Ann}_R(\pi^2)/\operatorname{Ann}_R(\pi))B\subseteq H_{B/R}$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Simultaneous factorization preserving two smooth loci
theorems.hypotheses: Write $E_T(\pi)$ for the equality $\operatorname{Ann}_T(\pi)=\operatorname{Ann}_T(\pi^2)$. Let $R$ be Noetherian with $E_R(\pi)$ and $E_L(\pi)$, and let $A,D$ be finitely presented $R$-algebras mapping to $L$. Assume $\pi$ is strictly standard in $A$ and a map $A/\pi^4A\to D/\pi^4D$ over $R$ commutes with the maps to $L/\pi^4L$.
theorems.statement: There is a finitely presented $R$-algebra $B$ mapping to $L$ through which both original maps factor, with $H_{D/R}B\subseteq H_{B/D}$ and $H_{D/R}B\subseteq H_{B/R}$.
